body.text: Āryavimalakīrtinirdeśo nāma mahāyānasūtram
1. buddhakṣetrapariśuddhinidānam namaḥ sarvātītapratyutpannānāgatebhyo buddhabodhi- sattvāryaśrāvakapratyekabuddhebhyaḥ /

evaṃ mayā śrutam- eakasmin samaye bhagavān vaiśālyāṃ viharati sma āmrapālīvane mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdham aṣṭābhirbhikṣusahasraiḥ, sarvairarhadbhiḥ kṣīṇāsravairniḥkleśairvaśībhūtaiḥ suvimuktacittaiḥ suvimuktaprajñairājāneyairmahānāgaiḥ kṛtakṛtyaiḥ kṛtakaraṇīyairapahṛtabhārairanuprāptasvakārthaiḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaiḥ sabhyagājñāsuvimuktacittaiḥ sarvacetovaśitāparamapāramitāprāptaiḥ /

dvātriṃśadā ca bodhisattvasahastraiḥ sārdham- abhijñānābhijñātairbodhisattvairmahābhijñāparikarmaniryātairbuddhādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitairdharmanagarapālaiḥ saddharmaparigrāhakairmahāsiṃhanādibhirdaśadikṣu sugarjitanādairanadhyeṣitaṃ sarvasattvānām kalyāṇamitrabhūtaistriratnagotrānācchedyakāribhirnibṛtamārapratyarthikaiḥ sarvaparapravādyanabhibhūtaiḥ smṛtibuddhyavabodhasamādhidhāraṇīpratibhānasampannaiḥ sarvāvaraṇaparyutthānavigatairanāvaraṇavimokṣa upasthitairanācchedyapratibhānairdānadamaniyamasaṃyamaśīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñopāyakauśalyapraṇidhānabalajñānapāramitāniryātairanupalabdhidharmakṣāntisamanvāgatairavaivartikadharmacakrapravartayadbhiralakṣaṇamudrāmudritaiḥ sarvasattvendriyajñānakuśalaiḥ sarvaparṣadanabhibhūtasya baiśāradyena bikrāmibhirmahāpuṇyajñānasaṃbhārasaṃcitavadbhiḥ sarvalakṣaṇānuvyaṃjanālaṃkṛtakāyairvariṣṭharūpadhāribhiścālaṃkārāpagataiḥ sumerūnnataśikhara iva yaśaḥkīrtyabhyudgatairvajradṛḍhādhyāśayena buddhadharmasaṃghe 'bhedyaśraddhāpratilabdhairdharmaratnaraśmyāmṛtavṛṣṭiṃ supravarṣayadbhiḥ sarvasattvānāṃ śabdavāgaṃgasvaraśabdaviśuddhyupetasvarairgambhīradharmapratītyasamutpāde pratipadyāntānantadṛṣṭivāsanānāṃ saṃdhisamantacchedairnirbhayasiṃhasadṛśairghoṣābhinirnādibhirmahādharmameghasvaranādibhiḥ samavisamadharmasamatikrāntairdharmaratnasya prajñāpuṇyasaṃbhārasamudāgamasya mahāsārthavāhaiḥ; utthāpanasya ca śāntasūkṣmaślakṣṇasya ca durdṛśasya duravagāhyasya dharmasya naye vicakṣaṇaiḥ; sarvasattvāgamanirgamasattvāśayagatyanupraveśa jñānaviṣayasamarpitaiḥ; asamasamabuddhajñāne 'bhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktairdaśabala vaiśāradya āveṇikabuddhadharme(ṣva-) adhyāśayena pratipannaiḥ; sarvāpāyabhairavadurgati binipātabhayasya parikhāyā uttīrya, saṃcintya sambhavasya gatyutpattideśikairmahāvaidyarājaiḥ
sarvasattvavinayasya vidhividvadbhiḥ sarvasattvānāṃ sarvakleśarogāvabodhaiḥ; yathāyogaṃ dharmabhaiṣajyayuktisuprayuktavadbhirguṇānant ākarasamarpitairanantabuddhakṣetrāṇi guṇavyūhena svālaṃkṛtavadbhiramoghadarśanaśravaṇairabandhyapādotsargaiḥ; koṭinayutaśatasahasrāprameyakalpe(ṣva-)pi guṇān parivarṇayet, guṇaugho 'nanto 'dhigataḥ / tadyathā-

samadarśināma bodhisattvena ca samāsamadarśinā ca samādhivikurvitarājena ca dharmeśvareṇa ca dharmaketunā ca prabhāketunā ca prabhāvyūhena ca ratnavyūhena ca mahāvyūhena ca pratibhānakūṭena ca ratnakūṭena ca ratnapāṇinā ca ratnamudrāhastena ca nityapralambahastena ca nityotkṣiptahastena ca nityatapasā ca nityanandahāsendriyeṇa ca prāmodyarājena ca devarājena ca praṇidhānavyasanānuprāptena pratisaṃvitprasādhanaprāptena ca gaganagaṃjena ca ratnapradīpadhareṇa ca ratnavīreṇa ca ratnanandinā ca ratnaśriyā cendrajālena ca jālinīprabheṇa cānupalabdhidhyānena ca prajñākūṭena ca ratnamuktena ca mārahantrā ca vidyuddevena ca bikurvaṇarājena ca nimittakūṭasamatikrāntena ca siṃhagarjitābhyavaghoṣaṇasvareṇa ca giryagrasamudghātarājena ca gandhahastinā ca gandhakuṃjaranāgena ca nityodyuktena cānikṣiptadhureṇa ca pramatinā ca sundarajātena ca padmaśrīgarbheṇa padmavyūhena cāvalokiteśvareṇa ca mahāsthāmaprāptena ca brahmamajālakena ca ratnaśvetāsanena ca mārajitā ca samakṣetrālaṅkāreṇa ca maṇiratnacchatreṇa ca maṇicūḍena ca maitreyeṇa ca mañjuśrīkumārabhūtena ca tairityādibhirdvātriṃśadā bodhisattvasahasraiḥ (sārdham)

catuṣka mahādvipāśoka-(nāma)-nāmalokadhātorbrahmaśikhyādayo daśasahasram brahmaṇāṃ bhagavato darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya cāgatāḥ / te 'pi tasyāṃ parṣadyeva saṃnipatitāḥ / nānācatuṣkamahādvīp(ebhyo) 'pi dvādaśasahasraṃ śakrāṇām āgatam / te 'pi tasyāṃ parṣadyeva saṃnipatitāaḥ / evam anyacca maheśākhyamaheśākhyā brahmā kauśikaśca lokapāladevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragarūḍakinnaramahoragā api tasyāṃ parṣadyeva saṃnipatitā abhūvan / evameva catuṣpariṣad bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā api tatra saṃnipatitā āsuḥ /

atha bhagavāṃśrīgarbhe siṃhāsane niṣaṇṇo 'nekaśatasahasraparṣadā parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto dharma deśayati sma / sumerūriva parvatarājaḥ samudrābhyudgataḥ sarvāḥ parṣado 'bhibhūya bhāsate tapati virocate sma śrīgarbhe sihāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ /

tato licchavikumāro ratnākaro bodhisatvo licchavikumārāṇām pañcaśatamātrañca saptaratnacchatraṃ samādāya, vaiśālyā mahānagaryā niśvarya, yenāmrapālīvanaṃca yena bhavavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāaḥ / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādayoaḥ śirasā vanditvā, bhagavati saptakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya te ratnacchatraṃ yathā dhāriṇo bhagavantam abhitrāyante sma / abhipālayitvaikānte sthuaḥ /

tāni niryātitāni ratnacchatrāṇi samanantaraṃ sadyo buddhānubhāvenaikībhūtvā, tena ratnacchatreṇāyaṃ sarvatrisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuaḥ saṃchāditaḥ pratibhāti sma / sa trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātupariṇāhaśva tasyaiva mahāratnacchatrasya madhye prabhāsito('bhūt) (ye) 'smin trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau kecana(parvatāḥ)- syuaḥ sumeruḥ parvatarājaśva himavantaparvataśca mucilindaparvataśva mahāmucilinda parvataśca gandhamādanaśca ratnaparvatacca kālaparvataśca cakravāḍaśca mahācakravāḍaśca- sarve te 'pi tasyaiva mahāratnacchatrasya madhye prabhāsitā(abhūvan) / yadasmin trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau kiṃcij (jala) syāt mahāsamudrasarastaḍāgapuṣkaraṇīnadīkunadīpalvalanimnaṃ- sarvam tadapi tasyaiva mahāratnacchatrasya madhye prabhāsitam (abhūt) / asmin trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātāvādityacandravimānāśva tārakārūpāṇi devabhavanāni ca nāgapurāṇi ca yakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakiṃnaramahoragāvāsāśva caturmahārājaprāsādāśva grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānyo yāvatakāḥ syuḥ; sarvāstā api tasyaivaikākino mahāratnacchatrasyābhāsaṃ gacchanti sma / daśadigloke bhagavatām buddhānāṃ yā dharmadeśanotpannā, sāpi tasmādekākino mahāratnachatrān nirgate svare nadati sma /

atha bhagavato 'smin evaṃ rūpe mahāprātihārye dṛṣṭe, sā sarvāvatī parṣadāścaryaprāptābhūt / tuṣṭodagrāttamanāḥ pramuditā prītisaumanasyajātā tathāgatam abhivandyānimiṣābhyāṃ netrābhyāṃ paśyatyasthāt /
tato ratnākaro licchavikumāro bhagavata idaṃ evaṃ rūpaṃ mahāprātihārya dṛṣṭvā, dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya, yena bhagavāṃstenāṃjaliṃ praṇamya, bhagavantam ābhirgāthābhirabhyanandat-

"viśālanetra śuddharucirapadmadalavat / śubhābhiprāya śamathapāragata paramaprāpta // kuśalakarmācitavanaprameyaguṇasāgara / namastubhyaṃ śramaṇāya śāntimārgasaṃniśritāya // puruṣavṛṣabhasya yūyannāyakasyarddhividhim paśyata / sugatasya sarvāṇyapi kṣetrāṇi pravaravyaktāni dṛśyante // tava dharmakathodārāmṛtagā / tāni sarvāṇyasmin gaganatale dṛśyante // tavottamadharmarājyam idam, dharmarāja / jinena ca jagadbhayo dharmadhanam pradalitam // dharmaprabhedanavijñāya paramārthasaṃdarśakāya / dharmeśvarāya dharmarājāya tubhyaṃ śirasā namaḥ // 'astināstya pagatāḥ sarva ime dharmā hetūn pratītyasamutpannāḥ / eṣvātmavedakakārakā na santi / kuśalapāpakarma kiṃcidavipraṇāśam' iti vacanenopadarśayasi // tvayā munīndra, mārātibalabalaṃ saṃjitya / paramapraśāntabodhyamaraṇakṣemaṃ prāptam // tattatra nirvedanacittamano 'pracāraiaḥ /
sarvatīrthikakugaṇairajñātam // adbhutaṃ dharmarājadevamanuṣyāṇāmabhimukham / triparivarta bahvākāraṃ praśāntasvabhāvaviśuddhaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayasi / tadanantaraṃ triratnam upadiśyate // ye dharmaratnena suvinītāḥ / te 'vitarkā nityapraśāntāḥ // tvaṃ hi jātijarāmaraṇāntago vaidyo varaḥ / aprameyaguṇasāgarāya śirasā namaḥ //

satkārasukṛtaissumerurivāprakampyaḥ / śīlavatsu ca duḥśīleṣu ca samam maitrī // samatāsaṃprasthito manaśvākāśavat / asmai sattvaratnāya kuryāt pūjānna kaḥ?
mahāmune imā hi parṣadaḥ saṃnipatitāḥ / tava mukhaṃ suprasādamanasā prekṣante // sarvairapi jinaḥ svābhimukhe dṛṣṭaḥ / taddhruvam jinasyāveṇikabuddhalakṣaṇam // bhagavata ekavāk pravartitā, paraṃ tu (sā) / parṣadbhirnānāvākṣu vijñāyate // vijñāyate sarvajagatā svakārtho yathā / taddhruvam jinasyāveṇikabuddhalakṣaṇam // tenaikavāksvavaghoṣaṇakāryeṇa / kecit vāsanāparibhāvitāḥ kecit pratipannaḥ // (yā) vimatyākāṃkṣāḥ, tā nāyakaḥ pratiprasrabhbhayati ma / taddhruvam jinasyāveṇikabuddhalakṣaṇam // daśabalanāyakavikrāmiṇe tubhyaṃ namaḥ / namaste 'bhayāya bhayavipramuktāya // āveṇikadharmānavasyaṃ supratipannāya / sarvajagannetre tubhyaṃ namaḥ / namaḥ sarvasaṃyojanabandhanacchedakāya // pāragatāya sthalasthitāya namaḥ / khinnajagattārakāya tubhyaṃ namaḥ / namaḥ saṃsāraprabṛttyām apratiṣṭhitāya // sattvagatisaṃprasthitaḥ sarvasahacaraḥ / paraṃ tu (te) sarvagativimuktamanaḥ // pariśuddhapadmamudake jātamudakena paryanupaliptam / munipadmena śūnyatā bhāvitā dhruvam // sarvākāranimittāni saṃpravāntāni / tvaṃ kasmiṃśvit praṇidhānakārī nāsi // pariśuddhasya buddhasya mahānubhāvo 'cintyaḥ / ākāśasadṛśam apratiṣṭhitaṃ vandāmyaham" //

atha bhagavantaṃ tābhirgāthābhirabhinandya, ratnākareṇa licchavikumāreṇa bhagavantam evamuktam- "bhagavan, ebhyo licchavikumārebhyaḥ paṃcaśatamātrebhyaḥ sarvebhyo 'nuttarasamyak saṃbodhyāṃ saṃpratipannebhyo 'bodhisattvānāṃ pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ kim'- iti pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ pṛcchadbhyo bhagavatā tathāgatenaibhyo bodhisattvebhyaḥ pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sūktam deśitaṃ syāt /

evamukte, bhagavān ratnākarāya licchavikumārāya sādhukāram adāt- "sādhu sādhu kumāra / sādhu (yathā) tvaṃ pariśuddaṃ buddhakṣetram ārabhya, tathāgatam pṛcchasi / tena hi kumāra tvaṃ śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru / bodhisattvānām pariśuddhaṃ buddha kṣetram ārabhya bhāṣiṣyehaṃ te" / -"sādhu bhagavan" / -ityuktvā licchavikumāro ratnākaraśva paṃcamātrāṇi licchavikumāraśatāni bhagavate pratyaśrauṣuaḥ /

bhagavāṃstānevam āmantrayate sma- "kulaputra (/), sattvakṣetraḥ hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetram / tatkasya hetoaḥ? yāvadbodhisattvaḥ sattvānupabṛṃhayati tāvadbuddhakṣetrasya parigrāhakaḥ / īdṛśasya buddhakṣetrasya parigrāhako yathā sattvā vinītā bhavanti / buddhakṣetrapraveśaṃ yathā sattvā buddhajñānapraveśaṃ gacchantyevaṃ rūpaṃ buddhakṣetram parigṛhṇāti / evaṃ rupaṃ buddhakṣetram parigṛhṇāti yathā buddhakṣetrapraveśam- āryajātendriyotpādaṃ sattvā gacchanti / tat kasya hetoḥ? kulaputrāḥ, bodhisattvānāṃ buddhakṣetraṃ hi sattvārthakriyotpattihetoaḥ / ratnākara, tadyathā- ākāśasame kicit kartukāmastathā kuryāt kiṃcāpyākāśe hi karaṇe cālaṃkāre ca tathā na yujyate / ratnākara sarvadharmān ākāśamān jñātvā, bodhisatvo yathā sattvaparipācanārthāya buddhakṣetraṃ kartukāmastathā buddhakṣetraṃ kuryāt kiṃcāpi buddhakṣetram ākāśe hi karaṇe na yujyate, alaṃkāre na yujyate /

"ratnākara, atha cāśayakṣetraṃ hi bidhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre śāṭhyamāyāpagatāḥ sattvā upapatsyante / kulaputra, adhyāśayakṣetraṃ hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre sarvakuśalamūlasaṃbhāropacitavantaḥ sattvā upapatsyante / prayogakṣetraṃ hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre sarvakuśaladharmopasthitāḥ sattvā upapatsyante / bodhisattvasyodāracittotpādo bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tasmistadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre mahāyānāṃprasthitāḥ sattvā upapatsyante / dānakṣetraṃ hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tasmiṃstadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre sarvasvaparityāginassattvā upapatsyante / śīlakṣetraṃ hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tasmistadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetra sarvāśayasahagatā daśakuśalakarmapathaparirakṣantaḥ sattvā upapatsyante / kṣāntikṣetraṃ hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tasmiṃstadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre dvātriṃśallakṣaṇalaṃkṛtāḥ kṣāntidamaparamaśamathapāramitāḥ sattvā upapatsyante / vīryakṣetraṃ hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tasmistadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre sarvakuśaladharmeṣvārabdhavīryāḥ sattvā upapatsyante / dhyānakṣetraṃ hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tasmistadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre smṛtisaṃprajanyasamāhitāḥ sattvā upatsyante; prajñākṣetraṃ hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tasmiṃstadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre samyaktvaniyatasattvā upapatsyante / catvāryapramāṇāni hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tasmiṃstadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre maitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣāvihāriṇassattvā upapatsyante / catvāri saṃgrahavastūni hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tasmiṃstadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre sarvavimuktiparigṛhītāḥ sattvā upapatsyante / upāyakauśalyaṃ hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tasmiṃstadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre sarvopāyacaryāvicakṣaṇāḥ sattvā upapatsyante / saptatriśadbodhipakṣyadharmā hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tasmistadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre smṛtyupasthānasamyakpradhānarddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṃgamārgapratipattijñāḥ sattvāupapatsyante / pariṇāmanā cittaṃ hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre sarvaguṇālaṃkārā āvirbhavanti / aṣṭākṣaṇapraśāntyupadeśo hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ;
tadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre sarvāpāyā atyantasamucchinnāḥ; aṣṭākṣaṇā apagatā bhavanti / pratyātmaśikṣāpadasthitiśva parasyāpacyanālāpo hi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tasmiṃstadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetra āpattiśabdo 'pi tu na nadyate / daśakuśalakarmapathapariśuddhirhi bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetraṃ; tasmiṃstadbodhiprāptibuddhakṣetre dhruvāyurmahābhogabrahmacaryasatyānuvartanavacanālaṃkāra- mañjuvākyābhedyaparṣannirbhinniniveśanakauśalyerṣyā- viprayogāvyāpādacittasamyagdṛṣṭisamanvāgatāḥ sattvā upapatsyante /
body.translated_text: <s>Ratnākara</s>, the field of intention (<s>āśayakṣetra</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings free from deceit and hypocrisy will be born. Son of good family, the field of higher intention (<s>adhyāśayakṣetra</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings who have accumulated all roots of merit will be born. The field of practice (<s>prayogakṣetra</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings established in all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> will be born. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s exalted generation of the mind of awakening (<s>udāracittotpāda</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> will be born. The field of generosity (<s>dānakṣetra</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings who relinquish all possessions will be born. The field of moral discipline (<s>śīlakṣetra</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings endowed with all good intentions who guard the ten paths of wholesome action will be born. The field of patience (<s>kṣāntikṣetra</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings adorned with the thirty-two marks, who have reached the perfection of patience, self-control, and supreme tranquility, will be born. The field of vigor (<s>vīryakṣetra</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings who have exerted vigor in all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> will be born. The field of meditation (<s>dhyānakṣetra</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings endowed with mindfulness, clear comprehension, and concentration will be born. The field of wisdom (<s>prajñākṣetra</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings who are assured of the right course (<s>samyaktvaniyata</s>) will be born. The four immeasurables (<s>catvāryapramāṇāni</s>) are the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings who dwell in loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity will be born. The four means of attraction (<s>catvāri saṃgrahavastūni</s>) are the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings encompassed by all liberations will be born. Skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings skilled in all practices of skillful means will be born. The thirty-seven factors of awakening (<s>saptatriṃśad bodhipakṣyadharmāḥ</s>) are the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings knowledgeable in the practice of the foundations of mindfulness, right exertions, bases of spiritual power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, and the path will be born. The mind of dedication (<s>pariṇāmanā citta</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, all ornaments of good qualities become manifest. The teaching for pacifying the eight inopportune states (<s>aṣṭākṣaṇa</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, all lower realms of existence are completely eliminated and the eight inopportune states are removed. Personal observance of the precepts and not criticizing others' transgressions is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, even the word 'transgression' is not heard. The purification of the ten paths of wholesome action (<s>daśakuśalakarmapatha</s>) is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field; in that <s>Buddha</s>-field upon attaining <s>Bodhi</s>, beings endowed with firm lifespan, great wealth, chaste conduct, truthful speech, pleasant words, gentle speech, harmonious assembly, skill in cutting through attachment, freedom from jealousy, absence of malice, and right view will be born.

body.text: "evaṃ, hi kulaputra, yādṛśo bodhisattvasya bodhicittotpādastādṛśo 'pyāśayaḥ / yādṛśa āśayastādṛśo 'pi prayogaḥ / yāvat prayogastāvaccādhyāśayaḥ / tāvadadhyāśayastāvacca nidhyaptiaḥ / yāvannidhyaptiatāvacca pratipattiaḥ / yāvat pratipattistāvacca pariṇāmanā / yāvat pariṇāmanā tāvaccopāyāḥ / yāvadupāyās tāvacca pariśuddhakṣetram / yathā pariśuddhakṣetram, pariśuddhasattvāstathā / yathā pariśuddhasattvāstathāpi pariśuddhajñānam / pariśuddhajñānaṃ yathā, tathāpi pariśuddhaśāsanam / yathā pariśuddhaśāsanaṃ, tathā ca pariśuddhajñānasādhanam pariśuddhajñānasādhanaṃ yathā, tathā punaḥ pariśuddhasvacittam /
body.translated_text: Thus, son of good family, as is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s generation of the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicittotpāda</s>), so too is the intention; as is the intention, so too is the practice; as is the practice, so too is the higher intention; as is the higher intention, so too is the resolution; as is the resolution, so too is the course of action; as is the course of action, so too is the dedication; as is the dedication, so too are the skillful means; as are the skillful means, so too is the purified field; as is the purified field, so too are the purified beings; as are the purified beings, so too is the purified knowledge; as is the purified knowledge, so too is the purified teaching; as is the purified teaching, so too is the purified accomplishment of knowledge; as is the purified accomplishment of knowledge, so too is the purified mind.

body.text: :tasmāt, kulaputra, bodhisattvena buddhakṣetrapariśuddhaniśvikīrṣayā svacittaparyavadāpanāya prayattavyam / tat kasya hetoḥ? yathā bodhisattvasya cittaṃ pariśuddham, tādṛśe buddhakṣetram pariśuddham bhavati" /
body.translated_text: Therefore, son of good family, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who wishes to purify the <s>Buddha</s>-field should strive to purify his own mind. Why is that? As the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind is pure, so is the <s>Buddha</s>-field pure.

body.text: tato buddhānubhāvenāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitadabhūt- 'yadi yathā cittaṃ pariśuddham, tādṛśe bodhisattvasya buddhakṣetram pariśuddhaṃ bhavet, bhagavataḥ śākyamunerbodhisattvacaryā carataḥ, tasya cittanna pariśuddhaṃ kim, yathā buddhakṣetram evaṃ rupam pariśuddhanna dṛśyate'?- tasyaitadabhūt /
body.translated_text: Then, through the <s>Buddha</s>'s power, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> had this thought: 'If the <s>Buddha</s>-field is pure in accordance with the purity of the mind, was the mind of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> not pure when he practiced the <s>Bodhisattva</s> course, that the <s>Buddha</s>-field does not appear pure in this way?' — such was his thought.

body.text: atha bhagavānāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya cetasaiva cetaḥ parivitarkam ājñāyāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat- "śāriputra, tat kiṃ manyase? sūryaśva candraḥ kinna pariśuddhau, yathā jātyandhairna dṛśyete?"- abravīt- "no hīdaṃ, bhagavan / tairjātyandhairduṣkṛtam, na tu sūryeṇa ca candreṇa hi duṣkṛtam" / -avocat- "tathā hi, śāriputra, kenacit sattvena tathāgatasya buddhakṣetraguṇālaṅkāravyūho na dṛśyate, sa sattvājñānena hi doṣaḥ, na tu tathāgatena tasmin doṣaḥ / tathāgatasya buddhakṣetraṃ hi pariśuddham, kiṃ tu tvayā tanna dṛśyate" /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing with his mind the thought of the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, spoke to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> thus: '<s>Śāriputra</s>, what do you think? Are the sun and the moon not pure, that they are not seen by those born blind?' — He replied: 'No indeed, Blessed One. That is the fault of those born blind, not the fault of the sun and moon.' — He said: 'Likewise, <s>Śāriputra</s>, when some being does not see the ornamental array of qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field, that is the fault of that being's ignorance, not the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s fault. The <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field is indeed pure, but you do not see it.'

body.text: tato brahmā śikhyāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputramevamabravīt- "bhadanta śāriputra, tathāgatasya buddhakṣetranna pariśuddham' iti mā bravīḥ / bhadanta śāriputra, pariśuddhaṃ bhagavato buddhakṣetram; tad yathā- paranirmitavaśartidevānām, bhadanta śāriputra, āvāsavyūho yathā, bhagavataḥ śākyamunerbuddhakṣetravyūho 'pi mayedṛśo dṛśyate"
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Śikhin</s> spoke thus to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, do not say that the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Buddha</s>-field is not pure! Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the Blessed One's <s>Buddha</s>-field is pure. Just as, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the splendid dwelling-array of the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, so too do I see the <s>Buddha</s>-field array of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>.'

body.text: tataḥ śāriputraḥ sthaviro brahmāṇaṃ śikhinamevamabravīt / "brahman, ahaṃ tvimāṃ mahāpṛthivīmutkūlanikūlakaṇṭakaprapātaśikharaśvabhragūthoḍigalla prākīrṇām paśyāmi" /
body.translated_text: Then the elder <s>Śāriputra</s> spoke thus to <s>Brahmā Śikhin</s>: 'O <s>Brahman</s>, I see this great earth as full of hills and hollows, thorns and precipices, peaks and crevices, pits and ditches, strewn about.'

body.text: brahmā śikhyabravīta- "tathā hīdṛśaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ pariśuddhanna dṛśyate / bhadanta śāriputra, utkūle nikūle citte buddhajñānāyāśayo niyatamapariśuddhaḥ / yebhyaḥ kebhyaśvit, bhadanta śāriputra, sattveṣu samacittatā ca buddhajñānāyāśayaḥ pariśuddhastairhīdaṃ buddhakṣetram pariśuddhaṃ dṛśyate" /
body.translated_text: <s>Brahmā Śikhin</s> said: 'It is because the <s>Buddha</s>-field, being thus, does not appear pure. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, one whose mind has hills and hollows regarding <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge has an intention that is certainly impure. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, for those who have an impartial mind toward all beings and a purified intention toward <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, this <s>Buddha</s>-field is seen as pure.'

body.text: atha bhagavānimaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātum pādāṅguṣṭhenāhanti sma / samanantarahato 'yaṃ lokadhāturanekaratnakūṭamanekaratnaśatasahasrasaṃbhāro 'nekaratnaśatasahasraprativyūho bhūtastad yathā- ratnavyūhasya tathāgatasyānantaguṇaratnavyūho lokadhāturiva, ayaṃ ca lokadhātustādṛśaḥ / tataḥ sāpi sarvāvatī pariṣadāśvaryaprāptā ratnapadmavyūhāsana ātmānamapi ca niṣaṇṇām cintāṃ karoti sma /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One pressed this trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s>) with his toe. Immediately this world-realm appeared adorned with many jewel-mounds, filled with hundreds of thousands of jewels, arrayed with hundreds of thousands of jewels — just like the world-realm of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnavyūha</s> (Jewel Array) with its infinite jewel-adorned array of qualities — and this world-realm appeared exactly so. Then that entire assembly, struck with wonder, perceived themselves seated upon jewel-lotus thrones.

body.text: atha bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputramavocat- "nanu tvaṃ, śāriputra, imaṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaṃ paśyasi?" abravīt- "dhruvam paśyāmi, bhagavan / sandṛśyanta ime 'dṛṣṭāśrutapūrvā vyūhāḥ" / abhāṣata- "śāriputra, idaṃ hi buddhakṣetrannityamīdṛśam, ki tu hīnasattvaparipācanārthāya tathāgato buddhakṣetremevaṃ bahudoṣaduṣṭaṃ deśayati / śāriputra, tadyathāpi nāma devaputrā ekasmin ratnabhājane bhojanaṃ bhakṣanti, api tu yathā- puṇyasaṃnicayabhedena divyāhārāmṛtapratyupasthitāḥ, evameva, śāriputra, sattvā ekasmin buddhakṣetra utpannā yathā-pariśuddhirbuddhānāṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūham paśyanti" /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Do you not see, <s>Śāriputra</s>, this array of qualities of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field)?' He replied: 'Indeed I see it, Blessed One! These arrays, never before seen or heard, are now visible.' He said: '<s>Śāriputra</s>, this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> is always like this, but the <s>Tathāgata</s> displays the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> as full of many faults for the purpose of ripening inferior beings. <s>Śāriputra</s>, just as the <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons) eat food from a single jeweled vessel, yet divine ambrosia appears according to their different accumulations of merit — even so, <s>Śāriputra</s>, beings born in the same <s>buddhakṣetra</s> see the array of qualities of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> according to the respective purity of the <s>Buddhas</s>.'

body.text: asmin buddhakṣetraguṇālaṅkāravyūhe dṛśyamāne, caturaśītyā prāṇisahasrai- ranuttarasamyaksambodhicittānyutpāditānyabhūvan / ye kecana licchavikumārāṇām pañcaśataṃ licchavikumāreṇa sārdhamupasaṃkrāntāḥ te 'pyānulomikīm kṣāntim prāpnuvan /
body.translated_text: When this array of qualities and adornments of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> was displayed, eighty-four thousand beings generated the aspiration for <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). And those five hundred <s>Licchavi</s> youths who had come together with the <s>Licchavi</s> youth also attained the <s>anulomikī kṣānti</s> (acquiescent patience).

body.text: atha bhagavāṃstā ṛdvividhīaḥ piṃḍayati sma; tataśva tadbuddhakṣetraṃ bhūyaḥ pūrvasvabhāvamāpannaṃ dṛśyate sma /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One withdrew those miraculous powers; and thereupon that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> was again seen as having returned to its former nature.

body.text: tatra śrāvakayānidevamanuṣyāṇāmetadabhūt- 'anityā vata saṃskārāḥ' / viditveti dvāṃtriśade prāṇisahasrebhyaḥ sarvadharmeṣu virajo vigatamalaṃ viśuddhaṃ dharmacakṣuḥ; aṣṭābhyo bhikṣusahasrebhyo 'nupādāyāśravebhyaścittāni vimuktānyabhūvan / catuśītyāpi buddhakṣetrodārādhimuktikaprāṇisahasraiḥ, sarvadharmān viṭhapana-pratyusthānalakṣaṇān viditvā, anuttarasabhyaksambodhicittānyutpāditāni /
body.translated_text: Then the thought arose in the gods and humans of the <s>śrāvakayāna</s>: 'Impermanent indeed are <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations)!' Having understood this, thirty-two thousand beings attained the pure, stainless, and immaculate <s>dharmacakṣus</s> (eye of Dharma) with regard to all <s>dharmas</s>; eight thousand monks had their minds liberated from the <s>āśravas</s> (defilements) without further clinging. And eighty-four thousand beings with noble aspiration for the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, having understood all <s>dharmas</s> as characterized by cessation and arising, generated the aspiration for <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening).

body.text: buddhakṣetrapariśuddhinidānasy aparivartaḥ prathamaḥ /
body.translated_text: End of the first chapter, entitled 'The Cause of the Purification of the <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-Field).'

body.text: 2. acintyopāyakauśalyam
body.translated_text: 2. Inconceivable Skillful Means

body.text: api ca tena kālena vaiśālyāmmahānagaryām eko vimalakīrtirnāma licchavirāsīt, pūrvajinakṛtādhikāro 'varopitakuśalamūlo 'nekabuddhaparyupāsitaḥ kṣāntipratilabdhaḥ pratibhānalabdho mahābhijñāvikrīḍito dhāraṇīpratilabdho vaiśāradyaprāpto nihatamārapratyarthiko gambhīradharmanetrī supratipannaḥ prajñāpāramitā niryāta upāyakauśalyagatiṃgataḥ pratibhānavat sattvāśayacaryāvijñaḥ sattvendriyavarāvarajñānaniryāto yathāpratyarhaṃ dharmaśāstā / asmin mahāyāne prayatya, jñātaḥ suniśvitaḥ karmakaro buddhasyeryāpathe vihārī paramabuddhisāgarānugataḥ sarvabuddhaiḥ saṃstutaḥ stobhitaḥ praśaṃsitaḥ sarvaśakrabrahmalokapālanamaskṛtaḥ saḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, at that time in the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, there was a <s>Licchavi</s> named <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, who had made offerings to former <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), had planted roots of merit, had attended upon innumerable <s>Buddhas</s>, had attained patience, had obtained eloquence, had played with the great supernatural powers, had attained <s>dhāraṇī</s>, had achieved fearlessness, had defeated <s>Māra</s> and his adversaries, had entered into the profound <s>Dharma</s> eye, was well-practiced, had arrived at the perfection of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), had gone to the destination of <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means), was endowed with eloquence, was expert in the conduct and dispositions of beings, was skilled in knowing the faculties of beings as superior or inferior, taught the <s>Dharma</s> as appropriate. Striving in this <s>Mahāyāna</s>, he was known and well-established, an agent of the <s>Buddha's</s> activity, dwelling in the <s>Buddha's</s> conduct, following the ocean of supreme wisdom, praised, lauded, and extolled by all <s>Buddhas</s>, and honored by all <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, and World-Protectors.

body.text: upāyakauśalyena sattvaparipācanārthāya vaiśālyāmmahānagaryā viharan, (so) 'nāthadaridrasattvasaṃgrahāyākṣayabhogaḥ / duḥśīlasattvasaṃgrahāya pariśuddhaśīlaḥ / dviṣṭātidviṣṭavyāpādi duaḥśīlakrodhanasattvasaṃgrahāya kṣāntidamaprāptaḥ / alasasattvasaṃgrahāyottaptavīryaḥ / vikṣiptacittasattvasaṃgrahāya dhyānasmṛtisamādhivihārī / dauṣprajñasattvasaṃgrahāya prajñāviniścayalābhī / yadyapyavadātavastrapariveṣṭitāḥ (sa) śramaṇacarita sampannaḥ / gṛhāvāse yadyapi viharan, kāmarūpārūpadhātvasaṃsṛṣṭaḥ / putradārāntaḥpure 'pi nityam brahmacārī / parivāraparivṛto yadyapi dṛśyamānaḥ pravivekacārī / bhūṣaṇālaṃkṛto dṛśyamānaḥ, kiṃ tu lakṣaṇopetaḥ / yadyapyāhārapānabhojanaṃ dṛśyamāno bhuñjan, sadā dhyānasya prītibhojanaṃ paribhuṅkte sma / sarvakrīḍādyūtakoṇeṣu dṛśyamāno 'pi, krīḍādyūtaraktān sattvān paripācayati sma nityamamoghacārī / sarvapāṣaṇḍikān yadyapi gaveṣī, buddhe 'bhedyābhiprāyasampannaḥ / laukikalokottaramantraśāstravijñāno 'pi sadā dharmasammodanandādhimuktaḥ / saṃsargasamantamadhye dṛśyamāno 'pi, sarvamadhye pramukhaḥ pūjitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Dwelling in the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s> for the purpose of ripening beings through <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means), he possessed inexhaustible wealth for gathering the destitute and unprotected beings. He maintained pure moral conduct for gathering beings of poor morality. He had attained patience and self-control for gathering beings overcome by hatred, extreme hostility, ill-will, poor morality, and anger. He possessed blazing energy for gathering lazy beings. He dwelt in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) for gathering beings of distracted minds. He attained the certainty of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) for gathering beings of poor understanding. Though clothed in white garments, he was accomplished in ascetic conduct. Though dwelling in the household life, he was untouched by the realms of desire, form, and formlessness. Though having sons, a wife, and a harem, he was ever a <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate). Though seen surrounded by attendants, he was a practitioner of solitude. Though seen adorned with ornaments, he was endowed with the marks. Though seen eating food and drink, he always enjoyed the nourishment of the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>. Though seen at all places of games and gambling, he constantly ripened beings attached to games and gambling, never acting in vain. Though he sought out all the <s>pāṣaṇḍikas</s> (heretical teachers), he possessed unshakeable devotion to the <s>Buddha</s>. Though expert in worldly and supramundane mantras and sciences, he was always devoted to the joy and delight of the <s>Dharma</s>. Though seen in the midst of worldly society, he was foremost and honored among all.

body.text: lokasāmagrīkaraṇārthāya jyeṣṭhamadhyakumārāṇāṃ sahāyībhāvaṃ gacchati sma dharmabhāṇakaḥ / sarvavyavahārapratipanno yadyapi, lābhabhoganirākāṅkṣaḥ / sattvadharṣaṇārthāya sarvapathacatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu dṛśyamāno 'pi, sattvarakṣaṇārthāya rājakāryeṣu ca prayuktaḥ / hīnayānādhimuktivāraṇāthārya mahāyāne ca sattvaparigrahārthāya sarvadharmaśravaṇikasaṃvācakeṣu dṛśyate sma / bālaparipācanārthāya sarvalipiśālāgāmyapi / kāmādīnavasamprakāśanārthāya gaṇikāgārāṇyapi sarvatrāvakrāmī / smṛtisampratiṣṭhāpanārthāya sarvamadyavikrayagṛhāṇi cāvakramati sma /
body.translated_text: For the purpose of bringing about the welfare of the world, he went as a companion of the eldest, middle, and youngest, as a preacher of the <s>Dharma</s>. Though engaged in all worldly transactions, he had no desire for profit or enjoyment. For the purpose of encouraging beings, he was seen at all roads, crossroads, and intersections, and for the purpose of protecting beings, he was engaged in royal affairs. To prevent attachment to the <s>Hīnayāna</s> and for gathering beings into the noble <s>Mahāyāna</s>, he was seen among all who teach and discuss the <s>Dharma</s>. For the purpose of ripening the young, he entered all schools of writing. For the purpose of revealing the dangers of <s>kāma</s> (desire), he entered the houses of courtesans everywhere. For the purpose of establishing <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), he entered all taverns and drinking houses.

body.text: dharmaśreṣṭhopadeśakāraṇācchreṣṭhyantare 'pi śreṣṭhisammatīyaḥ / sarvagrāhakādānaparicchedakāraṇādgṛhapatyantare ca gṛhapatisammatīyaḥ / kṣāntisauratyabalapratiṣṭhāpanakāraṇāt kṣatriyāntare kṣatriyasammatīyaḥ / mānamadadarpapraṇāśanakāraṇād brāhmaṇāntare 'pi brāhmaṇasammatīyaḥ / sarvarājakāryadharmānurūpājñākāraṇādamātyāntare cāmātyasammatīyaḥ / rājabhogaiśvaryasaṅgavivartanakāraṇātkumārāntare ca kumārasammatīyaḥ / kumārīparipācanakāraṇād antaḥpure 'pi kañcukisammatīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: For the purpose of teaching the supreme <s>Dharma</s>, he was respected among the <s>śreṣṭhins</s> (chief merchants). For the purpose of cutting off all grasping and giving, he was respected among the householders. For the purpose of establishing the power of patience and gentleness, he was respected among the <s>kṣatriyas</s> (warriors). For the purpose of destroying pride, arrogance, and conceit, he was respected among the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. For the purpose of issuing commands in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> in all royal affairs, he was respected among the ministers. For the purpose of turning away from attachment to royal enjoyments and sovereignty, he was respected among the princes. For the purpose of ripening the young women, he was respected even among the eunuchs of the inner palace.

body.text: prākṛtasya puṇyaṃ viśeṣeṇādhyālambanato janakāyena sārdhaṃ sāmagrīmāpannaḥ / īśvarādhipataya upadeśakāraṇācchakrāntare ca śakrasammatīyaḥ / jñānaviśeṣaśāsanakāraṇādbrahmāntare 'pi brahmasammatīyaḥ / sarvasattvaparipācanāl (lokapāleṣu) lokapālasammatīyaḥ / tathā hi licchavirvimalakīrtirapramāṇopāyakauśalyajñānasampanno vaiśālyāmmahānagaryāṃ viharati sma /
body.translated_text: He attained harmony with the people by specially fostering the merit of the common folk. For the purpose of teaching the lords and rulers, he was respected among the <s>Śakras</s>. For the purpose of teaching the special knowledge, he was respected among the <s>Brahmās</s>. For the sake of ripening all beings, he was respected among the World-Protectors. Thus the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, endowed with the knowledge of immeasurable <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means), dwelt in the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>.

body.text: sa upāyakauśalyenātmānaṃ glānanibhaṃ deśayitvā, tasya rogapraśnārthāya vaiśālyā mahānagaryā rājāmātyadhipakumāramaṇḍalabrāhmaṇagṛhapatiśreṣṭhinaigamajānapadāḥ, no hīdaṃ- prāṇinām bahusahasraṃ rogapṛcchanāyāgatam / tebhyastatra samāgatebhyo licchavirvimalakīrtirimameva caturmahābhūtakāyam ārabhya, dharmaṃ deśayati sma-
body.translated_text: By <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means), he displayed himself as if ill. For the purpose of inquiring about his illness, kings, ministers, lords, princes, circles of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, householders, and chief merchants of the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, as well as many thousands of beings from the countryside, came to visit. To all those who had gathered there, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, beginning with this very body composed of the four great elements, taught the <s>Dharma</s>:

body.text: "mitrāḥ, ayaṃ hi kāya evamanitya evamadhruvo 'nāśvāsaḥ / (sa hy-) evaṃ durbalo 'sārastathā hi luptaḥ parīttakālo duḥkho bahurogo vipariṇāmadharmaḥ / mitrāḥ, tathā hyasmin kāye bahurogabhājane hi- tasmin paṇḍito 'saṃvāsikaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Friends, this body is thus impermanent, thus unstable, unreliable. It is thus weak, insubstantial, indeed perishable, short-lived, full of suffering, full of diseases, and subject to change. Friends, since this body is a vessel of many diseases, the wise person should not dwell in it.

body.text: "mitrāḥ, ayaṃ kāyo dhāraṇan- na kṣamamāṇaḥ phenapiṇḍopamaḥ / ayaṃ hi kāyo 'cirasthitiko budbudopamaḥ / ayaṃ kāyaḥ kleśatṛṣṇotpanno marīcyupamaḥ / asāro 'yaṃ kāyaḥ kadalīstambhopamaḥ / asthirasnāyubandho vatāyaṃ yantropamaḥ / ayaṃ kāyo hi viparyāsotpanno māyopamaḥ / abhūtadarśanaṃ hyayaṃ kāyassvapnopamaḥ / pratibimbopamo 'yaṃ kāyaḥ pūrvakarmapratibimbo dṛśyamānaḥ / ayaṃ kāyaḥ pratyayādhīnaḥ, pratiśrutkopamastat / vikṣiptacitto (yathā) hyayaṃ kāyaḥ patanalakṣaṇo meghopamaḥ / ayaṃ kāyaḥ kṣaṇavināśanasahagataścānavasthito vidyuttulyaḥ / asvāmiko 'yaṃ hi kāyo nānāpratyayotpannaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Friends, this body is like a lump of foam, unable to withstand pressure. This body is like a bubble, not lasting long. This body is like a mirage, arising from the thirst of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). This body is like a plantain trunk, without essence. This body is like a mechanical device, bound by unstable sinews and bones. This body is like a magical illusion, arising from perversion. This body is like a dream, an appearance of the unreal. This body is like a reflection, an image of previous <s>karma</s> appearing. This body is dependent on conditions, like an echo. This body is like a cloud, of distracted mind and characterized by falling. This body is like lightning, accompanied by momentary destruction and unstable. This body is without a master, arising from various conditions.

body.text: "nirvyāpāro hyaṃ kāyaḥ pṛthivīsadṛśaḥ / āpasadṛśo 'yaṃ kāyo 'nātmakaḥ / ayaṃ kāyastejassadṛśo nirjīvaḥ / ayaṃ kāyo vāyusadṛśo niṣpudgalaḥ / ākāśasadṛśo 'yaṃ kāyo niḥsvabhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is without activity, like earth. This body is without self, like water. This body is without life, like fire. This body is without a person, like wind. This body is without own-nature, like space.

body.text: "ayaṃ kāyo mahābhūtasthāno 'bhūtaḥ / ātmātmīyarahito 'yaṃ kāyaḥ śūnyaḥ / tṛṇakāṣṭhābhittiloṣṭapratibhāsopamo 'yaṃ kāyo jaḍaḥ / ayaṃ hi kāyo vātayantrasamanvāgamena (yath-)otpanno vedanārahitaḥ / ayaṃ hi pūyamīḍhasaṃcitaḥ kāyastucchaḥ / nityalepaparimardanabhedanavidhvaṃsanadharmo 'yaṃ kāyo riktaḥ / ayaṃ hi kāyaścaturadhikacatuḥśatarogopadrutaḥ / sadā jarābhibhūto hyayaṃ kāyo jarodapānasadṛśaḥ / maraṇānto 'yaṃ kāyo 'ntāniśritaḥ / ayaṃ hi kāyaḥ skandhadhātvāyatanaparigṛhīto vadhakāśiviṣaśūnyagrāmopamaḥ / tasmin yuṣmābhirevaṃkāye nirvidudvegayorutpāditayostathāgatakāyādhimuktirutpādayitavyā /
body.translated_text: This body rests on the great elements and is unreal. This body is devoid of self and what belongs to self — it is empty. This body is inert, resembling grass, wood, a wall, or a clod of earth. This body is born through the operation of wind-mechanisms and is devoid of feeling. This body, filled with pus and mucus, is worthless. This body, whose nature is to be constantly soiled, rubbed, broken, and destroyed, is hollow. This body is afflicted by four hundred and four diseases. This body, always overcome by old age, is like a well of aging. This body, ending in death, rests on finality. This body, comprised of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), is like a murderer, a venomous serpent, or an empty village. Therefore, having generated revulsion and aversion toward such a body, you should generate aspiration toward the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: "mitrāḥ, tathāgatakāyo hi dharmakāyo jñānajaḥ / tathāgatakāyaḥ puṇyajo dānajaśśīlajassamādhijaḥ prajñājo vimuktijo vimuktijñānadarśanajo maitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣotpannodānadamasaṃyamotpanno daśakuśalakarmapathajaḥ kṣāntisauratyajasthiravīryakuśalamūlajo dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijaśśrutaprajñopāyajassaptatriṃśadbodhipākṣikadharmajaśśmathavipaśyanājo daśabalajaścaturvaiśāradyajo 'ṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmajassarvapāramitotpanno 'bhijñā-(tri-) vidyotpannassarvākuśaladharmaprahāṇasarvakuśaladharmasaṃgrahajaḥ satyajassamyaktvajo 'pramādajaḥ /
body.translated_text: Friends, the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (body of the Dharma), born of knowledge. The <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body is born of merit, born of generosity, born of moral discipline, born of concentration, born of wisdom, born of liberation, born of the vision of liberation-knowledge, born of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity, born of giving, self-control, and restraint, born of the ten paths of wholesome action, born of patience and gentleness, born of firm vigor and roots of merit, born of <s>dhyāna</s>, liberations, concentrations, and attainments, born of learning, wisdom, and skillful means, born of the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipākṣikadharma</s>), born of calm abiding (<s>śamatha</s>) and insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>), born of the ten powers, born of the four fearlessnesses, born of the eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, arisen from all perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), arisen from superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) and the three knowledges (<s>trividyā</s>), born of the abandonment of all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and the accumulation of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, born of truth, born of right conduct, born of diligence.

body.text: "mitrāḥ, tathāgatakāyo hyapramāṇakuśalakarmajaḥ / tasmin yuṣmābhiravaṃkāye 'dhimuktirutpādayitavyā / sarvasattvakleśarogaprajahanārthāya ānuttarasamyaksambodhicittamutpādayitavyam" /
body.translated_text: Friends, the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is born of immeasurable wholesome deeds. You should generate aspiration toward such a body. In order to eliminate the afflictions and diseases of all beings, you should generate the mind of supreme, perfect awakening (<s>anuttarasamyaksambodhi</s>).

body.text: evameva licchavirvimalakīrtistathā hi tasmai rogapraśnagaṇāya, yathā bahuśatānāṃ sattvasahasrāṇāmanuttarasamyaksambodhicittamutpāditam, tathā hyevaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati sma /
body.translated_text: Thus indeed did the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s> to the crowd that came to inquire about his illness, such that many hundreds of thousands of beings generated the mind of supreme, perfect awakening.

body.text: acintyopāyakauśalyasya parivarto nāma dvitīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: This is the second chapter, entitled 'Inconceivable Skillful Means' (<s>Acintyopāyakauśalya</s>).

body.text: 3. śrāvakabodhisattvapreṣaṇoktam
body.translated_text: 3. The Dispatching of <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Bodhisattva</s> Disciples

body.text: tato licchavervimalakīrteretadabhūt- "mayi glāne duaḥkhite ca mañcasyopari sanne, tathāgatenārhatā samyaksambuddhena, mānna samanvāhṛtyānukampānnopādāya, rogapṛcchananna kiñcidapyutsṛṣṭam" iti /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> had this thought: 'I am sick and suffering, lying upon my bed, yet the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, does not take me into consideration with compassion and has not sent anyone to inquire about my illness.'

body.text: atha bhagavāṃl- licchavervimalakīrterīdṛśaṃ cittasaṅkalpaṃ buddhvā, āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputramāmantrayate sma- "śāriputra, licchavervimalakīrte rogapṛcchanāya gaccha" //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the mental intention of the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: '<s>Śāriputra</s>, go to inquire about the illness of the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>.'

body.text: evamukte, bhagavantamāyuṣmāṃśāriputra etadavocat- "bhagavan, licchavervimalakīrte rogapṛcchanagamanannotsahe / tat kasya hetoḥ? bhagavan, abhijānāmi-
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the Blessed One: 'Blessed One, I am not able to go to inquire about the illness of that good man. Why is that? Blessed One, I recall —

body.text: "ekasmin samaya ekasmin vṛkṣa mūle mām pratisaṃlīnaṃ licchavirvimalakīrtirapi, yena tasya vṛkṣasya mūlaṃ tenopasaṃkramyaitadvadati sma- 'bhadanta śāriputra, yathā tvaṃ pratisaṃlīnastādṛśe pratisaṃlayane na pratisaṃlayitavyam' /
body.translated_text: 'One time, I was sitting in meditation at the foot of a tree, and the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> approached the foot of that tree and said to me: "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, you should not practice meditation in the way you are meditating."

body.text: "'yathā traidhātukakāyaśca cittaṃca na prajñāyete, tathā hi pratisaṃlaya / yathā nirodhānnottiṣṭhati sarvatrāpīryāpathamāvirbhavati, tathā hi pratisaṃlaya / yathā prāptilakṣaṇānutsṛjanātāyām pṛthagjanalakṣaṇamevāpi dṛśyate, tathā hi pratisaṃlaya / yathā punastava cittamadhyātmamanavasthitam, bāhyarūpe 'pi nānuvicarati, tathā pratisaṃlaya / yathā sarvadṛṣṭigateṣvacalo 'pi ca saptatriṃśadbodhipākṣikadharmābhāsaṃ gacchati, tathā hi pratisaṃlaya / yathā saṃsārāvacarakleśāprahāṇe nirvāṇasamavasaraṇamapi gacchati, tathā hi pratisaṃlaya / bhadanta śāriputra, ya evam pratisaṃlayane pratisaṃlīnāḥ, tān bhagavān pratisaṃlayana āmantrayate sma' /
body.translated_text: '"You should meditate such that neither body nor mind manifest in the three realms. You should meditate such that, without rising from cessation, all deportments still appear. You should meditate such that, without abandoning the marks of attainment, the marks of an ordinary person are also seen. You should meditate such that your mind is not established internally, nor does it wander in external forms. You should meditate such that, while unmoved by all views, you still approach the thirty-seven factors of awakening. You should meditate such that, without abandoning the afflictions of <s>saṃsāra</s>, you still arrive at <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, those who meditate thus in meditation — them the Blessed One calls truly meditating."

body.text: "ityukte, bhagavan, taṃ dharmameva śrutvā, tasmai prativādavisarjanasyāsamarthastūṣṇībhūto 'bhūvam / etasmāt kāraṇāt tasya satpuruṣasya rogapṛcchanagamanannotsahe" /
body.translated_text: 'Thus spoken, Blessed One, having heard that <s>Dharma</s> teaching, I was unable to offer any reply and remained silent. For this reason, I am not able to go to inquire about the illness of that good man.'

body.text: atha bhagavānāyuṣmantam mahāmaudgalyāyanam āmantrayate sma- "maudgalyāyana, licchavervimalakīrte rogapṛcchanāya gaccha" / maudgalyāyano 'pi tvavocat- "bhagavan, tasya satpuruṣasya rogapṛcchanagamanannotsahe / tat kasya hetoaḥ? bhagavan, abhijānāmi-
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: '<s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, go to inquire about the illness of the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>.' <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> also said: 'Blessed One, I am not able to go to inquire about the illness of that good man. Why is that? Blessed One, I recall —

body.text: "ekasmin samaye vaiśālyā mahānagaryā ekasmin vīthīdvāre gṛhapatibhyo dharmamadeśayam / tasmin samipe licchavirvimalakīrtirupasaṃkramya, māmetadvadati sma- 'bhadanta maudgalyāyana, yathāvadātavastrebhyo gṛhibhyo deśayasi, tathā hi dharmo 'vyapadeśyaḥ / bhadanta maudgalyāyana, sa dharmo yathādharma darśayitavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'One time, I was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to householders at a street entrance in the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>. At that time, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> approached me and said: "Venerable <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, you should not teach the <s>Dharma</s> to white-robed householders in the way you are teaching. Venerable <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> is inexpressible. Venerable <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> should be shown as it truly is."

body.text: "'dharmo hi, bhadanta maudgalyāyana, niḥsattvaḥ sattvarajo 'pagataḥ / nirātmakaḥ (sa) rāgarajo 'pagato nirjīva upapatticyutyapagataḥ yo 'nāśravaḥ, pūrvāntāparāntaparicchinnaḥ (saḥ) / śāntopaśamalakṣaṇas(sa)rāgarahitaḥ 'nālambanagāmī (so)' nakṣarassarvavācchinno 'nabhilāpyassarvataraṃgarahitaḥ / sarvānugata ākāśasamo varṇaliṅgākāravigataḥ sarvacaraṇāpagato mamābhāvo mamakārāpagatas (saḥ) / (so) 'vijñaptikaścittamanovijñānavigataḥ, pratipakṣābhāvakāraṇādatulyaḥ / hetupratikūlaḥ (sa) pratyayāvyavasthitaḥ /
body.translated_text: '"For the <s>Dharma</s>, venerable <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, is without beings, free from the stain of beings; without self, free from the stain of desire; without life-force, free from arising and passing away; without outflows, cut off from past and future. Of the nature of peace and tranquility, free from all desire; without object, it is like a letter — cutting off all speech, inexpressible, free from all waves. Following all things, it is like space — devoid of color, form, and shape. Free from all conduct, devoid of 'mine' and possessiveness. Without cognition, devoid of mind, mentation, and consciousness; without counterpart, it is incomparable. Contrary to causes, it is unestablished in conditions."

body.text: "'dharmadhātusamavasaraṇāt- (sa) sarvadharmān hi samādadhātyananugamananayena tathatānugataḥ / (so) 'tyantākampyaḥ; ataḥ sthito bhūtakoṭyāṃ ṣaḍviṣayeṣvāśrayarahitatvenākampyaḥ, apratiṣṭhitena yatra yatra gamanāgamanavyapagataḥ, śūnyatāsamavasaraṇaḥ / animittena susphuṭitaḥ (so) / apraṇihitalakṣaṇa eva, kalpanā apanayāpagataḥ / apakārarahitaḥ (so) 'prakṣepa utpādavyayāpagato 'nālayaścakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanaḥ paddhatisamatikrānto 'nunnato 'navanato 'vasthito 'calabhūtaḥ /
body.translated_text: '"Because it converges with the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), it encompasses all <s>dharmas</s> through the method of non-pursuit, following suchness (<s>tathatā</s>). It is utterly unshakable; established at the point of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), it is unshakable due to being without support in the six sense-objects; unestablished, it is free from coming and going wherever it may be; it converges with emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). It is clearly revealed through signlessness (<s>animitta</s>). It is of the nature of wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), free from conceptual elaboration. Free from harm, without projection, free from arising and passing away; without abode, it has transcended the paths of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; neither high nor low, it abides — unmoved and real."

body.text: "'sarvacaryāvigate, bhadanta mahāmaudgalyāyana, evaṃ dharme deśanā katham bhavati? bhadanta mahāmaudgalyāyana, sāpi dharmadeśanā nāmāropitavacanam / yacchravaṇam, tadapyāropitaśravaṇam / bhadanta maudgalyāyana, yatrāropitavacanannāsti, nāsti tatra dharmadeśanā, śravaṇaṃ ca jñānaṃ ca na staḥ / tadyathāpi nāma māyāpuruṣeṇa māyāpuruṣebhyo dharmo deśyeta /
body.translated_text: '"When the <s>Dharma</s> is free from all conduct, venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, how can there be teaching of it? Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, even that which is called 'Dharma teaching' is merely imputed speech. And that which is hearing is also imputed hearing. Venerable <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, where there is no imputed speech, there is no Dharma teaching, and neither hearing nor knowledge exist. Just as an illusory person would teach the Dharma to illusory persons —"

body.text: "'anena cittasthānena dharmo darśayitavyaḥ- tvayā sattvendriyakauśalyam karaṇīyam / prajñācakṣuṣā sudarśinā ca mahākaruṇābhimukhībhūtena ca mahāyānavarṇavādinā ca buddhakṛtajñena ca pariśuddhāśayena ca dharmaniruktivijñānena triratnagotrācchinnakaraṇārthāya tvayā dharmo darśayitavyaḥ' /
body.translated_text: '"With this mental attitude the <s>Dharma</s> should be shown: you should develop skill in the faculties of beings, with the eye of wisdom, with clear vision, facing great compassion, praising the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, with gratitude toward the <s>Buddha</s>, with a purified intention, with understanding of the expression of the <s>Dharma</s> — for the sake of not cutting off the lineage of the Three Jewels, you should show the <s>Dharma</s>."

body.text: "ityukte, bhagavan, tathaivam taddharmopadeśena tasyā gṛhapatipariṣado 'ṣṭābhirgṛhapati śatairanuttarasamyaksaṃbodhicittamutpāditam / ahaṃ tu, bhagavan, pratibhānāpagato 'bhūvam / etasmātkāraṇāttasya satpuruṣasya rogapṛcchanagamanannotsahe" /
body.translated_text: 'Thus spoken, Blessed One, through that <s>Dharma</s> instruction, eight hundred householders from that householder assembly generated the mind of supreme, perfect awakening. But I, Blessed One, was bereft of eloquence. For this reason, I am not able to go to inquire about the illness of that good man.'

body.text:
tato bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ mahākāśyapamāmantrayate sma- "kāśyapa, licchavevimalakīrte rogapṛcchanāya gaccha" / mahākāśyapo 'pi tvavocat "bhagavan, tasya satpuruṣasya rogapṛcchanagamanannotsahe / tat kasya hetoḥ? abhijānāmi-
"ekasmin samaye mama daridravīthyāṃ piṇḍapātāya sthitaṃ licchavirvimalakirtiḥ, tenopasaṃkramya, etadvadati sma- 'tathā hi mahāsattvagṛhā (ṇi) hitvā, daridragṛhāṇi gacchato bhadantasya mahākāśyapasya bhavantyekadeśamaitrī /
body.translated_text:
Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>: '<s>Kāśyapa</s>, go to inquire about the illness of the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>.' <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> also said: 'Blessed One, I am not able to go to inquire about the illness of that good man. Why is that? I recall —
'One time, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> approached me while I stood collecting alms in a poor neighborhood, and said: "Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, having passed by the houses of the great beings, you go to the houses of the poor — your loving-kindness is one-sided."

body.text: "'tasmāt, mahākāśyapa, dharmasamatāyāṃ sthātavyam / sarvakāle sarvasattvāntsamanvāhṛtya, piṇḍapātaḥ paryeṣṭitavyaḥ / nirāhārāhāraḥ paryeṣṭitavyaḥ / paripiṇḍagrāhavinodanārthāya piṇḍapātāya caritavyam / śūnyagrāmādhiṣṭhitena tvayā grāmaṃ praveṣṭavyam / puṃstrīparipācanārthāya grāmaṃ praveṣṭavyam / buddhavidyayā tvayāntargṛhe gantavyam /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, one should abide in the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmasamatā</s>). At all times, keeping all beings in mind, one should seek alms-food (<s>piṇḍapāta</s>). One should seek sustenance as if without sustenance. One should go on the alms-round for the purpose of dispelling the notion of receiving morsels. One should enter the village as one established in an empty village. One should enter the village for the purpose of maturing men and women. One should enter the inner house through the <s>Buddha</s>'s knowledge.

body.text: "'anādānena piṇḍapāta upādeyaḥ, jātyandhopamena rūpāṇi draṣṭavyāni, pratiśrutkānibhāḥ śabdāḥ śrotavyāḥ, vāyutulyā gandha ghrātavyāḥ, avijñaptikena rasā anubhavitavyāḥ, jñānasparśābhāvena spraṣṭavyāni sparṣṭavyāni, māyāpuruṣasya vijñānena dharmā veditavyāḥ / yau na ca svabhāvo na ca parabhāvastau nojjvalau / yadajvalanam, tanna śāmyati /
body.translated_text: 'Alms-food should be received without grasping; forms should be seen as by one born blind; sounds should be heard as if they were echoes; smells should be smelled as if they were wind; tastes should be experienced without conceptual cognition; tangibles should be touched without the existence of the touch of knowledge; <s>dharmas</s> should be known with the consciousness of an illusory person. That which has neither self-nature nor other-nature does not blaze. And what does not blaze does not cease.

body.text: "'yadi, sthavira mahākāśyapa, aṣṭamithyātvāvyatikramaṇe cāṣṭavimokṣasamāpattyāṃca mithyātvasamatayā samyaktvasamatām praviśase, ekapiṇḍapātamapi sarvasattvebhyo dadat, sarvabuddhebhyaśca sarvāryebhyo 'pyanuprayacchasi copanābhya, purata ātmanā bhojanaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ syāt, yathā na ca kleśasaṃprayukto na ca kleśavipramuktastathā hi paribhokṣyasi; na samāhito vā (samādhi-)samutthito va paribhokṣyasi saṃsāranirvāṇāpratiṣṭhitaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'If, elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, without transgressing the eight wrong states and yet entering the attainment of the eight liberations, through the equality of wrongness you enter the equality of rightness, then offering even a single morsel of alms-food to all beings and likewise offering to all <s>Buddhas</s> and all noble ones, you would be seen as eating food yourself—neither conjoined with defilements nor freed from defilements—thus shall you partake; neither in concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) nor risen from concentration shall you partake, established neither in <s>saṃsāra</s> nor <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: "'bhadanta, ye kecana tubhyaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ dadati, tebhyo mahāphalaṃ vālpaphalaṃ vā na bhavataḥ, na ca madhya(-phalaṃ) viśeṣa(-phalaṃ) vā / (te) buddhapravṛttiṃ samavasaranti, na tu śrāvakagatiṃ / sthavira mahākāśyapa, tathā hyamogharāṣṭrapiṇḍam paribhokṣyasi' /
body.translated_text: 'Venerable one, for those who give you alms-food, there arises for them neither great fruit nor small fruit, nor any intermediate or distinguished fruit. They enter the course of <s>Buddha</s>-activity, not the path of <s>śrāvakas</s>. Elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, thus shall you partake of alms-food that does not waste the nation.'

body.text: "ityukte, bhagavan, ahamimaṃ dharmopadeśaṃ śrutvā, āścaryādbhutaprāptaḥ sarvabodhisattvebhyaḥ praṇāmamakārṣam / 'yadi gṛhastho 'pyevaṃpratibhānasaṃpannaḥ ko 'nuttarasamyaksaṃbodhicittannotpādayed' [iti] cintayitvā, pūrvam mahāyāne 'prāpte, tadarvāṃmayā na kaścitsattvaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānayorviveśitaḥ / bhagavan, etasmātkāraṇāttasya satyuruṣasya rogapṛcchanagamanannotsahe" /
body.translated_text: When this was said, Blessed One, having heard this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, I was struck with wonder and amazement and bowed to all the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. 'If even a householder is endowed with such eloquence, who would not generate the mind of unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s>)?' — thinking thus, from that time onward I have not directed any being into the <s>Śrāvaka</s> or <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles, having not previously attained the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. For this reason, Blessed One, I am not able to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

body.text: atha bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimāmantrayate sma- "subhūte .......gaccha" / subhūtirapi tvavocat- "bhagavan, .........notsahe /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: '<s>Subhūti</s>, go...' <s>Subhūti</s> also said: 'Blessed One, I am not able...

body.text: "ekasmin samaye vaiśālyāmmahānagaryāṃ licchavervimalakīrtergehaṃ piṇḍapātāyāgatasya licchavirvimalakirtirme pātramiṣṭvā, (tat) praṇītāhāreṇa pūrayitvā, etadvadati sma-
body.translated_text: At one time, I had come to the house of the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> in the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s> for alms-food. The <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, having taken my bowl, filled it with excellent food, and said this:

body.text: "'bhadanta subhute, tvaṃcedāmiṣasamatayā sarvadharmasamatānvayaśca sarvadharmasamatayā buddhadharmasamatānvayaḥ, sāmpratamimaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuṃdhi / (bhuṃdhi,) bhadanta subhūte, yadi tvaṃ lobhadveṣamohānna pratinisṛjya taissārthaṃ tvapratiṣṭhitaḥ; satkāyadṛṣtyanuccālya, ekāyanamārgaṃ gataḥ; tvayāpi tvavidyābhava tṛṣṇayorahatayorvidyāvimuktī punaranavaropite (yadi), paṃcānantariyāṇi ca tava vimuktiśca samāni, tvanna ca vimukto na cāpi baddhaḥ, tvayā catvāryāryasatyāni na ca dṛṣṭāni satyaṃca nādṛṣṭam, phale tvaprāpte pṛthagjano 'pi nāsi, pṛthagjanadharmāt punaranivṛttastvanna cāryo na cānāryaḥ, bhūyo 'pi sarvadharmapratisaṃyuktastu sarvadharmasaṃjñāvipramuktaḥ, (imaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuṃdhi) /
body.translated_text: 'Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, if through the equality of material things (<s>āmiṣasamatā</s>) you follow the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>, and through the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> you follow the equality of <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, then eat this alms-food now. Eat, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, if without abandoning passion, hatred, and delusion you are not established together with them; if without uprooting the view of a self-existent body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), you have entered the one path; if without destroying ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) and craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), you have not again produced knowledge and liberation; if the five unpardonable sins (<s>pañcānantarīyāṇi</s>) and your liberation are equal, and you are neither liberated nor bound; if you have not seen the four noble truths (<s>catvāryāryasatyāni</s>) and the truth is not unseen; if you have not attained the fruit yet are not a common person either, and though not turned away from the nature of a common person you are neither noble nor ignoble; if moreover while connected with all <s>dharmas</s> you are freed from the perception of all <s>dharmas</s>—then eat this alms-food.

body.text: "'(bhuṃdhi, yadi) tvayā śāstā cādṛṣṭo 'śrutaśca dharmārdhaśca saṃgho 'paryupāsitaḥ / ye te ṣaṭ śāstāraḥ yadidam- pūraṇaḥ kāśyapaḥ, maskarī gośālīputraḥ, saṃjayī vairāḍīputraḥ kakudaḥ kātyāyanaḥ, ajitaḥ keśakambalaśca nirgrantho jñātiputras- tān bhadantasya śāstṝnniśrāya, tvam pravrajita (ścedbhuṃdhi) /
body.translated_text: 'Eat, if you have not seen the Teacher, have not heard the <s>Dharma</s>, and have not attended upon the <s>Saṅgha</s>. If those six teachers—namely, <s>Pūraṇa Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Maskarī Gośālīputra</s>, <s>Sañjayī Vairāḍīputra</s>, <s>Kakuda Kātyāyana</s>, <s>Ajita Keśakambala</s>, and <s>Nirgrantha Jñātiputra</s>—if you, venerable one, have gone forth relying on those as your teachers, then eat.

body.text: "'yena te ṣaṭ śāstāro gacchanti ten āryaḥ subhūtirapi gāmi (cet); sarvadṛṣṭigateṣu praviśan, tvamapi tvantamadhyāpratilabdhaḥ; tvaṃ (cet) punaraṣṭākṣaṇapratipannaḥ kṣaṇāprāptaḥ, saṃkleśasambhūtastvaṃ vyavadānānupagataḥ; yatsarvasattvānāmaraṇaṃ, tadbhadantasyāraṇaṃ (cet);tvaddāne 'viśodhite, bhadanta, ye kecittubhyaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ dadati, te paraṃ tu (cetsva-)vinipātakarāḥ; (yadi) tvaṃ sarvamārasahagataśca sarvakleśāstvatsahāyībhavaṃ gatāḥ; yaḥ kleśasvabhāvaḥ so 'pi (ced-) bhadantasya svabhāvo bhavati, tvayā sarvasattvaghātakacittam upasthāpitam, tvayā sarvabuddhānudhvaṃsanam (kṛtaṃ syāt), sarvabuddhadharmākīrti kṛtvā, saṃghe cāpratisaraṇastvañcenna kadāci parinirvāsi, tata imaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ bhuṃdhi /
body.translated_text: 'Wherever those six teachers go, if the noble <s>Subhūti</s> also goes; if entering into all views, you have attained neither end nor middle; if you have entered the eight inopportune states (<s>aṣṭākṣaṇa</s>) and have not attained the opportune moment; if you have arisen from defilement and have not reached purification; if the non-contention of all beings is your non-contention, venerable one; if your gift is not purified, venerable one, and whoever gives you alms-food, they become causes of their own downfall; if you are accompanied by all <s>Māras</s> and all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) have become your companions; if the nature of the <s>kleśas</s> is also your nature, venerable one; if you have generated the intention to harm all beings and have denigrated all <s>Buddhas</s>, having vilified all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>; and if you do not take refuge in the <s>Saṅgha</s> and you never attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>—then eat this alms-food.'

body.text: "ityukte, imaṃ tannirdeśaṃ śrutvā, bhagavan, mām 'taṃ kim bhāsiṣye 'haṃ, kiṃ vakṣyāmi, kiṃ karaṇīyam?' (iti) cintayamānaṃ, daśadikṣu tamobhūtāsu, tat pātramutsṛjya, gehāt pratiniḥsarantaṃ licchavirvimalakīrtiretadvadati sma-
body.translated_text: When this was said, having heard this discourse, Blessed One, thinking 'What shall I say? What shall I speak? What should be done?'—while the ten directions became dark around me, I set down that bowl and was about to leave the house, when the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said this:

body.text: "'bhadanta subhute, akṣarebhyo 'bhayenedaṃ pātraṃ pratīccha / bhadanta subhūte tat kiṃ manyase tathāgatasya nirmāṇe taduktaṃ syāt, tasmāt kiṃ bhaverbhītaḥ?'- taṃ- 'no hīdaṃ kulaputra' ityavacam / sa māmabravīt- 'bhadanta subhūte, māyānirmāṇasvabhāvebhyaḥ sarvadharmebhyo mā bhaiṣiḥ / tat kasya hetoḥ? teṣu sarveṣvapi vacaneṣu tatsvabhāveṣu tasmāhu nāma paṇḍitā akṣareṣvasaṅgāstebhyo 'trastāḥ tat kasya hetoḥ? teṣu sarveṣvakṣareṣu hyanakṣareṣu, (sarvaṃ) sthāpayitvā, vimokṣaḥ sarvadharmā hi vimokṣalakṣaṇāḥ / '
body.translated_text: 'Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, accept this bowl without fear of syllables! Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, what do you think—if a <s>Tathāgata</s>'s emanation had spoken thus, would you be afraid of it?' I said: 'No indeed, son of good family.' He said to me: 'Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, do not be afraid of all <s>dharmas</s>, which are of the nature of magical illusion and emanation. Why is that? In all those words, which are of that very nature, the wise are said to be unattached to syllables and unafraid of them. Why is that? All those syllables are in fact non-syllables. Setting aside everything, liberation—for all <s>dharmas</s> bear the mark of liberation.'

body.text: "asminnirdeśe deśite, devaputrāṇāṃ dviśataṃ dharmeṣu virajaṃ vītamalaṃ viśuddhaṃ dharmacakṣuśca devaputrāṇāṃ pañcaśatamanulomikīm kṣānti prāpnuvanti sma / ahaṃ tu pratibhānāpagatastasmai punarvisarjanasyāsamartho ('bhūvam) / etasmāt kāraṇāt, bhagavan tasya satpuruṣasya rogapṛcchanagamanannotsahe / "
body.translated_text: When this discourse was taught, two hundred <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods) attained the pure, stainless, spotless <s>Dharma</s>-eye regarding all <s>dharmas</s>, and five hundred <s>devaputras</s> attained acquiescent patience (<s>anulomikī kṣānti</s>). But I, bereft of eloquence, was unable to respond to him. For this reason, Blessed One, I am not able to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

body.text: tato bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputramāmantrayate sma- "pūrṇa,..... gaccha" / - pūrṇo 'pi tvavocat- "bhagavan..... notsahe..... /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>: '<s>Pūrṇa</s>, go...' <s>Pūrṇa</s> also said: 'Blessed One, I am not able...

body.text: "ekasmin samaye mām mahāvanasyaikasmin pṛthivīpradeśe sthitamādikarmikebhyo bhikṣubhyo dharma deśayantaṃ licchavirvimalakīrtistenāgata edad vadati sma-
body.translated_text: At one time, I was standing in a certain place in the great forest, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to monks who were beginners, when the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> came there and said this:

body.text: "'bhadanta pūrṇa, samāpattimanuprāpyaiṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāñcittam paśya, (dṛṣṭvā) ca dharma prativedasyasva / mahāratnabhājanaṃ pūtikenaudanena mā pīparaḥ / eṣāṃ bhikṣūṇām, jānīhi, adhyāśayaḥ kīdṛśaḥ / vaiḍūryamaṇiratnaṃ kācakamaṇinā mopamāhi /
body.translated_text: 'Venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, having first entered <s>samāpatti</s> (meditative attainment), examine the minds of these monks, and then teach the <s>Dharma</s>! Do not fill a great jewel-vessel with rotten rice gruel! Know first what is the disposition (<s>adhyāśaya</s>) of these monks. Do not compare the jewel of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) with a glass bead!

body.text: "'bhadanta pūrṇa, sattvendriyeṣvaniściteṣu, prādeśikendriyam mopasaṃhara / avraṇasya vraṇam mā prasūṣva / mahāmārgāvatārārthik(-ebhyo) vīrthīmañjarīm mā parigrahīaḥ / mahāsamudreṇa gokhurapadaṃ mā pīparaḥ / sumeru sarṣapaphale mā nikṣipa / dinakarasya prabhāṃ khadyotakena mā nirākuru / samyaksiṃhanādārthika(-ebhya) śṛgālarutam mā parigrahīḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, when the faculties (<s>indriya</s>) of beings are undetermined, do not apply a limited faculty! Do not produce a wound on one who has no wound! For those who wish to enter the great path, do not offer a narrow footpath! Do not fill a hoof-print with the great ocean! Do not place <s>Sumeru</s> in a mustard seed! Do not extinguish the radiance of the sun with a firefly! For those who wish the lion's roar of the right <s>Dharma</s>, do not offer the howl of a jackal!

body.text: "'bhadanta pūrṇa, eṣāṃ sarvabhikṣūṇāṃ hi mahāyānasampratipannanāṃ bodhicittaṃ bhrāntaṃ kevalam; bhadanta pūrṇa, ebhyaḥ śrāvakayānam mā prakāśaya / śrāvakayānaṃ hyabhūtam; sattvendriyakramajñāna ime śrāvakā mayā jātyandhasadṛśā matāḥ' /
body.translated_text: 'Venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, all these monks have indeed set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, yet their <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) has merely gone astray. Venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, do not proclaim the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle to them! For the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle is unreal. Through the knowledge of the gradations of the faculties of beings, these <s>śrāvakas</s> are regarded by me as similar to those born blind.'

body.text: "atha licchavau bimalakīrtau tena kālena tādṛśaṃ samādhi samāpanne, yathā tebhyo bhikṣubhyo vividhapūrvanivāsānusmṛtirbhavati, tebhyaḥ samyaksambodhyarthāya buddhānām pañcaśatam paryupāsitebhyaḥ kuśalamūlasamanvāgatebhyaḥ sva bodhicittamabhimukhībhūtvā, te satpuruṣasya pādayoaḥ śirasā praṇipatya pragṛhītāñjalayo 'bhūvan / (yathā) punaste 'nuttarasamyaksambodhyā avinivartanīyā bhavanti, tasmiṃstathā dharma darśitavati, bhagavan, cintayatomamaivamabhūt-
body.translated_text: "Then, at that time, when the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> entered such a <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), it produced in those monks the recollection of their various former lives. Having attended upon five hundred <s>Buddhas</s> for the sake of perfect awakening, endowed with roots of merit, their own <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) having become manifest, they bowed at the feet of that noble man with their heads, with palms joined together. (As a result) they became irreversible from <s>anuttarasamyaksambodhī</s> (supreme perfect awakening). When he had thus shown the <s>Dharma</s>, Blessed One, this thought arose in me:

body.text: "'śrāvakeṇa, paracittāśayānavivicya, na kasmaiciddharmo nirdeśyaḥ / tat kasya hetoaḥ? śrāvakastu sarvasattvavarāvarendriyavijño nāsti' yathā tathāgatorhan samyaksambuddhastathā nityasamāhito nāsti' / bhagavan, etasmātkāraṇāttasya satpuruṣasya rogapṛcchanagamanannotsahe / "
body.translated_text: "'A <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple), without discerning the intentions and dispositions of others' minds, should not teach the <s>Dharma</s> to anyone. What is the reason? A <s>śrāvaka</s> does not possess the knowledge of the superior and inferior faculties of all beings as does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, who is ever in <s>samādhi</s>.' Blessed One, for this reason I am unable to go to that noble man to inquire about his illness."

body.text: tato bhagavānāyuṣmantam mahākātyāyanamāmantrayate sma- "kātyāyana,..... gaccha" / kātyāyanastvavocat- "bhagavan,..... notsahe..... /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>: "<s>Kātyāyana</s>, go..." <s>Kātyāyana</s> replied: "Blessed One, I am unable..."

body.text: "ekasmin samaye bhagavatā bhikṣubhyo 'vavādakasūtre 'mantrite, tasya sūtrasya vacananirṇayāya māṃ dharma tadyathā - 'anityatāduḥkhanairātmya śāntyartham' deśayamānaṃ licchavirvimalakīrtistenopasaṃkramya, etadvadati sma -
body.translated_text: "On one occasion, when the Blessed One instructed the monks with a discourse on the admonishment <s>sūtra</s>, I was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> for the purpose of explaining the words of that <s>sūtra</s>—namely, 'impermanence, suffering, non-self, for the purpose of peace'—when the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> approached and said to me:

body.text: "'bhadanta mahākātyāyana, pracārasamprayuktāmutpādabhaṅgasahagatāṃ dharmatāṃ mā śādhi / yadatyantato 'nutpāditam, notpadyate, sañjanitanna bhaviṣyati; (yadatyantato) 'niruddham, na nirudhyate, niruddhanna bhaviṣyati, tadhyanityatāyā arthaḥ / yaḥ pañcaskandheṣu śūnyatādhigamenānupapattyavabodhārthaḥ, sa hi duḥkhasyārthaḥ / yātmanairātmyayorabhāvatā, sā nairātmyasyārthaḥ / yatsvabhāvaparabhāvāpagataṃ, tadhyajvalanam, yadajvalanam, tanna śāmyati; yadapraśāntam, tacchāntyā arthaḥ' /
body.translated_text: "'Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, do not teach a nature of phenomena connected with occurrence, accompanied by arising and passing away! That which is ultimately unarisen does not arise, and having arisen, will not continue to exist; that which is ultimately unceased does not cease, and having ceased, will not continue to exist—that is the meaning of impermanence. The meaning of suffering is the comprehension of non-arising in the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) through the realization of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). The meaning of <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self) is the non-existence of both self and non-self. The meaning of <s>śānti</s> (peace) is that which is free from own-nature and other-nature; that which is free of burning does not cease—that which does not cease, that is the meaning of peace.'

body.text: "asminupadeśe deśite, teṣāṃ bhikṣuṇāmanupādāyāsravebhyaścittāni vimuktānyabhūvan / bhagavan, etasmāt..... notsahe" /
body.translated_text: "When this instruction was taught, the minds of those monks were liberated from the <s>āśravas</s> (defilements) without further clinging. Blessed One, for this reason... I am unable."

body.text: atha bhagavanāyuṣmantamaniruddhamāmantrayate sma- "aniruddha,..... gaccha" / aniruddho 'pi tvavocat- "bhagavan, .....notsahe..... / ..... /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>: "<s>Aniruddha</s>, go..." <s>Aniruddha</s> also replied: "Blessed One, I am unable..."

body.text: "ekasmin samaye māmekasmimsḥcaṃkramaṇe caṃkramyamāṇaṃ, yenāhaṃ tenāgamya, śubhavyūho nāma mahābrahmā brahmaṇāṃ daśasahasreṇa sārdha taṃ deśamavabhāsya, mama pādau śirasābhivandya, ekānte sthita etadavocat- 'bhadantāniruddha, tvaṃ bhagavatāgradivyacakṣurvānākhyātaḥ; āyuṣmato 'niruddhasya divyacakṣuṣā kiyadarvāg dṛśyate?'- tam evamavacam- 'mitra, tadyathāpi nāma puruṣasya cakṣurvataḥ karatale saṃnihitamāmlaphalaṃ dṛśyate, tathā bhagavataḥ śākyamunerbuddhakṣetram, trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātum paśyāmī'ti /
body.translated_text: "On one occasion, when I was walking on a certain walking-meditation path, a great <s>Brahmā</s> named <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, together with ten thousand attendants of <s>Brahmā</s>, illuminating that place, bowed at my feet with his head, stood to one side, and said: 'Venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>, you have been declared by the Blessed One as the foremost among those with the divine eye. With the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>'s divine eye, how far can one see?' I said to him: 'Friend, just as a person with eyes sees an <s>āmla</s> fruit placed in the palm of his hand, so too do I see the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s> (trichiliocosm).'

body.text: "māmetadvadantaṃ licchavirvimalakīrtistaṃ deśamupasaṃkramya, mama pādau śirasābhivandya, etadavocat- 'bhadantasyāniruddhasya divyacakṣuḥ kimabhisaṃskāralakṣaṇaṃ vānabhisaṃskāralakṣaṇaṃ vā? tadyadyabhisaṃskāralakṣaṇam, syād bāhya pañcābhijñāsamam / yadyanabhisaṃskāra(-lakṣaṇam), anabhisaṃskāraḥ syādasaṃskṛtaḥ / sa darśanasyāśaktaścet, sthaviraḥ katham paśyet?'
body.translated_text: "When I said this, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> approached that place, bowed at my feet with his head, and said: 'Venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>, is the divine eye characterized by the conditioned or by the unconditioned? If it is characterized by the conditioned, it would be equal to the five superknowledges of non-Buddhists. If it is characterized by the unconditioned, then being unconditioned, it would be uncompounded. Being incapable of seeing, how then could the elder see?'

body.text: "ityukte 'bhūvaṃ tūṣṇībhūtaḥ / sa brahmā tu tasmātsatpuruṣādimaṃ nirdeśaṃ śrutvā, āścaryaprāpto 'bhivandanaṃ kṛtvā, etadabravīt- 'loke divyacakṣurvānasti kaḥ?'- āha- 'bhagavanto buddhā hi loke divyacakṣurvantaḥ; te hyanupatasamāhitasthāne sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi saṃpaśyantyubhābhyām aprabhāvitāḥ' /
body.translated_text: "Thus addressed, I became silent. But that <s>Brahmā</s>, having heard this instruction from that noble man, was filled with wonder. Having paid homage, he said: 'Who in the world possesses the divine eye?' He replied: 'The Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> possess the divine eye in the world. They, without falling into a state of <s>samādhi</s>, see all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), unaffected by both [the conditioned and the unconditioned].'

body.text: "atha brahmā (ca) daśa parijanasahasrāṇīmaṃ nirdeśaṃ śrutvā, adhyāśayenānuttarasamyaksaṃbodhicitaṃ saṃjanayante sma / te mahyaṃca tasmai satpuruṣāya namaskṛtvā, abhivandya, tatraivāntaradhāyiṣuḥ / ahaṃ tu pratibhānāpagato 'bhūvam / etasmāt.....notsahe" /
body.translated_text: "Then <s>Brahmā</s> and his ten thousand attendants, having heard this instruction, generated with higher intention the mind of <s>anuttarasamyaksambodhī</s> (supreme perfect awakening). Having paid homage and bowed to me and to that noble man, they vanished right there. I, however, became devoid of eloquence. For this reason... I am unable."

body.text: tato bhagavānāyuṣmantamupālimāmantrayate sma- "upāle,.....gaccha" / - upāliaḥ punaravocat- "bhagavan.....notsahe..... /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Upāli</s>: "<s>Upāli</s>, go..." <s>Upāli</s> replied: "Blessed One, I am unable..."

body.text: "ekasmin samaye dvau bhikṣū āpattimāpannau bhagavati lajjamānau bhagavatsamīpamanupasaṃkramya, tāvubhau yenāham tenopasaṃkramya, māvevaṃ vadataḥ- 'bhadantopāle, āvamāpattimāpannou ca lajjamānau bhagavatsamīpaṃ tvanupasaṃkramya, āyuṣmānupālirāvayoaḥ saṃśayaṃ prativinodayatu, āvāmāpattyāḥ praṇayatu' /
body.translated_text: "On one occasion, two monks who had committed an offense, being ashamed before the Blessed One, did not approach the Blessed One. Those two approached me, saying: 'Venerable <s>Upāli</s>, we have committed an offense, and being ashamed, we have not approached the Blessed One. May the venerable <s>Upāli</s> clear our doubt and free us from the offense.'

body.text: "ityukte, bhagavan, yena tābhyāṃ bhikṣubhyāṃ dharmakathāmadeśayam tena sa licchavirvimalakīrtirapyupasaṃkramya, māmetadvadati sma-
