body.translated_text: "Thus addressed, Blessed One, as I was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to those two monks, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> also approached and said to me:

body.text: "'bhadantopāle, tvayānayorbhikṣvorāpattirbhūyo dṛḍhā na kartavyā, nāvila(-tarā) kartavyā; anayorāpattivipratisāraṃ prativinodaya / bhadantopāle, āpattirhyadhyātmamapratiṣṭhitā, bahirdhāvyativṛttā; ubhayeṣvasatsu ca (sā) nopalabhyate / tat kasya hetoaḥ? bhagavānavocat cittasaṃkleśena sattvasaṃkleśaḥ; cittavyavadānena viśuddhiriti-
body.translated_text: "'Venerable <s>Upāli</s>, you should not make the offense of these two monks more rigid, nor should you make it more turbid. Remove the remorse regarding their offense. Venerable <s>Upāli</s>, an offense is not established internally, nor is it found externally; and when both are absent, it cannot be apprehended. What is the reason? The Blessed One said: "By the defilement of the mind, beings are defiled; by the purification of the mind, they are purified."

body.text: "'subhāṣitārthe, bhadantopāle, cittamadhyātmaṃ vā bahirdhā vā nāsti; ubhayeṣvasatsvapi (tan-)nopalabhyate / cittaṃ yathā tathāpyāpattiaḥ / yathāpattistathāpi sarvadharmāḥtathatāyā nātikrāmaṇti /
body.translated_text: "'On the well-spoken meaning, Venerable <s>Upāli</s>: the mind is not found internally, nor externally; and when both are absent, it cannot be apprehended. As is the mind, so too are offenses. As are offenses, so too are all <s>dharmas</s>—they do not go beyond <s>tathatā</s> (suchness).

body.text: "'bhadantopāle, yaścittasvabhāvaḥ- sa bhadantasya vimuktacittasya cittasvabhāvo yena kena cittasvabhāvena ki kadācana saṃkliṣṭo 'bhūt?' abravam-ḥ 'no hīdaṃ' / - āha- 'bhadantopāle, sarvasattvacittaṃ hi tatsvabhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: "'Venerable <s>Upāli</s>, that which is the own-nature of the mind—is the own-nature of the venerable's liberated mind ever defiled by any own-nature of mind whatsoever?' I said: 'No indeed.' He said: 'Venerable <s>Upāli</s>, the mind of all beings is of that very own-nature.

body.text: "'bhadantopāle, saṃkalpo hi kleśaḥ, nirvikalpo 'vikalpanā svabhāvaḥ / viparyāsaḥ saṃkleśa, aviparyāsaḥ svabhāvaḥ / ātmasamāropaḥ saṃkleśaḥ, nairātmyaṃ svabhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: "'Venerable <s>Upāli</s>, conceptual thought is defilement; non-conceptual, non-discriminating thought is own-nature. Perversion is defilement; non-perversion is own-nature. Imputation of self is defilement; <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self) is own-nature.

body.text: "'bhadantopāle, sarvadharmā hyupapadya, vinaśyanto 'pratiṣṭhitā māyābhravidhudupamāḥ / sarvadharmā anavasthitāḥ kṣaṇamātramapi na tiṣṭhanti / sarvadharmā hi svapnamarīcinibhā abhūtadarśanam / sarvadharmā udakacandrapratibimbakalpāś cittasaṃkalpāt samuchritāḥ / yaiḥ kaiścana tathāhi prajñāyate, te vinayadharā nāmocyante; ye kecanaivaṃ dāṃtāste sudāṃtāḥ' /
body.translated_text: "'Venerable <s>Upāli</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> arise and perish; they are unestablished—like illusions, clouds, lightning, and water-reflections. All <s>dharmas</s> are unstable and do not remain even for a moment. All <s>dharmas</s> are like dreams and mirages—appearances of the unreal. All <s>dharmas</s> are like the reflection of the moon in water, arising from mental conceptualization. By those who thus understand, they are called bearers of the <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline); those who are thus disciplined are the truly disciplined.'

body.text: "atha tau bhikṣū etadavadatām- 'ayaṃ gṛhapatiaḥ suprajñāvān; vinayadharāṇāṃ bhagavataiṣa hyagra ākhyāto bhadantopālistādṛśaḥ (suprajñāvān) nāsti' / tābhyāmevamavacam- 'bhikṣū, imaṃ yuvāṃ gṛhapatimmā pratijānītam / tat kasya hetoḥ? sthāpayitvā tathāgatam, ye kecanāsya pratibhānapratiprasrabdhyāḥ samarthāḥ śrāvakā vā bodhisattvā vā, te kecinna vidyante / asya prajñālokastajjātīyaḥ' /
body.translated_text: "Then those two monks said: 'This householder is very wise. The venerable <s>Upāli</s>, who was declared by the Blessed One as the foremost among bearers of the <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline), is not so wise as he.' I said to those two: 'Monks, do not regard this householder as ordinary. What is the reason? Aside from the <s>Tathāgata</s>, there are no <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) or <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are capable of matching his eloquence. His light of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) is of such a nature.'

body.text: "tatastau bhikṣū vicikitsām pratinisṛjya, tatraivādhyāśayenānuttarasamyaksambodhicittaṃ saṃjanayamānau, taṃ satpuruṣamabhivandya, etadavadatām- 'sarvasattvā api caivaṃrūpaṃ pratibhānaṃ labheran', iti / etasmāt .....notsahe" /
body.translated_text: "Then those two monks, abandoning their doubts, generated with higher intention the mind of <s>anuttarasamyaksambodhī</s> (supreme perfect awakening) right there. Having bowed to that noble man, they said: 'May all beings also attain such eloquence!' For this reason... I am unable."

body.text: atha bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ rāhulamāmantrayate sma- "rāhula,..... gaccha" / rāhulastvavocat- "bhagavān,..... notsahe..... /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Rāhula</s>: "<s>Rāhula</s>, go..." <s>Rāhula</s> replied: "Blessed One, I am unable..."

body.text: "ekasmin samaye 'nekalicchavikumārā yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkramya, māmevaṃ vadanti sma- 'bhadanta rāhula, tvaṃ bhagavato 'si putraḥ / cakravartirājyaṃ hitvā, pravrajya, ki tvayopalabdham, pravrajyāyā guṇānuśaṃsaṃ kim?' ityukte, māṃ tebhyo yathāyogam pravrajyāguṇānuśaṃsaṃ deśayantaṃ licchavirvimalakīrtirapi, yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkrānto mahyannamaskṛtvā, etadavocat-
body.translated_text: "Once, several <s>Licchavi</s> youths approached me and said: 'Venerable <s>Rāhula</s>, you are the son of the Blessed One. Having renounced the sovereignty of a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) and gone forth, what have you obtained? What are the virtues and benefits of the renunciant life?' When this was said, as I was teaching those [youths] the virtues and benefits of renunciation as appropriate, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> also approached me, bowed to me, and said:

body.text: "'bhadanta rāhula, yathā pravrajyā guṇānuśaṃsaṃ deśayasi tathā na deśayeḥ / tat kasya hetoḥ? pravajyā hi guṇarahitā, anuśaṃsāpagatā / bhadanta rāhula, yasmai saṃskṛtam pravartate tasmai guṇānuśaṃsam; pravrajyā tvasaṃskṛtayogaścāsaṃskṛte guṇānuśaṃsannāsti /
body.translated_text: "'Venerable <s>Rāhula</s>, you should not teach the virtues and benefits of renunciation in that way! Why? Because renunciation is devoid of virtues and free from benefits. Venerable <s>Rāhula</s>, that for which the conditioned operates—for that there are virtues and benefits. But renunciation is the practice of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), and in the unconditioned there are no virtues or benefits.

body.text: "'bhadanta rāhula, arūpiṇī hi pravrajyā rūpāpagatā, avarāgrāntadṛṣṭivigatā nirvāṇapathaḥ, paṇḍitairvarṇitā, āryaiḥ parigṛhītā sarvamāraparājayakarā, pañcagati niaḥsaraṇam, pañcacakṣuḥ śodhanā, pañcabalaprāptiḥ, pañcendriyāśrayaḥ; (sā)'nyebhyo 'pīḍā pāpadharmāsaṃsṛṣṭā paratīrthikasudamanaṃ, prajñaptisamatikrāntā kāmapaṃke gambhīraḥ, ādhāraṇarahitā mamābhāvā vītāhaṅkārā; anupādānam, anupāyāsaḥ, saṃkṣobhapratiniḥsargaḥ, svacittavinayaśca paracittarakṣaṇam, śamathasāmagrī, sarvatra niravadya(-tvam)- sā hi pravrajyā nāma / ye kecana tathā hi pravrajitāste supravrajitāḥ /
body.translated_text: "'Venerable <s>Rāhula</s>, renunciation is indeed formless, free from materiality, free from the views of lower and higher extremes, the path of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, praised by the wise, taken up by the noble ones, the defeater of all <s>Māras</s>, the escape from the five destinies, the purification of the five eyes, the attainment of the five powers, the support of the five faculties. It does no harm to others, is untouched by evil <s>dharmas</s>, is the subduer of non-Buddhist teachers, transcends mere designation, is the deep [ground] in the mire of desire, is without support, free from the notion of 'mine,' without ego-sense; it is non-grasping, non-disturbance, the abandonment of agitation, the training of one's own mind and the protection of others' minds, the prerequisite of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility), and blamelessness everywhere—that indeed is called renunciation. Those who have thus gone forth are well-renounced.

body.text: "'kumārāḥ, etādṛśe svākhyāte dharme pravrajata / buddhotpādo durlabhaḥ, kṣaṇasampadapi ca durlabhā, durlabhā punarmanuṣyagatiaḥ' /
body.translated_text: "'Youths, go forth in this well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>! The arising of a <s>Buddha</s> is rare, the opportune moment is also rare, and rarer still is a human birth.'

body.text: "te kumārā etadavadan- 'gṛhapate, asmābhiryathā śrutam tathāgatena(oktam)- mātāpitṛbhyāmanutsṛṣṭaḥ pravrājako na (bhavatī'-)ti / sa tānabravīt- 'kumārāḥ, anuttarasamyaksambodhicittaṃ saṃjanayamānāḥ prayatnena pratipatsyatha / (tathā hi) yūyaṃ tattvataḥ pravrajitāścopasampannāḥ' /
body.translated_text: "Those youths said: 'Householder, we have heard that the <s>Tathāgata</s> has said that one who is not released by one's parents cannot go forth.' He said to them: 'Youths, by striving to generate the mind of <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), you will truly practice. For in truth, you are [thereby] truly renounced and fully ordained.'

body.text: "atha trisahasraṃ dviśataṃ licchavikumārā anuttarasamyaksambodhicittamutpādayanti sma / bhagavan, etasmāt.....notsahe" /
body.translated_text: "Then three thousand two hundred <s>Licchavi</s> youths generated the mind of <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). Blessed One, for this reason... I dare not [go to inquire about his illness]."

body.text: tato bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma- "ānanda,.....gaccha" / ānanda; punaravocat- "bhagavan,.....notsahe..... /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: '<s>Ānanda</s>,... go.' <s>Ānanda</s> replied: 'Blessed One,... I dare not...

body.text: "ekasmin samaye bhagavataḥ kāya eko rogo niścārya, tasmai kṣīramākāṅkṣamāṇo 'hamekasya brāhmāṇamahāśālakulasya dvārasamīpe pātradhārī sthito ('bhūvam) / licchavirvimalakīrtirapi taddeśamupasaṃkramya, mahyannama skṛtvā, evaṃ vadati sma-
body.translated_text: "Once, when a certain illness had arisen in the Blessed One's body, I stood at the door of a certain great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> household, holding my bowl, desiring milk for him. The <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> also approached that place, bowed to me, and said:

body.text: "'bhadantānanda, kimartham kalyameva pātramādāya, asya kulasya dvārasamīpe sthito 'si?'- tamevamavacam- 'bhagavataḥ kāya eko rogo niścārya, tasmai kṣīreṇa prayojanāttad(-bhaiṣajyaṃ) paryeṣa' ityavādiṣam / sa māmetadavocat-
body.translated_text: "'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, for what purpose are you standing at the door of this household so early in the morning, holding your bowl?' I said to him: 'A certain illness has arisen in the Blessed One's body; because he needs milk, I am seeking that medicine.' He said to me:

body.text: "'bhadantānanda, evammā vagdhi / bhadantānanda, tathāgatasya hi kāyo vajrakaṭhinaḥ, sarvākuśalavāsanāprahīṇaḥ / tasmai sarvakuśaladharmopetāya rogaḥ kuto bhavet? ātaṃkastasmai kutaḥ?
body.translated_text: "'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, do not say such a thing! Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body is diamond-hard (<s>vajrakaṭhina</s>), free from all vestiges of unwholesome states. How could illness arise for one endowed with all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>? How could affliction come to him?

body.text: "'bhadantānanda, bhagavate 'nudhvaṃsanākaraṇāya tūṣṇīm pratigaccha / kañcidanyametanmā vagdhi / mahāmahaujaskā devaputrāśca buddhakṣetrasamāgatā bodhisattvā hi śroṣyanti / bhadantānanda, yadi parīttakuśalamūlopetaścakravartirājo 'pyarogaḥ, tasmā apramāṇakuśalamūlasahagatāya bhagavate rogaḥ kutaḥ? tat sthānanna bidyate /
body.translated_text: "'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, go away in silence, so as not to disparage the Blessed One. Do not say this to anyone else. The <s>devaputras</s> of great splendor and the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have assembled from [other] <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) will hear this. Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, if even a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) endowed with only limited roots of merit is free from illness, then how could illness arise for the Blessed One who possesses immeasurable roots of merit? That situation does not exist.

body.text: "'bhadantānanda, māṃ lajjitakaraṇāya pratigaccha / anyatīrthikāḥ, mīmāṃsakāḥ, paribrājakāḥ, nirgranthāḥ, ājīvikāśca hi śroṣyanti / ta evam- 'aho yadyeṣāṃ śāstā svāturatrāṇasyāpyasamarthaḥ, sattvāturāṇāṃ trāṇamiva (dātuṃ) kutaḥ śakrotī'(-ti) cintayiṣyanti / bhadantānanda, praticchādayamāno 'ntardhānaṃ gaccheḥ, kaścicchṛṇuyāt /
body.translated_text: "'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, go away, do not cause me shame. The non-Buddhist teachers, the <s>mīmāṃsakas</s> (ritualist philosophers), the wandering ascetics, the <s>nirgranthas</s> (Jain monks), and the <s>ājīvikas</s> will hear this. They will think: "Alas, if this teacher is unable to protect even himself from illness, how can he protect other beings who are ill?" Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, go away stealthily, concealing yourself; let no one hear this.

body.text: "'bhadantānanda, tathāgatā hi dharmakāyaḥ, na (sa) āhārapoṣitaṃ deham / tathāgatāḥ sarvalokadharmasamatikrānto lokottarakāyaḥ / tathāgatasya kāyo 'nupadravo vinivṛttāsravaḥ / tathāgatasya kāyo hyasaṃskṛtaḥ sarvasaṃskārāpagataḥ / bhadantānanda, īdṛśāya vyādhimeṣṭum, ayuktiścāsadṛśam' /
body.translated_text: "'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> have the <s>dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body), not a body nourished by food. The <s>Tathāgatas</s> have a supramundane body that has transcended all worldly <s>dharmas</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body is free from affliction, with all <s>āśravas</s> (defilements) eradicated. The <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body is unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), free from all conditioned formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>). Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, to attribute illness to such a body is improper and unseemly.'

body.text: "'ityukte, tatra 'kim mayā bhagavato mithyā śrutam, mithyodgṛhītam?' (iti) cintayamāno 'tilajjito bhūtvā, athāntarīkṣātsvaramaśrauṣam- 'ānanda, gṛhapatiryathā deśayati, tattathā; api tu bhagavati pañcakaṣāya kāla utpanne, ataḥ sattvā hīnena pradānacaritena damyāḥ / tataḥ, ānanda, alajjitaḥ kṣīramāhṛtya pratigacche '-tyavādīt /
body.translated_text: "When this was said, I thought: 'Have I then incorrectly heard and incorrectly grasped the Blessed One's [teaching]?' Becoming extremely ashamed, I then heard a voice from the sky: '<s>Ānanda</s>, what the householder teaches is true. Nevertheless, because the Blessed One has appeared in an age of the five corruptions (<s>pañcakaṣāya</s>), therefore he tames beings through humble conduct of giving. Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, be unashamed; go and bring the milk.'

body.text: "bhagavan, licchavervimalakīrteḥ praśnasamādhānopadeśastādṛśo ('bhut) / etasmādbhagavan,..... notsahe" /
body.translated_text: "Blessed One, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>'s instruction in resolving questions was of such a nature. For this reason, Blessed One,... I dare not [go]."

body.text: evameva pañcaśatamātrāḥ śrāvakā anutsahamānāḥ "svapratibhānam" bhagavantamavocan / yallicchavinā vimalakīrtinā saha kathitaṃ, tatsarvaṃ bhagavantamavocan /
body.translated_text: In just this way, five hundred <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), unable [to go], told the Blessed One of their own experiences—all that had been said to them by the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>.

body.text: atha bhagavān bodhisattcaṃ maitreyamāmantrayate sma - "maitreya,..... gaccha" / maitreyastvavocat- "bhagavan,..... notsahe..... /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: '<s>Maitreya</s>,... go.' But <s>Maitreya</s> said: 'Blessed One,... I dare not...

body.text: "ekasmin samaye santuṣitadevaputragaṇena (ca) tuṣitavaṃśadevaputraiḥ sārdha (yenāhaṃ), bodhisattvamahāsattvānāmavaivartikabhūmimārabhya, tathā hi dharmakathāṃ kathayamānaḥ, tena licchavirvimalakīrtirūpasaṃkramya, māmetadavocat-
body.translated_text: "Once, while I was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to the assembly of <s>Santuṣita</s> <s>devaputras</s> along with the <s>Tuṣitavaṃśa</s> <s>devaputras</s>, beginning with the irreversible stage (<s>avaivartikabhūmi</s>) of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> approached and said to me:

body.text: "'maitreya, yadi tvaṃ bhagavatānuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhyāmekajātipratibaddho vyākṛtaḥ, sa maitreyaḥ kayā jātyā vyākṛtaḥ? atītena kim? aho svidanāgatena? aho svitpratyupannena? tatra yātītajātiḥ, sā hi kṣīṇā / yadanāgatam, tadananuprāptam / pratyutpannajātyāṃ tu sthānannāsti / tad yathā bhagavatā- 'tathā hi bhikṣo, ekakṣaṇe tvaṃ jāyase, jīryase, mriyase, cyavase, upapadyasa' iti subhāṣitam / anutpāde niyāmāvakrāntiḥ, ajātikhyākṛtā /
body.translated_text: "'<s>Maitreya</s>, if you have been predicted by the Blessed One for <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) as one bound by a single birth, by which birth were you predicted? Was it the past? Or the future? Or the present? If the past birth, that has already ceased. If the future, that has not yet arrived. In the present birth, there is no abiding. As the Blessed One has well said: "Monk, in a single instant you are born, you age, you die, you pass away, and you are reborn." In the unborn, there is entry into the certainty of the right course (<s>niyāmāvakrānti</s>), predicted through the nature of non-arising.

body.text: "'anutpadyamānaścennābhisambudhyase; maitreya, kathaṃ vyākṛto 'si? tathatājātyā vā tathatānirodhena vā? tathatotpādanirodhāpagatā, anupatsyamānā cānirotsyamānā /
body.translated_text: "'If, not arising, you do not attain awakening, <s>Maitreya</s>, how were you predicted? By the arising of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) or by the cessation of <s>tathatā</s>? <s>Tathatā</s> is free from arising and cessation, neither arising nor ceasing.

body.text: "'yā sarvasattvānāṃ, sarvadharmāṇāñca sarvāryāṇāṃca tathatā, sā hi, maitreya, tavāpi tathātā / tvañcedevaṃvyākṛtaḥ, sarvasattvā apy-(evaṃ-) vyākṛtāḥ / tat kasya hetoḥ? tathatā hi dvayāprabhāvitā, nānātvāprabhāvitā / tena hi, maitreya, yadā tvaṃ bodhimabhisambhotsyase, tadā sarvasattvā api tādṛśāṃ bodhimabhisambhotsyante / tat kasya hetoḥ? bodhirhi sarvasattvānvayā / maitreya, yadā tvaṃ parinirvṛtastadā sarvasattvā api parinirvāyiṣyanti / tat kasya hetoḥ? (yadi) sarvasattvāḥ (syur) aparinirvṛtāḥ, tathāgataḥ (syād) aparinirvṛtaḥ / sarve te sattvāḥ suparinirvṛtāstena hi nirvāṇajātīyā dṛśyante / maitreya, tasmādimān devaputrān mā vipralambhasva, mā vañcayasva /
body.translated_text: "'That <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) which belongs to all beings, all <s>dharmas</s>, and all noble ones—that, <s>Maitreya</s>, is your <s>tathatā</s> as well. If you have been thus predicted, then all beings are also thus predicted. Why? Because <s>tathatā</s> is not differentiated by duality or multiplicity. Therefore, <s>Maitreya</s>, when you attain <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), all beings will also attain such awakening. Why? Because <s>bodhi</s> pervades all beings. <s>Maitreya</s>, when you attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, all beings too will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Why? If all beings were not attained to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> would not have attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. All those beings are well attained to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; therefore they are seen to be of the nature of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. <s>Maitreya</s>, therefore do not deceive or delude these <s>devaputras</s>.

body.text: "'bodhyānna kaścit pratiṣṭhite(vā) vivartate(vā) / tasmānmaitreya, imān devaputrāṃstāṃ bodhisaṅkalpadṛṣṭimutsarjaya / bodhinna kāyena nāpi cittenābhisambudhyati / bodhirhi sarvanimittavyūpaśamaḥ / bodhiḥ sarvālambanāropa rahitā, sarvamanasikārapracārāpagatā, sarvadṛṣṭigataparicchinnā, sarvaparitarkavigatā; bodhiḥ sarveñjitacetaścalanavisaṃyuktā, sarvapraṇidhānāpravṛtā, sarvodgrahaṇavirahitā, aśleṣapratipannā, dharmadhātuniśrayaniśritā, tathatānvayā bhūtakoṭyavasthitā manodharmābhāvenādvayā, ākāśasamasamā, utpādavyayasthityanyathātvābhāvenāsaṃskṛtā /
body.translated_text: '<s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) is that in which no one is established, nor does anyone turn away from it. Therefore, <s>Maitreya</s>, cause these <s>devaputras</s> to abandon that view of awakening as a mental construct. <s>Bodhi</s> is not realized by the body, nor by the mind. For <s>bodhi</s> is the complete pacification of all signs. <s>Bodhi</s> is free from the imputation of all objects of support, gone beyond the range of all mental activity, cut off from all views, devoid of all conceptual elaboration; <s>bodhi</s> is disjoined from all agitation and wavering of mind, not proceeding from any aspiration, free from all grasping, established in non-attachment, resting upon the support of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), following <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), abiding at the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), non-dual through the absence of mental <s>dharmas</s>, equal to space, unconditioned through the absence of arising, cessation, duration, or change.

body.text: "'bodhiḥ sarvasattvānāñcittacaryādhyāśayaparijñā, āyatanānāṃ dvārābhūtā sarvavāsanāpratisandhikleśavipramuktāsaṃsṛṣṭā, sthānāsthānavisaṃyogena viṣayāpratiṣṭhitā, - '-samantatodeśānavasthitā, prādurbhāvinī tathatānupasthitā / bodhirnāmamātrā, tannāmāpyacalam / āyūhaniryūhavigatā bodhirataraṅgā / bodhirnirupāyāsā, prakṛtyā pariśuddhā, prabhāsaḥ svabhāvaviśuddhā / bodhiranudgrahaṇā svanālambanā, sarvadharmasamatādhigamenābhinnā / bodhirudāharaṇa viśleṣeṇānupamā, suduravabodhā-yataḥ sūkṣmā /
body.translated_text: '<s>Bodhi</s> is the complete knowledge of the mental conduct, actions, and higher dispositions of all beings; it is the gateway of the sense-bases, free from and unassociated with all latent tendencies and defilements; disjoined from distinctions of tenable and untenable positions, not established in any object of experience; not established in any location whatsoever, manifesting without being fixed in <s>tathatā</s>. <s>Bodhi</s> is mere name, and even that name is unmoving. <s>Bodhi</s> is free from exertion and withdrawal, without waves. <s>Bodhi</s> is without disturbance, pure by nature, luminous by its own nature of purity. <s>Bodhi</s> is without grasping, resting in its own support, undifferentiated through the realization of the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>. <s>Bodhi</s> is incomparable through the separation of all illustrations, extremely difficult to comprehend because it is subtle.

body.text: "'bodhiścedākāśasvabhāvena sarvatragā, sā hi kāyena vā cittena vābhisambuddhanāy āsamarthā / tat kasya hetoḥ? kāyo hi tṛṇakāṣṭhakuḍyapathapratibhāsanibhaḥ / cittamarūpamasanidarśanamaniśrayamavijñaptikam" /
body.translated_text: 'Since <s>bodhi</s> is all-pervading by its nature of space, it is impossible to realize it through the body or the mind. And why is that? Because the body is like grass, wood, a wall, or a reflection; and the mind is formless, without appearance, without support, and without cognizability.'

body.text: "bhagavan, asminupadeśe prakāśite, tasyāḥ pariṣado dve śate devaputrāṇāmanutpattikadharmakṣāntim prāpnuvan / ahaṃ tvapagatapratibhāno 'bhūvam / etasmāt.....notsahe" /
body.translated_text: 'Blessed One, when this teaching was proclaimed, two hundred <s>devaputras</s> in that assembly attained <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (patience with the non-arising of dharmas). But I was left without eloquence. For this reason... I am unable.'

body.text: tato bhagavālliṃcchavikumāraṃ prabhāvyūhamāmantrayate sma- "prabhāvyūha,..... gaccha" / prabhāvyūho 'pyavocat- "bhagavan,..... notsahe..... /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the <s>Licchavi</s> youth <s>Prabhāvyūha</s>: '<s>Prabhāvyūha</s>,... go.' <s>Prabhāvyūha</s> also said: 'Blessed One,... I am unable...

body.text: "ekasmin samaye vaiśālyā mahānagaryā nirgato 'haṃ licchaviṃvimalakīrtim praviśantaṃ samāgamam / sa māmabhivādya, (tam) etadavādiṣam- 'gṛhapate, kuta āgataḥ?' sa māmabravīt- 'āgato bodhimaṇḍāt' / tamabravam- 'tadvodhimaṇḍannāma kimadhivacanam?' -sa māmetadavocat- 'kulaputra, bodhimaṇḍannāmatadhyakṛtrimakāraṇādāśayamaṇḍam, vyāpārakarmottāraṇakāraṇāttad hi yogamaṇḍam, viśeṣādhigamakāraṇāttad hyadhyāśaya maṇḍam, samavismāraṇakāraṇāttad hi bodhicittamaṇḍam /
body.translated_text: 'On one occasion, as I was going out of the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, I met the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> entering. He greeted me, and I said to him: "Householder, where have you come from?" He replied: "I have come from the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening)." I said: "What does this term <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> refer to?" He said to me: "Son of good family, the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> is the seat of intention, because of the cause of direct and uncreated action; it is the seat of <s>yoga</s> (practice), because of the cause of transcending the workings of <s>karma</s>; it is the seat of higher intention, because of the cause of special attainment; it is the seat of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the awakening mind), because of the cause of even recollection.

body.text: "'vipākāpratikāṅkṣaṇatākāraṇāttad hi dānamaṇḍam; tacchīlamaṇḍaṃ praṇidhānaparipūraṇāt; sarvasattveṣu pratighacittābhāvena kṣāntimaṇḍam; avinivartanīyakāraṇādvīryamaṇḍam; cittakarmaṇyatākāraṇād dhyānamaṇḍam; pratyakṣadarśanāt prajñāmaṇḍam /
body.translated_text: '"It is the seat of generosity (<s>dāna</s>), because of not expecting the ripening of results; it is the seat of moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>), because of the fulfillment of vows; it is the seat of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), because of the absence of a mind of hostility toward all beings; it is the seat of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), because of being irreversible; it is the seat of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), because of the workability of the mind; it is the seat of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), because of direct seeing.

body.text: "'sarvasattveṣu samacittakāraṇānmaitrīmaṇḍam; sarvopakramasahanakāraṇāt karuṇāmaṇḍam; dharmānandābhiratyadhimuktikāraṇānmuditāmaṇdam; anunaya pratighapratinisargāt tadhyupekṣāmaṇḍam /
body.translated_text: '"It is the seat of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), because of an equal mind toward all beings; it is the seat of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), because of bearing all adversities; it is the seat of sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), because of devotion to the bliss and delight of <s>Dharma</s>; it is the seat of equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), because of the abandonment of both attraction and aversion.

body.text: "ṣaḍabhijña (-prātpyā)'bhijñāmaṇḍam, nirvikalpādvimokṣamaṇḍam, sattvaparipācanādupāyāmaṇḍam, sarvasattvasaṃgrahakāraṇātsaṃgrahavastumaṇḍam, pratipattisākhyāpārācchravaṇamaṇḍam, yoniśaḥ pratyavekṣaṇānnidhyaptimaṇḍam, saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaprahāṇakāraṇādvodhipākṣipākṣikadharmamaṇḍam, sarvalokāvaṃcanātsatyamaṇḍam, avidyāsravakṣayājjarāmaraṇaṃ yāvadāsravakṣayakāraṇāt pratītyasamutpādamaṇḍam, yathābhūtamabhisambodhikāraṇātsarvakleśapraśamamaṇḍam /
body.translated_text: '"It is the seat of the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), through attaining the six superknowledges; it is the seat of liberation (<s>vimokṣa</s>), through non-conceptual thought; it is the seat of skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), through the ripening of beings; it is the seat of the means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), through gathering all beings; it is the seat of learning, through the completion of the practice of realization; it is the seat of reflection (<s>nidhyapti</s>), through careful examination with proper attention; it is the seat of the <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipākṣika dharma</s>), through the abandonment of the conditioned and the unconditioned; it is the seat of truth (<s>satya</s>), through not deceiving the entire world; it is the seat of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), because from the exhaustion of ignorance and the <s>āśravas</s> through aging and death, up to the exhaustion of the <s>āśravas</s>; it is the seat of the pacification of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), through realizing things as they truly are.

body.text: "sarvasattvaniḥsvabhāvāt tadhi sarvasattvamaṇḍam, śūnyatābhisambodhikāraṇāttad hi sarvadharmamaṇḍam, acalakāraṇātsarvamārapramardanamaṇḍam, praveśaviyogāttraidhātukamaṇḍam, abhayāsantrāsakāraṇāt siṃhanādanādino vīryamaṇḍam, sarvatrāninditakāraṇāttad hi sarvabalavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmamaṇḍam, kleśāśeṣakāraṇāttraividyatāmaṇḍam, sarvajñajñānasamudāgamāt tadhyekacittakṣaṇe sarvadharmaniravaśeṣādhigamamaṇḍam /
body.translated_text: '"It is the seat of all beings, because all beings are without own-nature; it is the seat of all <s>dharmas</s>, through the realization of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness); it is the seat of the crushing of all <s>Māras</s>, because of being unshakeable; it is the seat of the three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>), through the disjunction from entry; it is the seat of the lion's roar of fearlessness, through the vigor of one who is without fear and terror; it is the seat of the powers, fearlessnesses, and unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> (<s>āveṇika</s>), through being blameless everywhere; it is the seat of the triple knowledge (<s>traividyatā</s>), because of the complete exhaustion of <s>kleśas</s>; it is the seat of the realization of all <s>dharmas</s> without remainder in a single moment of mind, through the attainment of <s>sarvajñajñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge).

body.text: "'yāvattathā hi, kulaputra, bodhisattvāḥ pāramitāsamanvāgatāḥ, sattvaparipācanasamarpitāḥ, saddharmādhāraṇapratisaṃyutāḥ (tādṛśānāṃ) kuśalamūlasahagatānāṃ sarvāṇi pādaniḥkṣepaṇotkṣepaṇāni, bodhimaṇḍādāgatānī, buddhadharmebhya āgatāni, buddhadharmeṣu pratiṣṭhitāni' /
body.translated_text: '"Thus, son of good family, <s>bodhisattvas</s> endowed with the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), devoted to the ripening of beings, connected with the maintenance of the true <s>Dharma</s> — for such ones, accompanied by roots of merit, all their footsteps, both lifting and placing, come from the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>, come from the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, and are established in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>."'

body.text: "bhagavan, asminnirdeśe deśite, devamanuṣyāṇāṃ pañcaśatamātreṇa bodhicitta utpādite, ahaṃ tu tato 'pagatapratibhāno 'bhūvam / etasmāt.....notsahe" /
body.translated_text: 'Blessed One, when this teaching was expounded, five hundred gods and humans generated <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), but I was left without eloquence. For this reason... I am unable.'

body.text: atha bhagavān bodhisattvaṃ jagatīṃdharamāmantrayate sma- "jagatīṃdhara,.....gaccha" / -jagartīdharastvavocat- "bhagavan,.....notsahe..... /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Jagatīṃdhara</s>: '<s>Jagatīṃdhara</s>,... go.' <s>Jagatīṃdhara</s> said: 'Blessed One,... I am unable...

body.text: "ekasmin samaye svasthāne sthitikāle yenāhaṃ, māraḥ pāpīmānapsarasāṃ dvādaśasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ śakrasya veṣeṇa tūryañca saṅgītimupādāya, tenopasaṃkramya mama pādau śirasābhivandya, sa saparivāro mām puraskṛtavānekānte 'sthāt /
body.translated_text: 'On one occasion, while I was dwelling in my own place, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, surrounded by twelve thousand <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs), in the guise of <s>Śakra</s>, accompanied by music and song, approached and, bowing at my feet with his head, stood before me respectfully with his retinue to one side.

body.text: "tantu śakram devendraṃ cintayamānastametadavacam- 'kauśika, tubhyaṃ svāgatam / sarvakāmaraseṣvapramādaṃ kuru / kāyajīvabhogāt sārādānānityatāsaṃkalpaṃ bahulīkuru' /
body.translated_text: 'Thinking him to be <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, I said to him: "<s>Kauśika</s>, welcome! Be heedful amidst all the pleasures of desire! Cultivate frequently the perception of impermanence by extracting the essence from the body, life, and possessions."

body.text: "atha sa māmetadavādīt- 'satpuruṣa, imāni dvādaśasahasrāṇyapsarasām madgṛhāṇa ca imāstava parivāraṃ kurva-' iti vadati sma / tamevam- 'kauśika, ayogyavastu śramaṇāya śākyaputrāya mā dāḥ / tadhyasmabhyamayogyam' ityavadam / tasyāṃ kathāyāṃ kathitāyām, sa licchavirvimalakīrtirupasaṃkramya, māmevam- 'kulaputra, asmiñśakra evaṃ saṃjñāmmotpādaya / ayaṃ hi māraḥ pāpīmān / tvayi viḍambanārthamāgataḥ, (sa) śakro nāstī'- tyavadīt /
body.translated_text: 'Then he said to me: "Good sir, accept these twelve thousand <s>apsarases</s> from me, and make them your attendants." I said: "<s>Kauśika</s>, do not give such an unsuitable thing to an ascetic, a son of the <s>Śākyas</s>! That is not proper for us." While this conversation was taking place, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> approached and said to me: "Son of good family, do not think of this one as <s>Śakra</s>! This is <s>Māra</s> the Evil One; he has come to mock you. He is not <s>Śakra</s>."

body.text: "atha licchavirvimalakīrtistaṃ māraṃ pāpīmantamevam- 'māra pāpīman imā apsarasaḥ śramaṇāya śākyaputrāyāyogyāḥ; tena mahyaṃ tāḥ prayacche'- tyavocat / tato mārasya pāpīmato bhayabhītasya saṃvignasya- 'ayaṃ licchavirvimalakīrtirmadvañcanāyā āgacchatī'-tya (bhūt) / antardhānaṃ kartukāmaḥ so 'samarthaḥ; sarvarddhividhīrdarśayitvā, punarantardhānasyāsamartho 'bhūt /
body.translated_text: 'Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to <s>Māra</s> the Evil One: "<s>Māra</s>, Evil One, these <s>apsarases</s> are unsuitable for an ascetic, a son of the <s>Śākyas</s>; therefore, give them to me!" Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One became frightened and alarmed, thinking: "This <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> has come to deceive me!" Wishing to disappear, he was unable; even after displaying all his magical powers, he was still unable to vanish.

body.text: "athāntarīkṣād ghoṣoniścarati sma- 'pāpīman, imā apsaraso 'smai satpuruṣāyopanāmaya, purataśca svasthānaṃ gantuṃ śakṣyasi' / -tato māraḥ pāpīmān bhayabhīto 'nākāṅkṣamāṇastathā tā apsarasa upanāmayati sma /
body.translated_text: 'Then a voice resounded from the sky: "Evil One, give these <s>apsarases</s> to this good man, and only then will you be able to return to your own abode!" Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, frightened and unwilling, gave the <s>apsarases</s> to him.

body.text: "atha vimalakīrtistā apsarasaḥ pratigṛhya tā etadabravīt- 'yūyam pāpīmatā mahyaṃ dattāḥ; tenānuttarasamyaksambodhicittamutpādayata' / sa tābhyo bodhiparipākāvahānulomikābh kathāmakārṣīt; tāśca bodhicittamutpādayanti sma / tataḥ sa punastāsu- 'yūyametarhi bodhicittamutpādya, ito dharmasammode hṛṣṭādhimokṣayata, kāme (ṣu) ca hṛṣṭā mādhimokṣayate ' tyājñāpayati sma / tā abruvan- 'sā dharmasammodaratiḥ kim?'
body.translated_text: 'Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, having received those <s>apsarases</s>, said to them: "You have been given to me by the Evil One; therefore, generate the mind of <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening)." He spoke to them a discourse conducive to the ripening of awakening, and they generated <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). Then he further instructed them: "You have now generated <s>bodhicitta</s>; henceforth take delight in the joy of the <s>Dharma</s>, and do not take delight in desires." They asked: "What is this delight in the joy of the <s>Dharma</s>?"'

body.text: "so 'bravīt- '(sā) ratirbuddhe 'bhedyaśraddhā, dharmaśravaṇachando ratiḥ, saṅghaparyupāsane ratiḥ, nirmāṇatā ca gurusatkāre ratiḥ, dhātusamudaye ca viṣayāsthāne ca ratiḥ ghātakopamaskandhaprekṣaṇe ratiḥ, sarpaviṣamadhātuprekṣaṇe, śūnyagrāmanibheṣvāyataneṣu vivekaratiḥ, bodhicittasaṃrakṣe sattvahitaṅkararatiḥ, dānasaṃvibhāge śīlāsraṃsaneratiḥ, kṣāntyāṃ kṣamaṇadame, vīrye kalyāṇasampratipattyāṃ, dhyānaparibhoge ca prajñāyām kleśanirābhāse ca bodhyāmudāraratiḥ, māranigraharatiḥ, kleśasaṃvadhe buddhakṣetraviśodhane, lakṣaṇānuvyañjanasamutthāpanatārthaṃ sarvakuśalasannicaye, gambhīradharmaśravaṇātrāsaratiḥ, triṣu vimokṣamukheṣu paricayakaraṇe nirvāṇādhyālambane bodhimaṇḍālaṅkāre cākālaprāptyai nirvyāpāre ca sabhāgajanāya sevane cāsabhāgeṣvadveṣe cāpratighe ratiḥ, kalyāṇamitrebhyaḥ sevane, pāpamitravivarjane ca dharme cādhimuktiḥ, sā śraddhā, prāmodyaratiśropāyasaṃgraharatiścāpramāde bodhipakṣayadharmaniṣevaṇe ca ratiḥ / evaṃ hi bodhisattvadharmasammodābhiradhimuktiḥ' /
body.translated_text: He said: 'That delight consists of unbreakable faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, delight in hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, delight in attending upon the <s>Saṅgha</s>, delight in humility and respect for teachers, delight in the arising of the elements and disengagement from sense-objects, delight in contemplating the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) as like a murderer, delight in contemplating the elements (<s>dhātu</s>) as like a venomous serpent, delight in solitude regarding the sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) as like an empty village, delight in guarding the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) and acting for the welfare of beings, delight in sharing through generosity and not falling from moral discipline, delight in patience, forbearance, and self-control, delight in vigor and excellent practice, delight in the enjoyment of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and in wisdom the dispelling of afflictions, and exalted delight in awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), delight in subduing <s>Māra</s>, delight in purifying the <s>Buddha</s>-field, delight in accumulating all wholesome deeds for the sake of developing the marks and secondary characteristics, delight in hearing the profound <s>Dharma</s> without fear, delight in cultivating the three doors of liberation and in taking <s>nirvāṇa</s> as support while adorning the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>) without attaining it prematurely, delight in being free from contention, in associating with like-minded people, in not hating the unlike-minded, and in absence of hostility, delight in attending good spiritual friends and avoiding bad companions, and faith in the <s>Dharma</s> — that is the joy, delight, and commitment to skillful means in diligence and the cultivation of the factors of awakening. Such is the aspiration for the delight in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>-joy.'

body.text:
"atha māraḥ pāpīmāṃstā apsarasa etadabravīt- 'idānīmasmākamāvāsaṃ gacchata / -tā abruvan- 'tvayā vayamasmai gṛhapate dattāḥ; tena sābhprataṃ dharmasammodābhiratyadhimuktiḥ karaṇīyā kāme (ṣu) tvabhiratyadhimuktirakaraṇīyā / tato māraḥ pāpīmālliṃcchavi vimalakīrtimetadavocat- 'yadi bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvasvaparityāgī ca cittagrāhako nāsti, gṛhapate, imā apsarasāḥ preṣaya' / vimalakīrtirabravīt- 'imāḥ preṣyāḥ; tena pāpīman saparivāro 'pagaccha / sarvasattvadharmāśayaḥ paripūryatām' / atha tā apsaraso vimalakīrtaye 'bhivandanaṃ kṛtvā, etadavadan- 'gṛhapate, kathamasmābhirmārasthāne viharitavyam? "avocat- 'bhaginyaḥ, astyakṣayapradipo nāma dharmamukham / tena pratipadyata / tadapi, bhaginyaḥ, kim? yadidam-yadyapyekapradīpāt pradīpānāṃ śatasahasrāṇi prajvālitāni, sa pradipa'pacayanna gacchati / evameva,bhaginyaḥ, ekabodhisattvaḥ sattvānāṃ bahuśatasahasrāṇi bodhyāṃ sthāpayitvā, sa bodhisattvo 'napacayacittasmṛtiḥ, paryanapacaya uparivardhate / tathā ca sarvakusahaladharmā yathā yathānyebhyeḥ paribhāvitāś cākhyātāḥ, śāsanaṃ tathā tathā sarvakuśaladharmairvivardhate / tadhyakṣayapradīpo nāma dharma mukham / tasmin mārasthāne viharamāṇā apramānṇadevaputradevakanyānāṃ bodhicittamadhimucyadhvam / evaṃ hi syāta tathāgatakṛtajñāḥ, sarvasattvopajīvyāḥ ' / tatastā apsaraso licchavervimalakirteḥ pādau śirasābhivandya, māreṇa saha pratyagacchan / bhagavan, licchavervimalakīrtestadvikurvaṇaviśeṣaṇaṃ dṛstvā, etasmāt ........notsahe" / atha bhagavaṃśresthiputraṃ sudattam āmantrayate sma- "kulaputra. ...... gaccha " / sudattaḥ punaravocat- "bhagavan, ..... notsahe .... / " ekasmin samaye mām matpitṛniveśane mahāyajñakaraṇārthāya sarvaśramaṇabrāhmaṇebhyaḥ sarva daridraduḥkhitakṛpaṇavanīyakavihvalībhūtebhyaḥ saptadivasaṃ dānaṃ dadaṃ, tasmin mahāyajñakaraṇe 'ntimadivase licchavirvimalakīrtistāmmahāyajñabhūmimupasaṃkramya,
etadavadīt- 'śresthiputra, yathā tvaṃ yajñaṃ karoṣi tathā hi yajñaṃ mā kuruḥ, dharma yajñaṃ kuru / alaṃ ta āmiṣayajñena / tametadavadam - taddharmayajñaṃ kathaṃ deyam? '
body.translated_text:
Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One said to those <s>apsaras</s>: 'Now return to our abode.' They replied: 'You gave us to this householder; therefore, we should cultivate aspiration for the delight in the <s>Dharma</s>-joy, and should not cultivate delight in sensual pleasures.' Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One said to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: 'If the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> relinquishes all possessions and has no mental attachment, householder, send back these <s>apsaras</s>.' <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said: 'They are sent back. O Evil One, depart with your retinue! May the <s>Dharma</s>-aspiration of all beings be fulfilled.' Then those <s>apsaras</s>, having paid homage to <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, said: 'Householder, how should we conduct ourselves in <s>Māra</s>'s realm?' He said: 'Sisters, there is a <s>Dharma</s>-door called the Inexhaustible Lamp (<s>Akṣayapradīpa</s>). Practice accordingly. And what is it, sisters? Just as from one lamp, hundreds of thousands of lamps may be lit, yet that lamp does not diminish — even so, sisters, one <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having established many hundreds of thousands of beings in awakening, that <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mindfulness does not diminish but increases further. And likewise, however much all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are cultivated and taught to others, the teaching increases in all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. That is the <s>Dharma</s>-door called the Inexhaustible Lamp. While dwelling in <s>Māra</s>'s realm, inspire immeasurable gods and goddesses with the mind of awakening. Thus you will show gratitude to the <s>Tathāgata</s> and become a refuge for all beings.' Then those <s>apsaras</s>, bowing at the feet of the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, departed with <s>Māra</s>. Blessed One, having witnessed such a miraculous display of the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, for this reason... I am not able.' Then the Blessed One addressed the merchant's son <s>Sudatta</s>: 'Son of good family, ... go.' <s>Sudatta</s> also said: 'Blessed One, ... I am not able...'
'One time, in my father's house, for the purpose of performing a great sacrifice, I was giving gifts for seven days to all ascetics and brahmins, to all the poor, suffering, wretched, destitute, and distressed. On the last day of that great sacrifice, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> approached that great sacrificial ground and said: "Merchant's son, you should not perform the sacrifice as you are performing it. Perform a <s>Dharma</s>-sacrifice! Enough of this material sacrifice!" I asked him: "How should the <s>Dharma</s>-sacrifice be given?"

body.text: "sa māmabravīt- 'yena kena dharma yajñenāpūrvamacaramaṃ sattvā paripacyante, tadhi dharma yajñam / tadapi kiṃ? yaduta- bodhivyupahārasya mahāmaitri, saddharmasaṃgraheṇābhinirhṛtā mahākaruṇā, sarvasattvaprāmodyapalambhenābhinirhṛtā mahāmuditā, jñānasaṃgraheṇābhinirhṛtā mahopekṣā-
body.translated_text: He said to me: 'A <s>Dharma</s>-sacrifice is that by which beings are matured without beginning or end. And what is it? Namely: great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>) accomplished through the offering of awakening; great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) accomplished through the gathering of the true <s>Dharma</s>; great sympathetic joy (<s>mahāmuditā</s>) accomplished through bringing delight to all beings; great equanimity (<s>mahopekṣā</s>) accomplished through the gathering of knowledge —

body.text: ' 'śāntidamenābhinirhṛtā dānapāramitā, duḥśīlasattvaparipācanenābhinirhrritā śīlapāramitā, nairatmyadharmeṇābhinirhṛtā kṣāntipāramitā, bodhyārambheṇābhinirhṛtā vīryapāramitā, kāyacittavivekenābhinirhṛtā dhyānapāramitā, sarvajñajñānenābhinirhṛtā prajñāpāramitā- " ' sarvasattvaparipācanenābhinirhṛtā śūnyatābhāvanā, saṃskṛtapariśodhanenābhinirhṛtānimittabhāvanā, saṃcityopapattyābhinirhṛtāpraṇihitabhāvanā-
body.translated_text: 'The perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) accomplished through peace and self-control; the perfection of moral discipline (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) accomplished through maturing beings of poor conduct; the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) accomplished through the doctrine of non-self; the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) accomplished through undertaking awakening; the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) accomplished through seclusion of body and mind; the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) accomplished through the knowledge of omniscience — the cultivation of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) accomplished through maturing all beings; the cultivation of signlessness (<s>animitta</s>) accomplished through purifying the conditioned; the cultivation of wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>) accomplished through deliberately taking rebirth —

body.text: "' saddharmaparyudgrahaṇenābhinirhṛto balaparākramaḥ, saṃgrahavastunābhinirhṛtaṃ jīvitendriyam, sarvasattvabhṛtyaśiṣyabhavenabhinirhṛtā nirmāṇatā, asarātsāropādānenābhinirhṛtaḥ kāyajīvabhogalābhāḥ, ṣaḍanusmṛtyābhinirhṛta smṛtiḥ, saṃmodanīyadharmeṇābhinirhṛta āśayaḥ, sampratipatyābhinirhṛtājīvapariśuddhiḥ, śraddhāprāmodyasevanenābhinirhṛtamāryaparyupāsanam, anāryāpratighenābhirhṛto 'dhyāśayaḥ, pratipatyābhinirhṛtaṃ śravaṇakauśalyam, araṇādharmāvabodhenābhinirhṛta āraṇyāvāsaḥ, buddhajñānapratilābhenābhinirhṛtaṃ pratisaṃlayanam, sarvasattvakleśavimuktiyogenābhinirhṛtā yogācārābhūmiḥ-
body.translated_text: 'Strength and power accomplished through upholding the true <s>Dharma</s>; the life-faculty accomplished through the means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>); humility accomplished through becoming a servant and disciple to all beings; gains of body, livelihood, and enjoyment accomplished through extracting the essential from the unessential; mindfulness accomplished through the six recollections (<s>ṣaḍanusmṛti</s>); intention accomplished through the <s>Dharma</s> of delight; purity of livelihood accomplished through right practice; noble attendance accomplished through the cultivation of faith and joy; higher intention accomplished through non-hostility toward the ignoble; skill in learning accomplished through practice; forest-dwelling accomplished through understanding the <s>Dharma</s> of non-conflict; meditative seclusion accomplished through attaining <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge; the ground of yogic practice accomplished through the effort to liberate all beings from afflictions —

body.text: "'lakṣaṇānuvyañjanabuddhakṣetrālaṅkārasattvaparipācananenābhinirhṛtaḥ puṇyasambhāra, sarvadharmeṣvanupādeyāheyaikanayajñānenābhinirhṛtaḥ prajñāsambhāraḥ, sarvakleśāvaraṇākuśaladharmaprahāṇenābhinirhritaḥ sarvakuśalamūla sambhāraḥ, sarvajñajñānādhigamena ca kuśaladharmeṇa cābhinirhṛtaḥ sarvabodhipakṣadharmasamutpādaḥ- tadhi, kulaputra, dharmayajñam / tasmin dharmayajñe pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo yajñadāyakaḥ, yajñasukāraka, sadevake loke bhavati dakṣiṇīyaḥ ' /
body.translated_text: 'The accumulation of merit accomplished through maturing beings and adorning the <s>Buddha</s>-field with marks and secondary characteristics; the accumulation of wisdom accomplished through the knowledge of the one method of neither grasping nor rejecting all <s>dharmas</s>; the accumulation of all roots of merit accomplished through abandoning all afflictive obscurations and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>; the production of all factors conducive to awakening accomplished through the attainment of omniscient knowledge and wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — that, son of good family, is the <s>Dharma</s>-sacrifice. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is established in that <s>Dharma</s>-sacrifice is a sacrifice-giver, a well-performer of sacrifice, and is worthy of offerings in the world with its gods.'

body.text: " bhagavan, tasmin gṛhapatāvimamevaṃnirdeśaṃ deśitavati, tasyā brāhmaṇa pariṣado brāhmaṇānāṃ dviśatānāmanuttarasamyaksambodhicittamutpannam /
body.translated_text: Blessed One, when that householder had taught this very discourse, from that assembly of brahmins, two hundred brahmins generated the mind of supreme, perfect awakening.

body.text: "ahamapi śrāddha āścaryaprāptaḥ satpuruṣasya pādāvabhivandya,matkaṇṭhādavatārya śatasahasramūlyaṃ muktāhāramanuprayacchāmi sma / sa na pratīcchati sma / atha khalvahametadavocam- ' pratigṛhāṇa tvamim muktāhāraṃ, yaṃ cādhimucyase tasmai dehī' ti / sa taṃ muktāhāraṃ pratigṛhya ca dvau pratyaṃśau kṛtvā caikaṃ pratyaṃśaṃ tasmin yajñasthāne sarvalokaninditebhyo nagaradaridrebhyo dadāti sma; dvitiyaṃ pratyaṃśaṃ duṣprasahāya tathāgatāya niryātayāmāsa / evam rūpaṃ prātihāryaṃ darśayati sma, yathā sarvābhiḥ parṣadbhirmarīcirnāma lokadhāturduṣprasaho nāma tathāgataśca dṛśyete sma / sa ca muktahāra stasya duṣprasahasya tathāgatasya murdhnimuktāhārkūṭāgāraḥ saṃsthito 'bhūccaturasraścatuḥsthūṇaḥ samabhāgaḥ suvibhakto darśanīyo vicitraḥ /
body.translated_text: I too, filled with faith and struck with wonder, bowed at the feet of the good man, and removing from my neck a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand, I offered it to him. He did not accept it. Then I said: 'Accept this pearl necklace, and give it to whomever you wish.' He accepted the pearl necklace and divided it into two portions: one portion he gave to the most despised poor people of the city at that sacrificial ground; the second portion he offered to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Duṣprasaha</s> (Hard to Conquer). He displayed such a marvel that all the assemblies could see the world-realm called <s>Marīci</s> and the <s>Tathāgata</s> called <s>Duṣprasaha</s>. And that pearl necklace stood upon the head of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Duṣprasaha</s> as a pavilion of pearls — four-cornered, with four pillars, well-proportioned, beautifully divided, lovely, and variegated.

body.text: "sa evaṃ rūpaṃ prātihāryaṃ darśayya, vacanametadavocat- "' dāyako yo dānapatiryathā tathāgataṃ, tathā nagaradaridrān dakṣiṇīyān sañjānāti cāsaṃbhinnaṃ samamahākaruṇācittena vipākapratikāṅkṣī parityāgī, sa hi dharma yajña pariniṣpanna ' iti /
body.translated_text: Having displayed such a marvel, he spoke these words: 'A donor, a lord of giving, who regards the poor of the city as worthy of offerings just as the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who gives with an undivided mind of equal great compassion without expecting results — such a one has truly accomplished the <s>Dharma</s>-sacrifice.'

body.text: "atha te nagaradaridrās tat prātihāryaṃ dṛṣtvā, taṃ dharmopadeśamapi śrutvā, anuttarasamyaksambodhicittamutpādayanti sma / bhagavan, etasmāt kāraṇāttasya satpuruṣasya rogapṛcchanagamannotsahe " /
body.translated_text: Then those poor people of the city, having seen that miracle and having heard that <s>Dharma</s> discourse, generated the mind of supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhicitta</s>). Blessed One, for this reason I am not able to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

body.text: tathā hi sarve te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā api, yā tena satpuruṣeṇa sahāvakāśakathā" ye nanopadeśā uktāḥ tatsarvaṃ deśayanto gamannotsahante sma /
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, all those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> too, recounting all the discussions and instructions that had been spoken by that good man, were not able to go.

body.text: śrāvakabodhisattvapreṣaṇoktasya parivartastṛtīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: End of the third chapter, entitled 'The Dispatching of <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Bodhisattva</s> Disciples.'

body.text: 4 glānasaṃmodana (kathā)
body.translated_text: 4. Consolation of the Sick (<s>Glānasaṃmodana</s>)

body.text: tato bhagavān maṃjuśrīm kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma- "maṃjuśrīḥ, licchavervimalakīrte rogapṛcchanāya gaccha" / maṃjuśrīrapyavocat-
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful prince: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, go to inquire about the illness of the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>.' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> also said:

body.text: "bhagavan, licchavirvimalakīrtirdurāsado gambhīranaye pratibhānapratipannaḥ, vyatyastapadapuṣkalapadaniṣpādanakuśalaḥ, anācchedyapratibhānassarvasattveṣvapratihatabuddhisamarpitaḥ, sarvabodhisattvakarmaniryātaḥ, sarvabodhisattvapratyekabuddhaguhyasthāne supratipannassarvamārasthānavinivartakuśalaḥ, mahābhijñāvikrīḍita upāyaprajñāniryāto 'dvayadharmadhātvasaṃbhedagocarasya varāgraprāpto dharmadhātvekavyūhānantākāravyūhadharmadeśanākovidaḥ, sarvasattvendriyasamprāpakavyūhajño vicakṣaṇaḥ, upāyakauśalyagatigataḥ praśnanirṇayapratilabdhaḥ / sa parīttavarmasannāhasantoṣasyāsamarthaḥ, ki tu buddhādhiṣṭhānena tena gato yathābhūtaṃ yathānubhāvaṃ bhāṣitukāmo('smi)" /
body.translated_text: 'Blessed One, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> is difficult to approach — endowed with eloquence in the profound method, skilled in producing abundant and inversive phrases, possessed of inexhaustible eloquence, endowed with unobstructed intellect toward all beings, accomplished in all the activities of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, well-versed in the secret abode of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, skilled in turning back all the positions of <s>Māra</s>, one who sports with the great superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), who has gone forth through skillful means and wisdom (<s>upāyaprajñā</s>), who has attained the supreme excellence in the domain of non-dual <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) without division, expert in teaching the <s>Dharma</s> through the single array of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> in infinite modes and forms, discerning and skilled in knowing the array that reaches the faculties of all beings, one who has attained the resolution of all questions through skillful means. He is not content with donning a small armor of resolve. Nevertheless, by the <s>Buddha</s>'s power I will go to him, wishing to speak as it truly is and according to his might.'

body.text: atha tasyām pariṣadi teṣāṃ bodhisattvamahāśrāvakaśakrabrahmalokapālānāṃ ca devaputrāpsarasāmetabhūt- "(yatra) maṃjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaścā satpuruṣastāvubhāvabhilāpinau, tatra mahādharmakīrtikathā niyataṃ bhaviṣyatī" -ti / tato bodhisattvānāṃ lakṣaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃca pañcaśatamātraṃ bahuśakrabrahmalokapālāśca bahuśatasahasrāṇī devaputrāṇāṃca dharmaśravaṇārthaṃ maṃjuśriyaḥ kumārabhūtasya pṛṣṭhito 'gacchan / atha maṃjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ sarvaistairbodhisattvamahāśrāvakaśakrabrahmalokapāladevaputraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto vaiśālīmmahānagarīm praviśati sma /
body.translated_text: Then in that assembly, the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, great <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, world-protectors, <s>devaputras</s>, and <s>apsarases</s> had this thought: 'Where <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful prince, and that good man are — those two eloquent speakers — there will surely be a great proclamation of the <s>Dharma</s>.' Then a hundred thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s>, a mere five hundred <s>śrāvakas</s>, many <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, and world-protectors, and many hundreds of thousands of <s>devaputras</s> followed behind <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful prince, for the purpose of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful prince, surrounded and attended by all those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, great <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, world-protectors, and <s>devaputras</s>, entered the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>.

body.text: tato licchaveivimalakīrteretadabhūta- "maṃjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaśca bahuparivāra āgacchanti; tenedamme gṛhamadhiṣṭhā(-nena) śūnyaṃ (bhavatv)-" iti / (tataḥ) tadgṛhaṃ śūnyaṃ adhyatiṣṭhat / tatra dvāriko 'pi nābhavat / maṃco yasmin vimalakīrtiglānaḥ śāyī, āsīdekāsanam / taṃ sthāpayitvā tatra maṃco vā pīṭhikā vāsanaṃ kiñcinnādṛśyata /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> had this thought: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful prince, is coming with a great retinue; let this house of mine become empty by his supernatural power.' Then he made that house stand empty. Not even a doorkeeper was there. The couch upon which the sick <s>Vimalakīrti</s> lay — that was the only seat. Apart from that, no couch, stool, or seat was seen there.

body.text: atha maṃjuśrīḥ saparivāro yena vimalakīrterāvāsastenāgacchat; upasaṃkramya ca praviśya, tadgṛhaṃ śūnyamadrākṣīt / tatra dvāriko 'pi nābhavat / tasmāt, (yasmin) vimalakīrtiḥ śāyyāsīt, ekākimaṃcāganyamañcaṃ pīṭhikaṃ vāsanaṃ vā nādrākṣīt / tato licchavirvimalakīrtirmajuśriyam kumārabhūtamadarśat; dṛṣṭvaidavocat- "maṃjuśrīḥ, ehi svāgataḥ, maṃjuśrīḥ, ehi susvāgataḥ / pūrvamanāgato 'dṛṣṭo 'śruto dṛśyase" / maṃjuśrīrabravīt- "gṛhapate, yathā vadasi tathā yadāgatam, tadhi punarnāgacchati / yad gataṃ tadapi punarna gacchati / tat kasya hetoḥ? anāgata āgamo 'pi na prajñāyate, gate 'pi gamananna prajñāyate, yatkāraṇād yaddṛṣṭam, tat punarapi draṣṭavyannāsti /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s> with his retinue came to the dwelling of <s>Vimalakīrti</s>. Having approached and entered, he saw that house was empty. Not even a doorkeeper was there. Except for the single couch upon which <s>Vimalakīrti</s> lay, he saw no other couch, stool, or seat. Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> saw <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful prince, and having seen him, said: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, welcome! <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, well come! You who previously had not come, had not been seen, had not been heard — now you are seen.' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Householder, it is as you say. What has come does not come again. What has gone does not go again. Why is that? In what has not come, coming too is not discerned; in what has gone, going too is not discerned. And what has been seen — that again is not to be seen.

body.text: "kaccitte, satpuruṣa, kṣamaṇīyaṃ, kaccid yāpanīyaṃ, kaccitte dhāvato na kṣubhyante, kaccid duḥkhā vedanāḥ pratikrāmanti nābhikrāmanti? bhagavānapi - 'nanu tubhyamalpābādhatā, alpātaṃkatā, alpāturaḥ laghūttthānatāpi, yātrābalasukhānavadya (-tā-) sukhasparśavihāra(-te-)' tyakhyat / gṛhapate, ayaṃ te rogaḥ kasmādutpannaḥ? utpannaḥ kiyacciraṃ? kimāśritaḥ? kadā śāmyati?"
body.translated_text: 'Is it bearable for you, good man? Is it manageable? Are your bodily constituents not disturbed? Are painful sensations diminishing and not increasing? The Blessed One too said: "Surely you have little affliction, little ailment, little sickness; you rise easily, and your state is comfortable, with pleasant bodily sensations." Householder, from what has this illness of yours arisen? How long has it been since it arose? On what does it depend? When will it be pacified?'

body.text: vimalakīrtiravocat- "maṃjuśrīḥ, avidyā ca bhavatṛṣṇa yāvat, tāvadayamme rogo 'pi / yāvat sarvasattvānāṃ rogaḥ, tāvadapi me roogaḥ / yadā sarvasattvā vītarogāḥ, tadā rogo mamāpi na sambhavati / tat kasya hetoḥ? maṃjuśrīḥ, bodhisattvasya saṃsārasthānaṃ hi sattvāḥ); rogo hi saṃsārasthānam / yadā sarvasattvā vītarogāḥ, tadā bodhisattvo 'pyarogo bhavati /
body.translated_text: <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, as long as ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) and craving for existence (<s>bhavatṛṣṇā</s>) persist, so long does this illness of mine persist. As long as the illness of all beings persists, so long does my illness also persist. When all beings are free from illness, then my illness too will not arise. Why is that? <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, for the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the abode in <s>saṃsāra</s> is indeed for the sake of beings; and illness is the abode in <s>saṃsāra</s>. When all beings are free from illness, then the <s>bodhisattva</s> too becomes free from illness.

body.text: "maṃjuśrīḥ, tadyathāpi nāma śreṣṭhina ekaputro glāno bhavet; tadvādhakāraṇādubhāvapi mātāpitarau glānau bhavataḥ / yāvatsa ekaputro 'rogo 'bhūtaḥ, tāvadubhāvapi mātāpitarau duḥkhitau bhavataḥ / maṃjuśrīḥ, evameva bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattveṣv ekaputra iva priyaḥ; sarvasattveṣu glāneṣu so 'pi glāno bhavati / sattve (-ṣv-) aroge (-ṣu), so 'pyaglānaḥ / yadapi, maṃjuśrīḥ- 'ayaṃ te rogaḥ kasmādutpanna?' iti vadasi-bodhisattvānāṃ hi rogo mahākaruṇāyāḥ sanbhavati" /
body.translated_text: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, suppose a merchant's only son were to become ill; on account of his illness, both parents would also become ill. As long as that only son has not recovered, so long both parents would be in distress. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, just so, the <s>bodhisattva</s> loves all beings as if they were his only child. When all beings are ill, he too becomes ill. When beings are well, he too is well. And, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, as to your question "From what has this illness of yours arisen?" — the illness of <s>bodhisattvas</s> arises from great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>).'

body.text: maṃjuśrīravocat- "gṛhapate, kimasmiṃste śūnyāgāre na kaścit parivāro 'sti?"-abravīt- "maṃjuśrīḥ, sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇyapi śūnyāni" / - abhāṣata- "kena śūnyāni?"-āha- "śūnyatayā śūnyāni" / -abhāṣata- "śūnyatāyāṃ śūnyam kīm?" -āha- "saṅkalpo hi śūnyatā śūnyaḥ" / -abhāṣata- "śūnyatā ki saṅkalpāyāsamarthā?" -āha- "tasmin parikalpe śūnye, śūnyatā hi śūnyatāyāṃ nirvikalpā" / -abhāṣata- "gṛhapate ' śūnyatā yatrānveṣṭuṃ (yujjate)?" -āha- "maṃjuśrīḥ, śūnyatānveṣṭuṃ (yujjate) dviṣaṣṭidṛṣṭigatebhyaḥ" / -abhāṣata- "dviṣaṣṭodṛṣṭigatāni kuto 'nveṣṭuṃ (yujyate)?" -āha- "tānyanveṣtuṃ (yujjate) tathāgatasya vimuktyāḥ" / - abhāṣata- "iyaṃ tathāgatasya vimuktiḥ kuto 'nveṣṭuṃ (yujyate)?" -āha- "anveṣṭuṃ (yujyate) sarvasattvānām prathamacittacaryāyāḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Householder, why is this empty house of yours without any attendant?' He said: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all <s>Buddha</s>-fields too are empty.' He said: 'By what are they empty?' He said: 'They are empty by emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>).' He said: 'What is empty in emptiness?' He said: 'Conceptual construction (<s>saṅkalpa</s>) is empty in emptiness.' He said: 'Is emptiness incapable of conceptual construction?' He said: 'In that conceptual construction which is empty, emptiness is indeed free from conceptual elaboration (<s>nirvikalpā</s>) in emptiness.' He said: 'Householder, where should emptiness be sought?' He said: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, emptiness should be sought among the sixty-two views.' He said: 'Where should the sixty-two views be sought?' He said: 'They should be sought in the liberation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' He said: 'Where should this liberation of the <s>Tathāgata</s> be sought?' He said: 'It should be sought in the initial mental activity of all beings.

body.text: "maṃjuśrīḥ yat 'kinte na kaścit parivāro 'stī?' -ti vadasi- sarvamārāśca sarvaparapravādinaḥ santi me parivāraḥ / tat kasya hetoḥ? mārā hi saṃsārasya varṇavādinaḥ, saṃsāraśca bodhisattvasya parivāraḥ / parapravādiṣu dṛṣṭigatānāṃ varṇavādoiṣu, bodhisattvaḥ sarvadṛṣṭigatebhyo 'niṃjyaḥ / tasmāt sarvamārāśca sarvaparapravādino mama parivāraḥ" /
body.translated_text: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, as to your question "Is there no attendant for you?" — all <s>Māras</s> and all adherents of other doctrines (<s>parapravādin</s>) are my attendants. Why is that? The <s>Māras</s> are proclaimers of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and <s>saṃsāra</s> is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s attendant. The adherents of other doctrines are proclaimers of views, and the <s>bodhisattva</s> is unmoved by all views. Therefore, all <s>Māras</s> and all adherents of other doctrines are my attendants.'

body.text: maṃjuśrīrabhāṣata- "gṛhapate, rogaste kīdṛśaḥ?" - āha- "ārupyo 'sanidarśanaḥ" / -abhāṣata- "sa rogaḥ kiṃ kāyāpratisaṃyukta āhosviccittapratisaṃyuktaḥ?" -āha- "kāyavivekatayā (sa) kāyapratisaṃyukto nāsti, cittamāyādharmatayā cittapratisaṃyukto nāsti" / -abhāṣata- "gṛhapate, eṣāṃ caturṇā, yadidam-pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśadhātūnām, ko dhāturhanyate?" -āha- "maṃjuśrīḥ, yaḥ kaśca sarvasattvānāṃ rogadhātuḥ, tenāhamapi glānaḥ / maṃjuśrīḥ, katham bodhisattvena glāno bodhisattvaḥ sammodpanīyaḥ?"
body.translated_text: <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Householder, what is your illness like?' He said: 'It is formless and imperceptible.' He said: 'Is that illness connected with the body or connected with the mind?' He said: 'It is not connected with the body, due to the separateness of the body; nor is it connected with the mind, due to the illusory nature (<s>māyādharmatā</s>) of the mind.' He said: 'Householder, of these four — the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, and space — which element is afflicted?' He said: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, whatever is the element of illness in all beings, by that I too am ill. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, how should a sick <s>bodhisattva</s> be consoled by a <s>bodhisattva</s>?'

body.text: maṃjuśrīrabhāṣata "kāyo 'nitya iti-(saṃmodapanīyaḥ), na hi nirvidvirāgena / kāyo duḥkha iti-nirvāṇarasena hi na (saṃmodapanīyaḥ) / kāyo nairātmya iti-atha ca punaḥ sattvaparipācanena (saṃmodapanīyaḥ) / kāyaḥ śānta eveti-kintūpaśamena (saṃmodapanīyo) nāsti / sarvaduścarit upanīte, saṃkrāntyā na (saṃmodapanīyaḥ) / svātureṇānyeśu glāneṣu sattve(ṣu)kāruṇyapūrvāntaparyānta duḥkhānusmṛtisattvārtha kāryānusmṛtikuśalamūlasākṣātkārādiviśuddhyatṛṣṇānityodyogaṃ samārabhya, sarvarogābhāvakāraṇabhaiṣajyarājo bhaved-iti / tathā hi bodhisattvena glāno bodhisattvaḥ saṃmodapanīyaḥ" / maṃjuśrīrabhāṣata- "kulaputra, glānena bodhisattvena kathaṃ svacittaṃ nidhyāyitavyam?"
body.translated_text: <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: "[He should be consoled thus:] 'The body is impermanent'—but not by way of disgust and dispassion. 'The body is suffering'—but not by way of [seeking] the taste of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. 'The body is without self'—yet he should be consoled by the ripening of beings. 'The body is indeed peaceful'—but not consoled by [mere] quiescence. [He should be consoled] with regard to abandoning all evil conduct, but not by transmigration. [One who is ill oneself should generate] compassion toward other sick beings, recollecting suffering of past and future, recollecting the tasks to be done for the benefit of beings, making manifest the roots of merit, and so forth—through purification, freedom from craving, and constant exertion, one should become a king of medicine who eliminates all diseases. Thus indeed should a <s>bodhisattva</s> console an ill <s>bodhisattva</s>." <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: "Son of good family, how should an ill <s>bodhisattva</s> contemplate his own mind?"

body.text: vimalakīrtirāha- "maṃjuśrīḥ, glānena bodhisattvena hi svacittamevaṃ nidhyāyitavyam-vyādhiḥ pūrvāntābhūtaviparyāsakarmaparyutthānānniśrarati / abhūtasaṃkalpakleśotpanno ya āturo nāma dharmaḥ, ta(sya) paramārthata iha na kiṃcidupalabhyate / tat kasya hetoḥ? ayaṃ kāyaścaturmahābhūtebhyo bhūtaḥ; eṣu dhātuṣu kaścadadhipatirvā janako vā nāsti / asmin kāye 'nātmake, ātmābhiniveśaṃ sthāpayitvā, iha paramārthato yo rogo nāma so 'nupalambhaḥ; tasmādātmani hyabhiniveśe 'sati, rogamūlājñāyāṃ viharitavyam-iti; tena, ātmasaṃjñāyāṃ pratiprasrabdhāyāṃ, dharmasaṃjñotpādayitavyā /
body.translated_text: <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said: "<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, an ill <s>bodhisattva</s> should contemplate his own mind thus: 'Illness arises from the uprising of perverse <s>karma</s> and unreal conceptual inversion of the past. That which is called the state of being ill, arising from false conceptualization and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)—in ultimate reality nothing whatsoever is apprehended therein.' Why? This body has arisen from the four great elements; among these elements there is no master or progenitor. In this body devoid of self, having set aside the clinging to a self, in ultimate reality that which is called illness is unapprehendable. Therefore, when there is no clinging to a self, one should abide with the understanding of the root of illness. With the perception of self having been relaxed, the perception of <s>dharmas</s> should be generated.

body.text: "ayaṃ hi kāyo 'nekadharmasaṃnipātaḥ; utpadyamāno dharmā evopadyante; nirudhyamāno dharma eva nirudhyante / dharmāḥ parasparanna vedayanti na jānanti / te dharmā utpattyāmevam- 'ahamupapadya' iti-na cintayanti; nirodha'pyevam-'ahanniridhya' iti-na cintayanti /
body.translated_text: "This body is indeed a confluence of many <s>dharmas</s>; when it arises, <s>dharmas</s> alone arise; when it ceases, <s>dharmas</s> alone cease. These <s>dharmas</s> do not experience or know one another. Those <s>dharmas</s>, upon arising, do not think 'I arise'; upon cessation too, they do not think 'I cease.'

body.text: "tena dharmasaṃjñājñākaraṇārtha cittamutpādayitavyam- 'yanmayaivaṃ dharmeṣu saṃjñāyate, tadapi viparyāsaḥ / viparyāso hi mahārogaḥ / mayā rogavisaṃyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ, vyādhiprahāṇāyodyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ' / tatra tadvyādhivarjanaṃ kim? yaduta-ahaṃkāramamakāravarjanam / tadahaṃkāramamakāravarjanaṃ kim? yaduta-devayavisaṃyogaḥ / tatrā dhyātmabahirdhāsamudācārābhāvaḥ kim? yaduta-samatāyā acalaṃ, svacalaṃ, vyacalam / "samatā kim? matsamatāyā yāvannirvāṇasamatām / tat kasya hetoḥ? yadidam-mannirvāṇayorubhayorapi śūnyatākāraṇāt / tābhubau kena śūnyau? nāmavyavahārobhau śūnyau; tasmāttāvapariniṣpannau / tathā hi tena samatādarśanena roga evānanyaḥ / śūnyatānyathākāre 'sati, roga eva śūnyatā /
body.translated_text: "For the purpose of understanding the perception of <s>dharmas</s>, one should generate the thought: 'That by which I perceive <s>dharmas</s> in this way—that too is a perversion. Perversion is a great disease. I must free myself from disease; I must strive for the abandonment of illness.' What then is the avoidance of that illness? The abandonment of ego-sense (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) and possessiveness (<s>mamakāra</s>). What is the abandonment of ego-sense and possessiveness? Freedom from the duality [of self and other]. What is the absence of both internal and external manifestation? It is the unmoving, self-moving, and all-pervading [nature] of equality (<s>samatā</s>). What is equality? The equality of self and <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Why? Because both self and <s>nirvāṇa</s> are empty by nature. By what are they both empty? They are both empty of mere verbal designation; therefore they are both unestablished. Indeed, for one who sees equality in this way, illness is not something other [than equality]. When emptiness does not become something other, illness itself is emptiness.

body.text: "vedanā nirvedana draṣṭavyā / tena vedanānirodho na sākṣātkaraṇīyaḥ / parisamāptabuddhadharma ubhe vedane utsṛjet, kiṃ tu sarvadurgatisattveṣu mahākaruṇānutthāpanannāsti; tathā hi karaṇīyaṃ, yathaiṣu sattveṣu yoniśo nidhyaptyā vyādhirnirākṛto bhavati /
body.translated_text: "Sensation (<s>vedanā</s>) should be seen as non-sensation. Yet the cessation of sensation should not be directly realized [by the <s>bodhisattva</s>]. One who has fulfilled the <s>buddha-dharmas</s> would abandon both [pleasant and painful] sensations, yet there must be no cessation of the arising of great compassion toward all beings in the lower realms of existence. Thus indeed, by properly contemplating these beings, illness is eliminated.

body.text: "eṣu (sattveṣu) kaściddharmo nopasaṃhartavyo vā nirākaraṇīyo vā / tadādhāraparijñānārtha, yasmād roga utpannaḥ, teṣu dharmo deśayitavyaḥ / sa ādhāraḥ kim? yadidam-adhyālambanam ādhāraḥ / adhyālambanādhāre yāvadālamambanam, tāvad rogādhāraḥ / kasminadhyālambanam? traidhātukādhyālambanam / adhyālambanādhāraparijñā kim? yadutanālambanaṃ cānupalabdhiḥ / yānupalabdhistadhyanadhyālanbanam / anupalabdhiḥ kim? yadidam-ātmadṛṣṭiśca paradṛṣṭiḥ-ubhe dṛṣṭī nopalabhyete / ato 'nupalabdhirnāmocyate /
body.translated_text: "Among these [beings], no <s>dharma</s> should be applied or eliminated. For the purpose of understanding the basis [of illness], the <s>Dharma</s> should be taught to those from whom illness has arisen. What is that basis? It is attachment (<s>adhyālambana</s>) as the basis. As long as there is attachment, there is a basis for illness. In what is there attachment? There is attachment to the three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>). What is the understanding of the basis of attachment? Non-attachment and non-apprehension. What is non-apprehension? It is the non-apprehension of both the view of self and the view of other—both views are not apprehended. Therefore it is called non-apprehension.

body.text: "maṃjuśrīḥ, ātureṇa tathā hi bodhisattvena jarāvyādhimaraṇajātivarjanāya svacittaṃ nidhyāyitavyam / maṃjuśrīḥ, bodhisattvānāṃroga evaṃ rūpaḥ / yadyevanna bhavet, vyavasāyo nirārthako 'bhaviṣyat / tadyathāpi nāma pratyarthikopaghātena vīro nāmocyate, evameva jarāvyādhimaraṇaduḥkhaśamanena bodhisattvo nāmocyate /
body.translated_text: "<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, thus an ill <s>bodhisattva</s> should contemplate his own mind in order to abandon old age, illness, death, and birth. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, such is the illness of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. If it were not so, their endeavor would be purposeless. Just as one who defeats an adversary is called a hero, even so, one who pacifies the suffering of old age, illness, and death is called a <s>bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: "tena glānena bodhisattvenaivaṃ - 'yathā mama rogo 'bhūto 'san, tathā hi sarvasattvānāṃ rogo 'pyabhūto 'san-' ityupalakṣitavyam / evaṃ prekṣamāṇaḥ so 'nuśaṃsadarśanābhraṣṭaḥ sattveṣu mahākaruṇāmutpādayati, (anyat) sthāpayitvā cāgantukakleśaprahāṇāya sattveṣvabhiyogamahākaruṇāmutpādayati / tat kasya hetoḥ? anuśaṃsadarśanapatitayā mahākaruṇayā hi jātiṣu bodhisattvo nirvidyate / anuśaṃsadarśanaparyutthānāpagatayā mahākaruṇā bodhisattvo jātiṣu na nirvidyate / dṛṣṭiparyutthāne samuttiṣṭhati, sa na jāyate / cittaparyutthānāpagato jāyamānaḥ sa mukta iva jāyate, sa mukta ivotpadyate / mukta iva jāyamāno mukta ivotpadyamāno buddhasattvabandhanamuktidharmadeśanāyai samarthaśca pratibalo bhavati / yadidam bhagavatā-ātmanā baddhena paraṃ bandhanādvimocayet, tadhi sthānanna vidyate / ātmanā muktena paraṃ bandhanādvimocayet, tatsthānaṃ vidyata-iti bhāṣitam / tasmād bodhisattvo muktyai kuryānna bandhanāya /
body.translated_text: "That ill <s>bodhisattva</s> should observe thus: 'Just as my illness is unreal and non-existent, so too the illness of all beings is unreal and non-existent.' While observing thus, without falling into the perception of benefit [for oneself], he generates great compassion toward beings; except that he generates great compassion with effort toward beings for the abandonment of adventitious <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Why? A <s>bodhisattva</s> who has fallen into the perception of benefit becomes disgusted with births through that great compassion. But a <s>bodhisattva</s> whose great compassion is free from the defilement of perceiving benefit does not become disgusted with births. When one arises from the defilement of views, one is not born [in bondage]. Being free from the defilement of mind, one who is born is born as if liberated; one who arises, arises as if liberated. Being born as if liberated, arising as if liberated, one becomes capable and competent to teach the <s>Dharma</s> of liberation from bondage to <s>Buddha</s>-beings. As the Blessed One has said: 'That one who is bound himself could liberate another from bondage—that situation does not exist. That one who is liberated himself could liberate another from bondage—that situation exists.' Therefore, the <s>bodhisattva</s> should act for liberation, not for bondage.

body.text: "tatra bandhanaṃ kim? kimmuktiḥ? anupāye bhavamuktiparigraho bodhisattvasya bandhanam / upāyena bhavapravṛttyavakrāṃtirmuktiḥ / anupāyena dhyānasamādhisamāpattyāsvādo bodhisattvasya bandhanam / upāyena dhyānasamādhyāsvādo muktiḥ / upāyenānuddiṣṭa prajñā hi bandhanam / upāyena niṣṭhitaprajñāḥ muktiḥ / prajñānuddiṣṭopāyo bandhanam / prajñayā niṣṭhitopāyo muktiḥ /
body.translated_text: "What then is bondage? What is liberation? Grasping at existence and liberation without skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) is the <s>bodhisattva's</s> bondage. Entering into existence with skillful means is liberation. Without skillful means, the enjoyment of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) is the <s>bodhisattva's</s> bondage. With skillful means, the enjoyment of <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s> is liberation. Wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) not guided by skillful means is bondage. Wisdom accomplished through skillful means is liberation. Skillful means not guided by wisdom is bondage. Skillful means accomplished through wisdom is liberation.

body.text: "tatropāyānuddiṣṭaprajñābandhanaṃ kim? yaduta-śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitanidhyaptiśca lakṣaṇānuvyaṃjana buddhakṣetrālaṃkārasattvaparipācanānidhyaptirhyupāyānuddiṣṭaprajñā ca bandhanam / tatropāyaniṣṭhitaprajñāmuktiḥ kim? yadutalakṣaṇānuvyaṃjanabuddhakṣetrālaṅkārasattvaparipācanacittanidhyaptiśca śūnyatānimittā praṇihitaparijayakaraṇam, idaṃ hyupāyaniṣṭhitaprajñā ca muktiḥ / tatra prajñānuddiṣṭopāyabandhanaṃ kim? yadidaṃ-sarvadṛṣṭikleśaparyutthānānuśayānunayapratighāvasthitasya sarvakuśalamūlavyāpārabodhyapariṇāmanā hi prajñānuddiṣṭopāyaśca bandhanam / tatra prajñāniṣṭhitopāyamuktiḥ kim? yadidam- tayā sarvadṛṣṭikleśaparyutthānānuśayānuśayānunayapratighaparivarjakasya sarvakuśalamūlavyāpārabodhipariṇāmanayāparāmṛṣṭiḥ, sā hi bodhisattvasya prajñāniṣṭhitopāyaśca muktiḥ /
body.translated_text: "What is the bondage of wisdom not guided by skillful means? It is the contemplation of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>ānimitta</s> (signlessness), and <s>apraṇihita</s> (wishlessness) without the contemplation of the marks, minor marks, <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) adornment, and the ripening of beings—that is the bondage of wisdom not guided by skillful means. What is the liberation of wisdom accomplished through skillful means? It is the contemplation of the marks, minor marks, <s>buddhakṣetra</s> adornment, and the ripening of beings together with the mastery of <s>śūnyatā</s>, <s>ānimitta</s>, and <s>apraṇihita</s>—that is the liberation of wisdom accomplished through skillful means. What is the bondage of skillful means not guided by wisdom? It is the engagement in the activities of all roots of merit without dedicating them to <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), while remaining established in the latent tendencies, defilements, attractions, and aversions of all views—that is the bondage of skillful means not guided by wisdom. What is the liberation of skillful means accomplished through wisdom? It is the dedication to <s>bodhi</s> of the activities of all roots of merit, free from the latent tendencies, defilements, attractions, and aversions of all views, without grasping—that is the <s>bodhisattva's</s> liberation of skillful means accomplished through wisdom.

body.text: "maṃjuśrīḥ, tatra glānena bodhisattvenaivaṃ teṣu dharmeṣu nidhyāyitavyaṃ-yaḥ kāyacittaroge 'nityatāduḥkhaśūnyananairātmyasaṃbodhaḥ, sa tatprajñā / yaḥ kāyasya rogavivarjanenānutpādśca saṃsārāsraṃsane sattvārthaprayogānuyogaḥ, ayaṃ hi tadupāyaḥ / bhūyo 'pi yaḥ 'kāyacittarogāḥ parasparaṃ paraṃparayā na ca navā na ca jīrṇā (ity) avabodhaḥ, sa tatprajñā / yacca kāyacittarogopaśamanirodhayoranutthāpanaṃ, tattadupāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: "<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, thus an ill <s>bodhisattva</s> should contemplate those <s>dharmas</s>. That which is the comprehension of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self in the illness of body and mind—that is the wisdom [thereof]. That which is the endeavor for the benefit of beings without ceasing from <s>saṃsāra</s> while avoiding the illness of the body—that is the skillful means [thereof]. Furthermore, that which is the understanding that the illnesses of body and mind are neither new nor old, arising from mutual succession—that is the wisdom [thereof]. And that which is the non-cessation of the arising of the pacification and cessation of the illness of body and mind—that is the skillful means [thereof].

body.text: "maṃjuśrīḥ, tathā hi glānena bodhisattvena svacittaṃ nidhyāyitavyam; kiṃ tu tena nidhyaptyanidhyaptyorna biharitavyam / tat kasya hetoḥ? yadi nidhyaptyāṃ biharet, sa hi pṛthagjanasya dharmaḥ / athānidhyaptyāṃ biharet, sa śrāvakadharmaḥ / tasmād bodhisattvena nidhyaptyanidhyaptyorna viharitavyam / yattatrāpratiṣṭhitaṃ, tadvodhisattvagocaraḥ /
