body.translated_text: "<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, thus indeed the ailing <s>bodhisattva</s> should contemplate his own mind; however, he should dwell neither in calming nor in non-calming. What is the reason? If he were to dwell in calming, that would be the way of an ordinary person. If he were to dwell in non-calming, that would be the way of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple). Therefore the <s>bodhisattva</s> should dwell in neither calming nor non-calming. That which is unestablished in either—that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain.

body.text:
"yaḥ pṛthagjanagocaraścāryagocaraśca nāsti, sa hi bodhisattvagocaraḥ / yaḥ saṃsāragocare 'pi kleśagocarastu nāsti, sa bodhisattvasya gocaraḥ / yo nirvāṇāvabodhagocare 'pyatyantaparinirvāṇagocarastu nāsti, sa bodhisattvasya gocaraḥ / yaścaturmāradeśanāgocare 'pi sarvamāraviṣayasamatikrāntagocaraḥ, sa bodhisattvasya gocaraḥ / yaḥ sarvajñajñānaiṣaṇāgocare 'pyakālajñānaprāptigocarastu nāsti, sa hi bodhisattvasya gocaraḥ / yaścatuḥsatyajñānagocare 'pyakālasatyapratipādanagocarastu nāsti, sa hi bodhi sattvasya gocaraḥ / yo 'dhyātmapratyavekṣaṇagocare 'pi saṃcintyabhavapratikāṃkṣiparigrahagorastu nāsti, sa bodhisattvasya gocaraḥ / yo 'nutpādapratyavekṣaṇagocara'pi niyataprāptyavakrāntigocarastu nāsti, sa bodhisattvasya gocaraḥ / yaḥ pratītyasamutpādagocare 'pi sarvadṛṣṭiviṣyagocarastu nāsti, sa bodhisattvasya gocaraḥ /
yaḥ sarvasattvasaṃsargagocare 'pi kleśānuśayagocarastu nāsti, ......pe /
yo viveka-gocare 'pi kāyacittakṣayasthānagocarastu nāsti, ......pe /
yasraidhātukagocare 'pi dharmadhātuvyavacchedakaraṇāgocarastu nāsti, ......pe /
yaḥ śūnyatāgocare 'pi gūṇasarvathaiṣaṇāgocarastu, ......pe /
yo 'nimittagocare 'pi pramocayitavya sattvāvalambanavyavasāyagocarastu, ......pe /
yo 'praṇihitagocare 'pi saṃcintyabhavagatidarśanagocarastu, ......pe /
yo 'nabhisaṃskāragocare 'pi sarvakuśalamūlābhisaṃskārāsraṃsanagocarastu, ......pe /
yaḥ ṣaṭpāramitāgocare sarvasattvacittacaryāpārāyaṇagocaraḥ, ...... pe /
yaḥ ṣaḍabhijñāgocare 'pi kṣīṇāasravagocarastu nāsti, ......pe /
yaḥ saddharmasthānagocare kumārgānupalabdhigocaraḥ, ......pe /
yaścaturapramāṇagocare 'pi brahmalokajātyasaṃsargagocarestu, ......pe /
yaḥ ṣaḍanusmṛtigocare sarvāsravagocaro nāsti, ......pe /
yo dhyānasamādhisamāpattigocare 'pi samādhisamāpattivaśenānutpādagocarastu, ......pe /
yaḥ smṛtyusthānagocare 'pi kāyavedanācittadharmātirekagocarastu nāsti, ......pe /
yaḥ pradhāna gocare kuśalākuśaladvayālambanagocaro nāsti, ......pe /
ya ṛddhipādanirhāragocare 'pyanābhogarddhipādavaśagocaraḥ, ......pe /
ya paṃcendriyagocare sarvasattvendriyavarāvarajñānagocaraḥ, ......pe /
yaḥ paṃcabalāvasthānagocare tathāgatasya daśabalābhiratigocaraḥ, ......pe
yaḥ saptabodhyaṃgapariniṣpannagocare buddhipravicayajñānakauśalyagocaraḥ, ......pe /
yo mārgāśrayagocare 'pi kumārgānupalabdhigocarastu, ......pe /
body.translated_text: "That which is neither the domain of ordinary persons nor the domain of noble ones—that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is in the domain of <s>saṃsāra</s> yet not in the domain of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)—that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is in the domain of realizing <s>nirvāṇa</s> yet not in the domain of ultimate <s>parinirvāṇa</s>—that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is in the domain of teaching about the four <s>Māras</s> yet transcends the domain of all <s>Māra</s>'s realms—that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is in the domain of seeking omniscient knowledge yet not in the domain of attaining knowledge prematurely—that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is in the domain of knowing the four noble truths yet not in the domain of establishing the truths prematurely—that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is in the domain of inner contemplation yet not in the domain of deliberately embracing the desire for existence—that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is in the domain of contemplating non-arising yet not in the domain of definitively entering the assured course—that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is in the domain of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) yet not in the domain of all views—that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is in the domain of association with all beings yet not in the domain of the latent tendencies of afflictions... [and so forth]. That which is in the domain of solitude yet not in the domain of the exhaustion of body and mind... [and so forth]. That which is in the domain of the three realms yet not in the domain of cutting off the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality)... [and so forth]. That which is in the domain of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) yet is in the domain of seeking merit in every way... [and so forth]. That which is in the domain of signlessness yet is in the domain of the resolve to liberate beings by relying on them... [and so forth]. That which is in the domain of wishlessness yet is in the domain of displaying the paths of existence deliberately... [and so forth]. That which is in the domain of non-formation yet is in the domain of not abandoning the formation of all roots of merit... [and so forth]. That which is in the domain of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) is in the domain of having reached the far shore of the conduct and minds of all beings... [and so forth]. That which is in the domain of the six superknowledges yet not in the domain of the destruction of defilements... [and so forth].

body.text: yaḥ śamathavipaśyanāsamagrārambhagocare 'pyatyantopaśamāpatanagocarastu, ......pe /
body.translated_text: That which is in the domain of practicing both <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) together yet is in the domain that does not fall into ultimate quiescence... [and so forth].

body.text: yaḥ sarvadharmānutthāpanalakṣaṇāvabodhgocare 'pi lakṣaṇānuvyañjanabuddhakāyavibhūṣaṇasamutthāpanatāgocarastu, ......pe /
body.translated_text: That which is in the domain of realizing the characteristic of non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s> yet is in the domain of adorning the <s>Buddha</s>-body with the marks and signs... [and so forth].

body.text:
yaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhacāritra darśanagocare 'pi buddhadharmānapāyivyāpāragocarastu, ......pe /
yaḥ sarvasvabhāvātyantaviśuddhatāpannadharmānugamanagocare 'pi sarvasattva(nāṃ) yathādhimukti tatheryāqpathadarśanāgocarastu, ......pe /
body.translated_text: That which is in the domain of observing the conduct of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> yet is in the domain of activity that does not abandon <s>buddhadharmas</s> (qualities of a Buddha)... [and so forth]. That which is in the domain of following <s>dharmas</s> that have attained the ultimate purity of all own-natures yet is in the domain of showing deportment according to the inclinations of all beings... [and so forth].

body.text: yaḥ sarvabuddhakṣetrātyantavināśāviṣkaraṇāpagatā 'kāśasvabhāvādhigamagocare nanāvyuhā nekavyuhabuddhakṣetraguṇavyuyhadarśanāgocaraḥ, ......pe /
body.translated_text: That which is in the domain of realizing the space-like own-nature devoid of revealing the ultimate destruction of all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) yet is in the domain of seeing the ornamental array of qualities of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in various and manifold arrays... [and so forth].

body.text: yaḥ saddharmacakrapravartanamahāparinirvāṇāsaṃdarśanagocaraśca bodhisattvacaryā atyajanagocaraśca, ayamapi bodhisattvasya gocaraḥ" /
body.translated_text: That which is in the domain of turning the wheel of the true <s>Dharma</s> and displaying the great <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and also in the domain of not abandoning the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct—this too is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain."

body.text: asmin upadeśe nirdiśyamāne, teṣām maṃjuśrīyā kukārabhūtena sārdhamāgatānām devaputrāṇāmaṣtasahasrairanuttarasamyaksambodhicittamutpāditam /
body.translated_text: When this instruction was being taught, eight thousand <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons) who had come together with <s>Mañjuśrī</s> generated the mind of <s>anuttarasamyaksambodhī</s> (supreme perfect awakening).

body.text: glānasaṃmodana kathāyāḥ parivartaścaturthaḥ /
body.translated_text: End of the fourth chapter, entitled 'Visiting the Sick' (<s>Glānasaṃmodana</s>).

body.text: 5 acintyavimokṣanirdeśaḥ
body.translated_text: 5. Teaching on Inconceivable Liberation (<s>Acintyavimokṣanirdeśa</s>)

body.text: athāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaivaṃ bhavati sma- 'yadyasmin gṛha āsanānyapi na syuḥ, ime bodhisattvāśca mahāśrāvakāḥ kutra niṣīdanti?' tato licchavirvimalakīrtirāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya cittavitarka jñātvā, āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputramevamavocat-
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> had this thought: 'If in this house there are not even seats, where will these <s>bodhisattvas</s> and great <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) sit?' Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, knowing the thought in the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>'s mind, said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>:

body.text:
"bhadanta śāriputra, ki dharmārthika āgato 'si? āhosvidāsanārthikaḥ?" āha- "dharmārthika āgataḥ, nāsmyāsanārthikaḥ" / avocad- "bhadanta śāriputra, yadyato yo dharmārthikaḥ so 'pi svakāyārthiko na syāt, āsanachandīkṣaṇaṃ kuta āgatam? bhadanta śāriputra, yo dharmakāmaḥ, sa hi rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānakāmo nāsti, skandhadhātvāyatanakāmo nāsti / yo dharmakāmaḥ, sa kāmarūpārūpyadhātukāmo nāsti, / yo dharmakāmaḥ, sa buddhabhiniveśakāmo nāsti, dharmasaṃghābhiniveśakāmo nāsti /
"bhadanta śāriputra, punaraparaṃ yo dharmakāmaḥ, sa duḥkhaparijñānakāmo nāsti, samudayaprahāṇakāmo nāsti, nirodhasākṣātkārakāmo nāsti, mārgabhāvanākāmo nāsti / tat kasya hetoḥ? dharmo hyaprapañca'nakṣaraḥ; tato yad- 'duḥkhaṃ parijñātavyam, samudāyaḥ prahātavyaḥ, nirodhaḥ sākṣātkartavyaḥ, mārgo bhāvayitavya' ityuttarikaraṇīyaṃ, taddharmakāmo nāsti, tadhi prapañcakāmaḥ /
"bhadanta śāriputra, dharmo hyupaśāntaśca praśāntaḥ, tato ya utpādavināśanasamudācāraḥ, sa dharmakāmo nāsti, vivekakāmo nāsti; sa utpādavināśakāmaḥ / bhadanta śāriputra, punaraparaṃ dharmo ' rajo virajaḥ; tataḥ kaściddharmaśced yasmin anunayas-(syād-) antamaśo nirvāṇe 'pi, sa hi dharmakāmo nāsti; sa 'rāgarajaḥ kāmaḥ' / dharmo viṣayo nāsti / yā viṣayagaṇanā, sā dharmakāmo nāsti; sa viṣayakāmaḥ / dharmo hyanāvyūho 'nirvyuhaḥ; kaściddharmo yasminabhigrahaṇaṃ cotsargaḥ, sa dharmakāmo nāsti; sa hyabhigrahaṇotsargakāmaḥ /
body.translated_text:
"Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, have you come seeking the <s>Dharma</s> or seeking a seat?" He replied: "I have come seeking the <s>Dharma</s>, not seeking a seat." He said: "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, one who truly seeks the <s>Dharma</s> would not be concerned even about his own body—how then could the desire for a seat arise? Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, one who desires the <s>Dharma</s> does not desire form, feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; does not desire the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), or <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases). One who desires the <s>Dharma</s> does not desire the realms of desire, form, or formlessness. One who desires the <s>Dharma</s> does not desire attachment to the <s>Buddha</s>, does not desire attachment to the <s>Dharma</s> or the <s>Saṅgha</s>.
"Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, furthermore, one who desires the <s>Dharma</s> does not desire full knowledge of suffering, does not desire abandonment of the origin,

body.text: "dharmo 'nālayaḥ; ya ālayārāmāḥ, te na dharmakāmāḥ, te hyālayakāmāḥ / dharmo 'nimittaḥ śūnyaḥ; yeṣāṃ vijñānanimittānugamanam, te na dharmakāmāḥ, te nimittakāmāḥ / dharmo 'sahavāsaḥ; ye keciddharmeṇa saha viharanti, te na dharmakāmāḥ, te vihārakāmāḥ / dharmo dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñātannāsti; ye dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñāte caranti te dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñātakāmāḥ, na tu dharmakāmāḥ /
body.translated_text: "The <s>Dharma</s> is without clinging; those who delight in clinging do not desire the <s>Dharma</s>—they desire clinging. The <s>Dharma</s> is signless and empty; those who follow signs of consciousness do not desire the <s>Dharma</s>—they desire signs. The <s>Dharma</s> is not to be dwelt in; those who dwell together with the <s>Dharma</s> do not desire the <s>Dharma</s>—they desire dwelling. The <s>Dharma</s> is not seen, heard, thought, or cognized; those who engage in what is seen, heard, thought, or cognized—they desire the seen, heard, thought, and cognized, not the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: "bhadanta śāriputra,, dharmassaṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtannāsti; ye saṃskṛtāvacarāḥ te na dharmakāmāḥ, te saṃskṛragrahaṇakāmāḥ / bhadanta śāriputra, ata iccheśceddharma, tvayā sarvadharmā apratikāṃkṣitavyāḥ" /
body.translated_text: "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> is neither conditioned nor unconditioned; those who move within the conditioned do not desire the <s>Dharma</s>—they desire grasping at the conditioned. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, therefore, if you wish for the <s>Dharma</s>, you should have no expectation toward any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever."

body.text: asmin dharmopadeśe nirdiśyamāne, devaputrāṇām pañcaśata(sya) dharmeṣu viśuddhaṃ dharmacakṣurudapādi / atha licchavirvimalakīrtirmajuśrīkumārabhūtamabravīt- "maṃjuśrīḥ, daśadikṣu śatasahasrāṇyasaṃkhyeyāni buddhakṣetrāṇi buddhakṣetracārikāṃ caritvā, kasmin buddhakṣetre sarvottamāni sarvaguṇasampannāni siṃhāsanāni tvayā dṛṣṭāni?" evamavocat /
body.translated_text: When this instruction of the <s>Dharma</s> was being expounded, the pure <s>dharmacakṣus</s> (eye of Dharma) arose in five hundred <s>devaputras</s> with regard to the <s>dharmas</s>. Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful prince: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, having wandered through countless hundreds of thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) in the ten directions, in which <s>buddhakṣetra</s> have you seen the most supreme lion thrones, endowed with all excellent qualities?' Thus he spoke.

body.text: maṃjuśrīkumārabhūto licchavi bimalakīrtimetadavocat- "kulaputra, itaḥ pūrvāsmin dvātriśad-gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇyatikramya, asti merudhvajo nāma lokadhātuḥ / tatramerupradīpa rājo nāma tathāgatastiṣṭhiti dhriyate yāpayati / tasya tathāgatasya kāya(pramāṇaṃ) caturaśītiryojanaśatasahasrāṇī / tasya bhagavatassiṃhānapramāṇamaṣṭaṣaṣṭiryojanaśatasahasrāṇi / teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ kāya(pramāṇam) api dvicatvāriṃśadyojanaśatasahasrāṇi / teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ siṃhāsana(pramāṇam) api caturtriśadyojanaśatasahasrāṇi / kulaputra, tasmiṃstasya merupradīparājasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetre merudhvaje lokadhātau siṃhāsanāni santi sarvottamāni sarvaguṇasampannāni" /
body.translated_text: <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful prince, said to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: 'Son of good family, passing beyond <s>buddhakṣetras</s> equal in number to the sands of thirty-two Ganges rivers to the east of here, there is a world-realm called <s>Merudhvaja</s>. There the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Merupradīparāja</s> presently dwells, abides, and lives. The body of that <s>Tathāgata</s> measures eighty-four hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. The lion throne of that Blessed One measures sixty-eight hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. The bodies of his <s>bodhisattvas</s> also measure forty-two hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. The lion thrones of those <s>bodhisattvas</s> also measure thirty-four hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. Son of good family, in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Merupradīparāja</s>, in the world-realm <s>Merudhvaja</s>, there are the most supreme lion thrones, endowed with all excellent qualities.'

body.text: tatastena khalu samayena tādṛśamabhiprāyaṃ sañcintya, licchavinā vimalakīrtināsyā evaṃrupardvividhyā abhisaṃskāro 'bhisaṃskṛtaḥ, (yathā) merudhvajāllokadhātorbhagavatā merupradīparājena tathāgateta dvātriśatsiṃhāsanasahasrāṇyanupreṣitāni-etāvadunnatārohāṇyetāvadviśālānyetāvaddarśanīyāni, yāni tairbodhisattvaiśca tairmahāśrāvakaiśca taiḥśakrabrahmalokapāladevaputrairadṛṣṭapūrvāṇi / tānyuparivihāyasa āgatya, licchavervimalakīrtergṛhe pratiṣṭhānāni / dvātriṃśannānāsihāsanasahasreṣvanāyātena vahamāneṣu, tadhgṛhamapyetāvadviśālaṃ dṛṣyate sma / vaiśālyapi mahānagaryanivṛtābhūta; jambudvīpaścaturdvīpako (lokadhātu-)ścānivṛtāḥ, sarve te 'pi yathāpūrva dṛśyante sma /
body.translated_text: Then at that moment, having conceived such an intention, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> performed a feat of such miraculous power that the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Merupradīparāja</s> from the world-realm <s>Merudhvaja</s> sent thirty-two thousand lion thrones — of such great height, such breadth, and such beauty as had never been seen before by those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, those great <s>śrāvakas</s>, those <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, World-Protectors, and <s>devaputras</s>. Coming through the sky, they were placed in the house of the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>. Though thirty-two thousand diverse lion thrones arrived and were accommodated, that house appeared equally vast. The great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s> was not obstructed; <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and the four-continent world were not obstructed either — all appeared exactly as before.

body.text: atha licchavirvimalakīrtirmañjuśrīkumārabhūtametadavocat- "maṃjuśrīḥ, siṃhāsanānurupakāyādhiṣṭhitāstavamime ca bodhisattvāḥ sihāsane (ṣu) niṣīdata" / tato ye 'bhi'jñālābhibodhisattvāḥ, te dvicatvāriṃśadyojanaśatasahasrakāyādhiṣṭhitāḥ sihāsane(ṣu) niṣīdanti sma / ye bodhisattvāādikarmikāḥ, te teṣu sihāsaneṣu nīṣīditunnāśakan / tato licchavirvimalakīrtiryathā te bodhisattvāḥ pañcābhijñāyāṃ sidhyeyustathā hyevaṃ tebhyo bodhisattvebhyo dharma deśayi / te 'bhijñām prāpya, ( ṛddhyā) dvicatvāriśadyojanaśatasahasraśarīrāṇyabhinirmāya, teṣu sihāsaneṣu niṣidanti sma / teṣvāpi mahāśrāvakeṣu teṣu sihāsaneṣu niṣīditumasamartheṣu, licchavirvimalakīrtistata āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputramabravīt- "bhadanta śāriputra, sihasane niṣīda" / avocat- "satpuruṣa, eṣu sihāsaneṣūtkṛṣṭeṣu cātimātreṣu, niṣīditunna śakromi" / abravīt- "bhadanta śāriputra, tasmai bhagavate tathāgatāya merupradīparājāya kuru praṇāmañca niṣīdituṃ śakṣyasi" / atha te mahāśrāvakāstasmai bhagavate tathāgatāya merupradīparājāyābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purataste sihāsane(ṣu) nyaṣīdan /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful prince: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, let these <s>bodhisattvas</s> assume bodies proportionate to the lion thrones and be seated upon them.' Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had attained the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), having assumed bodies of forty-two hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>, sat upon the lion thrones. But the beginner <s>bodhisattvas</s> were unable to sit upon those lion thrones. Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> taught the <s>Dharma</s> to those <s>bodhisattvas</s> so that they might attain success in the five <s>abhijñās</s>. Having attained the <s>abhijñās</s>, they magically created bodies of forty-two hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> through supernatural power and sat upon those lion thrones. Even the great <s>śrāvakas</s> were unable to sit upon those lion thrones. Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, sit upon a lion throne.' He replied: 'Good sir, these lion thrones are too lofty and too large; I am unable to sit.' He said: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, bow down to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Merupradīparāja</s>, and you will be able to sit.' Then those great <s>śrāvakas</s>, having bowed to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Merupradīparāja</s>, sat upon the lion thrones.

body.text: athāyuṣmāṃśāriputro licchavi vimalakīrtimetadavocat- "kulaputra, āścarya (yathai-)vamutkṛṣṭātimātrāṇīdṛśanānāsahasrāṇi siṃhāsanānyetāvadalpagṛhaṃ praviśanti caibhirapi vaiśālī mahānagarī nivṛtā nāti, jambūdvīpasya grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānī ca caturmahādvīpako 'pi (lokadhātu-)śca na kicinnivṛtāḥ, api ca devanāgayakṣagandharvāsurgaruḍa kinnaramahoragasthānānyanivṛtāni pūrva yādṛśānyāyatyapi dṛśyante tathā" /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: 'Son of good family, it is wonderful that these many thousands of lion thrones, so lofty and immense, enter this small house without obstructing the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, and without obstructing the villages, cities, towns, kingdoms, and capitals of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, nor the four-continent world, and moreover without obstructing the abodes of <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — they all appear just as before.'

body.text: licchavirvimalakīrtirabrabīt- "bhadanta śāriputra, tathāgatebhyaśca bodhisattvebhyo 'cintyo nāma vimokṣo 'sti / tasminacintyavimokṣe viharan bodhisattva etāvadunnatātirekavipulaṃ sumeruṃ parvatarājaṃ sarṣapābhyantaram prakṣipan tasmin sarṣape 'vardhamāne ca sumerāvavyaye, (tādṛśāṃ) krīyāṃ deśayati / cāturmahārājakāyikadevāśca trayasriṃśadevā api 'kutra vayam prakṣiptāḥ', na jānanti / anyaistvṛdvividhineyikasattvaiḥ sa parvatarājassumeruḥ sarṣapābhyantaram prakṣiptam prajñāyate ca dṛśyate / sa hi, bhadanta śāriputra, bodhisattvānām acintyavimokṣaviṣayapraveṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is a liberation of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> called "Inconceivable" (<s>acintya</s>). A <s>bodhisattva</s> dwelling in that inconceivable liberation can cast the great king of mountains, <s>Sumeru</s>, so lofty and vast, into the interior of a mustard seed; and while the mustard seed does not expand and <s>Sumeru</s> does not diminish, he displays this feat. The <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods and the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods do not even know "where have we been cast?" Yet this casting of the king of mountains, <s>Sumeru</s>, into the interior of a mustard seed is perceived and seen by those beings who are to be guided through miraculous powers. This, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the domain of entry into the inconceivable liberation of <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: "bhadanta śāriputra, bhūyo 'pyacintyavimokṣavihāribodhisattvasya caturmahāsamudrasya skandhān ekoromakūpaṃ pravartayaḥ, matsyakūrmaśiśumāramaṇḍūkānyajalajaprāṇibhya upaghāto nāsti / nāgakṣagandharvāsurāṇāmapyevaṃ 'vayaṃ kutra viveśayitā iti na bhavati; tasyām kriyāyāṃ dṛśyamānāyāṃ, tebhyassattvebhya upaghātaśca saṃkṣobho nāsti /
body.translated_text: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, furthermore, a <s>bodhisattva</s> dwelling in the inconceivable liberation can pour the waters of the four great oceans into a single pore of the skin, without harm to the fish, turtles, crocodiles, frogs, and other aquatic creatures. The <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, and <s>asuras</s> do not even think "where have we been placed?" And in this feat being displayed, there is no harm or disturbance to those beings.

body.text: "ayamapya-(cintyavimokṣavihāribodhisattvas / trisāhasramahā-sāhasralokadhātuṃ kumbhakārasya cakramiva dakṣiṇahastenādāya ca pravartayya, gaṅgānadīvālukopamalokadhā(tūnāṃ dūraṃ kṣipati); kṣipta(śca) sattvā 'vayaṃ kutroddhṛtāḥ, kuta āgatā na jānanti / punareva gṛhītāḥ (sva) sthānameva pratiṣṭhāpitā āgamanagamananna jānanti, yadyapi sā kriyā saṃdṛśayate / "bhadanta śāriputra, bhūyo 'pyaprameyakālavaineyikasattvā vidyante, vidyante ca saṃkṣepya kālavaineyikāḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This too is a <s>bodhisattva</s> dwelling in the inconceivable liberation. Taking the great trichiliocosm in his right hand like a potter's wheel, he hurls it beyond <s>buddhakṣetras</s> equal in number to the sands of the Ganges; the beings who have been hurled do not know "where have we been taken from, where have we come?" He then takes it back and places it in its original position, and they do not know any coming or going, even though the feat is displayed. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, furthermore, there are beings who are to be guided over an immeasurable time, and there are beings who are to be guided in a brief time.

body.text: tatrācintyavimokṣavihāribodhisattvo 'prameyakālavaineyekasattvavaineyārthāya saptāhaṃ kalpātyayena, saṃkṣepyakālavaineyikasattvebhyaḥ kalpaṃ saptāhātyayena darśayate / tatrāprameyakālavaineyikasattvāḥ saptāhe kalpātyayaṃ jānanti / ye saṃkṣepyakālavaineyikasattvāḥ, te kalpaṃ saptāhenātītaṃ jānanti /
body.translated_text: 'Therein, a <s>bodhisattva</s> dwelling in the inconceivable liberation, for the sake of guiding beings who are to be guided over an immeasurable time, shows a <s>kalpa</s> passing in seven days; and for beings who are to be guided in a brief time, he shows seven days passing as a <s>kalpa</s>. Therein, those beings to be guided over an immeasurable time perceive the passing of a <s>kalpa</s> in seven days; and those beings to be guided in a brief time perceive a <s>kalpa</s> as having passed in seven days.

body.text: "tathā hyacintyavimokṣavihāribodhisattvaḥ sarvabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhānekabiddhakṣetre darśayate / cāpi sarvasattvān dakṣiṇakaratala ādhāya, cittajavanarddhividhyā gacchantyasarvabuddhakṣetrāṇyādarśayati, ki cāpyekabuddhakṣetrādacalitaḥ / daśadikṣu bhagavate buddhāya yāvat pūjanāni, sarvāṇi tānyekaromakūpe deśayati / daśadikṣu yāvaccandraścādityaśca tārakārūpāṇi, sarvāṇi tānyapyekaromakūpe darśayate /
body.translated_text: 'Thus a <s>bodhisattva</s> dwelling in the inconceivable liberation displays the array of qualities of all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in a single <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. Taking all beings in the palm of his right hand, through the miraculous power of mind-speed, he shows them all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> without moving from a single <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. He displays in a single pore of the skin all the offerings made to the <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions. He displays in a single pore of the skin all the moons, suns, and stars of the ten directions.

body.text: "daśadikṣu vāyumaṇḍalāni yāvaduttiṣṭhanti, sarvāṇi tāni mukhena pītvā, tasya kāyo 'vinaṣṭaśca teṣāṃ buddhakṣetrāṇām tṛṇavanaspatayo 'prapatitāḥ / daśadikṣu sarva taṃ buddhakṣetradahana kalpoddāhāgnirāśi svodaraṃ prakṣipya, yat karma tena karaṇīyaṃ, tat karoti / adhastādgaṅgānadīvālukāsama(ani) buddhakṣetrā(ṇya) atikramya, sa (ekaṃ) biddhakṣetramūrdhvamutkṣipya cāruhya, ūrdhva gaṅgānadīvālukāsamā(ni) buddhakṣetrā(ṇya) atikramya, upariṣṭāt-tadyathāpi nāma mahāsthāmnā puruṣeṇa sūcyagreṇa badarapatramucchritam-evamevotkṣiptaṃ (biddhakṣetran) nikṣipati /
body.translated_text: 'He drinks in through his mouth all the wind-circles that arise in the ten directions, yet his body is unharmed and the grasses and trees of those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> do not fall. He casts into his own belly the fire of the world-conflagration at the end of a <s>kalpa</s> from all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions, and that fire accomplishes what it must. Passing below through <s>buddhakṣetras</s> equal to the sands of the Ganges, he lifts up a single <s>buddhakṣetra</s> and, ascending above, passes through <s>buddhakṣetras</s> equal to the sands of the Ganges, and places it above — just as a strong man might lift a jujube leaf on the tip of a needle — even so does he lift and place that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>.

body.text: "tathā hyacintyavimokṣavihāribodhisattvaḥ sarvasattvarupamadhitiṣṭhati / cakravartirājasya rūpamadhitiṣṭhati; evamevādhitiṣṭhati lokapālaśakrabrahmaśrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvasarvasattvabuddharūpam /
body.translated_text: 'Thus a <s>bodhisattva</s> dwelling in the inconceivable liberation assumes the form of all beings. He assumes the form of a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch); just so, he assumes the forms of World-Protectors, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, all beings, and <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: "(sa bodhisattvo) daśadikṣu sattvānāṃ sarvāgramadhyahīnaśabdaprasiddhaḥ / yāḥ kāścana śabdaprajñaptayaḥ, tāḥ sarvā buddhaghoṣarutaṃca buddhadharmasaṃghaśabdamadhitiṣṭhiti, tasmāt śabdasvarād anityatāduḥkhaśūnyanairātmyaśabdasvaraṃ niścārayati; daśadikṣu bhagavān buddo yāvadākāramupadeśena darśayati, tebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ śabdasvarebhyo niścārayati /
body.translated_text: That <s>Bodhisattva</s> is renowned among all the highest, middling, and lowest beings in the ten directions for all sounds. Whatever verbal designations there may be, they all abide in the sound and voice of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>. Therefore, from that sound and voice he sends forth the sound of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self. In whatever manner the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> teaches through various forms in the ten directions, from all those sounds and voices he sends them forth.

body.text: "bhadanta śāriputra, ayaṃ hyacintyavimokṣavihāribodhisattvaviṣayapraveśaḥ kiṃcinmātraṃ kevalaṃ darśitaḥ / bhadanta śāriputra, (tattvataḥ) kalpābhyadhikaṃ vā tadatikrāntaṃ vācintyavimokṣavihāribodhisattvaviṣayapraveśopadeśam daeśanīyam (abhaviṣyat) / atha mahākāśyapaḥ sthavira imaṃ bodhisattvācintyavimokṣopadeśaṃ śrutvā, āścaryādbhutaprāptaḥ śāriputraṃ sthavirametadavocat-
body.translated_text: Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, this entry into the domain of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who dwells in the inconceivable liberation (<s>acintyavimokṣa</s>) has been shown only to a small extent. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in truth, to fully expound the entry into the domain of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who dwells in the inconceivable liberation would take more than a <s>kalpa</s> or beyond. Then the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, having heard this teaching on the inconceivable liberation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, was struck with wonder and amazement, and said to the elder <s>Śāriputra</s> —

body.text: "āyuṣmaṃśāriputra, tadyathāpi nāma jātyandhapuruṣasyābhimukhaṃ sarvarūpopapannānām kriyāṇām darśitānāmapi tena jātyandhenaikarupamapi tu na dṛśyate; evamevāyuṣmaṃśāriputra, asyācintyavimokṣamukhasya deśanākāle sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhebhyo jātyandhasamebhyaścakṣurnāsti caikamātrācintyadvāramapyanabhimukhībhūtam / imamacintyavimokṣaṃ śrutvā, ko vicakṣaṇo 'nuttarasamyaksaṃbodhicittanna janayet?
body.translated_text: Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, just as if all manner of beautiful colored forms were displayed before a person born blind, yet that person born blind would not see even a single form — even so, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, at the time of teaching this door of inconceivable liberation, all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, being like those born blind, have no eyes and cannot approach even a single door of the inconceivable. Having heard this inconceivable liberation, what wise person would not generate the mind of supreme, perfect awakening?

body.text: "(asmābhiḥ) praṇaṣṭendriyairdagdhapūtikabījasadṛśairasmai mahāyānāya bhājanābhūtairidānīm kathaṃ karaṇīyam? (asmābhir) imaṃ dharmopadeśaṃ śrutvā, ārtasvaraṃ kranditvā, sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaistrisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau śabdamādātavyam / sarvabodhisattvairimamacintyavimokṣaṃ śrutvā, yuvako rājaputro yathā mukuṭaṃ gṛhaṇīyācca prāmodyena mūrdhni pratigrahīṣyati, cāsmin svādhimuktibalamutpādayitavyam / yāsmin acintyavimokṣa'dhimuktiḥ, tasyāṃ sarvamārā api ki kuryuḥ?"
body.translated_text: As for us, whose faculties are destroyed, who are like burnt and rotten seeds, who are unfit vessels for this <s>Mahāyāna</s> — what can we do now? Having heard this <s>Dharma</s> teaching, we should cry out with anguished voices, and all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> should raise a cry throughout this trichiliocosm! All <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having heard this inconceivable liberation, should receive it upon their heads with joy, as a young prince would receive a crown, and should generate the power of aspiration toward it. For one who has aspiration toward this inconceivable liberation — what can all the <s>Māras</s> do?

body.text:
mahākāśyapena sthavirenāsmanupadeśe deśite, dvātriṃśaddevaputrasahasrāṇyanuttarasamyaksaṃbodhicittamutpādayanti sma /
tato licchavirvimalakīrtirmahākāśyapaṃ sthavirametadavocat- "bhadanta mahākāśyapa, daśadikṣvaparimāṇalokadhātuṣu ye kecinmārā mārakāriṇaḥ, sarve te 'cintyavimokṣavihāribodhisattvāścopāyakauśalyena sattvaparipācanārthammārakāriṇaḥ / "bhadanta mahākāśyapa, daśadikṣvaparimāṇalokadhātuṣu bodhisattve(bhyo) ye hastapadaśrotraghrāṇalohitasnāyvasthimajjācakṣuḥ pūrvakāyaśīrṣāṅgapratyaṃgarājyarāṣṭrapradeśabhāryāputraduhitṛdāsadāsyaśvahastiratha-vāhanasuvarṇajātarūpamaṇimuktāśaṅkhasfaṭikaśilāpravāḍavaiḍūryānarghaṇiratnāhārapānarasavastrayācakāḥ saṃbādhaṃ kurvanti, sarve te 'pi yācakā yadbhūyasācintyavimokṣavihāribodhisattvā upāyakauśalyenemāṃ (bodhisattva-)adhyāśayadṛḍhatāṃ deśayanti / tat kasya hetoḥ? bhadanta mahākāśyapa, bodhisattveṣu kaṭukatapasaivaṃ deśayatsu, akṛtāvakāśe janakāyāya bodhisattvasaṃbādhakaraṇānubhāvo nāsti / akṛtāvakāśe (janakāyena) hananotthāpanam aśakyam / "bhadanta kāśyapa, tadyathāpi māna khadyotakena sūryamaṇḍalābhāso 'nākramaṇīyaḥ; evameva bhadanta kāśyapa, akṛtāvakāśe (janakāyena) bodhisattvākramaṇotthāpanamaśakyam / bhadanta mahākāśyapa, tadyathāpi nāma kuñjaramātaṅgāya nāgarājāya gardabheta prahāradānamakṣamaṇīyam; evameva bhadanta mahākāśyapa, bodhisattvābhāvena bodhisattvasambādhakaraṇaśakyam / (yadya) api kho pana bodhisattvaḥ khalu bodhisattvāya sambādhaṃ kuryāt (tad-) bodhisattvasambādhakaraṇaṃ bodhisattvaḥ kṣamate / "bhadanta mahākāśyapa, ayaṃ hyacintyavimokṣavihāribodhisattvānāmupāyajñānabalapraveśaḥ" /
body.translated_text:
When the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> delivered this teaching, thirty-two thousand sons of gods generated the mind of supreme, perfect awakening.
Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>: 'Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, all those who are <s>Māras</s> or who act as <s>Māras</s> in the immeasurable world-realms of the ten directions — all of them are <s>Bodhisattvas</s> dwelling in the inconceivable liberation, who act as <s>Māras</s> through skillful means for the purpose of maturing beings. Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, in the immeasurable world-realms of the ten directions, those who harass <s>Bodhisattvas</s> by begging for their hands, feet, ears, nose, blood, sinews, bones, marrow, eyes, torso, head, limbs, kingdom, realm, province, wife, son, daughter, male and female servants, horses, elephants, chariots, vehicles, gold, silver, jewels, pearls, conch, crystal, coral, lapis lazuli, and priceless gems, food, drink, flavors, and garments — all those beggars are for the most part <s>Bodhisattvas</s> dwelling in the inconceivable liberation, who through skillful means teach this firmness of <s>Bodhisattva</s> aspiration. Why is that? Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, when <s>Bodhisattvas</s> demonstrate such severe austerities, ordinary beings who have not created the opportunity do not have the power to harass <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Without having created the opportunity, one cannot overthrow them. Venerable <s>Kāśyapa</s>, just as a firefly cannot encroach upon the brilliance of the sun's orb, even so, venerable <s>Kāśyapa</s>, one who has not created the opportunity cannot overthrow a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, just as a donkey cannot deliver a blow to the lord elephant, the king of elephants, even so, venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, without being a <s>Bodhisattva</s> one cannot harass a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. But if a <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to harass another <s>Bodhisattva</s>, that harassment a <s>Bodhisattva</s> can endure. Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, this is the entry into the power of skillful knowledge of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who dwell in the inconceivable liberation.'

body.text: acintyavimokṣanirdeśasya parivartaḥ paṃcamaḥ /
body.translated_text: This is the fifth chapter, the exposition of the Inconceivable Liberation (<s>Acintyavimokṣanirdeśa</s>).

body.text: 6 devī
body.translated_text: 6. The Goddess (<s>Devī</s>)

body.text: atha maṃjuśrīkumārabhūto licchavi vimalakīrtim evamavocat- "satpuruṣa, bodhisattvena sarvasattvāḥ kathaṃ draṣṭavyāḥ?"- abravīt- "maṃjuśrīḥ, tadyathāpi nāma vijñaḥ puruṣa udakacandraṃ prakṣete, evameva bodhisattvena sarvasattvā draṣṭavyāḥ / maṃjuśrīḥ, tadyathāpi nāma māyākāro māyākāranirmitamanuṣyaṃ prekṣate, evameva bodhisattvena sarvasattvā draṣṭavyāḥ / maṃjuśrīḥ, tadyathāpi nāmādarśamaṇḍale mukhaṃ dṛśyam, evameva bodhisattvena sarvasattvā draṣṭavyāḥ / maṃjuśrīḥ, tadyathāpi nāma mṛgatṛṣṇikājalam bodhisattvena sarvasattvā draṣṭavyāḥ / maṃjuśrī, tadyathāpi nāma pratiśrutkāghoṣanādiḥ /////
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the Crown Prince, said to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: 'Good sir, how should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> view all beings?' He replied: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, just as a wise person would look at the moon reflected in water, so should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> view all beings. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, just as a magician would look at a person created by magic, so should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> view all beings. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, just as one's face is seen in the surface of a mirror, so should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> view all beings. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, just as the water of a mirage, so should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> view all beings. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, just as the sound of an echo ...

body.text:
ākāśamegharāśiḥ ///// fenapiṇḍasya
pūrvāntaḥ ///// ) budbudodayavyayau ///// kadalīsārāpekṣeva ///// ///// vidyuccyutiriva ///// paṃcamadhātusadṛśāḥ ///// saptamāyatanasadṛśāḥ ///// ārupyeṣu rūpadarśanasadṛśā ///// dagdhabījād ///// 'ṅkuraniṣpattiriva ///// maṇḍūkasya romācchādanaṃ yathā ///// ṃaraṇārthikasya krīḍāratiriva ///// srotāpannasya satkāyadṛṣṭiryathā ///// sakṛdāgāmini tṛtīyabhava iva ///// anāgāmini garbhāvakrāntiḥ ///// ///// arhati rāgadveṣamohāḥ ///// kṣāntilābhibodhisattve mātsaryadauḥśīlyavyāpādavihisācittam ///// tathāgate vāsanā ///// jātyandhajanena rūpa darśanam ///// nirodhasamāpatti(lābhina) ānāpānaḥ ///// akāśe śakuneḥ padam ///// ///// paṇḍakalāṃgularohaṇaḥ ///// vandhyāputraprāptiḥ ///// tathāgatanirbhitasya kleśotpattiḥ ///// vibodhe svapnadṛṣṭadarśanam ///// asaṅkalpe kleśaḥ ///// ahetukatvādagnyotpādaḥ parinirvṛtasya pratisandhiriva bodhisattvena sarvasattvāḥ pratyavekṣyāḥ / maṃjuśrīḥ, evam paramārthata eva nairārmyaprabodhena sarvasattvāḥ pratyavekṣyāḥ" /
body.translated_text: ... like a mass of clouds in the sky ... like a ball of foam ... the past ... like the arising and passing of a bubble ... like looking for pith in a plantain tree ... like a flash of lightning ... like the fifth element ... like the seventh sense-base ... like seeing form in the formless realms ... like a sprout from a burnt seed ... like hair growing on a frog ... like desire for play and pleasure in one who seeks death ... like the view of a self-existing collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) in a stream-enterer (<s>srotāpanna</s>) ... like a third existence for the once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>) ... like entry into a womb for the non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>) ... like desire, hatred, and delusion in an <s>Arhat</s> ... like miserliness, immorality, malice, and thoughts of harm in a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has attained patience ... like latent tendencies in a <s>Tathāgata</s> ... like seeing forms by one born blind ... like inhalation and exhalation for one who has attained the cessation attainment ... like the track of a bird in the sky ... like a eunuch fathering children ... like a barren woman's offspring ... like the arising of afflictions in one emanated by the <s>Tathāgata</s> ... like seeing dream-visions after awakening ... like afflictions without conceptualization ... like fire arising without a cause ... like the rebirth-linking of one who has attained final <s>nirvāṇa</s> — so should a <s>Bodhisattva</s> examine all beings. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, thus, through the awakening to non-self in the ultimate sense, all beings should be examined.

body.text: abravīt- "kulaputra, yadi bodhisattvena sarvasattvā evam pratyavekṣyāḥ, kathamatha sarvasattveṣu mahāmaitryupapatsyate?"- āha- "maṃjuśrīḥ, yadā bodhisattvastathā hi pratyavekṣate- 'evaṃ dharma parijñāya, ebhyaḥ sattvebhyo darśayāmi'- ti tataḥ sarvasattveṣu samyakśaraṇamaitryupapadyate-
body.translated_text: <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Son of good family, if a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should examine all beings in this way, how then will great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>) toward all beings arise?' He replied: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, when a <s>Bodhisattva</s> examines thus — "Having fully understood the <s>Dharma</s> in this way, I shall show it to these beings" — then there arises in him a truly founded loving-kindness toward all beings —

body.text: "anupādānakāraṇādupaśāntamaitrī, kleśābhāvenātāpamaitrī, tryadhvasamatākāraṇādyadyadupamatā maitrī, paryutthānābhāva kāraṇādavirodhamaitrī, ādhyātmikabāhyāsambhedakāraṇādadvayamaitrī, suniṣṭhākāraṇādakṣobhyamaitrī, abhedyābhiprāyavajrakāraṇāddṛḍhamaitrī, svabhāvaviśuddhikāraṇād viśuddhimaitrī, āśayasamatākāraṇāt samatāmaitrī, arihananakāraṇādarhanmaitrī, anācchedyasattvaparipācanakāraṇād bodhisattvamaitrī, bhūyo 'pi tathatādhigamakāraṇāt tathāgatamaitrī, sattvāpasvāpanasuprabodhanakāraṇād buddhamaitrī, svayamabhisaṃbodhikāraṇāt svayaṃbhūmaitrī, tulyarasakāraṇād bodhimaitrī, anunayapratighaprahāṇakāraṇādanāropamaitrī, mahāyānaparyavabhāsakaraṇato mahākaruṇāmaitrī, śūnyatānairātmyapratyavekṣaṇakāraṇādaparikhedamaitrī, ācāryamuṣṭyabhāvakāraṇādadharmadānamaitrī, duḥśīlasattvāpekṣākāraṇāt śīla-maitrī, svapararakṣākāraṇāt kṣāntimaitrī, sarvasattvabhāravahanakāraṇād vīryamaitrī, anāsvādakāraṇād dhyānamaitrī, kālenāsādhanakāraṇāt prajñāmaitrī, samantadvāradarśanakāraṇādupāyamaitrī, abhiprāyapariśuddhikāraṇādakuhanamaitrī, paścāttāpakaraṇato niścalamaitrī, anaṅgaṇakāraṇādadhyāśayamaitrī, akṛtrimakāraṇādamāyāvimaitrī, buddhasukhapratiṣṭhāpanakāraṇāt sukhamaitrī / maṃjuśrīḥ, sā hi bodhisattvasya maitrī / "
body.translated_text: "Because of non-clinging, it is pacified <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). Because of the absence of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), it is non-tormenting <s>maitrī</s>. Because of the equality of the three times, it is calmed <s>maitrī</s>. Because of the absence of mental disturbance, it is non-conflicting <s>maitrī</s>. Because of non-differentiation of inner and outer, it is non-dual <s>maitrī</s>. Because of firm resolve, it is unshakeable <s>maitrī</s>. Because of unbreakable intention like a thunderbolt, it is firm <s>maitrī</s>. Because of the purity of own-nature, it is pure <s>maitrī</s>. Because of equality of intention, it is <s>maitrī</s> of equanimity. Because of destroying enemies, it is <s>arhat</s> <s>maitrī</s>. Because of uninterrupted ripening of beings, it is <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>maitrī</s>. Because of further realization of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), it is <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>maitrī</s>. Because of awakening beings from sleep, it is <s>Buddha</s> <s>maitrī</s>. Because of self-awakening, it is self-arisen <s>maitrī</s>. Because of equal flavor, it is <s>bodhi</s> <s>maitrī</s>. Because of abandoning attachment and aversion, it is <s>maitrī</s> without imputation. Because of illuminating the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, it is <s>maitrī</s> of great compassion. Because of contemplating <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self), it is unwearying <s>maitrī</s>. Because of no closed fist of a teacher, it is <s>maitrī</s> of <s>Dharma</s>-giving. Because of caring for beings of poor morality, it is <s>maitrī</s> of moral conduct. Because of protecting both self and others, it is <s>maitrī</s> of patience. Because of bearing the burden of all beings, it is <s>maitrī</s> of vigor. Because of non-savoring, it is <s>maitrī</s> of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). Because of not accomplishing prematurely, it is <s>maitrī</s> of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Because of showing the universal door, it is <s>maitrī</s> of skillful means. Because of purity of intention, it is <s>maitrī</s> without deception. Because of having no cause for regret, it is steadfast <s>maitrī</s>. Because of being without blemish, it is <s>maitrī</s> of higher intention. Because of being without pretense, it is <s>maitrī</s> without deceit. Because of establishing the bliss of the <s>Buddha</s>, it is blissful <s>maitrī</s>. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that indeed is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s <s>maitrī</s>."

body.text:
abravīt- "tasya mahākaruṇā kim?" āha- "yadyat kuśalamūlaṃ syāt kuśalamūlaṃ syāt, (tat) sarvasattvebhya utsṛjati" / abravīt- "tasya mahāmuditā kim?" / āha- "yaḥ (sa) dānāt prītimanobhūto 'vipratisāraḥ" / abravīt- "tasyopekṣā kim?" āha- "yaḥ (sa) ubhayārthotpādaḥ" / -
abravīt- "saṃsārabhayabhītena ki pratisartavyam?" āha- "saṃsārabhayabhītena maṃjuśrīrbodhisattvena buddhamāhātmyaṃ pratisartavyam" /
body.translated_text:
He asked: "What is his great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>)?" He replied: "Whatever roots of merit he may have, he relinquishes them all to all beings." He asked: "What is his great joy (<s>mahāmuditā</s>)?" He replied: "He who is delighted in mind from giving, free from regret." He asked: "What is his equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>)?" He replied: "He who generates benefit for both."
He asked: "What should one who is frightened by the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> take refuge in?" He replied: "<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> frightened by the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> should take refuge in the greatness of the <s>Buddha</s>."

body.text: āha- "buddhamahātmye sthātukāmena kutra sthātavyam?" āha- "buddhamahātmye sthātukāmena sarvasattvasamatāyāṃ sthātavyam /" āha- "sarvasattvasamatāyāṃ sthātukāmena kutra sthātavyam" āha- "sarvasattvasamatāyāṃ sthātukāmena sarvasattvapramokṣāya sthātavyam" /
body.translated_text: He asked: "One who wishes to abide in the <s>Buddha</s>'s greatness—where should he abide?" He replied: "One who wishes to abide in the <s>Buddha</s>'s greatness should abide in the equality of all beings." He asked: "One who wishes to abide in the equality of all beings—where should he abide?" He replied: "One who wishes to abide in the equality of all beings should abide for the sake of liberating all beings."

body.text: abravīt- "sarvasattvapramokṣāya kartukāmena kathaṃ karaṇīyam?" āha- "sarvasattvapramokṣāya kartukāmena kleśapramokṣaḥ karaṇīyaḥ" / abravīt- "kleśaprahātukāmena kathaṃ prayoktavyam?" āha- "kleśaprahātukāmena yoniśaḥ prayoktavyam" / abravīt- "kathaṃ prayujyamāno yoniśaḥ prayujyate?" āha- "anutpādānirodhayoḥ prayogo hi yoniśaḥ prayogo 'sti" / abravīt- "anudayaḥ kim, kim anirodhaḥ?" āha- "akuśalānudayaśca kuśalānirodhaḥ" / abravīt- "kuśalākuśalamūlaṃ kim?" āha- "satkāya -(dṛṣṭi) rmūlam" / abravīt- "satkāya - (dṛṣṭi) mūlaṃ kim?" āha- "satkāya - (dṛṣṭi) mūlaṃ rāgaḥ" / abravīt- "ki rāgamūlam?" -āha- "rāgasya mūlaṃ hyabhūtaparikalpaḥ" /
body.translated_text: He asked: "One who wishes to work for the liberation of all beings—how should he act?" He replied: "One who wishes to work for the liberation of all beings should accomplish liberation from <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)." He asked: "One who wishes to abandon afflictions—how should he practice?" He replied: "One who wishes to abandon afflictions should practice properly (<s>yoniśas</s>)." He asked: "How does one practicing properly practice?" He replied: "The practice of non-arising and non-ceasing—that is the proper practice." He asked: "What is non-arising? What is non-ceasing?" He replied: "The non-arising of the unwholesome and the non-ceasing of the wholesome." He asked: "What is the root of the wholesome and unwholesome?" He replied: "The view of the perishable body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) is the root." He asked: "What is the root of the view of the perishable body?" He replied: "Attachment (<s>rāga</s>) is the root of the view of the perishable body." He asked: "What is the root of attachment?" He replied: "The root of attachment is unreal conceptualization (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>)."

body.text: abravīt- "abhūtaparikalpasya kiṃ mūlam?" āha- "abhūtaparikalpasya hi) viparyastā saṃjñā mūlam" / āha- "viparyastāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ ki mūlam??" -(āha- "viparyastāyāḥsaṃjñāyā) apratiṣṭhānaṃ mūlam" / āha- "apratiṣṭhāyāḥ kiṃ mūlam?" āha- "yanmaṃjuśrīrapratiṣṭhānaṃ, na tasya kiṃcinmūlam / iti hyapratiṣṭhānamūlapratiṣṭhitāḥ sarvadharmāḥ" /
body.translated_text: He asked: "What is the root of unreal conceptualization?" He replied: "Perverted perception (<s>viparyasta saṃjñā</s>) is the root of unreal conceptualization." He asked: "What is the root of perverted perception?" He replied: "Groundlessness is the root of perverted perception." He asked: "What is the root of groundlessness?" He replied: "<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that which is groundless—it has no root whatsoever. Thus indeed all <s>dharmas</s> are established on the root of groundlessness."

body.text: atha tasmin gṛhe kasyacitsthānasya devī, teṣāṃ bodhisattvānām mahāsattvānāmimāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ śrutvā, hṛṣṭodagrā cāttamanāḥ, audārikamātmabhāvamabhisaṃdṛśya, divyapuṣpaistān bodhisattvān mahāsattvāṃśca mahāśrāvakānabhikirati sma / yāni ca bodhisattvānāṃ kāye 'bhyavakīrṇāni puṣpāni, tāni bhūmau prapatanti sma / yāni mahāśrāvakānāṃ kāya āpannāni puṣpāni, tāni tatraiva prasaktāni bhūmau na prapatanti sma / tataste mahāśrāvakā ṛddhividhiprātihāryeṇa puṣpānyādhunanti sma, api kho pana tāni na prapatanti sma /
body.translated_text: Now, in that house there was a certain goddess who, having heard this <s>Dharma</s> teaching of those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, was delighted, joyful, and elated. Manifesting an exalted form, she scattered divine flowers upon those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> and great <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples). The flowers that fell upon the bodies of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> fell to the ground. But the flowers that fell upon the bodies of the great <s>śrāvakas</s> stuck there and did not fall to the ground. Then those great <s>śrāvakas</s> tried to shake off the flowers by means of their miraculous powers, but even so the flowers did not fall off.

body.text: atha sā devayāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat- "bhadanta śāriputra, imāni puṣpānyādhūya kiṃ kariṣyasi?" āha- "devi, imāni puṣpāni na yujyante; tasmādimāni puṣpāni riṃcāmi" / devyabravīt - "bhadanta śāriputra, evammā vādīḥ / tat kasya hetoḥ? yujyanta imāni puṣpāni / tat kasya hetoḥ? yatastāni puṣpāni nirvikalpāni / nirvikalpeṣu śāriputraḥ sthavira eva kalpayati ca vikalpayati / bhadanta śāriputra, yat svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajitāḥ kalpayanti ca vikalpayanti, tadhi na yujyate / sthavīre kalpayati ca vikalpayati, yannirvikalpaṃ tadhi yujyate /
body.translated_text: Then that goddess said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, why do you try to shake off these flowers?" He replied: "Goddess, these flowers are not proper for a monk; therefore I cast them off." The goddess said: "Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, do not speak thus. What is the reason? These flowers are indeed proper. What is the reason? These flowers are free from conceptual discrimination. It is the elder <s>Śāriputra</s> himself who discriminates and conceptualizes. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, for those who have gone forth in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, to discriminate and conceptualize—that is not proper. It is the elder who discriminates and conceptualizes. That which is free from discrimination—that is proper.

body.text: "paśya, bhadanta śāriputra-tathā hi kalpavikalpaprahāṇakāraṇād bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ kāye puṣpāni na sajjanti / tadyathāpi nāma bhayajātīyamanuṣye 'manuṣyairavatāro labhyate, evameva saṃsārabhayabhīteṣu rūpaśabda gandharasaspraṣṭavyebhyo 'vatāraḥ pratilabhyaḥ / ye sarvasaṃskārakleśabhayāpagatāḥ, tebhyo rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāni ki kariṣyanti? yeṣu vāsanāprahīṇā, teṣu puṣpa (anya) pi sajjanti; yeṣāṃ tu vāsanā prahīṇā, teṣāṃ kāye puṣpa(ani) na sajjanti / tasmāt sarvavāsanāvighātakānāṃ kāye puṣpānya saktāni" /
body.translated_text: "Look, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>—because the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> have abandoned discrimination and conceptualization, the flowers do not stick to their bodies. Just as, for example, non-human beings gain access to a person who is by nature fearful, in the same way, for those who are afraid of the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>, form, sound, smell, taste, and touch gain access. For those who have transcended the fear of all conditioned afflictions, what will form, sound, smell, taste, and touch do to them? In those in whom latent tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>) are not abandoned, the flowers stick; but in those in whom latent tendencies are abandoned, the flowers do not stick to their bodies. Therefore the flowers do not stick to the bodies of those who have destroyed all latent tendencies."

body.text: tata āyuṣmāṃśāriputrastāṃ devīmetadavocat- "devi, tvamimaṃ gehaṃ praviśya kiyacciracaritam?" devyāha- "sthaviro vimokṣaṃ praviṣṭo yāvat, (tac-)ciram" / abravīt- "devi, tvamasmin gehe sthitvā, aciraṃ dṛṣṭā" / āha- "sthaviro vimokṣaṃ praviṣṭaḥ kiyacciram?"-atha sthavirastūṣṇībhūto 'bhūt / āha- "mahāprajñāvatāmagryaḥ sthaviraḥ kasmānmaunī cedānīṃ sahasā praśnanna pariharasi?" abravīt- "devi, vimokṣa'nabhilāpyaśca sa yathā vaktavyaḥ, (tan) na jānāmi" / āha- "yāni svavireṇākṣarāṇyuktāni, sarvāṇi tāni vimokṣalakṣaṇāni / tat kasya hetoḥ? yo vimokṣaḥ, sa hyanantaragataśca na bahirdhā nobhayaścānupalabdhaḥ / evameva tānyakṣarāṇyanantaragatāni na ca bahirdhā nobhayāni cānupalabdhāni / tasmāt, bhadanta śāriputra, akṣarāpakarṣaṇena vimokṣammāprativedayasva / tat kasya hetoḥ? yataḥ sarvadharmasama(tā)ryavimokṣaḥ" / abravīt - "devi, rāgadveṣamohāpagateṣu vimokṣa nanu nāsti?" devyāha- "'rāgadveṣamohāpagateṣu vimokṣa' iti sa hyabhimānikebhya upadeśaḥ / ye 'nabhimānikāḥ, tebhyo hi rāgadveṣamohasvabhāvatā vimokṣaḥ" /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to that goddess: "Goddess, how long have you been in this house since you entered?" The goddess replied: "As long as the elder has entered liberation—that long." He said: "Goddess, you have been in this house a very long time." She replied: "How long has the elder entered liberation?" Then the elder became silent. She said: "The elder, who is foremost among those of great wisdom—why are you now suddenly silent and do not answer the question?" He replied: "Goddess, liberation is inexpressible; therefore I do not know how to speak of it." She said: "All the syllables spoken by the elder—all of them have the characteristics of liberation. What is the reason? Liberation is neither found within, nor without, nor in between. Likewise, those syllables are neither found within, nor without, nor in between. Therefore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, do not indicate liberation by withdrawing from syllables. What is the reason? Because the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> is itself liberation."

body.text: athāyuṣmāṃśāriputrastāṃ devimetadavocat- "sādhu, devi; ki prāpya, ki sākṣātkṛtya tvamevaṃpratibhānavatī?" / āha- "bhadanta śāriputra, mayā na kiñcit prāptaṃ vā sākṣātkṛtaṃ vā / ato me pratibhāna īdṛśaḥ / yeṣāmevam 'asmābhi prāptañca sākṣātkṛtam' iti, te hi svākhyātadharmavinaye ''timānikā ucyante" / abravīt- "devi, tvaṃ ki śrāvakayānīyā pratyekabuddhayānīyā vā mahāyānīyā vā?" āha- "śrāvakayānaṃ darśayatī, ahaṃ śrāvakayāninī / dvādaśa(aṃga) pratītyasamutpādeadvāreṇāvatāraṇen-āhaṃ pratyekabuddhayāninī / anutsṛṣṭāyāmmahākaruṇāyām ahammahāyānīyā / "bhadanta śāriputra, api tu khalu punaryathā campakavane praviṣṭe, eraṇḍagandho na ghrāyate, campakavane praviṣṭe 'pi kho pana campakagandho ghrāyate; evameva, bhadanta śāriputra, asmin buddhadharmaguṇagandhopete gehe vihāriṇā śrāvakapratyekabuddhagandho na ghrāyate / "bhadanta śāriputra, ye śakrabrahmalokapāladevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuagaruḍakiṃnaramahoragā asmin gehe niviṣṭāḥ, tepayasya satpuruṣasya dharma śrutvā, buddhadharmaguṇagandhena bodhicittamutpādya prakrāntāḥ / "bhadanta śāriputra, asmin gehe dvādaśa varṣāṇi mahāmaitrīmahākaruṇā samarpitāṃ cācintyabuddhadharmasamprapuktāṃ (kathāṃ) sthāpayitvā, śrāvakapratyekabuddhasahagatāṃ kathāṃ purā nāśrauṣam / bhadanta śāriputra, asmin gṛhe 'ṣṭavidhā āścaryadbhutaprāptā dharmāḥ satatasamitamābhāsaṃ gacchanti / katame 'ṣṭau?
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to that goddess: 'Excellent, O goddess! What have you attained, what have you directly realized, that you have such eloquence?' She said: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, I have neither attained anything nor directly realized anything. Therefore my eloquence is such. Those who think "we have attained and directly realized" — they are called conceited in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.' He said: 'Goddess, do you belong to the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s>, or the <s>Mahāyāna</s>?' She said: 'When I show the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, I am a <s>Śrāvakayānin</s>. By entering through the door of the twelve-fold dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), I am a <s>Pratyekabuddhayānin</s>. Since I have not abandoned great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), I am a <s>Mahāyānin</s>. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, moreover, just as when one enters a campaka grove, the smell of castor oil is not perceived, but rather the fragrance of campaka flowers is perceived — just so, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, for one dwelling in this house that is filled with the fragrance of <s>Buddha-dharma</s> qualities, the scent of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> is not perceived. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, world-protectors, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> who have entered this house — they all, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> from this good man, depart having generated <s>bodhicitta</s> through the fragrance of <s>Buddha-dharma</s> qualities. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in this house for twelve years, setting aside discourse connected with great loving-kindness, great compassion, and inconceivable <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, I have never before heard discourse connected with <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in this house, eight wonderful and marvelous <s>dharmas</s> constantly shine forth. What are these eight?

body.text: "asmin gṛhe satatasamitaṃ suvarṇavarṇaprabhā / ato rātrīdivanna prajñāyate / asmin gṛhe candrasūryau na ca dṛśyete / ayaṃ prathama āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'In this house there is constantly a radiance of golden color. Therefore, neither night nor day can be discerned. In this house, neither the moon nor the sun is seen. This is the first wonderful and marvelous quality.

body.text: "punaraparaṃ, bhadanta śāriputra, ye praviśanti idaṃ gṛhaṃ, teṣāṃ samanantarapraviṣṭānāṃ sarvakleśā na bādhante / ayaṃ dvitīya āścaryādbhūto dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, whoever enters this house — as soon as they enter, all their <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) no longer trouble them. This is the second wonderful and marvelous quality.

body.text: "punaraparaṃ, bhadanta śāriputra, asmin gṛhe sadā śakrabrahmalokapālāśca sarvabuddhakṣetrāgatā bodhisattvā avirahitāḥ / ayaṃ tṛtīya āścaryādbhūto dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in this house, <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, world-protectors, and <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have come from all <s>Buddha</s>-fields are always present without absence. This is the third wonderful and marvelous quality.

body.text: "punaraparaṃ, bhadanta śāriputra, asmin gṛhe satatasamitaṃ dharmāvadhoṣaṇañca ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktā kathā cāvaivartikadharmacakrakathā 'virahitāḥ / ayaṃ caturtha āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in this house, there are constantly the proclamation of the <s>Dharma</s>, discourse connected with the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), and discourse on the irreversible turning of the <s>Dharma</s> wheel — always present without absence. This is the fourth wonderful and marvelous quality.

body.text: "punaraparaṃ, bhadanta śāriputra, asmin gṛhe sadā divyamānuṣyadundubhisaṅgītavādyaṃ krīyate; tebhyo dundubhibhyo buddhadharma(sya) āprameyabidhighoṣaḥ sarvakāleṣūtpadyate / āyaṃ pañcama āścaryādbhūto dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in this house, divine and human drums, songs, and music are always being played; and from those drums, the immeasurable sound proclaiming the <s>Buddha-dharma</s> arises at all times. This is the fifth wonderful and marvelous quality.

body.text: "punaraparaṃ, bhadanta śāriputra, asmin gṛhe sarvaratnasampūrṇāścaturakṣayamahānidhayo vidyante / tadanubhāvena sarvairdaridraiśca vyasanibhiḥ prapannam, (mahānidhi-) kuṇḍamapi tvakṣayam / ayaṃ ṣaṣṭha āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in this house there are four great inexhaustible treasure-stores filled with all jewels. By their power, all the poor and afflicted are provided for, and the treasure-vessel itself is inexhaustible. This is the sixth wonderful and marvelous quality.

body.text: "punaraparaṃ, bhadanta śāriputra, asmin gṛhe tathāgatāḥ śākyamuniścāmitābhaścākṣobhyaśca ratnaśrīśca ratnārciśca ratnacandraśca ratnavyūhaśca duṣpahaśca sarvārthasiddhaśca mahāratnaśca sihaprasiddhiśa sihasvaraścādayo daśadikṣvaparimāṇatathāgatā asya satpuruṣasya sahacittamātreṇa samāgacchanti cāgatāstathāgataguhyannāma dharmamukhapraveśaṃ nidarśya pratigacchanti / ayaṃ saptama āścaryādbhūto dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in this house, <s>Tathāgatas</s> — <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Amitābha</s>, <s>Akṣobhya</s>, <s>Ratnaśrī</s>, <s>Ratnārci</s>, <s>Ratnacandra</s>, <s>Ratnavyūha</s>, <s>Duṣpraha</s>, <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, <s>Mahāratna</s>, <s>Siṃhaprasiddhi</s>, <s>Siṃhasvara</s>, and others — immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s> from the ten directions come at the mere arising of a thought of this good man, and having come, they reveal the <s>Dharma</s> entrance called the Secret of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and then depart. This is the seventh wonderful and marvelous quality.

body.text: "punaraparaṃ, bhadanta śāriputra, asmin gṛhe sarvadevaveśmavyūhāścasarvabuddhakṣetraguṇālaṅkārā ābhāsaṃ gacchanti / ayamaṣṭama āścaryādbhūto dharmaḥ / "bhadanta śāriputra, asmin gṛhe teṣvaṣṭāsvāścaryādbhuteṣu dharmeṣvābhāsaṃ gacchatsu cedṛśācintyadharme dṛśyamāne, kaḥ śrāvakadharmamicchet?" abravīt- "devi, yadi te strībhāvāt syādvikāraḥ, kimaparādhaḥ?" āha- "yāvad dvādaśa varṣāṇi strībhāvamme mṛgyamāṇā, (so)- 'dyāpi (mayā) nopalabhyate / bhadanta śāriputra, tasyai māyākāreṇa nirmitāyai striyai evaṃ 'yadi te strībhāvāt syādvikāraḥ, kimaparādha?' ityukte, tat ki kathayeta?" abravīt- "tatra kicitsaṃpariniṣpannannāsti" / āha- "bhadanta śāriputra, evameva sarvadharmeṣvapariniṣpanneṣu ca māyānirmāṇasvabhāveṣu, tvaṃ 'yadi strībhāvāt syādvikāraḥ, kimaparādha?' iti (pṛcchan)-tat ki manyase?" atha sā devyetādṛśādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitābhūt, yathā śāriputraḥ sthaviro yādṛśa sā devī tādṛśā dṛśyate sma; sā devyapi yādṛśaḥ śāriputraḥ, sthavirastādṛśo dṛśyate sma / tataḥ sā śāriputrasya rūpamāpannā devī taṃ devīrūpāpannaṃ śāriputramevam- "bhadanta śāriputra, yadi strībhāvāt syādvikāraḥ, kimaparādha?" iti pṛcchati sma / devīrūpāpannaḥ śāriputra etadavocat- "mama puruṣarūpasyāntarhitasya, strīkāyāpanno yo vikārastanna jānāmi" / āha- "yadi sthaviraḥ strīrūpāt prativikārasya samarthaḥ syāt, sarvāḥ striyaḥ strībhāvāt parivarteran / yathā sthaviraḥ strī-(rūpe) dṛśyate, tathā sarvāḥ striyo 'pi strīrūpeṣu dṛśyamānāḥ stryabhāvāt strīrūpeṣu dṛśyante / tato bhagavatā 'sarve dharmāḥ strīpuruṣābhāvā iti saṃghāya bhāṣītam" /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in this house, the arrays of all the celestial palaces and the ornamental qualities of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields shine forth. This is the eighth wonderful and marvelous quality. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, when these eight wonderful and marvelous qualities constantly shine forth in this house, and such inconceivable <s>dharmas</s> are seen, who would wish for the <s>dharma</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s>?' He said: 'Goddess, if you could transform from your female state, what would be wrong [with that]?' She said: 'For twelve years I have sought my female nature and even today I cannot find it. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, if one were to say to a woman created by a magician, "If you could transform from your female state, what would be wrong?" — what would she reply?' He said: 'Nothing whatsoever is established there.' She said: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, just so, when all <s>dharmas</s> are unestablished and of the nature of magical illusion and emanation, why do you think "If you could transform from your female state, what would be wrong?"' Then that goddess, by such a supernatural transformation, caused the elder <s>Śāriputra</s> to appear in the form of the goddess, and the goddess herself appeared in the form of <s>Śāriputra</s>. Then the goddess, having assumed <s>Śāriputra</s>'s form, asked that <s>Śāriputra</s>, who had assumed the goddess's form: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, if you could transform from your female state, what would be wrong?' <s>Śāriputra</s>, having assumed the goddess's form, said: 'My male form has disappeared, and I have obtained a woman's body — I do not understand this transformation.' She said: 'If the elder were capable of transforming from the female form, then all women could transform from their female state. Just as the elder is seen in female form, so too all women, though seen in female forms, are seen in female forms due to the non-existence of femaleness. Therefore, the Blessed One declared to the <s>Saṅgha</s>: "All <s>dharmas</s> are devoid of male and female."'

body.text:
atha sā devī tadadhiṣṭhānamutsṛjati sma, āyuṣmāṃśca śāriputraḥ punaḥ svarūpopasaṃhito 'bhūt / atha sā devī śāriputrametadavocat- "bhadanta śāriputra, kva te strīputtalī?" abravīt- "(sā) mayā na ca kṛtā na cāpi vikṛtā / āha- "evameva sarvadharmā apyakṛtāścāvikṛtāḥ / yadakṛtaṃcāvikṛtaṃca-tadhi buddhavacam" / abravīt- "devī, itaścyutvā kutropapatsyase?" āha- "yatra tathāgatanirmāṇānyutpadyante, tatrāhamapyupapatsye" / abravīt- "tathāgatanirmāṇeṣu na bhavataścyutpattī" / āha- "sarve dharmāśca tathaiva cyutyupattyapagatāḥ" /
abravīt- "devi, keva cireṇa tvaṃ bodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase?" āha- "yadā, sthavira, pṛthagjanadharmasaṃpanno bhaviṣyasi, tadāpi bodhimabhisambuddhāmi" / abravīt- "devi, (yad-) ahaṃ pṛthagjanadharmasaṃpanno bhaveyam, tadasthānam" / āha- "bhadanta śāriputra, evameva(yad-) ahamapi bodhimabhisaṃbudhyāmi, tadasthānam / tat kasya hetoḥ? bodhirasthāne pratiṣṭhitā; ato 'sthāne na kaścidabhisaṃbuddhati" /
body.translated_text:
Then that goddess released that supernatural transformation, and the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> was restored to his own form. Then that goddess said to <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, where is your female puppet?' He said: 'It was neither made by me nor was it transformed.' She said: 'Just so, all <s>dharmas</s> too are neither made nor transformed. That which is neither made nor transformed — that is the <s>Buddha</s>'s word.' He said: 'Goddess, when you pass away from here, where will you be reborn?' She said: 'Wherever the emanations of the <s>Tathāgata</s> arise, there I too shall be reborn.' He said: 'But <s>Tathāgata</s> emanations have neither passing away nor rebirth.' She said: 'All <s>dharmas</s> too are likewise free from passing away and rebirth.'
He said: 'Goddess, how long will it take for you to attain <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)?' She said: 'Elder, when you become endowed with the qualities of a common person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), then I too will attain <s>bodhi</s>.' He said: 'Goddess, that I should become endowed with the qualities of a common person — that is impossible.' She said: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, just so, that I too should attain <s>bodhi</s> — that is impossible. Why? Because <s>bodhi</s> is established in the impossible; therefore no one attains it from the impossible.'

body.text: śāriputraḥ sthaviro 'vocat- "tathāgatenākhyātam- 'gaṃgānadīvālukāsamāstathāgatā abhisaṃbuddhāḥ, abhisaṃbudhyantyabhisaṃbhotsyanta' iti" / devyāha- "bhadanta śāriputra, 'atītānāgatapratyutpannā buddhā iti tadhyakṣaragaṇanāsaṃketādhivacanam / atītānāgatapratyutpanneṣu buddheṣvabhūteṣu, bodhistryadhvasamatikrāntā / sthaviraḥ kim arhattvalābhī?" abravīt- "aprāptihetorlābhī" / āha- "evamevābhisaṃbodhyabhāvahetorabhisaṃbodhiḥ" / tato licchavirvimalakīrtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputraṃ sthavirametadavocat- "bhadanta śāriputra, iyaṃ devī buddhānāṃ dvinavatikoṭinayutāni paryupāsya, abhijñājñānavikrīḍitā praṇidhānasaṃbhūtā kṣāntilābhinī, avaivartika- saṃprasthitā sattvaparipācanārthāya praṇidhānavaśena yatheṣṭaṃ tathāvasthitā" /
body.translated_text: The elder <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared: "<s>Tathāgatas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> have attained awakening, are attaining awakening, and will attain awakening."' The goddess said: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, "<s>Buddhas</s> of the past, future, and present" — that is a conventional designation through syllables and counting. In the non-existence of <s>Buddhas</s> of the past, future, and present, <s>bodhi</s> transcends the three times. Elder, have you attained the fruit of <s>arhatship</s>?' He said: 'I have attained it through the cause of non-attainment.' She said: 'Just so, awakening comes through the cause of non-awakening.' Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to the venerable elder <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, this goddess has attended upon ninety-two <s>koṭi-nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. She sports with the superknowledges and knowledges, is born of her vows, has attained patience, is set forth irreversibly, and abides as she wishes by the power of her vow for the purpose of ripening beings.'

body.text: 7 tathāgatagotram
body.translated_text: 7. The Lineage of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>Tathāgatagotram</s>)

body.text: tato maṃjuśrīkumārabhūto licchavi vimalakīrtimetadavocat- "kulaputra, atha katham bodhisattvo buddhadharmeṣu gati gacchati?" āha- 'maṃjuśrīḥ; yadā bodhisattvo 'gati gacchati tadā bodhisattvo buddhadharmeṣu gati gacchati" / abravīt- "bodhisattvasya āgatigamanaṃ kim?"
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful prince, said this to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: "Son of good family, how does a <s>bodhisattva</s> progress in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>?" He replied: "<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, when a <s>bodhisattva</s> progresses in non-progression, then the <s>bodhisattva</s> progresses in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>." He asked: "What is the <s>bodhisattva's</s> non-progressive progression?"

body.text:
āha- "yadā (bodhisattvaḥ) paṃcānantarīyāṇāṃ gatigāmī, vyāpādavihiṃsāpradveṣo 'pi na bhaviṣyanti / narakagatigāmī (saḥ), paraṃ tu sarvakleśavirajāḥ / tiryaggatigāmī tu (sa) maurkhyāndhakārāpagataḥ / (so) 'suragatigāmi ca mānamadadarpavigataḥ; yamalokagatigāmī sarvapuṇyajñānasaṃbhāropāttavān; anijyārūpyagatigāmī, paraṃ tu tadgatinna samavakramati / "(sa) rāgagatigāmi ca sarvakāmasaṃbhogavīratarāgaḥ; dveṣagatigāmī sarva sattvāpratihataḥ; mohagatigāmī sarvadharmeṣu prajñānidhyapticittasamarpitaḥ / "mātsaryagatigāmī kāyajīvitanirapekṣaḥ (sa) ādhyātmikabāhyāni vastū(-ny-) utsṛjati / duḥśīlagatigāmī, paraṃ tvalpāvadye 'pi bhayadarśī (sa) sarvadhūtaguṇasaṃlekheṣu santiṣṭhate; vyāpādakhilapratighagatigāmī cātyantāvyāpanno maitrīvihārī; kausīdyagatigāmi cāpratiprasrabdho vīryamārabhamāṇaḥ sarvakuśalamūlaparyeṣaṇābhiyukto bhavati / indriyavyabhicāragatigāmi svabhāvasamāpanno 'moghadhyānaḥ, dauṣprajñagatigāmī prajñāpāramitāgatimupasaṃkramya, (sa) sarvalaukikalokottaraśāstrapaṇḍitaḥ / "kuhanalapanākāragatigāmī ca sandhyābhāṣyeṣu kuśalaḥ (sa) upāyakauśalyacaryāniryātaḥ; mānagati darśayan (sa) sarva lokasetuvedikā bhavati, kleśagatigāmī, paraṃ tvatyantasaṃkleśarahitaḥ svabhāvapariśuddhaḥ / "māragatigāmī ca sarvabuddhadharmeṣvaparapraṇeyaḥ; śrāvakagatigāmi (sa) sattvāṃstvaśrutadharma śrāvayati, pratyekabuddhagatigāmī sarvasattvaparipācanārthammahākaruṇādutpannaḥ, daridragatigāmī tvakṣayaparibhogaratnapāṇiḥ; upahatendriyagatigāmi (sa) tvabhirūpo lakṣaṇasamalaṃkṛtaḥ, hīnakulīnagatigāmī puṇyajñānasaṃcayena tathāgatavaṃśāt prajāyate; durbaladurvarṇamandagatigāmī darśanīyo nārāyaṇapratirūpakakāyalābhī / "sarvasattvebhya āturaduḥkhacaryā deśayamāno maraṇabhayasamatikrānttas(sa) sumārita(bhayaḥ); paribhogagatigāmī sarvāṇveṣaṇarahito 'nityatāsaṃjñāyām bahupratyavekṣaṇaḥ, bodhisattvo 'ntaḥpurānekarasān deśayamānaḥ ki tu vivekacārī kāmakardamottīrṇaḥ / dhātvāyatanagatigāmī(sa) dhāraṇīipratilabdho nānāpratibhānavibhūṣitaḥ;
tīrthikagatigāmī tīrthyaḥ (sa) na bhavati, sarvalokagatigāmi sarvagtyapratinirvartī, nirvāṇagatigāmī saṃsāraprabandhaṃ notsṛjati / maṃjuśrīḥ, ityevaṃ bodhisattvo 'gati gacchan buddhadharmeṣu gati gacchati" / atha licchavirvimalakīrtirmañjuśrīkumārabhūtametadavocat- "mañjuśrīḥ, ki tathāgatagotram?" abravīt- "kulaputra, satkāyo hi gotraṃ tathāgatānām / avidyābhavatṛṣṇā hi gotram / rāgadveṣamohacaturviparyāsa pañcanīvaraṇaṣaḍāyatanasaptavijñānasthitya-aṣṭamithyātvanavāghāta-vastu daśākuśalakarmapathā hi gotram / kulaputra, idaṃ tathāgatagotram; saṃkṣepāt, kulaputra, dvāṣaṣṭirdṛṣṭigatāni hi tathāgatagotram" / āha- "mañjuśrīḥ, kasmāt samanvāhṛtyaidbhāṣase?" abravīt- "kulaputra, asaṃskṛtadarśanasamavrakrāntisthānenānuttarasamyaksambodhicittotpādo 'śakyaḥ / kleśākarasaṃskṛtasthānasatyādarśanenānuttarasamyaksambodhicittotpādaḥ śakya /
body.translated_text: He replied: "When the <s>bodhisattva</s> goes the course of the five heinous acts (<s>pañcānantarīya</s>), yet there will be no malice, harm, or hatred. He goes the course of hell, yet is free from all defilements (<s>kleśas</s>). He goes the course of animals, yet is free from the darkness of ignorance. He goes the course of <s>asuras</s>, yet is free from pride, intoxication, and arrogance. He goes the course of <s>Yama's</s> realm, yet has acquired the equipment of all merit and knowledge. He goes the course of the immovable and formless [realms], yet does not enter into them. He goes the course of passion (<s>rāga</s>), yet is the most dispassionate, free from all desire-enjoyment. He goes the course of hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), yet is unobstructed toward all beings. He goes the course of delusion (<s>moha</s>), yet his mind is devoted to the contemplation of wisdom in all <s>dharmas</s>. He goes the course of avarice (<s>mātsarya</s>), yet disregarding body and life, he relinquishes all internal and external possessions. He goes the course of immorality, yet seeing danger even in slight offenses, he abides in all the observances of ascetic qualities. He goes the course of malice, hostility, and aversion, yet is utterly free from malice and dwells in loving-kindness. He goes the course of laziness, yet without relaxing, exerting vigor, he is devoted to seeking all roots of merit. He goes the course of distracted faculties, yet is naturally accomplished in unerring meditation. He goes the course of poor wisdom, yet having approached the course of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), he is learned in all worldly and supramundane sciences. He goes the course of deceit and flattery, yet is skilled in conventional expressions and accomplished in the practice of skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>). Displaying the course of pride, he becomes a bridge and railing for all the world. Going the course of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), yet he is utterly free from all defilement, pure by nature. Going the course of <s>Māra</s>, yet he cannot be led by others in all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. Going the course of <s>śrāvakas</s>, he causes beings to hear the <s>Dharma</s> they have not heard. Going the course of <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, great compassion has arisen in him for the purpose of ripening all beings. Going the course of poverty, yet his hand holds inexhaustible jewels of enjoyment. Going the course of impaired faculties, yet he is handsome, adorned with the marks. Going the course of low birth, yet through the accumulation of merit and knowledge, he is born from the lineage of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Going the course of weakness, ugliness, and dullness, yet he is beautiful and attains a body like that of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. While showing the conduct of illness and suffering to all beings, he has transcended the fear of death. Going the course of material possessions, yet he is free from all seeking and greatly contemplates the perception of impermanence. The <s>bodhisattva</s>, while displaying the many pleasures of the inner palace, is a practitioner of solitude, having risen above the mire of desire. Going the course of elements and sense-bases, he has obtained <s>dhāraṇī</s> and is adorned with various forms of eloquence. Going the course of non-Buddhist teachers, yet he does not become one of them. Going the course of all worlds, yet he does not return to any destiny. Going the course of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, yet he does not abandon the continuity of <s>saṃsāra</s>. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, thus the <s>bodhisattva</s>, going the non-course, progresses in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>." Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said this to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: "<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what is the <s>Tathāgata's</s> lineage (<s>gotra</s>)?" He said: "Son of good family, <s>satkāya</s> (the view of the existing body) is the lineage of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), craving for existence (<s>bhavatṛṣṇā</s>) is the lineage. Passion, hatred, delusion, the four perversions, the five hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>), the six sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), the seven stations of consciousness (<s>vijñānasthiti</s>), the eight wrong [paths], the nine causes of anger (<s>āghātavastu</s>), and the ten unwholesome courses of action are the lineage. Son of good family, this is the <s>Tathāgata's</s> lineage. In brief, son of good family, the sixty-two [wrong] views are the <s>Tathāgata's</s> lineage." He asked: "<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, with what consideration do you say this?" He replied: "Son of good family, one who has entered the station of seeing the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) cannot generate the mind of <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). But from the station of seeing the conditioned realm, the mine of <s>kleśas</s>, the generation of the mind of supreme perfect awakening is possible.

body.text: "kulaputra, tadyathāpi nāma jāṃgala pradeśe kusumāni-utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkasaugandhīkāni notpadyante; paṃkapulina utpāditāni cet, kusumāni-utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkasaugandhikānyutpadyante / kulaputra, evamevāsaṃskṛtaniyataprāptisattvebhyo buddhadharmā notpadyante / kleśapaṃkapulinopapannasattvebhyo buddhadharmā utpadyate /
body.translated_text: "Son of good family, just as in a dry, barren land, flowers such as <s>utpala</s>, <s>padma</s>, <s>kumuda</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, and <s>saugandhika</s> lotuses do not grow; but when produced in muddy marshes, these flowers—<s>utpala</s>, <s>padma</s>, <s>kumuda</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, and <s>saugandhika</s>—do grow. Son of good family, just so, <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> do not arise in beings who have attained the certainty of the unconditioned. <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> arise in beings born in the muddy marshes of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).
