body.text: "tadyathāpi nāmākāśe bījanna virohati, bhuvi paraṃtu vartamānaṃ birohati; evamevāsaṃskṛtaniyataprāptisattvebhyo buddhadharmo notpadyate; sumerusamāṃ satkāyadṛṣṭimutpādya bodhicittamutpadyate tataśca buddhadharmā virohanti / "kulaputra, anena paryāyeṇa sarve kleśāstathāgatagotraṃ draṣṭavyāḥ / kulaputra, tadyathāpi nāma mahāsamudre 'praviṣṭe, anardhyaratnamanuprāptumaśakyam; evameva, kleśasāgare 'praviṣṭe, sarvajñatām tasmādutpādayitumaśakyam" / atha mahākāśyapaḥ sthaviro maṃjuśrīkumārabhūtāya sādhūkāramadāt- "sādhu, sādhu / maṃjuśrīḥ, idaṃ vacanaṃ suprabhāṣitam, iadaṃ tattvam / kleśā-s tathāgatagotram, asmadvidhebhyas-tu bodhicittotpādaśca buddhadharmamabhisamboddhuṃ kathaṃ śakyam? pañcānantarīyasaṃyogena hi bodhicittotpādaḥ śakyaśca buddhadharmā apyabhisambodhanīyāḥ / tadyathāpi nāma vikalendriyapuruṣāya pañca kāmaguṇā nirguṇāścāsamarthāḥ evameva parivarjitasarvasaṃyojanāya śrāvakāya sarve buddhadharmā nirguṇaścāsamarthā ḥ; tasmai pratyālambanamasamartham /
body.translated_text: "Just as seeds do not sprout in the sky, but they sprout when planted in the earth; even so, <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> do not arise in beings who have attained the certainty of the unconditioned. But by generating <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (the view of self-existence) as great as <s>Sumeru</s>, <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) arises, and from it the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> sprout. Son of good family, by this reasoning, all <s>kleśas</s> should be seen as the <s>Tathāgata's</s> lineage. Son of good family, just as without entering the great ocean, one cannot obtain priceless jewels; even so, without entering the ocean of <s>kleśas</s>, one cannot generate <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience)." Then the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> praised <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: "Excellent, excellent, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>! This word is well spoken; this is the truth. <s>Kleśas</s> are the <s>Tathāgata's</s> lineage. But for those like us, how can we generate <s>bodhicitta</s> and realize the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>? Only through connection with the five heinous acts can <s>bodhicitta</s> be generated and the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> realized. Just as for a man with impaired faculties, the five strands of sensual pleasure are without benefit and powerless; even so, for a <s>śrāvaka</s> who has abandoned all fetters, all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> are without benefit and powerless; reliance upon them is impossible for him.

body.text: "maṃjuśrīḥ, ataḥ pṛthagjanāstathāgate kṛtajñāḥ, ki tu śrāvakā akṛtajñāḥ / tat kasya hetoḥ? yadarthaṃ pṛthagjano buddhaguṇaśravaṇena triratnagotramanucchinnakaraṇārthamanuttarasamyaksambodhicittotpādaṃ karoti; śrāvakastu yāvajjīvam buddhadharmabalavaiśāradyāni śrutvāpyanuttarasamyaksambodhicittotpāde 'samarthaḥ" / tatassarvarūpasandarśano nāma bodhisattvastasyām parṣadi sannipatito niṣaṇṇo ('bhūt) / sa licchavi vimalakīrtimetadavocat- "gṛhapate, kva te mātāpitarau ca putradārāśca dāsadāsīkarmakarapauruṣeyāḥ? kva te mitrajñātisālohitāḥ? tava parivārāśvahastirathapattivāhanāni kva?" evamabravīt / licchavirvimalakīrtiḥ sarvarūpasandarśanaṃ bodhisatvamimā gāthā abhāṣata-
body.translated_text: "<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, therefore ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) are grateful to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, whereas <s>śrāvakas</s> are ungrateful. Why? Because an ordinary person, upon hearing the <s>Buddha's</s> qualities, generates the mind of <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) for the purpose of not severing the lineage of the Three Jewels; but a <s>śrāvaka</s>, even after hearing of the powers and fearlessnesses of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> throughout his entire life, is incapable of generating the mind of supreme perfect awakening." Then a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Sarvarūpasandarśana</s> (Revealer of All Forms), who had assembled and was seated in that assembly, said this to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: "Householder, where are your parents, sons, wife, male and female servants, workers, and attendants? Where are your friends, relatives, and kinsmen? Where are your retinue and vehicles—horses, elephants, chariots, and infantry?" Thus he spoke. The <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> addressed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvarūpasandarśana</s> in these verses:

children.translated_text: "For purified <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the mother is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom),
the father is <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means); from these two, the guides are born.
Delight in the <s>Dharma</s> is the wife; <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) are the two daughters.
The two truths of the <s>Dharma</s> are the sons; the dwelling is the mind intent upon the meaning of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness).
All <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are the disciples who obey their will.
The factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) are the friends; through them, supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) is born.

children.text: sahāyās- teṣāṃ sadāsaṃvāsāḥ santi ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Their constant companions and associates are the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections).
The means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) are the women's quarters; <s>Dharma</s>-teaching is their music and song.
Their garden is the factors of awakening in bloom,
the fruit is liberation and knowledge; the trees bear the great wealth of <s>Dharma</s>.
The liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>) are the ponds, filled with the water of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration),
covered with pure lotuses; those who bathe therein become immaculate.
The superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) are their vehicles; the unsurpassed <s>Mahāyāna</s> [is their great vehicle].
The charioteer is <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening); the path is the eightfold path of peace.
Their ornaments are the [thirty-two] marks and the eighty minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>).
Wholesome intention, modesty (<s>hrī</s>), and conscientiousness (<s>apatrāpya</s>) are their garments.
Wealthy with the true <s>Dharma</s>, their practice is <s>Dharma</s>-teaching,
pure practice is the great gain; their dedication is for the purpose of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening).

children.text: śayanañca bhavanti catvāri dhyānāni śuddhājīvena saṃstṛtāste /
children.translated_text: Their bed is the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations); they are sustained by pure livelihood.
Knowledge is their awakening; they are always accomplished in hearing.
Their food is the nectar of immortality; their drink is the flavor of liberation.
Pure intention is their bathing; moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>) is their fragrant ointment.
By destroying the enemy of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), they are unconquered heroes.
They have vanquished even the four <s>Māras</s>,
and have raised aloft the banner of the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening).
They intentionally display birth, yet they are unborn and unarisen.
They shine forth in all <s>kṣetras</s> (fields), like the risen sun.

children.text: vināyake (bhyaḥ) sarvapūjanaiḥ buddhānāṃ koṭyai pūjāṃ kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: Having made offerings of all kinds to the Guides, to <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>Buddhas</s>,
they never think: 'We must attend upon the <s>Buddhas</s>.'
Though they move through <s>buddhakṣetras</s> for the welfare of beings,
knowing the fields to be like space, they have no perception of beings in beings.
Whatever are the forms, sounds, and voices of all beings,
the fearless <s>bodhisattvas</s> display them all in a single instant.
Though they know the deeds of <s>Māra</s>, they follow <s>Māra</s>'s ways;
having reached the perfection of skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), they display all those activities.
They become aged and diseased, and display themselves as dead,
for the ripening of beings — playing with the <s>dharma</s> of illusion (<s>māyā</s>).
They display the conflagration at the end of a <s>kalpa</s>, burning up the earth,
to show impermanence to beings who hold the perception of permanence.
Invited by hundreds of thousands of beings in a single kingdom,
they eat in the homes of all, and direct all toward awakening.
Whatever mantras, sciences, or various crafts there may be,
in all of them they have reached perfection, bringing happiness to all beings.
However many heretical sects exist in the world, they go forth among them all;
having entered into their various views, they ripen those beings.

children.text: candrā vā bhonti sūryā vā śakrabrahmaprajeśvarāḥ /
children.translated_text: They become moons or suns, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, or lords of creatures;
they become water, fire, earth, and wind likewise.
During intermediate <s>kalpas</s> of disease, they become the supreme medicine;

children.text: yena te sattva mucyante sukhī bhonti anāmayāḥ //
children.translated_text: by which those beings are freed and become happy, free from illness.
During intermediate <s>kalpas</s> of famine, they become food and drink;
having removed hunger and thirst, they teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings.
During intermediate <s>kalpas</s> of weapons, they become meditators on loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>);
they establish many hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of beings in non-malice.
In the midst of great battles, they become impartial;
the <s>bodhisattvas</s> of great power promote peace and reconciliation.
Whatever hells there may be in the inconceivable <s>buddhakṣetras</s>,
they intentionally go there for the sake of the welfare of beings.
Whatever destinies are known among the animal realms,

children.text: sarvatra dharma deśenti tena ucyanti nāyakāḥ //
children.translated_text: they teach the <s>Dharma</s> everywhere — therefore they are called Guides.

children.text: kāmabhogāṃ (-śca) darśenti dhyānaṃ ca dhyāyināṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: They display sensual pleasures and <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) likewise for meditators;

children.text: vidhvastamāraṃ kurvanti avatāraṃ na denti te //
children.translated_text: they destroy <s>Māra</s> and do not give him an opening.

body.text: agnimadhye yathā padmamabhūtaṃ taṃ vinirdiśet //
body.translated_text: Like a lotus in the midst of fire, which is declared to be impossible,

body.text: evaṃ kāmāṃśca dhyānaṃ ca abhūtaṃ te vidarśayī //
body.translated_text: even so, they show both desires and <s>dhyāna</s> as impossible.

children.translated_text: They intentionally become courtesans, for the purpose of attracting men;

children.text: rāgāṅkuraṃ ca saṃlobhya buddhajñāne sthāpayanti te //
children.translated_text: having caught them with the hook of desire, they establish them in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.
They constantly become village headmen, caravan leaders, royal chaplains,
chief ministers and ministers, for the welfare of beings.

children.text: daridrāṇāṃ ca sattvānāṃ nidhānā bhonti akṣayāḥ /
children.translated_text: For impoverished beings, they become inexhaustible treasures;

children.text: teṣāṃ dānāani datvā ca bodhicittaṃ janenti te //
children.translated_text: having given gifts to them, they cause them to generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening).

body.text: mānastabdheṣu sattveṣu mahānagnā bhavanti te //
body.translated_text: Among beings stiffened with pride, they become great wrestlers,

body.text: sarvamānasamuddhataṃ bidhi prārthenti uttamām //
body.translated_text: uprooting all pride, they seek the supreme method.

children.translated_text: For beings overcome by fear, they always stand before them;

children.text: abhayaṃ teṣu datvā ca paripācenti bodhaye //
children.translated_text: having given them fearlessness, they ripen them toward awakening.
Having become <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) with the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), practicing <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy),
they establish beings in moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>), patience, gentleness, and self-restraint.
Seeing beings who need attendance upon a teacher, these fearless ones

children.text: ceṭā bhavanti dāsā vā śiṣyatvamupayānti ca //
children.translated_text: become servants or slaves, and even become disciples.

children.text: yena yenaiva cāṃgena sattvo dharmarato bhavet /
children.translated_text: By whatever means a being may become delighted in the <s>Dharma</s>,
they display all those activities, well-trained in great skillful means (<s>upāya</s>).

children.text: yeṣām anantā śikṣā hi anantaścāpi gocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Those whose training is infinite and whose range is infinite,
endowed with infinite knowledge, they are liberators of infinite beings.
Not in <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, not in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,
could even the <s>Buddhas</s> themselves speaking find the end of their virtues.
Setting aside those of meager wisdom,

children.text: asmin dharme śrute kovidaḥ ko na praṇidadhātyuttamabodhyai?" //
children.translated_text: who, being learned, having heard this <s>Dharma</s>, would not aspire to supreme awakening?

body.text: 8 advayadharmamukhapraveśaḥ
body.translated_text: 8. Entrance into the Gate of the Non-Dual <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Advayadharmamukhapraveśa</s>)

body.text:
atha licchavirvimalakīrtistān bodhisattvānetadavocat- "satpuruṣāḥ, kimasti bodhisattvānāmadvayadharmamukhapraveśaḥ? astu svabhidhānam" /
dharmavikurvaṇo nāma bodhisattvastatra tasmin saṃnipāta etadavocat- "kulaputra, utpādabhaṅgau hi dvayam; yadanutpannamajātam tasmin kaścidbhaṅgo nāsti / anutpattikadharmakṣānti prāptirasyadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaḥ śrīgupto 'bhāṣata- "'ahañca mame ' -ti tadhi dvayam / ātmasamāropābhāve mama (bhāvo) nāsti / yaḥ samāropābhāvaḥ, sa hyadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaḥ śrīkūṭo 'bravīt- "saṃkliṣṭañca vyavadānannāma te dvayam / saṃkliṣṭaparijñāne vyavadānamanyanā nāsti / sarvamanyanāsūnmūlanānugatimārgaḥ so 'dvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvo bhadrajyotirāha- "calaśca manyanā tau hi dvayam / yo 'calaḥ, (tat-) manyanākaraṇam, amanasikāro 'nadhikāraḥ / adhikāraviprayogaḥ so 'dvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaḥ subāhuravocat- "bodhicittaṃ ca śrāvakacittannāma-te hi dvayam / yanmāyācittasamadarśanaṃ tanna ca bodhicittanna ca śrāvakacittam / yā cittasya samalakṣaṇatā, sā hyadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvo 'nibhiṣa āha- "ādānañcānādānaṃ, te dvayam / yadanupādānaṃ, tannopalabhyate / yannopalabhyate, tasmin kalpanāpakarṣaṇākaraṇam / sarvadharmākaraṇamanācāraḥ, sa hyadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaḥ sunetro 'vocat- "ekalakṣaṇatvañcālakṣaṇatvannāma, te dvayam / yat kalpanākaraṇaṃ saṅkalpākaraṇam, (tad) ekalakṣaṇatvālakṣaṇatvākaraṇam / yo lakṣaṇāvilakṣaṇe samalakṣaṇatāpraveśaḥ, so 'dvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvastiṣyo 'bravīt- "kuśalākudhalam iti, te dvayam / yat kuśalākuśalānutthāpanam, nimittānimittayoradvayāvabodhaḥ, (tad-) advayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaḥ siho 'bhāṣata- "sāvadyañcānavadyamiti, te dvayam / yat prabhedajñānabajreṇābandhanāniḥsaraṇaṃ, tadadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaḥ sihamatiravocat- "idaṃ sāsravam, idamanāsravamiti-te hi dvayam / yat samatādharmaprāptyāsravānāstravasaṃjñākaraṇañcasaṃjñābhāvaḥ, (yaḥ) samatāyāṃ na ca samatāprāptir na ca saṃjñāgranthiḥ, ya evamavatāraḥ, tadadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaḥ sukhādhimukto 'bhāṣata- "idaṃ hi sukham idaṃ sukhannāstīti-te dvayam / suviśuddhajñānataḥ sarvasaṃkhyāvigatā cākāśasamāliptā buddhiḥ, sādvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvo nārāyaṇo 'bravīt- "idaṃ hi laukikam, idaṃ lokottaramiti te dvayam / yā lokasya svabhāvaśūnyatā, tasyāṃ kiñcidapyuttaraṇannāsti, avatāro nāsti, na cādhigati rna cānadhigatiḥ / yasyānuttaraṇam anavatāro 'nadhigatiścānadhigatyabhāvaḥ, tadhyadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvo vinayamatirāha "saṃsāraśca nirvāṇamiti-te dvayam / saṃsārasvabhāvadarśanena saṃsāraśca parinirvāṇanna staḥ / yadevaṃ jñātaṃ, tadadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisatttvaḥ pratyakṣadarśano 'vocat- "kṣayākṣayau nāma-tau dvayam / kṣayohi sukṣīṇaḥ / yaḥ sukṣīṇastasminna (kiñcit) kṣapayitavyam; ato 'kṣaya ucyate / yo 'kṣayaḥ sa kṣaṇikaśca, kṣaṇike kṣayo nāsti / tadevanamupraviṣṭam advayadharmadvārāvagāho nāma" /
bodhisattvaḥ samantagupto 'brabīt- "ātmanairātbhyamiti-te dvayam / ātmabhāve 'nupalabhyamāne, kiṃ nairātmyaṃ kuryāt? (tat-) tayoḥ svabhāvadarśanenādvayam advayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvo vidyuddevo 'bhāṣata- "vidyāvidye 'ti-te dvayam / avidyāyāḥ svabhāva iva, tathaiva vidyāpi / yāvidyā bhavati, sāvyākṛtā, asaṃkhyeyā, saṃjñāpathātikrāntā / asyāṃ yo 'bhisamayaḥ, so 'dvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaḥ priyadarśana āha- "rūpaṃ khalu śūnyam / rupannāśanena na śūnyam, api kho pana rūpasvabhāvaḥ śūnyaḥ / evameva vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānaṃ (-ca) śūnyate 'ti-te dvayam / vijñānaṃ khalu śūnyatā / vijñānannāśanena na śūnyam, api kho pana vijñānasvabhāvaḥ śūnyaḥ / yo 'smin pañcopādānaskandhe (ṣv) evameva jānāti, evaṃ jñānena vijñaḥ, so 'dvaye praviśati" /
bodhisattvaḥ prabhāketuravocat- "caturdhātuno 'nyatrākāśadhāturanya iti-te dvayam / caturdhātu punarākāśasvabhāvam / pūrvānto 'pyākāśasvabhāvaḥ / aparāntaścākāśasvabhāvaḥ / evameva pratyutpannam / yat tathā dhātvavatārajñānam, tadadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvo 'gramatirabhāṣata- "cakṣuśca rūpannāma-te dvayam / ye cakṣuḥparijñānena rūpe 'lobho 'dveṣo 'mohaḥ tadhi śāntirnāma / evameva śrotraśabdo, ghrāṇagandhau, jihvārasau, kāyaspraṣṭavye, manodharmau-te dvayam / ye ca manaḥ parijñānāddharme(-ṣv) alobho 'dveṣo 'moohaḥ-tadhi śāntirnāma / evaṃ śāntivihāro 'dvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvo 'kṣayamatirāha- "dānasarvajñatāpariṇāmane-te dvayam / dānasvabhāvaḥ sarvajñatā / sarvajñatāsvabhāvaḥ pariṇāmanā / evameva śīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñāsarvajñatāpariṇāmane-te dvayam / sarvajñatā hi (śīlakṣāntivīryadhyāna-) prajñāsvabhāvaḥ; pariṇāmanā ca sarvajñatāsvabhāvaḥ / tasmin ekanaye 'vatāraḥ, so 'dvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvo gambhīramatirabhāṣata- "śūnyatāyā anyatrānimittāpraṇihitamapyanyamiti-te dvayam / yacchūnyama, tasminna kiñcinnimittam / animitte 'praṇihitam / apraṇihite cittamānovijñānāsañcāraḥ / yat sarvavimokṣamukheṣu draṣṭavyameka vimokṣamukhaṃ, tadadvayamukhapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaḥ śāntendriyo 'bravīt- "buddhadharmasaṅghā iti-te dvayam / buddhasya svabhāvo hi dharmaḥ, dharmasya ca svabhāvaḥ saṅgha / sarve te punarasaṃskṛtāḥ / asaṃskṛtaṃ hyākāśa (samam) sarvadharmanaya ākāśatulyaḥ / yadevamanugamanaṃ, tadhyadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvo 'pratihatekṣaṇo 'bhāṣata- "satkāyaśca satkāyanirodha iti-tau dvayam / satkāya eva nirodhaḥ / tat kasya hetoḥ? satkāyadṛṣṭyanutpāde 'sati yat tathā dṛṣṭayā 'satkāya' iti vā 'satkāyanirodha' iti tadkalpyam; akalpyaṃ nirvikalpam / atyantākalpanayā nirodhasvabhāvo bhavati / asambhavo 'vināśas-so 'dvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaḥ subinīto 'vocat- "kāyavākcittasaṃvaro nāma tadadvayam / tat kasya hetoḥ? ime dharmā anabhisaṃskāralakṣaṇāḥ / tat kāyānabhisaṃskāraṃ, tallakṣaṇe 'pi vāganabisaṃskārañca cittānabhisaṃskāram / tat sarvadharmānabhisaṃskāraṃ, taditi jñātavyamanuveditavyam / tat tadanabhisaṃskārajñānam, tadhyadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaḥ puṇyakṣetra āha- "puṇyāpuṇyānijyābhusaṃskārābhisaṃskāraṇate 'ti - te dvayam / yat puṇyāpuṇyānizyānabhisaṃskāram, tadadvayam / puṇyāpuṇyānijyābhisaṃskārāṇāṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ śūnyatā / tasyā puṇyaṃ vāpuṇyaṃ vānijyaṃ vā na bhavanti / abhisaṃskaraṇatāpi ca na bhavati ya evamanabhinirhāraḥ, sa hyadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaḥ padmavyūho 'bravīt- "ātmaparyutthānādutpādaḥ, tadhi dvayam / ātmaparijñā dvayānutthāpanam / tathādvayasthāne 'vijñaptikenāvijñāptikam-tadhyadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaḥ śrīgarbho 'bhāṣata "upalambhena prabhedaḥ-taddvayam / yo 'nupalambhas-taddvayam / tato yāvanupādānanotsargau, tadhyadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaścandrottaro 'bravīt- "andhakārālokāviti-tau dvayam / andhakārālokābhāvaḥ-tadadvayam / tat kasya hotoḥ? evaṃ nirodhasamāpanne na cāndhakāro na cālokaḥ / sarvadharmalakṣaṇatvaṃ tathaivāpi / yo 'syāṃ samatāyāmavatāraḥ, so 'dvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvo ratnamudrāhasto 'vocat- "nirvāṇabhiratiśca saṃsārāratis-te dvayam / ye nirvāṇānabhiratiśca saṃsāranaratis-te 'dvayam / tat kasya hetoḥ? yad bandhanānniḥsaraṇamākhyāyate, ki tu yadatyantato 'bandhanam, tanmokṣaṃ kuto gaveṣī? (yad) abandhanāniḥsaraṇayorbhikṣuṇā ratyaratī na labhyete, na tadhyadvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvo ratnakūṭarāja āha- "mārgakumārgāviti-tau dvayam / mārgāvagāhe kumārgānācāraḥ / anācārasthānam mārgasaṃjñā vābhūtamārgasaṃjñā (vā) na bhavati / saṃjñāparijñā hi matidvayānavatāraḥ / so 'dvayapraveśaḥ" /
bodhisattvaḥ satyarato 'bhāṣata - "satyamṛṣe nāma te dvayam / yadi satyadarśanena satyatā(pi) na samanudṛśyate,mithyādṛṣṭiḥ kuto dṛśyate? tat kasya hetoḥ? māṃsacakṣuṣā na dṛśyate, dṛśyate prajñācakṣuṣā adarśanena yathāvidarśanā, tathā (hi) dṛśyate / yatra na ca darśananna ca vidarśanā taddvayapraveśaḥ" / tathaiva te bodhisattvāḥ svakasvakanirdeśaṃ deśayitvāḥ, maṃjuśrīkumārabhūtadametavocan- "maṃjuśrīḥ, bodhisattvosyādvayapraveśaḥ kim?"
maṃjuśrīrabravīt- "satpuruṣāḥ, yadyapi sarvairyuṣmābhiḥ subhāṣitam, sarva tad yuṣmābhiruktaṃ hi dvayam / sthāpayitvaikopadeśam (api), (yad) anabhilāpyam, abhāṣyam, anuktam, anavaghoṣyam, avyapadeśyam, prajñaptirahitam tadhyadvayapraveśaḥ" /
tato maṃjuśrīkumārabhūto licchavi vimalakīrtimetad avocat- "asmābhiḥ svakasvakanirdeśe vyākhyāte, kulaputra, tvamapyadvayadharmamukhanirdeśāya svabhidhānaṃ kuru" /
atha licchavirvimalakīrtistūṣṇībhūto 'bhūta /
tato maṃjuśrīkumārabhūto licchavivimalakīrtaye sādhukāram adāt- "sādhu, sādhu, kulaputra / ayaṃ hi bodhisattvānām advayapraveśaḥ / tasmin akṣaravacanavijñaptipracāro nāsti" /
asmin nirdeśe deśite, bodhisattvānām pañcasahasreṇādvayadharmamukhapraveśenānutpattikadharmakṣāntiḥ pratilabdhā /
body.translated_text:
Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: 'Good sirs, what is the entry of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> into the <s>Dharma</s>-door of non-duality (<s>advayadharmamukha</s>)? Let each speak according to his own understanding.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Dharmavikurvaṇa</s> in that assembly said: 'Sons of good family, arising and destruction — that is duality. What is unborn and unproduced has no destruction. The attainment of the acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>) — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śrīgupta</s> declared: '"I" and "mine" — that is duality. When the superimposition of self does not exist, there is no "mine." The absence of superimposition — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śrīkūṭa</s> said: 'Defilement and purification — those are duality. When defilement is fully understood, there is no consideration of purification. The path that follows the uprooting of all considerations — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhadrajyotis</s> said: 'Distraction and consideration — those are duality. Where there is no distraction, there is no consideration, no mental engagement, no activity. Freedom from activity — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Subāhu</s> said: 'The mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) and the mind of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> — those are duality. When the mind is seen as equal to an illusion, there is neither the mind of awakening nor the mind of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>. The sameness of the nature of mind — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Anibhiṣa</s> said: 'Grasping and non-grasping — those are duality. What is not grasped is not apprehended. What is not apprehended involves no conceptual elaboration. The non-performance of all <s>dharmas</s>, non-conduct — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Sunetra</s> said: 'Having one characteristic and being without characteristics — those are duality. When there is no conceptualization and no volition, there is no making of one characteristic or no characteristic. The entry into the sameness of characteristics and non-characteristics — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Tiṣya</s> said: 'Wholesome and unwholesome — those are duality. When neither the wholesome nor the unwholesome is produced, there is the realization of non-duality in both signs and signlessness — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Siṃha</s> declared: 'Blameworthy and blameless — those are duality. When through the diamond of discriminating knowledge there is release from bondage — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Siṃhamati</s> said: '"This has outflows" and "this is without outflows" — those are duality. When through attainment of the <s>Dharma</s> of equality there is no designation of outflows or non-outflows, and no designation exists; when in equality there is neither attainment of equality nor the knot of designation — such an entry is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Sukhādhimukta</s> declared: '"This is happiness" and "this is not happiness" — those are duality. Through perfectly pure knowledge, an intelligence free from all enumeration and undefiled like space — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> said: '"This is worldly" and "this is supramundane" — those are duality. The world is empty by nature; in that there is no crossing over, no entering, no attainment, and no non-attainment. Where there is no crossing over, no entering, no attainment, and no absence of non-attainment — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vinayamati</s> said: '<s>Saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> — those are duality. By seeing the true nature of <s>saṃsāra</s>, there is neither <s>saṃsāra</s> nor <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. When this is known — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Pratyakṣadarśana</s> said: 'Exhaustion and inexhaustibility — those are duality. What is exhausted is truly exhausted. In what is truly exhausted, there is nothing to be exhausted — therefore it is called inexhaustible. What is inexhaustible is momentary, and in the momentary there is no exhaustion. Such an entry is the comprehension of the non-dual <s>Dharma</s>-door.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantagupta</s> said: 'Self and non-self — those are duality. When self is not apprehended, what would one make non-self? By seeing the true nature of both — that is non-duality, the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Vidyuddeva</s> declared: 'Knowledge and ignorance — those are duality. The nature of ignorance is the same as the nature of knowledge. Ignorance is indeterminate, innumerable, and transcends the path of designations. The realization of this — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Priyadarśana</s> said: 'Form is empty. Form is not empty through the destruction of form; rather, the very nature of form is empty. Likewise, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are empty — those are duality. Consciousness is emptiness. Consciousness is not empty through the destruction of consciousness; rather, the very nature of consciousness is empty. One who knows thus regarding the five aggregates of clinging (<s>pañcopādānaskandha</s>) — through such knowledge the wise one enters non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Prabhāketu</s> said: 'The four elements are different from the space element — those are duality. But the four elements are of the nature of space. The past is also of the nature of space. The future is also of the nature of space. The present likewise. The knowledge of thus entering the elements — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Agramati</s> declared: 'The eye and form — those are duality. When through full understanding of the eye there is non-attachment, non-aversion, and non-delusion regarding form — that is called peace. Likewise, ear and sound, nose and smell, tongue and taste, body and tangibles, mind and <s>dharmas</s> — those are duality. When through full understanding of the mind there is non-attachment, non-aversion, and non-delusion regarding <s>dharmas</s> — that is called peace. Such dwelling in peace is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Akṣayamati</s> said: 'Generosity and dedication to omniscience — those are duality. The nature of generosity is omniscience. The nature of omniscience is dedication. Likewise, moral discipline, patience, vigor, meditation, wisdom, and dedication to omniscience — those are duality. Omniscience is the nature of wisdom; dedication is the nature of omniscience. The entry into that single method — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Gambhīramati</s> declared: 'Emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is different, signlessness (<s>animitta</s>) and wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>) are different — those are duality. What is empty has no sign in it. In the signless there is no wish. In the wishless there is no movement of mind, mentation, and consciousness. What is to be seen in all the doors of liberation as one door of liberation — that is the entry into the non-dual door.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śāntendriya</s> said: '<s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s> — those are duality. The nature of the <s>Buddha</s> is the <s>Dharma</s>; the nature of the <s>Dharma</s> is the <s>Saṅgha</s>. All of them are unconditioned. The unconditioned is like space; the method of all <s>dharmas</s> is equal to space. Such a following — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Apratihatekṣaṇa</s> declared: 'The composite of personality (<s>satkāya</s>) and the cessation of the composite of personality — those are duality. The composite of personality is itself cessation. Why? One who does not produce the view of the composite of personality (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) neither conceives "composite of personality" nor "cessation of the composite of personality." The inconceivable is beyond conceptualization. Through ultimate non-conceptualization, it becomes of the nature of cessation. Non-arising and non-destruction — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Suvinīta</s> said: 'Restraint of body, speech, and mind — those are duality. Why? These <s>dharmas</s> are characterized by non-formation. What is the non-formation of body, that in its characteristic is also the non-formation of speech and the non-formation of mind. What is the non-formation of all <s>dharmas</s> — that should be known and realized. That knowledge of non-formation — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Puṇyakṣetra</s> said: 'Meritorious, demeritorious, and imperturbable formations and their formation — those are duality. The non-formation of meritorious, demeritorious, and imperturbable — that is non-duality. The intrinsic characteristic of meritorious, demeritorious, and imperturbable formations is emptiness. In that, there is no merit, no demerit, no imperturbable, and no formation. Such non-production — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Padmavyūha</s> said: 'The arising from self-afflictions — that is duality. Full understanding of self is the non-arising of duality. Thus in the abode of non-duality, through the uncognizable there is the uncognizable — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śrīgarbha</s> declared: 'Through apprehension there is differentiation — that is duality. Non-apprehension — that is non-duality. From that, as far as non-grasping and non-relinquishing — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Candrottara</s> said: 'Darkness and light — those are duality. The absence of darkness and light — that is non-duality. Why? In the attainment of cessation, there is neither darkness nor light. The characteristic of all <s>dharmas</s> is just so. The entry into that equality — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Ratnamudrāhasta</s> said: 'Delight in <s>nirvāṇa</s> and aversion to <s>saṃsāra</s> — those are duality. Non-delight in <s>nirvāṇa</s> and non-aversion to <s>saṃsāra</s> — that is non-duality. Why? If liberation is declared through release from bondage, yet what is ultimately without bondage — where would one seek liberation? When a <s>bhikṣu</s> finds neither delight nor aversion in bondage and release — that is the entry into non-duality.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Ratnakūṭarāja</s> said: 'The right path and the wrong path — those are duality. One who enters the right path does not follow the wrong path. One who abides in non-conduct has neither the notion of the right path nor the notion of the wrong path. The full understanding of notions — that is the entry into non-duality of the intellect.'
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Satyarata</s> declared: 'Truth and falsehood — those are duality. If, even when seeing truth, one does not perceive truth itself, how could a false view be seen? Why? It is not seen with the fleshly eye; it is seen with the eye of wisdom. Through non-seeing, just as is the seeing — so it is seen. Where there is neither seeing nor non-seeing — that is the entry into non-duality.'
Thus, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having each given their own exposition, said to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the Crown Prince: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s entry into non-duality?'
<s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'Good sirs, although all of you have spoken well, everything you have said is still duality. Setting aside even a single teaching, that which is inexpressible, unspeakable, unsaid, unannounced, undesignated, and free from conceptual designation — that is the entry into non-duality.'
Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the Crown Prince, said to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: 'We have each given our own exposition. Son of good family, now you too give your own declaration for the teaching of the non-dual <s>Dharma</s>-door.'
Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> remained silent.
Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the Crown Prince, praised the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, son of good family! This is indeed the entry of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> into non-duality. In it, there is no movement of syllable, word, or cognition.'
When this teaching was taught, five thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s> attained the acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>) through the entry into the non-dual <s>Dharma</s>-door.

body.text: advayadharmamukhapraveśasya parivarto 'stamaḥ
body.translated_text: End of the eighth chapter, entitled 'Entrance into the Gate of the Non-Dual <s>Dharma</s>' (<s>Advayadharmamukhapraveśa</s>).

body.text:
9 nirmāṇabhojyādānam
athāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitadabhūt- "madhyāhna āpanne, ime mahābodhisattvāścennottiṣṭhanti, ime 'nnaṃ kutra bhuñjanta" iti /
tato licchavirvimalakīrtirāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya cittavitarka cetasā jñātvā, āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat- "bhadanta śāriputra, tathāgatena ye 'ṣṭau vimokṣā ākhyātāḥ, teṣu vimokṣeṣu tiṣṭha, āmiṣasammiśritavicāreṇa dharmammā śrauṣīḥ / bhadanta śāriputra, muhūrta pratīkṣasva; ananubhūtapūrvāhāraṃ bhakṣayiṣyasi" /
tatastadā licchavirvimalakīrtistathārūpaṃ samādhi samāpadyate sma, īdṛśad rdhyabhisaṃskāramabhisaṃskaroti sma, (yathā tad) ūrdhvadiśi buddhakṣetram, ito dvicatvāriśadgaṅgānadīvālukāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇy) atikramya, yat sarvagandhasugandhā nāma lokadhātuḥ, tebhyo bodhisattvebhyaśca tebhyo mahāśrāavakebhyo darśayati sma / tatra sugandhakuṭo nāma tathāgato 'dya tiṣṭhiti, dhriyate, yāpayati / tasmillokadhātau(yo) daśadikṣu sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇām manuṣyadev (ebhyo) gandha utpadyate, tasmādviśiṣṭataro (gandhas) tasya lokadhātordāruṇa utpadyate / tasmillokadhātau śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ nāmadheyamapi nāsti / kevalaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ gaṇasannipātāya sa sugandhakūūṭastathāgato dharma deśayati / tasmillokadhātau sarvāṇi kūṭāgārāṇi dhūpamayāni; sarvacaṃkramaṇodyānavimānāni ca dhūpamayāni / yatteṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ juṣṭānnaṃ, tasya gandhenāprameyalokadhātavaḥ sfuṭāḥ /
tena khalu samayena bhagavān sugandhakūṭastathāgatastairbodhisattvaissahabhojanakhādanārtha niṣaṇṇo ('bhvat) / tatra mahāyānasamprasthito gandhavyūhatarpaṇo nāma devaputro bhagavataśca teṣāṃ bodhisattvānām upasthāne ca paryupāsane 'bhiyukto ('bhūt) / tatastayā sarvāvatyā parṣadā tasmilokadhātau sa bhagavāṃśca te bodhisattvā bhojanāya racitā niṣaṇṇā dṛśyante sma /
atha licchavirvimalakīrtiḥ sarvān tān bodhisattvānetadavocat- "satpuruṣāḥ, yuṣmanmadhye kastasmād buddhakṣetrādāhārādānāyotsahate?" atra maṃjuśriyo 'dhiṣṭhānena na kaścidutsahate sma / tato licchavirvimalakīrtimaṃjuśrīkumārabhūtametadavocat- "maṃjuśrīḥ, īdṛśaste parivāro nanu na lajjā (karaḥ)? āha- "kulaputra, tathāgatena 'nāśikṣitāy ātimanyanā kartavye ' ti nanu na proktam?"
atha licchavirvimalakīrtistasyāḥ śayyāyā anutthāya, teṣāṃ bodhisattvānām abhimukhaṃ nirmitabodhisattvasya suvarṇavarṇapratirūpakaṃ lakṣaṇānuvyañjasvalaṅkṛtaṃ kāyaṃ nirmimīte sma / yena sa sarvaparivāro dhyāmīkṛtaḥ, tādṛśo rūpe avabhāsamāgacchati sma /
tato licchavirvimalamīrtistaṃ nirmitabodhisattvametadavocat- "kulaputra, ūrdhvadiśi gaccha; dvācatvāriśadgaṅganadīvālukopamāni buddhakṣetrāṇyatikrabhya, (tatr) asti sarvagandhasugandhā nāma lokadhātuḥ / tatra sugandhakūṭo nāma tathāgato 'dya bhojanakhādanārtha niṣaṇṇaḥ / tatropasaṃkramya, tasya tathāgatasya pādau śirasābhivandya, etannivedaya- 'licchavirvimalakīrtirbhagavataḥ pādau śatasahasrakṛtvaḥ śirasābhivandya, bhagavatyalpābādhatām alpātaṅkatāṃ laghūttathānatāṃ yatrāṃ balaṃ sukhamh anavadyatāṃ sukhasparśavihāratāṃ rog (ābhāvaṃ) pṛcchati caivamapoi kathayati / bhagavān bhojanasyāvaśeṣam me dadātu / tena sahālokadhātau (vimalakīrti-) rbuddhakārya kariṣyati / (ye) hīnādhimuktikasattvāḥ, ta udārādhimukti janayiṣyanti, tathāgatalakṣaṇān ca vardhanta' iti" / atha sa nirmitabodhisattvo licchavivimalakīrtaye 'sādhv' iti kṛtvā, pratyaśrauṣīt / ullokitamukhasteṣāṃ bodhisattvānām abhimukhādapakrāmāti sma, te bidhisattvāstu tadgamananna paśyanti sma / tataḥ sa nirmitabodhisattvo (yena) sarvagandhasugandhā nāma lokadhātuḥ; tenopagamya, tasya bhagavataḥ sugandhakūṭasya tathāgatasya pādau śirasābhivandya, etadavocat-
body.translated_text:
9. The Offering of Food through Emanation (<s>Nirmāṇabhojyādāna</s>)
Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> had this thought: 'The midday has arrived; if these great <s>bodhisattvas</s> do not rise, where will they eat their food?'
Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, knowing the mental deliberation of the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> with his mind, said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, abide in those eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>) that the <s>Tathāgata</s> has proclaimed. Do not listen to the <s>Dharma</s> with thoughts mixed with material things! Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, wait a moment; you shall eat food such as you have never before experienced.'
Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> entered a certain <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and performed such a feat of miraculous power that he showed all those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and great <s>śrāvakas</s> a <s>Buddha</s>-field in the upward direction, beyond forty-two <s>Buddha</s>-fields as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, a world-realm called <s>Sarvagandhasugandhā</s> (All-Fragrant). There a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sugandhakūṭa</s> (Fragrant Peak) presently lives, endures, and sustains himself. In that world-realm, the fragrance that arises is more excellent than the fragrances of gods and humans in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields of the ten directions. In that world-realm, not even the name of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> exists. That <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sugandhakūṭa</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> solely for the assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. In that world-realm, all palaces are made of fragrance, and all walkways, gardens, and aerial vehicles are made of fragrance. The fragrance of the food enjoyed by those <s>bodhisattvas</s> pervades immeasurable world-realms.
At that time, the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sugandhakūṭa</s>, was seated together with those <s>bodhisattvas</s> for the purpose of eating and partaking of food. There, a <s>devaputra</s> (son of the gods) named <s>Gandhavyūhatarpaṇa</s>, who had set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, was devoted to attending upon and serving the Blessed One and those <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Then that entire assembly in that world-realm — the Blessed One and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> — were seen seated and arranged for the meal.
Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to all those <s>bodhisattvas</s>: 'Good men, which among you would venture to go to that <s>Buddha</s>-field to bring food?' Through the supernatural power of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, none dared venture. Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful prince: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is not such a retinue of yours a cause for shame?' He said: 'Son of good family, has not the <s>Tathāgata</s> declared: "The untrained should not be despised"?'
Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, without rising from that couch, emanated before those <s>bodhisattvas</s> a body of an emanated <s>bodhisattva</s> — golden in color, beautiful in form, adorned with the marks and secondary signs — such that by his radiance the entire retinue was outshone.
Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to that emanated <s>bodhisattva</s>: 'Son of good family, go in the upward direction. Having passed beyond forty-two <s>Buddha</s>-fields as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, there is a world-realm called <s>Sarvagandhasugandhā</s>. There a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sugandhakūṭa</s> is now seated for the purpose of eating and partaking of food. Approach him, bow your head at the feet of that <s>Tathāgata</s>, and convey this: "The <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> bows his head a hundred thousand times at the feet of the Blessed One, inquires about the Blessed One's health — that he has little affliction, little ailment, rises easily, has a comfortable state, strength, happiness, blamelessness, pleasant bodily sensations, and absence of illness — and says this: 'May the Blessed One give me the remainder of his food. With it, <s>Vimalakīrti</s> will perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm. Beings of inferior aspiration will generate noble aspiration, and the marks of the <s>Tathāgata</s> will increase.'" Then that emanated <s>bodhisattva</s>, assenting to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> with 'Very well,' departed upward facing those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> did not see his departure. Then that emanated <s>bodhisattva</s> went to the world-realm called <s>Sarvagandhasugandhā</s>, approached the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sugandhakūṭa</s>, bowed his head at his feet, and said this:

body.text: "bhagavan, bodhisattvo vimalakīrtirbhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya, bhagavatyalpābādhatām alpātaṅkatāṃ laghūtthānatāṃ yātrāṃ balaṃ sukham anavadyatāṃ sukhasparśavihāratāṃ rog(ābhāvaṃ) pṛcchati / sa bhagavataḥ pādau satasahasrakṛtvaḥ śirasābhivandya, etad yācati- 'bhagavān bhojanasya bhojyāvaśeṣamme dadātu / tenāsmin sahālokadhātau (vimalakīrti-)rbuddhakārya kariṣyati / (ye) hīnādhimuktikasattvāḥ, te buddhadharmodāramatyadhimukti janayiṣyanti, tathāgatalakṣaṇāni ca vardhanta'-iti" /
body.translated_text: 'Blessed One, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> bows his head at the feet of the Blessed One, inquires about the Blessed One's health — that he has little affliction, little ailment, rises easily, has a comfortable state, strength, happiness, blamelessness, pleasant bodily sensations, and absence of illness — and having bowed his head a hundred thousand times at the feet of the Blessed One, makes this request: "May the Blessed One give me the remainder of his food. With it, <s>Vimalakīrti</s> will perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm. Beings of inferior aspiration will generate the noble aspiration for the excellent <s>Buddha-dharma</s>, and the marks of the <s>Tathāgata</s> will increase."'

body.text: atha te bhagavataḥ sugandhakūṭasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrasya bodhisattvā āścaryādbhutaprāptāḥ taṃ bhagavantaṃ sugandhakūṭaṃ tathāgatametadavocan- "bhagavan evaṃrūpo mahāsattvaḥ kuta āgataḥ? sa sahālokadhātuḥ kvāsti? "hīnādhimuktikā" nāma tadasti kim?" iti te bodhisattvāstaṃ bhagavantamevaṃ pṛcchanti sma /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sugandhakūṭa</s>, struck with wonder and amazement, said to the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sugandhakūṭa</s>: 'Blessed One, from where has such a great being come? Where is that <s>Sahā</s> world-realm? What does the term "beings of inferior aspiration" mean?' Thus those <s>bodhisattvas</s> questioned the Blessed One.

body.text: tato bhagavāṃstān bodhisattvānetadavocat- "kulaputrāḥ, ito 'dhodiśi dvivacatvāriśadgaṅgānadīvālukāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇy atikramya, asti sahā nāma lokadhātuḥ / tatra śākyamunirnāma tathāgataḥ pañcakaṣāyabuddhakṣetre hīnādhimuktikebhyaḥ sattvebhyo dharma deśayati / tatra so 'cintyavimokṣavihārī vimalakīrtirnāma bodhisattvaḥ bodhisattvebhyo dharma deśayati / sa mannāmaparikīrtan (ārthāya) cāsya lokadhātoḥ praśaṃsāsamprakāśanā (-'rthāya) ca teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ kuśalamūlasutaptakaraṇārthāya nirmitabodhisattvaṃ preṣayati" /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said to those <s>bodhisattvas</s>: 'Sons of good family, below this place, having passed beyond forty-two <s>Buddha</s>-fields as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, there is a world-realm called <s>Sahā</s>. There a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings of inferior aspiration in a <s>Buddha</s>-field afflicted by the five degenerations (<s>pañcakaṣāya</s>). There, a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, who abides in the inconceivable liberation (<s>acintyavimokṣa</s>), teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. He has sent this emanated <s>bodhisattva</s> for the purpose of proclaiming my name, for the purpose of praising and making known this world-realm, and for the purpose of causing the roots of merit of those <s>bodhisattvas</s> to be well-matured.'

body.text: tataste bodhisattvā etadavocan- "bhagavan, tasya bodhisattvasya māhātmyam, yāvadidaṃ nirmāṇañca tasyaivaṃrūpardhibalavaiśāradyāni bhūtāni" / sa bhavānavocat- "tasya bodhisattvasyedṛśām māhātmyam, (yathā) daśadikṣu sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu nirmāṇā (ni) preṣayati, tāni nirmāṇāni ca teṣāṃ buddhakṣetrāṇāṃ sarvasattvakārya-(ārtha) buddhakāryeṇa pratyupasthitāni bhavanti" /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> said: 'Blessed One, how great is the majesty of that <s>bodhisattva</s>, that his emanation possesses such miraculous power, strength, and fearlessness!' The Blessed One said: 'Such is the majesty of that <s>bodhisattva</s> that he sends emanations to all <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions, and those emanations are present performing the <s>Buddha</s>'s work for the sake of all beings in those <s>Buddha</s>-fields.'

body.text: atha bhagavān sugandhakūṭastathāgataḥ sarvagandhasamanvāgate bhājane sarvagandhavāsitaṃ bhojanaṃ chorayati sma; tattasmai nirmitabodhisattvāyādāt / tatastadā bodhisattvānāṃ navatiśatasahasrāṇi tena gamikāni- "bhagavan, vayamapi tāṃ sahāṃ lokadhātuṃ, taṃ bhagavantaṃ śākyamuni darśanāya, vandanāya, paryupāsanāya. taṃ ca vimalakīrti ca tān bodhisattvān darśanāya gacchāmaḥ" / sa bhagavānavocat- "kulaputrāḥ, gacchata yasyedānīṃ kālaṃ manyadhve /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sugandhakūṭa</s>, poured fragrance-infused food into a vessel completely permeated with all fragrances and gave it to that emanated <s>bodhisattva</s>. Then at that time, ninety hundred thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s> wished to go with him: 'Blessed One, we too wish to go to that <s>Sahā</s> world-realm to see and pay homage to and attend upon the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, and to see <s>Vimalakīrti</s> and those <s>bodhisattvas</s>.' The Blessed One said: 'Sons of good family, go if you now think the time is right.'

body.text: "kulaputrāḥ, te sattvā unmādāśca pramattāḥ khalv abhaviṣyan; tena gacchata gandhāpagatabhūtāḥ / tasya sahālokadhātoste sattvā avasādamāsādayanti; tasmāhu svarūpān nivartadhvam / tasmillokadhātau hīnasaṃjñām utpādya, pratighasaṃjñām motpādayata / tat kasya hetoḥ? kulaputrāḥ, buddhakṣetreṃ hyākāśakṣetram / sattvaparipācanārthāya bhagavanto buddhāḥ sarvān buddhagocarānna darśanti" /
body.translated_text: "Sons of good family, those beings would become intoxicated and maddened; therefore go, having left behind the fragrances! In that <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, those beings become despondent; therefore return to your own forms. Do not generate a perception of inferiority regarding that world-realm, nor a perception of aversion. What is the reason? Sons of good family, a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) is like space. The Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, for the sake of ripening beings, do not show all their domains of activity."

body.text: atha sa nirmita bodhisattvastat (sarvagandhavāsitaṃ) bhojyaṃ samādāya, bodhisattvānāṃ navatiśatasahasraiḥ sārdha buddhānubhāvena ca vimalakīrteradhiṣṭhānena eekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtena tatraīva tasyāḥ sarvagandhasugandhālokadhātvā antarhitaśca licchavivimalakīrtergṛhe niṣīdati sma / atha licchavirvimalakīrtiryādṛśāni pūrvasiṃhāsanāni, tādṛśānāṃ navatiśatasahasrāṇyadhitiṣṭhati sma / teṣu te bodhisattvā nyaṣīdan / tatassa nirmita bodhisattvastadbhojyapūrṇabhājanaṃ vimalakīrtaye 'dāt /
body.translated_text: Then that emanated <s>bodhisattva</s>, taking the food from the All-Fragrance world, together with ninety thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s>, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s> and by the sustaining force of <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, in a single moment disappeared from that All-Fragrance world-realm and sat down in the house of the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>. Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> magically created ninety thousand lion-thrones, similar to the previous ones, and the <s>bodhisattvas</s> sat upon them. Then that emanated <s>bodhisattva</s> offered the vessel full of food to <s>Vimalakīrti</s>.

body.text: tatastasya bhojyasya gandho vaiśālīm mahānagarīṃ saṃnyavikṣat; sāhasralokadhātuṃ yāvacca ghrāyate smāsvādyagandhaḥ / ye vaiśālyā brāhmāṇagṛhapatayaśca licchavyadhipo licchavicandracchattraśca taṃ gandhamāghrāya, āścaryaprāptā adbhutaprāptāḥ prasannakāyacittā licchavīnāṃ caturaśītisahasraiḥ paripūrṇaiḥ saha vimalakīrtergṛham praviśanti sma /
body.translated_text: Then the fragrance of that food pervaded the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s> and was smelled as far as the trichiliocosm—a delicious fragrance. The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, and the <s>Licchavi</s> chief <s>Candracchatra</s>, having smelled that fragrance, were filled with wonder and amazement. With body and mind serene, together with a full eighty-four thousand <s>Licchavis</s>, they entered the house of <s>Vimalakīrti</s>.

body.text: te tasmin gṛhe bodhisattvān sampūrṇasihāsaneṣu tanmātronnatātimātraviśāleṣu niṣaṇṇān paśyanti sma / dṛṣṭvā, tairadhimuktiśca pramuditotpāditāḥ / sarve te tān mahāśrāvakāṃ ca tān mahābodhisattvānabhivandya, ekānte 'sthuḥ / bhūmyavacaradevaputrāśca kāmāvacararūpāvacaradevaputrāśca tena gandhena coditā vimalakīrtergṛhaṃ samāgacchanti sma /
body.translated_text: They saw in that house the <s>bodhisattvas</s> seated on those great, exceedingly high and vast lion-thrones. Having seen them, they were filled with delight and faith. They all bowed to those great <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) and great <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and stood to one side. <s>Devaputras</s> (divine sons) of the earth realm, <s>devaputras</s> of the desire realm, and <s>devaputras</s> of the form realm, summoned by that fragrance, also came to the house of <s>Vimalakīrti</s>.

body.text: atha licchavirvimalakīrtiḥ śāriputraṃ sthaviraṃ ca tān mahāśrāvakānetadavocat- "bhadantāḥ, tathāgatabhojyam mahākaruṇāparivāsitāmṛtaṃ bhakṣayata, prādeśikacittatāṃ tu mopaprajñāpayata / dānabhoge 'samarthā abhaviṣyata" / tataḥ kecicchrāvakā etanmanyante sma- "svalpabhojanam ihānayaitādṛśapariṣadā kathaṃ bhojanīyam?" iti / tatassa nirmitabodhisattvastāṃ śrāvakānetadavocat- "āyuṣmantaḥ, yuṣmatprajñāpuṇye tathāgatasya prajñāpuṇyābhyām mā tolayata / tat kasya hetoḥ? tadyathāpi nāma caturmahāsamudrāḥ kṣīṇāḥ sambhaveyuḥ, ki tvasmin bhojane na kiñcitkṣayo 'bhaviṣyat / (evameva) sarve sattvā tasya bhojanasya kalpaṃ sumerumātrālopān bhakṣayeyuḥ, ki tvidaṃ kṣayannāyāsyat / tat kasya hetoḥ? so 'kṣayaśīlaprajñā samādhimayasya tathāgatabhojanasya bhājanāvaśeṣaḥ kṣayaṃ yātunna śaknoti" /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to the elder <s>Śāriputra</s> and those great <s>śrāvakas</s>: "Venerable ones, eat the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s food, the ambrosia infused with great compassion; but do not generate a narrow mind. You would become incapable of enjoying the gift." Then some <s>śrāvakas</s> thought: 'This is only a small amount of food—how can such a great assembly be fed?' Then that emanated <s>bodhisattva</s> said to those <s>śrāvakas</s>: "Venerable ones, do not compare your wisdom and merit with the wisdom and merit of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. What is the reason? Just as the four great oceans might be exhausted, yet this food would never be diminished. Even if all beings were to eat portions the size of Mount <s>Sumeru</s> from this food for an entire <s>kalpa</s>, would it be exhausted? It would not. What is the reason? The remainder of the vessel of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s food, which arises from inexhaustible moral discipline, wisdom, and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), cannot be exhausted."

body.text: atha tato bhojanāt sarvāvatī sā parṣat tṛptā bhūtā / na ca tadbhojanaṃ kṣīyate / yaiśca bodhisattvaiḥ śrāvakaiśca śakrabrahmalokapālaistadanyaiśca sattvaistadbhojanaṃ bhuktam, teṣāṃ tādṛśaṃ sukhaṃ kāye 'vakrāntaṃ yādṛśaṃ sarvasukhamaṇḍitāyāṃ lokadhātau bodhisattvānāṃ sukham / sarvaromakūpebhyaśca teṣāṃ tādṛśo gandhaḥ pravāti, tadyathāpi nāma tasyāmeva sarvagandhasugandhāyāṃ lokadhātau vṛkṣāṇāṃ gandhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, from that food, the entire assembly was satisfied and full, yet the food was not depleted. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, world-protectors, and other beings who ate that food experienced such bliss in their bodies as that of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> in the world-realm adorned with all happiness. And from all their pores there emanated a fragrance like the fragrance of the trees in that All-Fragrance world-realm.

body.text: tatassaṃprajānalliṃcchavirvimalakīrtirbhagavataḥ sugandhakūṭasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrādāgatān bodhisattvānetadavocat- "kulaputrāḥ, tasya tathāgatasya sugandhakūṭasya dharmadeśanā kīdṛśā"? te 'vadan- "sa tathāgato 'kṣaraniruktibhyāṃ dharmanna darśayati / tena gandhenaiva bodhisattvā vinitā bhavanti / ye gandhavṛkṣāḥ, yeṣāṃ mūleṣu te bodhisattvā niṣaṇṇāḥ, tebhyo (yādṛśo) gandhastebhyo (bodhisattvebhyaḥ), tādṛśo niścarati / ghrātamātra eva tasmin gandhe, sarvabodhisattvaguṇākaro nāma samādhi (staiḥ) pratilabhyate / prāptamātra eva tasmin samādhau, sarveṣu teṣu bodhisattvaguṇā utpadyante" /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, comprehending fully, said to those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had come from the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sugandhakūṭa</s> (Fragrance Heap): "Sons of good family, what is the <s>Dharma</s> teaching of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sugandhakūṭa</s> like?" They said: "That <s>Tathāgata</s> does not teach the <s>Dharma</s> by means of syllables or words. By that fragrance alone, the <s>bodhisattvas</s> are disciplined. Beneath the fragrant trees where those <s>bodhisattvas</s> sit, from those trees such fragrance emanates to those <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Upon merely smelling that fragrance, they attain a <s>samādhi</s> called 'Treasury of All <s>Bodhisattva</s> Qualities.' Upon attaining that <s>samādhi</s>, all the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s> arise in them."

body.text:
atha te bodhisattvā licchavi vimalakīrtimetadavadan- "iha bhagavāṃ śākyamuniḥ kīdṛśāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ prakāśayati?" āha- "satpuruṣāḥ, ime sattvā hi durvineyāḥ; ebhyaḥ khaṭuṃkadurvineyasattvebhyaḥ khaṭuṃkadurvineyavineyakathāḥ prakāśayati / ke khaṭuṃkadurvineyāḥ vineyāḥ? khaṭuṃkadurvineyakathā katamā? tadyathā-
"ime hi nairayikāḥ, iyaṃ hi tiryagyoniḥ, ayaṃ yamalokaḥ, imāni hyakṣaṇāni, ime vihīnendriyāḥ /
"idaṃ hi kāyaduścaritaṃ, ayaṃ hi kāyaduścaritasya vipākaḥ / idaṃ vāgduścaritaṃ, ayaṃ vāgduścaritasya vipākaḥ /
idaṃ manoduścaritaṃ, ayaṃ manoduściritasya vipākaḥ / "ayaṃ hi prāṇātipātaḥ, iyamadattādānaṃ, ayaṃ kāmamithyācāraḥ, ayaṃ mṛṣāvādaḥ, ayaṃ paiśunyavādaḥ, ayaṃ pāruṣyavādaḥ, ayaṃ saṃbhinnapralāpaḥ, iyaṃ hyabhidhyā, ayaṃ vyāpādaḥ, iyaṃ mithyādṛṣṭiḥ, ayaṃ hi teṣāṃ vipākaḥ /
"idaṃ mātsarya, idaṃ mātsaryasya falaṃ; idaṃ dauḥśīlyam,(idaṃ dauḥśīlyasya falaṃ); ayaṃ krodhaḥ, (idaṃ krodhasya falam); idaṃ kausīdyam, idaṃ kausīdyasya falam; iyaṃ hi dauṣprajñā, idaṃ dauṣprajñāfalam /
"ayaṃ śikṣāpadasamatikramaḥ, ayaṃ hi prātimokṣaḥ; idaṃ kāryam, idamakāryam; ayaṃ yogācāraḥ; idaṃ prahāṇam; idamāvaraṇam, idamanāvaraṇam; iyamāpattiḥ, idamāpattivyutthānaṃ; ayaṃ mārgaḥ, ayaṃ kumārgaḥ; idaṃ kuśalam, idamakuśalam; idaṃ sāvadyam, idamanavadyam; idaṃ sāsravaṃ idamanāsravam; idaṃ laukikam ' idaṃ lokottaram; idaṃ saṃskṛtam, idamasaṃskṛtam ayaṃ hi saṃkleśaḥ, idaṃ vyavadānam; ayaṃ saṃsāraḥ, idaṃ nirvāṇam iti /
"evamanekavidyaṃ dharma deśayan, (śākyamunistathāgataḥ sattvānām) aśvakhaṭuṃkacittaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati / tadyathāpi nāma khaṭuṃkāśvo vā hastī vā 'rvāk marmahatā vinītā bhavanti, evameva khaṭuṃkadurvineyāḥ sattvā api sarvaduḥkhaprakāśanakathāyā vinītā bhavanti" /
body.translated_text:
Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> said to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: "What kind of <s>Dharma</s> teaching does the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> expound here?" He replied: "Noble ones, these beings are indeed difficult to discipline. For these stubborn, difficult-to-discipline beings, he expounds teachings suited to stubborn, difficult-to-discipline beings. What are these stubborn, difficult-to-discipline beings? And what are the teachings for the stubborn and difficult to discipline? They are as follows:
"'These are the hell realms; this is the animal realm; this is the world of <s>Yama</s>; these are the inopportune states; these are beings with deficient faculties.
"'This is bodily misconduct; this is the ripening of bodily misconduct. This is verbal misconduct; this is the ripening of verbal misconduct. This is mental misconduct; this is the ripening of mental misconduct.
"'This is killing; this is taking what is not given; this is sexual misconduct; this is false speech; this is divisive speech; this is harsh speech; this is idle chatter; this is covetousness; this is ill-will; this is wrong view; this is their ripening.
"'This is miserliness; this is the fruit of miserliness. This is immorality; this is the fruit of immorality. This is anger; this is the fruit of anger. This is laziness; this is the fruit of laziness. This is poor wisdom; this is the fruit of poor wisdom.
"'This is transgression of the training rules; this is the <s>prātimokṣa</s> (code of discipline). This should be done; this should not be done. This is proper practice; this should be abandoned. This is an obstruction; this is not an obstruction. This is an offense; this is the remedy for an offense. This is the path; this is the wrong path. This is wholesome; this is unwholesome. This is blameworthy; this is blameless. This has outflows; this is without outflows. This is mundane; this is supramundane. This is conditioned; this is unconditioned. This is defilement; this is purification. This is <s>saṃsāra</s>; this is <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'
"Thus, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> in these many ways, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> establishes the minds of beings like stubborn horses. Just as a stubborn horse or elephant is disciplined only when struck on its vital points, even so these stubborn, difficult-to-discipline beings are disciplined through the exposition of all forms of suffering."

body.text: te bodhisattvā avadan- "tathā bhagavato buddhasya śākyamunermāhātmyaṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam / āścarya hi hīnadaridrakhaṭuṃkasattvadamanaṃ / ye (ca) bodhisattvā evaṃvidha audārike buddhakṣetre 'vasthitāḥ, teṣāmacintyamahākaruṇā" /
body.translated_text: Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> said: "Thus the greatness of the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> is established. How wonderful indeed is the taming of lowly, poor, stubborn beings! And those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who dwell in such a rough <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) as this—their great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) is inconceivable."

body.text:
tato licchavirvimalakīrtirabravīt- "tat tatheti, satpuruṣāḥ; yathā vadatha (tat) tathā / ye bodhisattvā ihotpannāḥ, eṣām mahākaruṇā sudṛḍhā / te 'tasmillokadhātāvekasyāṃ jātyāṃ sattvebhyo bahvartha kurvanti / tasyāṃ sarvagandhasugandhāyāṃ likadhātau kalpānāmapi satasahasrāṇi sattvebhya īdṛśamartha kartunna śaknuvanti / tat kasya hetoḥ? satpuruṣāḥ, asyāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau daśa parigrahāvahāḥ kuśalasaṃnicayadharmāḥ saṃvidyante / te 'nyasmin buddhakṣetre na bhavanti / katame daśa? tadyathā-
"dānena daridrasaṃgrahaḥ; śīlena duḥśīlasaṃgrahaḥ; kṣāntyā kaṭukasaṃgrahaḥ; vīryeṇa kusīdasaṃhgrahaḥ; dhyānena vikṣiptacittasaṃgrahaḥ; prajñayā duṣprajñasaṃgrahaḥ; akṣaṇaprāptebhyo 'ṣṭābhyo 'kṣaṇebhyo 'tikramaṇadeśanā; pradeśakāribhyo mahāyānadeśanā kuśalamūlenānavaropitakuśalamūlasaṃgrahaḥ; caturbhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhiḥ satatasamitaṃ sattvaparipācanam / te daśa pragrahāvahāḥ kuśalasaṃnicayadharmā anyasmin buddhakṣetre na saṃvidyante" /
bodhisattvā avadan- "anvitāḥ katibhirdharmairbodhisattvāḥ, asyāḥ sahāyā lokadhātvāścyutvā, akṣatānupadrutāḥ pariśuddhabuddhakṣetraṃ gamiṣyanti?" āha- "anvitā aṣṭābhirdharmairbodhisattvāḥ, asyāḥ sahāyā lokadhātvāścyutvā, akṣatānupadrutāḥ pariśuddhabuddhakṣetraṃ gamiṣyanti / katame 'ṣṭau? (bodhisattvaiḥ pratyavekṣitavyam)- " 'sarvasattvā mayānugrahyāḥ, icchaṃstvebhyo na kicid hitaṃ / sarvasattvānāṃ sarvaduḥkhaṃ kṣāmyam, tat-(prāptāni) sarvakuśalamūlāni sarvasattvebhya utsraṣṭavyānīti / sarvasattveṣvapratihato (bhavāni) / śāstarīva sarvabodhisattvanandī (bhavāni) / śrutāśrutadharmā śrutvā, (bhavāny-) apratikṣepaḥ / paralābha īrṣyāpagataḥ svalābhenāgarvaśca cittanidhyapto (bhavāni) / ātmaskhalitāni pratyavekṣamāṇaḥ paradiṣānna codayāmi / apramādarataśca sarvaguṇān saṃpratīcchamī'(ti) / tairaṣṭābhirdharmairanvitā bodhisattvāḥ, sahāyā lokadhātvāścyutvā, akṣatānupadrutāḥ parisuddhabuddhakṣetraṃ gamiṣyanti" /
body.translated_text:
Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said: 'It is so, good sirs; it is as you say. The <s>bodhisattvas</s> born here have strong great compassion. In a single birth in this world-realm, they accomplish more for beings than could be accomplished in a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s> in that <s>Sarvagandhasugandha</s> world-realm for beings. And why is that? Good sirs, in this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm there exist ten <s>dharmas</s> that bring about the accumulation of merit, which do not exist in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. What are the ten? They are:
"Gathering the poor through generosity (<s>dāna</s>); gathering those of poor morality through moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>); gathering the harsh through patience (<s>kṣānti</s>); gathering the lazy through vigor (<s>vīrya</s>); gathering those of distracted minds through meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>); gathering those of poor understanding through wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>); teaching how to overcome the eight inopportune states for those who have fallen into them; teaching the <s>Mahāyāna</s> to those of limited scope; gathering those who have not planted roots of merit through roots of merit; and constantly ripening beings through the four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>). These ten <s>dharmas</s> that bring about the accumulation of merit are not found in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s>.'
The <s>bodhisattvas</s> asked: 'Endowed with how many <s>dharmas</s> will <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having departed from this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, go unharmed and unafflicted to a purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s>?' He said: 'Endowed with eight <s>dharmas</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s> having departed from this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm will go unharmed and unafflicted to a purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. What are the eight? A <s>bodhisattva</s> should reflect: "All beings are to be benefited by me, yet I wish for nothing in return. I must endure all the suffering of all beings. All roots of merit that I have obtained must be relinquished for the sake of all beings. I must be unobstructed toward all beings. I must rejoice in all <s>bodhisattvas</s> as if they were the Teacher. I must not reject <s>dharmas</s>, whether heard or unheard. I must be free from jealousy toward the gains of others, and not be conceited about my own gains, with a composed mind. I must examine my own faults and not criticize the faults of others. I must delight in diligence and accept all good qualities." Endowed with these eight <s>dharmas</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s> having departed from this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm will go unharmed and unafflicted to a purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s>.'

body.text: atha licchavivimalakīrtinā ca maṃjuśrīkumārabhūtena caivaṃ tasyāṃ parṣadi saṃnipatitebhyastathā hi dharme deśite, śatamātrāṇāṃ praṇisahasrāṇām anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhicittānyutpāditāni / bodhisattvānāṃ daśabhiḥ sahasrairanutpattikadharmakṣāntiḥ pratilabdhā /
body.translated_text: Then, when the <s>Dharma</s> had been thus taught to that assembly by the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> and <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful prince, a hundred thousand beings generated the aspiration for <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), and ten thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s> attained <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (patience with the non-arising of dharmas).

body.text: nirmāṇabhojyādānasya parivarto navamaḥ /
body.translated_text: End of the ninth chapter, on the Offering of Magically Created Food.

body.text: 10 kṣayākṣayannāma dharmayautakam
body.translated_text: 10. The <s>Dharma</s> Gift Named the Imperishable (<s>Kṣayākṣaya</s>)

body.text:
tena khalu punaḥ samaya āmrapālīvane bhagavatā dharme nirdiśyamāne, sa maṇḍalamāḍo vistīrṇo viśālo 'bhūt; sā parṣacca suvarṇavarṇa iva saṃniviṣṭā('bhūt) /
tataḥ āyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat- "bhagavan, atredamāmrapālīvanaṃ vistīrṇaṃca viśālabhūtaṃ, sarvāvatī parṣadapi suvarṇavarṇe dṛśyate / kasya khalvidaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ?" bhagavānavocat- "ānanda, idaṃ licchavivimalakīrtimaṃjuśrīkumārabhūtayoḥ prabhūtaparivāreṇa parivṛtayoḥ puraskṛtayostathāgatasamīpāgamanapūrvanimittaṃ" /
atha licchavirvimalakīrtimaṃjuśrīkumārabhūtametadavocat- "maṃjuśrīḥ, ime mahāsattvā api namasyanti tathāgataṃ dṛśyamānāḥ, tasmāhvāvāṃ tathāgatasya samīpaṃ gamiṣyāvaḥ" / maṃjuśrīrāha- "kulaputra, gamiṣyāvo yasyedānīṃ kālaṃ manyase" /
body.translated_text:
Then at that time, as the Blessed One was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> in the <s>Āmrapālī</s> grove, the grounds became vast and expansive; and the entire assembly appeared as if golden-colored.
Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the Blessed One: 'Blessed One, this <s>Āmrapālī</s> grove has become vast and expansive, and the entire assembly appears golden-colored. What is the omen of this?' The Blessed One said: '<s>Ānanda</s>, this is the omen of the approach of the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> and <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful prince, together with a great retinue, surrounded and preceded by attendants, coming into the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'
Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful prince: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, these great beings too wish to pay homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> upon seeing him; therefore let us go together into the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Son of good family, let us go, if you think it is now the right time.'

body.text:
tato licchavirvimalakīrtirevaṃrūpam ṛddhyabhisaṃskāramabhisaṃskaroti sma, yathā taissiṃhāsanaissākaṃ sarvāvatīṃ parṣadaṃ dakṣiṇapāṇau pratiṣṭhāpya, yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya, parṣadaṃ bhūmau pratiṣṭhāpayati sma / bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya, saptakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtyaikānte 'sthāt /
atha te 'pi sugandhakūṭasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrādāgatā bodhisattvāḥ siṃhāsanebhyo 'vatīrya, bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya, bhagavate kṛtāñjalibhūtā namaskurvanta ekānte 'sthuḥ / sarve te 'pi bodhisattvā mahāsattvāśca mahāśrāvakāśca siṃhāsanebhyo 'vartīya, bhagavataḥ pādau śīrasābhivandya, ekānte 'sthuḥ / evameva sarve te śakrabrahmalokapāladevaputrā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya, ekānte 'sthuḥ /
body.translated_text:
Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> performed such a feat of miraculous power that he placed the entire assembly, together with the lion thrones, upon his right palm and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he placed the assembly upon the ground. He bowed at the feet of the Blessed One with his head, circumambulated him seven times, and stood to one side.
Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had come from the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sugandhakūṭa</s> also descended from the lion thrones, bowed at the feet of the Blessed One with their heads, and stood to one side with palms joined, paying homage to the Blessed One. Likewise, all those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> and great <s>śrāvakas</s> descended from the lion thrones, bowed at the feet of the Blessed One with their heads, and stood to one side. Similarly, all those <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, World-Protectors, and <s>devaputras</s> bowed at the feet of the Blessed One with their heads and stood to one side.

body.text:
tato bhagavān, tān bodhisattvān dharmakathayā saṃpraharṣayitvā, etadavocat- "kulaputrāḥ, svakasvakasiṃhāsaneṣu niṣīdata" / bhagavataitadukte, te nyaṣīdan /
atha bhagavāṃśāriputramāmantrayate sma- "śāriputra, bodhisattvānāṃ varasattvānāṃ vikurvaṇāni nanu tvayā dṛṣṭāni?" āha- 'dhruvaṃ, bhagavan, dṛṣṭāni" / bhagavānavocat- "tataste kīdṛśā saṃjñotpannā?" āha- "dhruvaṃ, bhagavan tato me 'cintyasaṃjñotpannā / teṣāṃ karaṇamevamacintya dṛṣṭaṃ, yathā cintātulanāgaṇanā aśakyāḥ" /
atha bhagavantamāyuṣmānānanda etadavocat- "bhagavan, apūrvaghrāto gandhaḥ śrūyamāṇaḥ, īdṛśo 'sti kasya gandhaḥ?" bhagavān avocat- "ānanda, te bodhisattvāḥ kāyasya sarvaromakūpebhya (idṛśaṃ) gandhaṃ niḥśvasanti" / śāriputro 'pyāha- "āyuṣmanānanda, asmatkāyasya sarvaromakūpebhyo 'pīdṛśo gandho niścarati" / āha- "kuto gandha āgataḥ?" āha- "ayaṃ licchavirvimalakīrtiḥ sugandhakūṭasya tathāgatasya sarvagandhasugandhālokadhātorbuddhatrādbhojanamādatte sma / paribhuktvā, sarveṣāṃ, kāyādīdṛśo gandho niścarati" /
tata āyuṣmānānando licchavi vimalakīrtimetadavocat- "ayaṃ gandhaḥ kiyacciramāviṣkaraṇamāyāti?" āha- "yāvadannamajīrṇam / ānanda āha- "kiyacciracaritaṃ tadannaṃ jīrṇa bhaviṣyati?" āha- "saptāharātrāntare jīrṇa bhaviṣyati / tato 'pi yāvatsaptāhamevabhojaḥ parisfuṭaṃ bhaviṣyati / ajīrṇe 'pi (bhojane), na kācit pīḍā jāyate /
body.translated_text:
Then the Blessed One, having delighted those <s>bodhisattvas</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, said: 'Sons of good family, be seated upon your own respective lion thrones.' When the Blessed One spoke thus, they sat down.
Then the Blessed One addressed <s>Śāriputra</s>: '<s>Śāriputra</s>, have you not seen the miraculous transformations of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the supreme beings?' He said: 'Indeed, Blessed One, I have seen them.' The Blessed One said: 'Then what kind of perception arose in you regarding them?' He said: 'Indeed, Blessed One, the perception of the inconceivable arose in me. Their activity was seen as so inconceivable that it was beyond thought, calculation, and counting.'
Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the Blessed One: 'Blessed One, an unprecedented fragrance is being perceived! What is this fragrance?' The Blessed One said: '<s>Ānanda</s>, those <s>bodhisattvas</s> exhale this fragrance from all the pores of their bodies.' <s>Śāriputra</s> also said: 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, from all the pores of our bodies too, this very fragrance is emanating.' He asked: 'Where has this fragrance come from?' He said: 'This <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> received food from the <s>Buddha</s> of the <s>Sarvagandhasugandha</s> world-realm of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sugandhakūṭa</s>. Having eaten it, this fragrance emanates from the bodies of all.'
Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: 'How long will this fragrance continue to manifest?' He said: 'Until the food is digested.' <s>Ānanda</s> asked: 'How long before this food is digested?' He said: 'It will be digested within seven days and nights. And even for seven days it will be clearly present without eating further. Even while the food is undigested, no discomfort arises.'

body.text: "yaiśca bhadanta ānanda bhikṣubhiranavakrāntaniyāmairetadbhojanaṃ bhuktam, teṣāmevāvakrāntaniyāmānāṃ pariṇaṃsyati / yairavakrāntaniyāmairetadbhojanaṃ bhuktaṃ, yāvatte 'parimuktacittāḥ" (teṣān-) na pariṇaṃsyati / yairanutpāditabodhircittaiḥ sattvai paribhuktam / ' teṣāmutpāditabodhicittānāṃ pariṇaṃsyati / yairutpāditabodhicittairbhuktam ' teṣāṃ nāpratilabdhakṣāntikānāṃ pariṇaṃsyati / yaiḥ pratilabdhakṣāntikairbhuktam, teṣāmekajātipratibaddhānāṃ pariṇaṃsyati /
body.translated_text: 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, for those monks who have eaten this food but have not yet entered the fixed course of certainty, it will be digested only when they enter the fixed course of certainty. For those who have entered the fixed course of certainty and eaten this food, it will not be digested until they have liberated their minds. For those beings who have eaten it without having generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, it will be digested when they generate <s>bodhicitta</s>. For those who have eaten it having generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, it will not be digested until they attain patience. For those who have eaten it having attained patience, it will be digested when they become bound to one more birth.'

body.text:
"bhadantānanda,tadyathāpi nāmasarannāma bhaiṣajyamudare 'vatīrya, yāvat sarvāṇi viṣāṇyanapagatāni, (tāvan-) na pariṇaṃsyati; tadbhaiṣajyaṃ paścāt pariṇaṃsyati / evameva, bhadantānanda, yāvat sarvakleśaviṣāṇyanapagatāni, tadbhojananna pariṇaṃsyati / tadbhojanaṃ paścāt kevalaṃ pariṇaṃsyati /
"tata āyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat- "idam, bhagavan, bhojanaṃ hi buddhakārya karoti" / āmantrayate sma- "tat tathā, ānanda; yathā vadasi, tat tatheti /
body.translated_text:
'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, just as the medicine called "<s>Saran</s>," having entered the stomach, does not get digested until all poisons have been eliminated — only afterward does that medicine get digested — even so, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, until all the poisons of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) have been eliminated, that food will not get digested; that food will be fully digested only afterward.'
Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the Blessed One: 'This food, Blessed One, indeed accomplishes the work of the <s>Buddha</s>.' He addressed him: 'It is so, <s>Ānanda</s>; it is as you say, it is so.'

body.text: "saṃvidyante, ānanda, buddhakṣetrāṇi, yeṣu bodhisattvā buddhakārya kurvanti; saṃvidyante buddhakṣetrāṇi, yeṣu prabhayā buddhakārya kṛtaṃ, ..... yeṣu bodhivṛkṣeṇa..., .....tathāgatalakṣaṇarūpadarśanena....,..... ......cīvareṇa....., bhojyena....... , .... jalena....., ...... udyānena......, ..... vimānena....., .... kūṭāgāreṇa buddhakārya kṛtaṃ; saṃvidyante ca ānanda, buddhakṣetrāṇi, yeṣu nirmāṇena buddhakārya kṛtaṃ / ānanda, saṃvidyante punarbuddhakṣetrāṇi, (yeṣv) ākāśena buddhakārya kṛtaṃ / evamevākāśāntarīkṣaṃ buddhakārya kṛtaṃ / anena te sattvā vaineyikā bhavanti" / "evameva, ānanda, svapnapratibimbodakacandrapratiśrutkāmāyāmarīcyudāharaṇākṣaraniruktidarśanena tebhyaḥ sattvebhyo buddhakārya kṛtaṃ / saṃvidyante 'pi buddhakṣetrāṇi, yeṣvakṣaravijñaptyā buddhakārya kṛtaṃ / ānanda, yatrāvacanānabhilāpānidarśanānudāhāreṇa tebhyaḥ sattvebhyo buddhakārya kṛtaṃ, (tatra) evaṃ pariśuddhabuddhakṣetrāṇi saṃvidyante /
body.translated_text: "There exist, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) in which <s>bodhisattvas</s> perform the <s>Buddha's</s> work; there exist <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in which the <s>Buddha's</s> work is performed through radiance... through the <s>bodhi</s>-tree... through the display of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> form with marks... through the robe... through food... through water... through a park... through a celestial palace... through a mansion. And there exist, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in which the <s>Buddha's</s> work is performed through emanations. <s>Ānanda</s>, there further exist <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in which the <s>Buddha's</s> work is performed through space. Just so, through the sky itself the <s>Buddha's</s> work is performed. By these means, those beings become disciplined." "Even so, <s>Ānanda</s>, through the display of dreams, reflections, the moon in water, echoes, illusions, mirages, exemplifications, syllables, and etymologies, the <s>Buddha's</s> work is performed for those beings. There also exist <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in which the <s>Buddha's</s> work is performed through the cognizance of syllables. <s>Ānanda</s>, there exist such completely pure <s>buddhakṣetras</s> where, without speech, without discourse, without demonstration, and without exemplification, the <s>Buddha's</s> work is performed for those beings.

body.text: "bhagavatām, ānanda buddhānām īryāpathopabhogaparibhogena sattvadamanārthamakṛtabuddhakārya kiñcinnāsti / ānanda, taiścaturbhirmāraiśca caturaśītīśatasahasraiśca kleśamukhaiḥ, (yaiḥ) sattvāḥ saṃkliṣṭāḥ, sarvaistairbuddhā bhagavanto buddhakārya kurvanti /
body.translated_text: "<s>Ānanda</s>, among the deportment, enjoyments, and possessions of the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, for the purpose of taming beings, there is nothing at all that does not perform the <s>Buddha's</s> work. <s>Ānanda</s>, through those four <s>Māras</s> and through the eighty-four hundred thousand gateways of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) by which beings are defiled—through all of those, the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> perform the <s>Buddha's</s> work.

body.text: "idaṃ hyānanda, sarvabuddhadharmamukhapraveśo nāma dharmamukham / te 'smin dharmamukhe praviṣṭā bodhisattvāḥ sarvodāraguṇavyūhānvitabuddhakṣetreṣu na ca dīnā vottamā vā / sarvodāraguṇavyūhānvitabuddhakṣetreṣu (te), na codagrā vā garvitā vā, tathāgateṣu pratimānam utpādayanti / bhagavanto buddhā (yathā) sarvadharmasamatādhigatāḥ sattvaparipācanārthāya nānāprakārabuddhakṣetrāṇi darśayanti, tadāścaryam /
body.translated_text: "This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Dharma</s>-door called 'The Entry into All <s>Buddha-dharma</s> Gateways.' Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have entered this <s>Dharma</s>-door are neither diminished nor elated in <s>buddhakṣetras</s> endowed with the array of all excellent qualities. In <s>buddhakṣetras</s> endowed with the array of all excellent qualities, they are neither proud nor conceited; they generate a measure of [understanding of] the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. It is wonderful that the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, having realized the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>, display <s>buddhakṣetras</s> of various kinds for the purpose of ripening beings.

body.text: "ānanda, tadyathāpi nāma buddhakṣetrāṇāṃ guṇā anyo 'nyaṃ nānāvidhāḥ, ki tu kriyāmārgeṇa prasāritabuddhakṣetrāṇyākāśaṃc ābhinnāni / evameva, ānanda, tathāgatānāṃ rūpakāyā nānāvidhāḥ, paraṃ tu tathāgatānāmasaṃgajñānaṃ hyābhinnam /
body.translated_text: "<s>Ānanda</s>, just as the qualities of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> are various and different from one another, yet the <s>buddhakṣetras</s> spread through the path of practice and space are undivided; even so, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>rūpakāyas</s> (form-bodies) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are various, yet the unattached knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> is indeed undivided.
