body.text: "ānanda, sarvabuddhānāṃ rūpavarṇatejaḥ kāyalakṣaṇābhijātaśīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktijñānadarśanabalavaiśāradyā-('veṇika-) buddhadharmamahāmaitrīmahākaruṇāhitābhiprāyeryāpathacaryāmārgāyuṣpramāṇadharmadeśanāsattvaparipācanasattvavimocana-(buddha-)kṣetrapariśodhanāni sarvabuddhadharmapariniṣpanne samāni / atas (tathāgatāḥ) samyaksaṃbuddha ityucyante, (ucyante) tathāgatā buddhā iti /
body.translated_text: "<s>Ānanda</s>, the form, complexion, radiance, bodily marks, noble birth, moral discipline, <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), liberation, knowledge-and-vision, the powers, fearlessnesses, unique <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> (<s>āveṇika</s>), great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), beneficent intention, deportment, conduct, the path, the measure of lifespan, <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, the ripening of beings, the liberation of beings, and the purification of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>—in the complete accomplishment of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, these are equal for all <s>Buddhas</s>. Therefore they are called Perfectly Awakened Ones (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>); they are called <s>Tathāgatas</s>; they are called <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: "sukhamavagantum, ānanda, teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ vākyānāṃ yadarthavyāsaśca vacanavibhajanaṃ, tanna sukaram, yadyapyāyuṣpramāṇante kalpasaṃnihitaṃ (syāt) / (ye) trisāhasra (mahāsāhasralokadhātv-)antarbhūtāḥ sattvāḥ (syuḥ), tvamivānando bahuśrutānāṃ smṛtidhāraṇīprāptānāmagratāṃ prāptāḥ, sarve ta ānandapratirūpakasattvāḥ kalpamapi darśyamānāsteṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ vākyānāṃ-'samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ, tathāgataḥ, buddha, iti-niyatārtham avagantumasamarthāḥ / tathā hyānanda, buddhabodhirapramāṇā, acintye tathāgatānāṃ prajñā pratibhānañca" /
body.translated_text: "<s>Ānanda</s>, it is easy to understand these three terms, but the detailed meaning and the analysis of the words—that is not easy, even if the measure of one's lifespan were a <s>kalpa</s>. All the beings within this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s> (billion-world realm), even if they all were foremost among the learned, like you, <s>Ānanda</s>, having attained <s>dhāraṇī</s> and retentive memory—all those beings, even if they were replicas of <s>Ānanda</s>, demonstrating for an entire <s>kalpa</s>, would be unable to comprehend the definitive meaning of those three words: 'Perfectly Awakened One,' '<s>Tathāgata</s>,' '<s>Buddha</s>.' Thus, <s>Ānanda</s>, the awakening of the <s>Buddhas</s> is immeasurable; the wisdom and eloquence of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> is inconceivable."

body.text: atha bhagavantamāyuṣmānānanda etatvocat- "bhagavan, adyāgreṇa 'bahuśrutānām agryo 'ham' iti na pratijānāmi" / bhagavānavocat- "dainyam, ānanda, motpādaya / tat kasya hetoḥ? śrāvakeṣu, na kintu bodhisattveṣu, tvāṃ samanvāhṛtya, 'bahuśrutānāmagryo ('sī-)tyākhyātam mayā / ānanda, bodhisattv ekṣaṇaṃ tu nikṣipa; te hi paṇḍitaiḥ pramāṇagrāhyāḥ / sarvasamudrāṇām, ānanda, gambhīratāṃ pramātuṃ śakyam, paraṃ tu bodhisattvānāṃ prajñājñānasmṛtidhāraṇīpratibhānagambhīratāṃ pramātunna śakyam /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, from this day onward I shall not claim 'I am the foremost among the learned.'" The Blessed One said: "Do not feel downcast, <s>Ānanda</s>. Why? It is among the <s>śrāvakas</s>, not among the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, that I have declared you to be the foremost among the learned, with you in mind. <s>Ānanda</s>, set aside the <s>bodhisattvas</s>; they are not to be measured by the learned. <s>Ānanda</s>, it is possible to measure the depth of all the oceans, but it is not possible to measure the depth of the <s>bodhisattvas'</s> wisdom, knowledge, <s>dhāraṇī</s>, and eloquence.

body.text: "ānanda, upekṣāstu te bodhisattvacaryāsu / tat kasya hetoḥ? (yaḥ), ānanda, anena licchavirvimalakīrtinaikapūrvāhṇe darśito vyūhaḥ, sarva ṛddhiprāptaśrāvakāśca pratyekabuddhāḥ kalpānāmapi śatasahasrakoṭīḥ sarvarddhinirmāṇaprātihāryaiḥ (taṃ) darśayitunna śaknuvanti /"
body.translated_text: "<s>Ānanda</s>, disregard the conduct of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Why? <s>Ānanda</s>, the array that was displayed by this <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> in a single forenoon—all the <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> who have attained supernatural powers would be unable to display that array, even in a hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, with all their miraculous displays."

body.text:
tatassarve te tathāgatasya sugandhakūṭasya buddhakṣetrādāgatāḥ pragṛhītāñjalibodhisattvāstathāgatamabhivanditvā, etadvacanamavocan- "bhagavan, vayamatrāsmin buddhakṣetra avaropitahīnasaṃjñāmanasikārān prahātumicchāmaḥ / tat kasya hetoḥ? bhagavatāṃ buddhānām, bhagavan, buddhaviṣay opāyakauśalyamacintyam / te sarvasattvaparipācanārtha yathā kāmaḥ, tathā tathā kṣetravyūhān deśayanti / asmabhyam, asmatsarvagandhasugandhālokadhātuṃ gatvā, bhagavān bhagavadanusmṛtyāvahadharmayautakaṃ dadātu" / etadavocan /
bhagavānāmantryate sma- "kulaputrāḥ, asti kṣayākṣayannāma bodhisattvavimokṣaḥ / tasmin yuṣmābhiḥ śikṣitavyam / sa katamaḥ? kṣayo nāma hi saṃskṛtam, asaṃskṛtam hyakṣayaḥ / tasmin bodhisattvena saṃskṛtanna kṣapayitavyam, asaṃskṛte na sthātavyam /
body.translated_text:
Then all those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had come from the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sugandhakūṭa</s> (Fragrant Peak), joining their palms, bowed to the <s>Tathāgata</s> and said: "Blessed One, we who had initially planted a low perception and mental attitude regarding this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> now wish to abandon it. Why? The skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) of the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> in the domain of the <s>Buddha</s> is inconceivable. For the purpose of ripening all beings, they display field-arrays in whatever manner they wish. Grant us, Blessed One, some <s>Dharma</s>-gift to take with us as a memento of the Blessed One, when we return to our world-realm, <s>Sarvagandhasugandhā</s>." Thus they spoke.
The Blessed One addressed them: "Sons of good family, there is a <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation called <s>kṣayākṣaya</s> (exhaustion-and-inexhaustibility). You should train in it. What is it? That which is called 'exhaustion' (<s>kṣaya</s>) is the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>); that which is 'inexhaustible' (<s>akṣaya</s>) is the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). The <s>bodhisattva</s> should not exhaust the conditioned, nor should he abide in the unconditioned.

body.text:
"tasmin saṃskṛtākṣayo hi tadyathā- mahāmaitryavināśaḥ, mahākaruṇānutsarjanam, adhyāśayasaṃviveśitasya sarvajñacittasyāsampramoṣaḥ, sattvaparipācane 'khedaḥ, saṃgrahavastūnāmanutsargaḥ, saddharmaparigrahārtha kāyajivitotsargaḥ, kuśalamūleṣvasaṃtuṣṭiḥ, pariṇāmanākauśalye niyojanam, dharmaparyeṣaṇāyāmakausīdyam, dharmadeśanāyāmācāryamuṣṭayakaraṇam, tathāgatadarśanapūjārthodyogaḥ, saṃcintyopapattyātrāsaḥ, saṃpattyāṃ ca vipattyāmanunnatiranavanatā, aśikṣiteṣvanatimanyanā ca śikṣiteṣu śastarīva priyacintā, sfītakleśeṣu yoniśa upasaṃhāraḥ, viveka āramaśca tasminaśleṣaḥ, svasukha anassaktiścāsaktiḥ parasukhe, dhyānasamādhisamapattiṣvavīcisaṃjñā, saṃsāra udyānanirvāṇasaṃjñā, yācakeṣu kalyāṇamitrasaṃjñā, sarvasvaparityāge sarvajñatāpūraṇasaṃjñā, duḥśīleṣu guptisaṃjñā, pāramitāsu mātṛpitṛsaṃjñā, bodhipakṣyadharmeṣu svāmisevāsaṃjñā sarvakuśalamūlasaṃcayenāsantuṣṭiśca sarvabuddhakṣetra guṇaiḥ svakṣetraniṣpādanā, lakṣaṇānuvyañjanaparipūraṇārtham anargaḍayajñavisarjanam, sarvapāpākaraṇena kāyavākcittālaṅkāraḥ, kāyavākcittapariśuddhyāsaṃkhyeyakalpān saṃsaraṇam, cittaparākrameṇāpramāṇabuddhaguṇaśravaṇe 'navalīnatā, kleśaśatrunigrahāya tīkṣṇaprajñāśastradhāraṇam, sarvasattvabhāraharaṇāya skandhadhātvāyatanājñā, mārasenāṃ hantuṃ vīryyajvalanam, niradhimānatāyai jñānaiṣaṇā, dharmodgrahaṇārtham alpecchatā ca santuṣṭiḥ, sarvalokasantoṣaṇāya sarvalokadharmāsaṃbhedaḥ, lokena saha sāmagrīkaraṇārtha sarveryāpathāvināśaḥ, sarvakriyāsamprakāśanāyābhijñopasaṃhāraḥ, sarvaśrutadhāraṇāya dhāraṇīsmṛtijñānāni, sarvasattvasaṃśayacchedanāyendriyavarāvarajñānam, dharmadeśanāyā apratihatādhiṣṭhānam, pratibhānaprāptisulābhenāpratihatapratibhānam, kuśalakarmapathapariśuddhyā devamanuṣyasampattyāsvādanam caturapramāṇaprabhāvanayā brahmamārgapratiṣṭhāpanam, dharmadeśanābhyarthanayā cānumodanāsādhukāreṇa buddhasvarapratilabhbhaḥ, kāyavāgmanaḥ saṃvareṇa viśeṣagāmitayā ca sarvadharmāśleṣeṇa buddheryāpathapratilambhaḥ,
bodhisattvasaṃghasaṃgraheṇa mahāyānāvatāraṇatā, sarvaguṇāvipraṇāśenāpramādaḥ / kulaputrāḥ, (yo) bodhisattva evaṃ hi dharmābhiyuktaḥ, (sa) bodhisattvaḥ saṃskṛtanna kṣapayanti /
body.translated_text:
The inexhaustibility in the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) consists of the following: not destroying great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), not abandoning great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), not losing the mind of omniscience that is established through higher intention, tirelessness in maturing beings, not abandoning the means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), sacrificing body and life for the sake of upholding the true <s>Dharma</s>, dissatisfaction with roots of merit, dedication to skillful dedication, diligence in seeking the <s>Dharma</s>, not holding back in teaching the <s>Dharma</s> like a teacher with a closed fist, eagerness in worshiping and seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s>, fearlessness in deliberately taking rebirth, neither elation in prosperity nor dejection in adversity, not disdaining those who are unlearned and cherishing the learned like a teacher, disciplined application regarding those with abundant afflictions, delight in solitude without attachment to it, non-attachment to one's own happiness and investment in the happiness of others, regarding meditation, concentration, and attainment as being like the <s>Avīci</s> hell, regarding <s>saṃsāra</s> as a garden and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, regarding beggars as spiritual friends, regarding the relinquishing of all possessions as fulfilling omniscience, regarding the immoral with the notion of protection, regarding the perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>) as mother and father, regarding the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣyadharma</s>) as service to one's lord, dissatisfaction with the accumulation of all roots of merit, accomplishing one's own field with all the qualities of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, releasing priceless sacrifices for the sake of fulfilling the marks and secondary characteristics, adorning body, speech, and mind through the non-performance of all evil, purifying body, speech, and mind through wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s> for innumerable <s>kalpas</s>, not being disheartened upon hearing the immeasurable qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> through the valor of the mind, wielding the sharp sword of wisdom to subdue the enemy of afflictions, knowledge of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) for the sake of bearing the burden of all beings, kindling the fire of vigor to defeat <s>Māra</s>'s army, seeking knowledge for the sake of being free from conceit, contentment and few desires for the sake of grasping the <s>Dharma</s>, not violating any worldly conventions for the sake of satisfying all the world, not disrupting all deportments for the sake of harmony with the world, application of superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) for the sake of manifesting all activities, knowledge of <s>dhāraṇī</s>-memory for the sake of retaining all that is heard, knowledge of the higher and lower faculties for the sake of cutting through the doubts of all beings, unimpeded resolve for teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, unimpeded eloquence through the easy attainment of ready speech, enjoyment of divine and human prosperity through purification of the paths of wholesome action, establishment on the path of <s>Brahmā</s> through cultivation of the four immeasurables, attainment of the voice of the <s>Buddha</s> through soliciting <s>Dharma</s> teaching, rejoicing and approval, attainment of the <s>Buddha</s>'s deportment through restraint of body, speech, and mind, through progress toward distinction, and through non-attachment to all <s>dharmas</s>,
entry into the <s>Mahāyāna</s> through gathering the assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and diligence through not losing any good qualities. Sons of good family, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is thus devoted to the <s>Dharma</s> does not exhaust the conditioned.

body.text: "kim asaṃskṛte 'sthānam? yadā śūnyatāyāṃ vyantīkaraṇam, śūnyatāsākṣātkaraṇantu nāsti; animittavyantīkaraṇam, paraṃ tvanimittasākṣātkaraṇannāsti; apraṇihitavyantīkaraṇam, ki tvapraṇihitasākṣātkaraṇannāsti; anabhisaṃskāravyantī-karaṇam, anabhisaṃskārasākṣātkaraṇantu nāsti /
body.translated_text: What is non-abiding in the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>)? There is the practice of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), but no direct realization of emptiness; there is the practice of signlessness (<s>animitta</s>), but no direct realization of signlessness; there is the practice of wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), but no direct realization of wishlessness; there is the practice of non-formation (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>), but no direct realization of non-formation.

body.text: "anityatāpratyavekṣā, paraṃ tu kuśalamūlāsantuṣṭiḥ; duḥkhapratyavekṣā, kiṃ tu saṃcintyopapattiḥ; nairātmyapratyavekṣā, ātmaparityāgastu nāsti /
body.translated_text: There is contemplation of impermanence, yet no dissatisfaction with roots of merit; there is contemplation of suffering, yet deliberate taking of rebirth; there is contemplation of non-self, yet no abandoning of self-sacrifice.

body.text: "śāntipratyavekṣā, paraṃ tūpaśamānutthāpanam; vivekapratyavekṣā, ki tu kāyacittenautsukyam; anālayapratyavekṣā, api tu śucidharmālayapratikṣepo nāsti; anutpādapratyavekṣā, sattvānāṃ tu bhārādānadhāraṇam; anāsravapratyavekṣā, paraṃ tu saṃsāraprabandhotthāpanakaraṇam; apracārapratyavekṣā, sattvaparipācanārtha pracārotpādaḥ; nairātmyapratyavekṣā, api tu sattvamahākaruṇānutsargaḥ; aprarohaṇapratyavekṣā, api tu khalu punaḥ śrāvakaniyatyapātaḥ /
body.translated_text: There is contemplation of peace, yet no cessation of pacification; there is contemplation of solitude, yet eagerness of body and mind; there is contemplation of non-abode, yet no rejection of the abode of pure <s>dharmas</s>; there is contemplation of non-arising, yet bearing and carrying the burden of beings; there is contemplation of being without outflows, yet undertaking the continuation of <s>saṃsāra</s>; there is contemplation of non-movement, yet producing movement for the sake of maturing beings; there is contemplation of non-self, yet not abandoning great compassion for beings; there is contemplation of non-growth, yet not falling into the fixed course of a <s>Śrāvaka</s>.

body.text: "(sarvadharmeṣu) tucchariktaniḥsārāsvāmikāniketapratyavekṣā, paraṃ tvatucchapuṇye cāriktajñāne ca paripurṇasaṃkalp (eṣu) ca svayambhūjñānābhiṣeke ca svayambhūjñānābhiyoge ca nītārthabuddhagotre pratiṣṭhā /
body.translated_text: There is contemplation of all <s>dharmas</s> as worthless, empty, without essence, without owner, and without abode, yet the resolve is set upon non-worthless merit, non-empty knowledge, and full intentions — establishing oneself in the consecration of self-born knowledge, in the practice of self-born knowledge, and in the lineage of the <s>Buddha</s> of definitive meaning.

body.text: kulaputrāḥ, evaṃ hi tādṛśadharmādhimuktabodhisattvo 'saṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, saṃskṛtañcāpi na kṣapayati /
body.translated_text: Sons of good family, thus a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has such aspiration toward the <s>Dharma</s> neither abides in the unconditioned nor exhausts the conditioned.

body.text:
punaraparaṃ, kulaputrāḥ, bodhisattvaḥ puṇyasambhārasya samabhinirhārārtham asaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, jñānasambhārasamabhinirhārārtha saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati /
mahāmaitrī samanvāgataḥ (so) 'saṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, mahākaruṇāsamanvāgataḥ (sa) saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati /
body.translated_text:
Furthermore, sons of good family, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not abide in the unconditioned for the sake of accomplishing the accumulation of merit, and does not exhaust the conditioned for the sake of accomplishing the accumulation of knowledge.
Endowed with great loving-kindness, he does not abide in the unconditioned; endowed with great compassion, he does not exhaust the conditioned.

body.text: "sattvaparipācanārthāya (so) 'saṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, buddhadharmādhimuktikāraṇāt (sa) saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati / buddhalakṣaṇaparipūraṇārtham asaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, sarvajñajñānaparipūraṇārtha saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati / upāyakauśalyakāraṇādasaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, prajñāsuniścitaḥ (sa) saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati / buddhakṣetrapariśodhanārthamasaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, buddhādhiṣṭhānakāraṇāt saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati / sattvārthānubhavakāraṇādasaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, dharmārtha samprakāśanakāraṇāt saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati /
body.translated_text: For the sake of maturing beings, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of aspiration toward the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, he does not exhaust the conditioned. For the sake of fulfilling the marks of the <s>Buddha</s>, he does not abide in the unconditioned; for the sake of fulfilling omniscient knowledge, he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of firm determination in wisdom, he does not exhaust the conditioned. For the sake of purifying the <s>Buddha</s>-field, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment, he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of carrying out the welfare of beings, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of illuminating the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s>, he does not exhaust the conditioned.

body.text: "kuśalamūlasaṃcayārthāyāsaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, kuśalamūlavāsanākāraṇāt saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati / praṇidhānaparipūraṇārthamasaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, apraṇihitakāraṇāt saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati / āśayapariśuddhikāraṇādasaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, adhyāśayapariśuddhikāraṇāt saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati / pañcabhijñāvikrīḍanatākāraṇād asaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, buddhajñānasya ṣaḍabhijñārthāya saṃskṛtanna kṣapayayi /
body.translated_text: For the sake of accumulating roots of merit, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of the imprints of roots of merit, he does not exhaust the conditioned. For the sake of fulfilling his vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), he does not exhaust the conditioned. For the sake of purifying intention, he does not abide in the unconditioned; for the sake of purifying higher intention, he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of playing with the five superknowledges, he does not abide in the unconditioned; for the sake of the six superknowledges leading to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, he does not exhaust the conditioned.

body.text: "pāramitāsaṃcayaparipūraṇārtham asaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, kālaparipūrikāraṇāt saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati / dharmadhanasaṃgrahārthamasaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, prādeśikadharmāspṛhaṇatākāraṇāt saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati / dharmabhaiṣajyasaṃgrahārthamasaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, yathāyogaṃ dharmabhaiṣajyaprayogārthāya saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati /
body.translated_text: For the sake of accumulating and fulfilling the perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of fulfilling the times, he does not exhaust the conditioned. For the sake of gathering the treasure of the <s>Dharma</s>, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of not coveting partial <s>dharmas</s>, he does not exhaust the conditioned. For the sake of gathering the medicine of the <s>Dharma</s>, he does not abide in the unconditioned; for the sake of applying the medicine of the <s>Dharma</s> as appropriate, he does not exhaust the conditioned.

body.text: "pratijñādhairyārthāyāsaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati; pratijñāhānyāḥ paścāt (yathā) aghigaccheta, (sa) saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati / sarva dharmauṣadhyādhānārthāyāsaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, evam mṛdudharmauṣadhaprayogārtha saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati / sa sarvakleśarogaparijñānakāraṇādasaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati, sarvarogasaṃśamanārtha saṃskṛtakṣayannecchati / kulaputrāḥ, ityevaṃ bodhisattvaḥ saṃskṛtanna kṣapayati cāsaṃskṛte na tiṣṭhati / sa hi bodhisattvānāṃ kṣayākṣayannāma vimokṣaḥ / tasmin, satpuruṣāḥ, yuṣmābhirapi yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ" /
body.translated_text: For the sake of steadfastness in his vow, he does not abide in the unconditioned; so that he may realize his vow without decline, he does not exhaust the conditioned. For the sake of providing the remedy of all <s>dharmas</s>, he does not abide in the unconditioned; for the sake of applying the gentle remedy of <s>dharma</s>, he does not exhaust the conditioned. For the sake of fully understanding all affliction-diseases, he does not abide in the unconditioned; for the sake of pacifying all diseases, he does not wish to exhaust the conditioned. Sons of good family, thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> neither exhausts the conditioned nor abides in the unconditioned. That is the liberation of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> called 'exhaustion-inexhaustibility' (<s>kṣayākṣaya</s>). In that, good sirs, you too should practice.

body.text: atha te bodhisattvāḥ, imamupadeśaṃ śrutvā tuṣṭā udagrā āttamanasaḥ pramuditāḥ prītisaumanasyajātāḥ, bhagavatpūjanārthaca tebhyo bodhisattvebhyaścāsmai dharmaparyāyāya pūjanārthaṃ /, sarvamimaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuṃ sarvānekacūrṇagandhadhūpapuṣṣairjānumātram ācchādayanti sma / bhagavataḥ parṣanmaṇḍalamabhikīrya, bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya, bhagavate triḥpradakṣiṇīkṛtya, udānamudānayāmāsuḥ / tatas (te) 'smādbuddhakṣetrādantarhitā ekakṣaṇalavamuhūrtena tasyāṃ sarvagandhasugandhāyāṃ lokadhātvānnyaṣīdan /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having heard this teaching, were delighted, elated, joyful, happy, and filled with pleasure and gladness. For the sake of worshiping the Blessed One, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, they covered this entire trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s>) knee-deep with various powdered incense, perfumes, and flowers. Having showered the Blessed One's assembly, having bowed at the Blessed One's feet with their heads, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, they uttered exclamations of wonder. Then, having disappeared from this <s>Buddha</s>-field in a single instant, they arrived in that world-realm of All-Fragrance (<s>Sarvagandhasugandha</s>).

body.text: 11 abhiratilokadhātvādānaṃ tathāgatākṣobhyasandarśanaṃ ca
body.translated_text: 11. The Bringing of the World-Realm <s>Abhirati</s> and the Display of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>

body.text: atha bhagavāṃllicchavi vimalakīrtimetadavocat- "kulaputra, yadā tathāgataṃ draṣṭumicchasi, tadā kathaṃ paśyasi tathāgatam?" evamāmantrayate sma / licchavirvimalakīrtibhagavantametadavocat- "bhagavan, yadāhaṃ tathāgataṃ draṣṭukāmaḥ, tadādhruvaṃ tathāgatādarśanena (taṃ) paśyāmi / (tathāgataṃ) pūrvāntādanutpannaṃ cāparāntamagacchantaṃca pratyutpanne 'dhvanyapyapratiṣṭhitaṃ paśyāmi / tat kasya hetoḥ?
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: 'Son of good family, when you wish to see the <s>Tathāgata</s>, how do you see the <s>Tathāgata</s>?' Thus he addressed him. The <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to the Blessed One: 'Blessed One, when I wish to see the <s>Tathāgata</s>, then I see him through the certainty of seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s> as not-seen. I see the <s>Tathāgata</s> as unarisen from the past, not going to the future, and not established even in the present time. Why is that?

body.text: "(tathāgato) rūpatathatāsvabhāvaśca rūpāpagataḥ, vedanā-........ saṃjñā ...... saṃskāra........vijñānatathatā svabhāvaśca vijñānāpagataḥ / caturdhātvapratiṣṭhitas (tathāgata) ākāśadhātusamaḥ, ṣaḍāyatanānutpannaḥ, cakṣuḥ śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanomārgasamatikrāntaḥ / (tathāgatas-) traidhātukāsaṃkīrṇaḥ, malatrayarahitaḥ, vimokṣatrayānugataḥ, trividyāprāptaḥ, apratilabdha(śca) sampratilabdhaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> is of the nature of the suchness (<s>tathatā</s>) of form, yet gone beyond form; of the nature of the suchness of sensation... perception... formations... of the nature of the suchness of consciousness, yet gone beyond consciousness. Not established in the four elements, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is equal to the element of space; unarisen in the six sense-bases, having transcended the paths of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. The <s>Tathāgata</s> is unmixed with the three realms, free from the three stains, conformed to the three liberations, attained in the three knowledges, and truly attained through non-attainment.

body.text: "sa) sarvadharmeṣvaśleṣaniṣṭhāgataḥ, bhūtakoṭyapagataḥ, tathatāsupratiṣṭhitaḥ so 'nyonyavigataḥ / (tathāgato) hetvanutpādito 'pratyayapratibaddhaḥ, lakṣaṇāpagataḥ, asalakṣaṇaḥ, na caikalakṣaṇo na ca bhinnalakṣaṇaḥ, akalpitaḥ, asaṃkalpitaḥ, avikalpitaḥ / (tathāgataḥ) pāre nāsti, apāre ca nāsti, nāsti madhye 'pi; iha vā tena vā tatra vānyatra vā nāsti / vijñānena (so) 'jñātavyaḥ, vijñānasthānannāsti; (sa) na ca tamo na cālokaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'He has reached the culmination of non-attachment to all <s>dharmas</s>, gone beyond the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), well-established in suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), free from mutual relation. The <s>Tathāgata</s> is not produced by causes, not bound by conditions, gone beyond marks, without false marks, neither of a single mark nor of diverse marks, unconstructed, unconceived, undiscriminated. The <s>Tathāgata</s> does not exist on this shore, does not exist on the other shore, does not exist in the middle; nor here, nor there, nor elsewhere, nor anywhere. He is not to be known through consciousness; there is no abode of consciousness for him. He is neither darkness nor light.

body.text: "(tathāgato) nāmāpagato nimittāpagataḥ, (sa) nāsti durvalo vā balavān vā, na ca deśastho na ca pakṣasthitaḥ, kuśalākuśalāpagataḥ, saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtāpagataḥ, kaścidabhilāpyo 'rtho nāsti; dānamātsaryaśīladauḥ śīlyakṣāntivyāpādavīryakausīdyadhyānauddhatyaprajñādauṣprajñāsu(so) 'nabhilāpyaḥ / (tathāgato) nāsti satyaṃ vā mṛṣā vāvadhāraṇaṃ vāanavadhāraṇaṃ vā, na ca jagadvidhirna ca jagadabidhiḥ, sarvavādacaryātyantasamucchinnaḥ / (sa) kṣetrabhāvo vā kṣetrābhāvo vā nāsti, na ca dakṣiṇīyo na ca dānānupabhogaḥ, na grāhitavyaṃ vā spṛśeyaṃ vā nimittaṃ vā / (so) 'saṃkṛtaḥ, saṃkhyāvigataḥ, samatāsamaḥ, dharmatāsamāsamaḥ, atulyavīryaḥ, tulanāsamatikrāntaḥ, gamanaṃ vā, āpannaṃ vā, samatikrāntaṃ vā (sa) nāsti / "(tathāgato) 'dṛṣṭaḥ, aśrutaḥ, amataḥ, avijñātaḥ, sarvagranthāpagataḥ, sarvajñajñānasamatāprāptaḥ, sarvadharmasama(tā)nirviśeṣaprāptaḥ, sarvatra niravadyaḥ, akiñcinaḥ, kaṣāyarahitaḥ, akalpaḥ, avikalpaḥ, akṛtaḥ, anutpannaḥ, ajātaḥ, abhūtaḥ, asaṃbhūtaḥ; abhāvī, anabhāvī, abhayaḥ, anālayaḥ; aśokaḥ anānandaḥ, ataraṃgaḥ, sarvavyavahāranirdeśāvaktavyaḥ / "tathāgatakāyo hi, bhagavan, īdṛśaḥ; sa evaṃ draṣṭavyaḥ / ya evaṃ paśyati, samyak paśyati saḥ / yo 'nyathā paśyati, sa mithyā paśyati" / tata āyuṣmāṃśāriputro bhagavantametadavocat- "sa kulaputro vimalakīrtiḥ, bhagavan, kasmādbuddhakṣetrāccyutvā, asmin buddhakṣetra āgataḥ?" bhagavānāmantrayate sma- "śāriputra, imaṃ satpuruṣaṃ 'tvaṃ kasmāccyutvā, iha jāta?' iti pṛccha" / tata āyuṣmāṃśāriputro licchavi vimalakīrtimetadavocat- "kulaputra, tvaṃ kasmāccyutvā, iha jātaḥ?" vimalakīrtirāha-
body.translated_text:
'The <s>Tathāgata</s> is gone beyond name, gone beyond signs. He is neither weak nor strong, neither situated in a place nor positioned on a side, gone beyond wholesome and unwholesome, gone beyond conditioned and unconditioned. There is no expressible meaning regarding him; he is inexpressible with regard to generosity and miserliness, moral discipline and immorality, patience and malice, vigor and laziness, meditation and agitation, wisdom and poor understanding. The <s>Tathāgata</s> is neither truth nor falsehood, neither determination nor non-determination, neither the creator of the world nor the non-creator of the world. All discourse and conduct are utterly cut off in him. He is neither the existence nor the non-existence of a field; he is neither a worthy recipient nor one who does not enjoy gifts; he is neither to be grasped, nor touched, nor signified. He is unconditioned, gone beyond enumeration, equal to equality, equal to the equality of <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality), of incomparable power, having transcended all comparison. He is neither going, nor arrived, nor passed beyond.'
'The <s>Tathāgata</s> is unseen, unheard, unthought, unknown, gone beyond all bonds, having attained the equality of the knowledge of the omniscient, having attained equality with all <s>dharmas</s> without distinction, blameless everywhere, possessing nothing, free from defilement, beyond conceptual construction, beyond discrimination, unmade, unarisen, unborn, non-existent, unbecome; without existence, without non-existence, without fear, without attachment; without sorrow, without joy, without waves — inexpressible in any conventional designation.'
'Blessed One, such indeed is the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; thus should it be seen. Whoever sees thus, sees rightly. Whoever sees otherwise, sees wrongly.' Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the Blessed One: 'Blessed One, from which <s>Buddha</s>-field did this son of good family <s>Vimalakīrti</s> pass away to be born in this <s>Buddha</s>-field?' The Blessed One addressed him: '<s>Śāriputra</s>, ask this good man yourself: "From where did you pass away to be born here?"' Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: 'Son of good family, from where did you pass away to be born here?' <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said:

body.text: "yaḥ sthavireṇa sākṣātkṛtadharmaḥ, kiṃ tasmiścyutyutpattī staḥkecit?" āha- "tasmin dharme keciccyutyutpattī na staḥ" / āha- "bhadanta śāriputra, sarveṣu dharmeṣvevameva cyutyuttyapagateṣu, kasmādevaṃ 'tvaṃ kasmāccyutvā, iha jāta?' iti manyase? bhadanta śāriputra, māyākāranirmitau cet strīṃ vā puruṣaṃ vā 'tvaṃ kasmāccyutvā, iha jāta?' iti pṛcchet, tatsamādhānaṃ kim (abhaviṣyat)?" āha- "nirmāṇañceccyutyutpattyapagataṃ, tat kiṃ vyasarjayiṣyat?" āha- "bhadanta śāriputra, nanu na 'sarvadharmā nirmāṇasvabhāvā iti tathāgatenākhyātam?" āha- "tat tatheti, kulaputra" / āha- "sarveṣu dharmeṣu, bhadanta śāriputra, nirmāṇasvabhāveṣu, kasmādidaṃ 'tvaṃ kasmāccyutvā, iha jāta?' iti manyase? bhadanta śāriputra, cyutirnāmābhisaṃskārasaṃvarta lakṣaṇā; utpattirnāma-sābhisaṃskārasantatilakṣaṇā / tato bodhisattvo yadyapi mriyate, kuśalamūlābhisaṃskāranna kṣapayati / sa yadyapi jāyate, akuśalasantatinna pratisandadhāti" / atha bhagavānāayuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat- "śāriputra, ayaṃ satpuruṣa ihāgatobhiratilokadhātorakṣobhyasya tathāgatasyāntikāt" / āha- "āścaryam, bhagavan, (yathā) 'yaṃ satpuruṣaḥ, etāvadviśuddhabuddhakṣetrādāgato ('smin) bahulātyayaduṣṭe buddhakṣetre 'bhinandati" / tato licchavirvimalakīrtirabravīt- "śāriputra, tat ki manyase? sūryaprabhāsāḥ kimandhakārasahitāḥ?" āha- "no hīdaṃ, kulaputra" / "nanu tau na sahitau?" āha- "tau, kulaputra, asahitau / sūryamaṇḍala abhyudgatamātre, sarvāndhakārā vigacchanti" / āha- "kasmājjambudvīpe sūrya udayati?" āha- "tadhyālokakaraṇārthaṃcāndhakārāpakarṣaṇārtham" / āha- "evameva, bhadanta śāriputra, bodhisattvaḥ sattvapariśodhanārthaṃ ca jñānālokakaraṇārtha ca mahāndhakārāpakarṣaṇārtha saṃcintyāpariśuddhakṣetreṣu jāyate / kleśaiḥ sārdhanna virahati, sarvasattvānāṃ tu kleśāndhakāraṃ vinodayati" / tataḥ sarvāsāṃ tāsāṃ parṣadāṃ 'sābhiratilokadhātuśca so 'kṣobhyastathāgataśca te bodhisattvāśca te mahāśrāvakā asmābhirdraṣṭavyā iti bhāvanābhūt /
body.translated_text: 'In the <s>Dharma</s> that you, elder, have directly realized — is there any passing away or rebirth in it?' He said: 'In that <s>Dharma</s> there is no passing away or rebirth.' He said: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, when all <s>dharmas</s> are likewise free from passing away and rebirth, why do you think "From where did you pass away to be born here?" Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, if a magician were to create a woman or a man and you were to ask "From where did you pass away to be born here?" — what would the answer be?' He said: 'If an emanation is free from passing away and rebirth, what could one reply?' He said: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, has not the <s>Tathāgata</s> declared that all <s>dharmas</s> are of the nature of emanation?' He said: 'That is so, son of good family.' He said: 'When all <s>dharmas</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, are of the nature of emanation, why do you think "From where did you pass away to be born here?" Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, passing away is characterized by the dissolution of conditioned formations; rebirth is characterized by the continuity of conditioned formations. Therefore, even though a <s>bodhisattva</s> dies, he does not exhaust the formations of roots of merit; even though he is born, he does not continue the series of unwholesome [formations].' Then the Blessed One said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: '<s>Śāriputra</s>, this good man has come here from the world-realm <s>Abhirati</s>, from the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>.' He said: 'Wonderful, Blessed One, that this good man, having come from such a pure <s>Buddha</s>-field, delights in this <s>Buddha</s>-field that is full of many faults and evils.' Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said: '<s>Śāriputra</s>, what do you think? Does the radiance of the sun go together with darkness?' He said: 'No indeed, son of good family.' 'Do they not go together?' He said: 'Son of good family, they do not go together. As soon as the disc of the sun has risen, all darkness disappears.' He said: 'Why does the sun rise in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>?' He said: 'For the purpose of bringing light and dispelling darkness.' He said: 'Just so, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> intentionally takes birth in impure <s>Buddha</s>-fields for the purpose of purifying beings, for the purpose of bringing the light of knowledge, and for the purpose of dispelling great darkness. He does not remain with the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), but dispels the darkness of the afflictions of all beings.' Then all those assemblies had this aspiration: 'May we see this world-realm <s>Abhirati</s>, and that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>, and his <s>bodhisattvas</s> and great <s>śrāvakas</s>.'

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvāsāṃ tāsāṃ parṣadāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya, licchavi vimalakīrtimetadavocat- "kulaputra, iyaṃ hi parṣattāmabhiratilokadhātuṃ cākṣobhyaṃ tathāgataṃ draṣṭumicchati; tena tasyai parṣade deśaya" / atha licchavaye vimalakīrtaya evaṃ bhavati sma- "asmāt siṃhāsanād anutthāya, tāmabhiratilokadhātuṃ ca bodhisattvānām anekaśatasahasrāṇi ca sacakravāḍa parvataparivṛtabhavanān devanāgayakṣagandharvāsurāṃśca (tāṃ lokadhātuṃ) sanadītaḍāgotsasarassamudraparikhāṃ ca sasumerugiryalpaharmyā ca sacandrasūryatārakāṃ ca sadevanāgayakṣagandharvasthānāṃ ca sabrahmabhavanaparivārāṃ ca sagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭranaranarīgṛhāṃ ca sabodhisattvaśrāvakaparṣadaṃ cākṣobhyasya tathāgatasya bodhivṛkṣaṃ cāpi parṣatsāgare niṣaṇṇaṃ ca dharma deśayantamakṣobhyaṃ tathāgataṃ ca tāni padmāni, daśadikṣu yāni sattveṣu buddhakārya kurvanti, (tatsarvam upādāsyāmi) / (yās) tisro ratnaniḥśreṇyo jambudvīpādyāvat trayāstriśabhavanaṃ, tāsvabhyāryaniḥśreṇīṣu trayastriṃśā devā akṣobhyasya tathāgatasya darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya ca jambudvīpam upayānti, (tāsu ca) jambudvīpasya manuṣyāstrayastriṃśānāṃ devānāṃ darśanāya trayastriṃśabhavanam ārohanti, (tāśca) tāmevaṃrupām apramāṇaguṇasañcayām abhiratilokadhātum āpskandhādyāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanaṃ kumbhakārasya cakramivopādāya, kevalaṃ chittvā, dakṣiṇapāṇinā ca puṣpamālāmiva gṛhītvā, asyāṃ ca sahālokadhātau prakṣepsyāmi / prakṣipya, asyai sarvaparṣade nirdekṣyāmi" / tato licchavirvimalakīrtiretādṛśaṃ samādhi samāpadyate smaitādṛśaṃ caddhryabhisaṃskāramabhisaṃskaroti sma, (yathā-)bhiratilokadhātuṃ, tāṃ kevalaṃ chittvā, dakṣiṇapāṇinā gṛhītvā, asyāṃ sahālokadhātau prakṣipati sma /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing with his mind the thoughts of all those assemblies, said to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: "Son of good family, this assembly wishes to see the <s>Abhirati</s> world-realm and the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>; therefore show it to this assembly." Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> thought: "Without rising from this lion-throne, I shall take up that <s>Abhirati</s> world-realm together with many hundreds of thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, its dwellings surrounded by <s>Cakravāḍa</s> mountains, its <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, and <s>asuras</s>, its rivers, lakes, springs, ponds, and ocean-moats, its Mount <s>Sumeru</s> and lesser mountains, its moon, sun, and stars, its abodes of <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, its <s>Brahmā</s> realms with their retinues, its villages, cities, towns, districts, kingdoms, and houses of men and women, its assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>śrāvakas</s>, the <s>Bodhi</s> tree of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>, and the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s> himself seated in an ocean-like assembly teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, and those lotuses that perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work among beings in the ten directions—all of this I shall take up. And those three jeweled stairways from <s>Jambudvīpa</s> up to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, upon which the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods descend to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> for seeing, paying homage to, attending upon, and hearing the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>, and upon which the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> ascend to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven to see the gods—all of this <s>Abhirati</s> world-realm, of such immeasurable accumulated qualities, from <s>Ākāśa</s> up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven, I shall cut away entirely like a potter's wheel, seize with my right hand as if it were a flower garland, and cast it into this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm. Having cast it here, I shall show it to this entire assembly." Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> entered such a <s>samādhi</s> and performed such a miraculous feat that he cut away the <s>Abhirati</s> world-realm entirely, seized it with his right hand, and cast it into this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm.

body.text: tatra ye śrāvakabodhisattvadevamanuṣyā divyacakṣurabhijñāprāptāḥ, te krandati sma- "bhagavan, upādīyāmahe / sugata, upādīyāmahe / sugata, asmabhyaṃ śaraṇaṃ kurva"-iti yācante sma / vinayārtha bhagavān tānetadavocat- "bodhisattvena vimalakīrtinohyadhve; sa hi madgocaro nāsti" / tatrānyadevamanuṣyādibhiḥ-kutrohyāmahe-hyajñātamadṛṣṭam / sābhiratilokadhāturasyāṃ sahālokadhātau prakṣipyamāṇāpi, asyāṃ lokadhātau pūrṇatvaṃ vonatvaṃ vā na jñāyete sma, na ca saṃbādho vā bandhanaṃ vā / sāpyabhiratilokadhāturanūnatvā yathāpūrva, paścāttathā dṛśyate sma / atha bhagavāṃśākyamunistāḥ sarvāḥ parṣada āmantrayate sma- "he mitrāṇi, paśyatābhiratilokadhātuṃ cākṣobhyaṃ tathāgataṃ cemān buddhakṣetraśrāvakabodhi sattvavyūhān" / te 'vocan- "dhruvam, bhagavan, paśyāmaḥ" / āha- "(yo) bodhisattva etādṛśaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigrahītukāmaḥ, (tena) tathāgatasyākṣobhyasya bodhisattvānāṃ sarvacaryā anuśikṣitavyāḥ" /
body.translated_text: There, those <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, gods, and humans who had attained the superknowledge of the divine eye cried out: "Blessed One, we are being carried away! <s>Sugata</s>, we are being carried away! <s>Sugata</s>, grant us refuge!" — thus they pleaded. The Blessed One, for the purpose of discipline, said to them: "You are being carried by the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>; this is not my domain." But others among the gods and humans there said: 'Where are we being carried? We do not know, we cannot see.' That <s>Abhirati</s> world-realm, even though cast into this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, showed neither fullness nor deficiency in this world-realm; neither was there any crowding or constriction. And the <s>Abhirati</s> world-realm appeared undiminished, just as before. Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> addressed all those assemblies: "Friends, behold the <s>Abhirati</s> world-realm, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>, and these ornamental arrays of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), <s>śrāvakas</s>, and <s>bodhisattvas</s>." They said: "Indeed, Blessed One, we see them." He said: "A <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to attain such a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should train in all the practices of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>."

body.text:
tathā hyabhiratilokadhātusaṃdarśanasyārddhiprātihāryeṇa cākṣobhyatathāgatasaṃsarśanenāsyāḥ sahālokadhātoścaturdaśadevamanuṣyaprajāyutairanuttarasamyaksambodhicittānyutpāditāni / sarve 'pi tasyāmabhiratilokadhātau janituṃ praṇidhānamakārṣuḥ, bhagavāṃśca sarveṣāṃ teṣāmabhiratilokadhātāvupapatti vyākaroti sma / licchavirvimalakīrtistathā hi sarvāstān, yāvat paripācanīyānasyāṃ sahālokadhātau, sattvān vipācya, tāmabhiratilokadhātuṃ yathāsthānaṃ punaḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati sma / tato bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat- "nanu paśyasi, śāriputra, tāmabhiratilokadhātuṃ cākṣobhyaṃ tathāgatam?" āha- "dhruvam, bhagavan paśyāmi / sarvasattvebhyo 'stu tādṛśo buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaḥ / sarve sattvāśca bhavantu kulaputro licchavirvimalakīrtiryathā tādṛśarddhisampannāḥ / lābhā naḥ sulabdhā yadvayaṃ tādṛśaṃ satpuruṣaṃ paśyāmaḥ / ye sattvāḥ pratyupannasya vā parinirvṛtatathāgatasya vemaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śṛṇvantyantaśaḥ, lābhāsteṣāmapi sulabdhā bhaveyuḥ / kaḥ punarvādo ya (imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ) śrutvā, adhimucyante pattīyantyudgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyantyadhimucya, deśayiṣyanti prapaṭanti parebhyaśca saṃprakāśayiṣyanti bhāvanādhigamānuyuktā (bhaviṣyanti)? "ye sulabdhā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ, dharmaratnanidhi te pratilapsyante / ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ svādhyāyanti, te bhavanti tathāgatasya sahāyāḥ / ya etaddharmādhimuktan satkurvanti paryupāsanti ca, te hi bhūtā dharmapālāḥ / ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ samyag likhanti dhārayiṣyanti mānayiṣyanti, teṣāṃ gṛhe tathāgato vihariṣyati / ye 'smin dharmaryāye 'numodante, te parirakṣanti sarvapuṇyāni / ye kecidito dharmaparyāyādantaśaścatuṣpādikāmapi gāthāmudgṛhya, parebhyo deśayeyuḥ, te hi mahādharmayajñaṃ kuryuḥ / ye(ṣām) asmin dharmaparyāye kṣāntiśca chandaśca buddhiścāsāvabodhanādarśanādhimuktayaḥ, tebhyastadeva vyākaraṇam /
abhiratilokadhatvādānasya tathāgatākṣobhyasaṃdarśanasya ca parivarta ekādaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Through the miraculous display of showing the <s>Abhirati</s> world-realm and the encounter with the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>, fourteen <s>nayutas</s> of gods and humans of this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm generated the mind of <s>anuttarasamyaksambodhī</s> (supreme perfect awakening). All of them made the aspiration to be reborn in the <s>Abhirati</s> world-realm, and the Blessed One prophesied their rebirth in the <s>Abhirati</s> world-realm. Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, having thus ripened all those beings in this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm who were to be ripened, restored the <s>Abhirati</s> world-realm to its original place. Then the Blessed One said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Did you not see, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that <s>Abhirati</s> world-realm and the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>?" He replied: "Indeed, Blessed One, I see them. May all beings possess such an ornamental array of <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) qualities! May all beings become like the son of good family, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, endowed with such miraculous powers! It is our great gain that we see such a noble person. And those beings who hear this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse), whether during the lifetime of the <s>Tathāgata</s> now present or after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>—it is also their great gain. How much more so for those who, having heard it, have faith,

body.text: 12 pūrvayogaḥ saddharmaparīndanā ca
body.translated_text: 12. Former Connections and the Entrustment of the True <s>Dharma</s>

body.text: atha bhagavantaṃ śakro devānāmindra etadavocat- "purā, bhagavan, tathāgatānmaṃjuśrīkumārabhūtācca dharmaparyāyānāṃ bahuśatasahasrāṇyaśrauṣam, paraṃ tu yathāsmāddharmaparyāyādīdṛśācintyavikurvaṇanayapraveśanirdeśaḥ purā na kadācidaśrauṣam /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said to the Blessed One: "Previously, Blessed One, I heard many hundreds of thousands of <s>dharmaparyāyas</s> (discourses) from the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and from the prince <s>Mañjuśrī</s>. However, I have never before heard a teaching on the entry into the method of such inconceivable transformations as this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>.

body.text:
"ye sattvāḥ, bhagavan, imaṃ dharmaparyāyamudgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti, te 'pi niḥsaṃśayametādṛśadharmabhājanaṃ bhaveyuḥ / kaḥ punarvādo ye bhāvanādhigamanānuyuktā (bhaviṣyanti)? te chetsyanti sarvadurgati-(mārgam), tebhyaḥ sarvasugatimārgo vivṛtaḥ; sarvabuddhaiste dṛṣṭā bhaviṣyanti; te sarvaparapravādighnā bhaviṣyanti; sarvamārāstaiḥ suparājitā bhaviṣyanti; te viśodhitabodhisattvamārgā bhaviṣyanti, bodhimaṇḍasamāśritāstathāgatagocare samavasaranti /
"kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā, bhagavan yau dhārayiṣyata imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ, tābhyāṃ sarvaparivāreṇa saha satkāraṃ paryupāsanaṃ kariṣyāmi / (teṣu) grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu, yeṣvayaṃ dharmaparyāyaścaryate nirdiśyate prakāśyate, tena dharmaśravaṇāya saparivāro gamiṣyāmi / aśraddheṣu kulaputreṣu śraddhāmutpādayiṣyāmi, śrāddhānāṃ dhārmikena rakṣāvaraṇa gupti kariṣyāmi" /
body.translated_text:
"Those beings, Blessed One, who will take up this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, hold it, recite it, and master it—they will undoubtedly become vessels of such <s>Dharma</s>. How much more so those who will devote themselves to its practice and realization! They will cut off all paths to lower realms; the path to all happy destinies will be opened for them. They will be seen by all <s>Buddhas</s>. They will defeat all disputants of other doctrines. All <s>Māras</s> will be well-conquered by them. They will have purified the <s>bodhisattva</s> path, will be established on the seat of awakening, and will enter into the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.
"Blessed One, whatever son or daughter of good family shall uphold this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, I, together with my entire retinue, shall pay homage and attend upon them. In whatever villages, cities, towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> is practiced, expounded, and proclaimed, I shall go there with my retinue to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. I shall generate faith in sons of good family who lack faith, and for those who have faith, I shall provide protection, shelter, and guardianship in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>."

body.text: evamukte, bhagavāṃśakraṃ devānāmindrametadāmantrayate sma- "sādhu, devendra, sādhu / (yat) tvayā subhāṣitam, tasmiṃstathāgato 'pyanumodate / (yā), devendra, atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ bhagavatāṃ buddhānāṃ bodhiḥ, sāsmāddharmaparyāyānnirdiṣṭā / ato devendra, ye kecit kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vemaṃ dharmaparyāyamudgrahīṣyanti, antaśaḥ pustake likhiṣyanti, udgrahīṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti, te hyatītānāgatapratyutpannān bhagavato buddhān pūjayiṣyanti /
body.translated_text: When this was spoken, the Blessed One addressed <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'Excellent, Lord of the Gods, excellent! Well said by you; the <s>Tathāgata</s> too rejoices in this. Lord of the Gods, the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones of the past, future, and present, has been expounded from this <s>Dharma</s> discourse. Therefore, Lord of the Gods, whatever sons or daughters of good family take up this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, even write it in a book, take it up, recite it, and master it — they will have worshipped the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones of the past, future, and present.

body.text: "ayaṃ, devendra, trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātustathāgataiḥ paripūrṇaḥ (syāt, paripūrṇas) tadyathāpi nāmekṣuvanairvā naḍavanairvā veṇuvanairvā tilavanairvā khadiravanairvā; (yairayaṃ lokadhātuḥ) paripūrṇastāṃstathāgatān, klpaṃ vā kalpādhikaṃ vā, kulaputroo vā kuladuhitā vā mānayedgurukuryāt satkuryāt pūjayet sarvapūjāsukhopadhānaiḥ / teṣāṃ parinirvṛtānāmapi tathāgatānāmekaikasya tathāgatasya pūjanārtha sarvaratnamayaṃ vistareṇa caturmahādvīpakalokapramāṇamārohe brahmalokasamprāptamucchritacchatrapatākayaṣṭisūpaśobhitam ekāntakaṭhorākuthitaśārīrikadhāstūpaṃ (kuryāt) / sa evameva sarvatathāgatānāṃ pratyekaṃ stūpaṃ kṛtvā, tat kalpaṃ vā kalpādhikaṃ vā sarvapuṣpagandhadhvajapatākaiḥ pūjayedghaṭṭiyadundubhitūryaiśca /
body.translated_text: 'Suppose, Lord of the Gods, this great trichiliocosm were filled with <s>Tathāgatas</s>, as dense as groves of sugarcane, or reeds, or bamboo, or sesame, or acacia; and suppose a son or daughter of good family were to honor, revere, respect, and worship those <s>Tathāgatas</s> with all provisions of comfort for a <s>kalpa</s> or more. And after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, for the worship of each and every <s>Tathāgata</s>, one were to build a <s>stūpa</s> made entirely of precious jewels, as vast as the four-continent world in extent, reaching up to the <s>Brahma</s> world in height, adorned with raised umbrellas, banners, and poles, densely packed with <s>śarīra</s> (relics). Having built such a <s>stūpa</s> for each of all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, one were to worship them for a <s>kalpa</s> or more with all flowers, fragrances, banners, flags, bells, and drums.

body.text:
"tat ki manyase, devendra, api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tato nidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet?" āha- "bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata / kalpakoṭiśatasahasrairapi tasya puṇyaskandhasya paryantamanuprāptumaśakyam" / bhagavānāmantrayate sma- "adhimucyasva., devendra, tvayānugantavyam yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vemamacintyavimokṣanirdeśasya dharmaparyāyamudgṛhṇīyādvācayet paryavāpnuyāt, (so 'smād-) bahu(taraṃ) puṇyaṃ prasavet / tat kasya hetoḥ? bhagavatāṃ buddhānāṃ hi bodhiḥ, devendra, dharmasambhavā; sā ca dharmapūjāyai śakyā, na paraṃ tvāmiṣeṇa (pūjyā) / anene paryāyeṇa, devendra, tvayaivaṃ veditavyam" /
"bhūtapūrva, devendra, atīte 'dhvanyasaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairasaṃkhyeyataraivipulairaprameyairacintyaistebhyaḥ pareṇa paratareṇa yadāsīt tena kālena tena samayena bhaiṣajyarājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddhobhagavān vicāraṇe kalpe mahāvyūhāyāṃ lokadhātau / tasya bhaiṣajyarājasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksambuddhasya viśatyantarakalapānāyuṣpramāṇamabhūt / tasya ṣaṭtriśatkoṭinayutāḥ śrāvaka(saṃnipāto) 'bhūt dvādaśakoṭinayutā bodhisattva(saṃnipāto) 'bhūt /
body.translated_text: 'What do you think, Lord of the Gods — would that son or daughter of good family produce much merit from that cause?' He said: 'Much, Blessed One! Much, Well-Gone One! Even in a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, it would be impossible to reach the end of that mass of merit.' The Blessed One said: 'Accept this, Lord of the Gods; you should understand that a son or daughter of good family who takes up, recites, and masters this <s>Dharma</s> discourse of the Teaching of the Inconceivable Liberation would produce far more merit than that. And why is that? Because the <s>bodhi</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, Lord of the Gods, arises from the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: "tena khalu punaḥ samayena ratnacchattro nāma rājodapādi cakravartī cāturdvīpaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ / purṇa cāsyābhūt sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarupiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām /
body.translated_text: 'Then at that time, a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) named <s>Ratnacchattra</s> arose, lord of the four continents, endowed with the seven treasures. He had a full thousand sons, heroes and warriors, of excellent bodily form, crushers of enemy armies.

body.text: "sa ratnacchattro rājā pañcāntarakalpān sarvasukhopadhānairbhagavantaṃ bhaiṣajyarājaṃ tathāgataṃ saparivāraṃ mānayati sma / teṣu pañcāntarakalpeṣvatīteṣu, devendra, ratnacchattro rājā sahasraṃ putrānetasavocat- 'he, vitta / ahaṃ tathāgatamapūjayam / ata idānīṃ yūpamapi pūjayata tathāgatam' / tataste rājakumārāḥ pitre ratnacchattrāya rājñe sādhukāraṃ dattvā, tasmai pratyaśrauṣuḥ / te ca saha gaṇena tathāgataṃ bhaiṣajyarājaṃ pañcāntarakalpān sarvasukhopadhānaiḥ satkaronti sma /
body.translated_text: 'King <s>Ratnacchattra</s> honored the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> together with his retinue with all provisions of comfort for five intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. After those five intermediate <s>kalpas</s> had passed, Lord of the Gods, King <s>Ratnacchattra</s> said to his thousand sons: "My sons, I have worshipped the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Now you too should worship the <s>Tathāgata</s>." Then those princes, giving their approval to their father King <s>Ratnacchattra</s>, agreed. Together with their retinue, they honored the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> for five intermediate <s>kalpas</s> with all provisions of comfort.

body.text: "teṣu candracchattrasya nāma rājaputrasya rahogatasyaivaṃ bhavati sma- 'tasyāḥ pūjāyā anyā viśiṣṭatarodārā pūjā nanu bhavatī' ti / buddhādhiṣṭhānenāntarīkṣāddevā etadāhuḥ- 'dharmapūjā hi, satpuruṣa, sarvapūjāsūttamā / sa āha- 'sā dharmapūjā kimasti?' devā āhuḥ- 'tasya, satpuruṣa, tathāgatasya bhaiṣajyarājasya samīpaṃ gatvā, sā dharmapūjā kimastīti pṛccha / bhagavāṃste vyākariṣyati' /
body.translated_text: 'Among them, the prince named <s>Candracchattra</s>, while in solitude, had this thought: "Is there not another worship that is more distinguished and noble than this worship?" Through the <s>Buddha</s>'s power, gods from the sky spoke thus: "Good sir, the worship of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmapūjā</s>) is indeed the highest of all worships." He asked: "What is this worship of the <s>Dharma</s>?" The gods replied: "Good sir, go to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> and ask what the worship of the <s>Dharma</s> is. The Blessed One will explain it to you."

body.text: "atha, devendra, candracchattro rājakumāro yena bhagavān bhaiṣajyarājastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya, bhagavatpādau śirasā vanditvā, ekānte 'sthāt / ekāntasthitaścandracchattro rājaputro bhagavantaṃ bhaiṣajyarājaṃ tathāgatametadavocat- 'dharmapūjā nāma, bhagavan, sā kimasti?'
body.translated_text: 'Then, Lord of the Gods, Prince <s>Candracchattra</s> approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. Having approached and bowed at the Blessed One's feet with his head, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, Prince <s>Candracchattra</s> said to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>: "What, Blessed One, is the worship of the <s>Dharma</s>?"

body.text: "sa bhagavānāmantrayate sma- 'kulaputra, dharmapūjā hi tathāgatabhāṣitā gambhīrasūtrāntāḥ gambhīrāvabhāsāḥ sarvalokavipratyanīkā durvigāhyā durdṛśā duravabodhāḥ sūkṣmā nipuṇā atarkāvacarāḥ / (te sūtrāntā) bodhisattvapiṭakāntarbhūtā dhāraṇīsūtrāntarājamudrāmudritā avaivartika(dharma-) cakrasaṃdarśakāḥ ṣaṭpāramitāsambhūtāḥ sarvagrāhāparigṛhītāḥ / "'(te sūtrāntā) bodhipakṣyadharmadsamanvāgatā bodhyaṅganiṣpādanāparyāpannāḥ sattvamahākaruṇāvatāraṇā mahāmaitrīsaṃdarśakāḥ sarvamāradṛṣṭigatāpagatāḥ pratītyasamutpādasaṃdarśakāḥ /
body.translated_text: 'The Blessed One said: "Son of good family, the worship of the <s>Dharma</s> consists in the profound <s>sūtrāntas</s> spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> — profound in their illumination, contrary to the entire world, hard to fathom, hard to see, hard to understand, subtle, refined, and beyond the range of reasoning. These <s>sūtrāntas</s> are included in the <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s>, sealed with the royal seal of the <s>dhāraṇī</s> discourse, showing the irreversible <s>Dharma</s> wheel, born from the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), free from all grasping. They are endowed with the <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>), accomplishing the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), leading beings into great compassion, showing great loving-kindness, free from all views and paths of <s>Māra</s>,

body.text: "'(dharmeṣu te sūtrāntā) anātmakā niḥsattvā nirjīvā niṣpudgalāḥ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitānabhisaṃskārānutpādāsambhavasamprayuktāḥ / (te) bodhimaṇḍaṃ samudāgacchanti dharmacakrapravartakāḥ / praśaṃsitās- (te) varṇitā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādhipatibhiḥ / (sūtrāntāste) saddharmavaṃśāsraṃsanā dharmakośagrāhakā dharmapūjāvarāpannāḥ / sarvāryajanaiḥ parigṛhītās (te) sarvabodhisattvacaryāḥ samprakāśayanti bhūtārthadharmapratisaṃvidāpannāḥ / dharmasūtrāntā anityatāduḥkhanairātmyaśānti (-nirdeśa-) nairyānikāḥ /
body.translated_text: '"In those <s>sūtrāntas</s>, <s>dharmas</s> are without self, without a being, without a life-force, without a person; they are conjoined with emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), signlessness (<s>animitta</s>), wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), non-formation, non-arising, and non-origination. They lead to the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>) and set turning the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>. They are praised and lauded by the lords of <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>. Those <s>sūtrāntas</s> maintain the lineage of the true <s>Dharma</s>, guard the treasury of the <s>Dharma</s>, and attain the highest worship of the <s>Dharma</s>. Embraced by all noble ones, they illuminate all the practices of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, endowed with the analytical understanding of the true meaning of the <s>Dharma</s>. Those <s>Dharma</s> <s>sūtrāntas</s> teach impermanence, suffering, non-self, and peace.

body.text: "'mātsaryadauḥśīlyavyāpādakausīdyamuṣitasmṛtiduṣprajñāvasāda parapravādikudṛṣṭisarvālambanābhiniveśāṃ jahati (te) sarvabuddhastomitāḥ, saṃsārapakṣapratipakṣā nirvāṇasukhaṃ samprakāśayanti / ye tādṛśasūtrāntāḥ samprakāśanadhāraṇapratyavekṣaṇasaddharmasaṃgrahāḥ, sā hi dharmapūjā nāma /
body.translated_text: '"They cause the abandonment of miserliness, poor morality, ill-will, laziness, lost mindfulness, poor understanding, despondency, and all attachments to heretical views and false doctrines of other systems. Praised by all <s>Buddhas</s>, they are the antidote to <s>saṃsāra</s> and illuminate the happiness of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. The illumination, maintenance, examination, and preservation of the true <s>Dharma</s> of such <s>sūtrāntas</s> — that is called the worship of the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: "'punaraparaṃ, kulaputra, dharmapūjā hi dharmā-(nu-)dharmanidhyaptirdharmā-(nu-) dharmapratipattiḥ pratītyasamutpādasamādānaṃ; (sā) sarvāntagrāhadṛṣṭirahitā, anutpādānopapattikṣāntiḥ, nairātmyaniḥsattvapraveśaḥ, hetupratyayo ravirodho 'vivādo 'kalahaḥ, ahaṃkāramama(kārā-)pagatā /
body.translated_text: '"Furthermore, son of good family, the worship of the <s>Dharma</s> consists in reflection in accord with the <s>Dharma</s>, practice in accord with the <s>Dharma</s>, and undertaking <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination). It is free from all extreme views and grasping; it is the patience with non-arising and non-cessation (<s>anutpādānopapattikṣānti</s>), the entry into non-self and non-being. It is without contention, without dispute, without quarrel regarding causes and conditions, free from the notions of 'I' and 'mine.'

body.text: "'(dharmapūjā) hyarthapratisaraṇanna vyañcanapratisaraṇam, jñānapratisaraṇanna vijñānapratisaraṇam, nītārtha sūtrapratisaraṇanna neyārthasaṃvṛtyabhiniveśaḥ, dharmatāpratisaraṇanna pudgaladṛṣṭyupalabdhigrahaṇābhiniveśaḥ; yathābuddhadharmamavabodhaḥ, anālayapraveśaḥ, alayasamuddhātaḥ; pratītyasamutpādasya dvādaśāṃge(ṣu) tadyathā- avidyānirodhād yāvajjarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā nirudhyanta ityakṣayasattvadṛṣṭyabhinirhāreṇābhisampannaṃ sarvadṛṣṭyadarśanaṃ ca-sā hi, kulaputra, anuttarā dharmapūjā nāma' /
body.translated_text: '"The worship of the <s>Dharma</s> takes refuge in meaning, not in words; takes refuge in knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), not in consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>); takes refuge in definitive <s>sūtras</s>, without attachment to those requiring interpretation and conventional meaning; takes refuge in the nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmatā</s>), without grasping through the view of a person. It is the understanding of the <s>Buddhadharma</s> as it truly is, the entry into non-attachment, the uprooting of attachment. It consists in the twelve links of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), namely: from the cessation of ignorance up to the cessation of old age, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, mental anguish, and vexation — accomplished through the realization of the indestructible view of beings, and the non-seeing of all views. This, son of good family, is the unsurpassed'

body.text:
"tatassa rājaputraścandracchattraḥ, devendra, bhagavato bhaiṣajyarājāttathāgatāddharmapūjāmevaṃ śrutvā, anulomikīṃ dharmakṣānti prāpnoti sma / sarvavastravibhūṣaṇeṣu tasmai bhagavata upanāmiteṣu, etadvacanamavocat- 'bhagavati tathāgate parinirvṛte, saddharmaparigrahapūjanārtha saddharma parigrahītum utsahe / adhitiṣṭhatu māmevaṃ bhagavān, yathāhaṃ māraparapravādino nihatya, saddharma parigṛhṇīyām' /
"tathāgatastasyādhyāśayaṃ buddhvā, 'paścimakāle pāścimasamaye saddharmanagaraṃ pālayiṣyase rakṣiṣyasi parigrahīṣyasī'-(ti) vyākaroti sma /
"atha sa rājaputraścandracchattrastathā tathāgatapratiṣṭhitaśraddhayāgāradanāgārikāṃ pravrajitaḥ kuśale(ṣu) dharme(ṣū) vīryamārabhate sma / ārabdhivīryaḥ sthitvā, kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu supratiṣṭhitaḥ so 'cireṇa dhāraṇīgatigataḥ pañcabhijñā utpādayati sma / so 'nācchedyapratibhānapratilābhī, bhagavati bhaiṣajyarāje tathāgate parinirvṛte, abhijñādhāraṇīivaśena dharmacakraṃ pravartayati sma / sa bhagavān bhaiṣajyarājastathāgato yathā, tathā daśāntarakalpān (dharmacakram) anupravartayati sma /
"tathā hi, devendra, candracchattrasya bhikṣoḥ saddharmaparigrahābhiyogena koṭidaśaśataṃ sattvā anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi(mārg-) āvaivartikā abhūvan / prāṇināṃ catvāriśannayutāni śrāvakapratyekabuddhayāne vinītāny (abhūvan) / apramāṇasattvāḥ svargeṣūtpadyante sma /
"manyethāḥ, devendra, anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena ratnacchattro nābhābhudrājā cakravartī / na khalu punastvayaivaṃ draṣṭavyam / tat kasya hetoḥ? ayameva sa ratnārcistathāgatastena kālena tena samayena ratnacchattro nāma rājā cakravartyabhūt / (ye) tasya ratnacchattrasya rājñaḥ putrāḥ sahasramabhūvan, te santīme vartamānasya bhadrakalpasya bodhisattvāḥ / asmin bhadrakalpe pūrṇabuddhānāṃ sahasramutpadyante / teṣāṃ catvāro hi-krakucchandādaya utpannapūrvāḥ / avaśiṣṭā api prādurbhaviṣyanti-kakutsundādayo yāvadrocaṃ / ante roco nāma tathāgata utpadyate / "manyethāḥ, devendra, anyaḥ sa tena kālena ten samayena candracchattro nāma rājaputro 'bhūt tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyarājasya tathāgatasya saddharmaparigrāhakaḥ / na khalu punastvayaivaṃ draṣṭavyam / tat kasya hetoḥ? ahameva sa, devendra, tena kālena tena samayena candracchattro nāma rājaputro 'bhūvam /
body.translated_text:
"Then that prince <s>Candracchattra</s>, O lord of gods, having heard from the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> about the <s>Dharma</s>-offering, attained <s>anulomikī dharmakṣānti</s> (acquiescent patience with the <s>Dharma</s>). He offered all his garments and ornaments to the Blessed One and said: 'When the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, I am ready to uphold the true <s>Dharma</s> for the purpose of venerating and preserving it. May the Blessed One empower me so that I may defeat <s>Māra</s> and the proponents of other doctrines and uphold the true <s>Dharma</s>.'
"The <s>Tathāgata</s>, knowing his higher aspiration, predicted: 'In the last age, in the final period, you will guard, protect, and uphold the fortress of the true <s>Dharma</s>.'
"Then that prince <s>Candracchattra</s>, with faith established in the <s>Tathāgata</s>, went forth from the household life into homelessness and began to exert vigor in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Having stood firm with vigor exerted, well-established in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, he soon attained the course of <s>dhāraṇī</s> and developed the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges). Having obtained inexhaustible eloquence, after the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> had attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, he turned the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel through the power of his superknowledges and <s>dhāraṇī</s>. As the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> had [turned it], so he continued turning the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel for ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s>.
"Thus, O lord of gods, through the monk <s>Candracchattra's</s> devotion to upholding the true <s>Dharma</s>, a thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of beings became irreversible on the path to <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). Forty <s>nayutas</s> of living beings were trained in the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles. Immeasurable beings were reborn in the heavens.
"Do you think, O lord of gods, that king <s>Ratnacchattra</s>, the <s>cakravartin</s>, was someone else at that time? You should not view it so. Why? That very <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnārcis</s> was at that time the <s>cakravartin</s> king named <s>Ratnacchattra</s>. The thousand sons of king <s>Ratnacchattra</s>—they are the <s>bodhisattvas</s> of the present <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon). In this <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>, a full thousand <s>Buddhas</s> will arise. Of these, four, beginning with <s>Krakucchanda</s>, have already arisen. The remaining ones, beginning with <s>Kakutsunda</s> up to <s>Roca</s>, will also appear. At the end, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Roca</s> will arise.
"Do you think, O lord of gods, that prince <s>Candracchattra</s>, who upheld the true <s>Dharma</s> of the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, was someone else at that time? You should not view it so. Why? I myself, O lord of gods, was at that time that prince named <s>Candracchattra</s>.

body.text:
"anena paryāyeṇa, devendra, vedyam- yāvattathāgatapūjāḥ, (tāsu) dharmapūjā hyuttamā nāma, varā paramā varāgrā praṇītottarānuttareti / tasmāttarhi, devendra, nāmiṣeṇa dharmapūjayā pūjā me kartavyā / nāmiṣeṇa satkāro me kartavyaḥ, dharmasatkātreṇa mānayitavyam" /
atha bhagavān maitreyaṃ bodhisattvammahāsattvamāmantrayate sma- "imāmahaṃ maitreyāsaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭisamudānītāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhi tvayi parīndāmi, yathā paścime kāle paścime samaye 'yamevaṃrūpo dharmaparyāyastvadadhiṣṭhānena parigṛhīto jambudvīpe vardheta na cāntardhīyeta, tat kasya hetoḥ? anāgate 'dhvani, maitreya, (ye) 'varipitakuśalamūlāḥ kulaputrakuladuhitṛdeva nāgayakṣagandharvāsurā anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhisamprasthitāḥ, ta imaṃ dharmaparyāyanna śrutvā, dhvaṃsiṣyante / evaṃrupaṃ sūtrāntaṃ śrutvā, prahṛṣṭāḥ śraddhāṃ pratilapsyante śirasā cā- (bhivandya, taṃ) grahīṣyanti / teṣāṃ kulaputrakuladuhitṝṇāṃ rakṣaṇārthāya, maitreya, tena kālena tvayāyamīdṛśaḥ sūtrāntaḥ sfaraṇīyaḥ /
body.translated_text:
"By this reasoning, O lord of gods, it should be understood that among all offerings to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-offering is called the supreme, the excellent, the paramount, the most excellent, the highest, the most sublime, the unsurpassed. Therefore, O lord of gods, the offering to me should be made not with material gifts but with the <s>Dharma</s>-offering. Honor should be paid to me not with material gifts but by honoring me through the <s>Dharma</s>."
Then the Blessed One addressed the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: "I entrust to you, <s>Maitreya</s>, this <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) that I have accumulated over incalculable <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, so that in the last age, in the final period, this very <s>Dharma</s>-discourse (<s>dharmaparyāya</s>), upheld by your empowerment, may flourish and not disappear in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Why? In the future, <s>Maitreya</s>, there will be sons and daughters of good family, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, and <s>asuras</s> who have planted roots of merit and have set forth toward <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s>. If they do not hear this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, they will be ruined. But upon hearing such a <s>sūtra</s>, they will be delighted, will gain faith, and will venerate it with bowed heads and will take it up. For the sake of protecting those sons and daughters of good family, <s>Maitreya</s>, you must at that time propagate this very <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: "ime hi, maitreya, bodhisattvānāṃ dve mudre / katame dve? nānāpadavyañjanaprasannasya mudrā gambhīreṇa dharmanayenātrastasya yathābhūtaṃ pratipannakasya mudrā ca / te, maitreya, bodhisattvānāṃ dve mudre / tato ye bodhisattvā nānāpadavyañjanaprasannāstatparāḥ, te hyādikarmikā acirabrahmacāriṇo veditavyāḥ / ye, maitreya, bodhisattvā asya gambhīrasyānupaliptasya sūtrāntasya yamakavyatyastāhārasya granthaṃ vā paṭalaṃ vā paṭhanti śṛṇavantyadhimucyante deśayanti, (te) hi cirabrahmacāriṇo veditavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: "There are, <s>Maitreya</s>, two seals of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. What are the two? The seal of one who delights in various elaborate words and syllables, and the seal of one who, unfearful of the profound method of the <s>Dharma</s>, has practiced in accordance with reality. <s>Maitreya</s>, those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are devoted to delight in various elaborate words and syllables should be known as beginners, newly ordained ones (<s>ādikarmika</s>). But those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Maitreya</s>, who read, hear, accept, and teach the text or chapter of this profound, untainted <s>sūtra</s> with interwoven meanings—they should be known as long-ordained ones (<s>cirabrahmacārin</s>).

body.text: "ādikarmikāstataḥ, maitreya, bodhisattvā dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmātmānaṃ vraṇayanti gambhīre ca dharme na nidhyāyanti / katame dve? aśrutapūrva gambhīraṃ sūtrāntaṃ śrutvā, trastāśca saṃśayitā nānumodante / sa evamasmābhiraśrutapūrvaḥ kuta āgata iti (pṛcchantastaṃ) tyajanti / ye kulaputrā gambhīraṃ sūtrāntamudgṛhṇanti gambhīradharmabhājanabhūtāśca gambhīraṃ dharma deśayanti, tebhyo na sevanti cāsamāgamā na paryupāsate tāṃ ca na satkurvanti / antatasteṣvavarṇamapi niścārayanti / tābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmādikarmikabodhisattvā ātmānaṃ vraṇayanti gambhīre ca dharme nāvakalpayanti /
body.translated_text: "Beginner <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Maitreya</s>, injure themselves in two ways and do not contemplate the profound <s>Dharma</s>. What are the two? First, upon hearing a profound <s>sūtra</s> they have never heard before, they become frightened and doubtful, and do not rejoice. They reject it, asking, 'This, which we have never heard before—where has it come from?' Second, they do not serve, do not associate with, do not attend upon, and do not honor those sons of good family who take up the profound <s>sūtra</s> and who are vessels for the profound <s>Dharma</s> and who teach the profound <s>Dharma</s>; and they even disparage them. By these two causes, beginner <s>bodhisattvas</s> injure themselves and do not become suited to the profound <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text:
"tābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ gambhīrādhimuktika bodhisattvā ātmānaṃ vraṇayanti cānutpattikadharmakṣāntinna labhante / katame dve? ādikarmikānaciracaritān bodhisattvān avamanyante vimānayanti, na (samā-)dāpayanti na (vi-)varanti na deśayanti / gambhīre (dharme) 'lpaśraddhāḥ śikṣānna mānayanti, lokasya cāmiṣadānena na tu dharmadānena sattvānupakurvanti /
"maitreya, gambhīradhimuktikabodhisattvā ābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmātmānaṃ vraṇayanti cānutpattikadharmakṣānti śīghranna labhante" / evamāmantrayate sma /
bhagavantaṃ bodhisattvo maitreya etadavocat- "bhagavatā yathā subhāṣitam, bhagavan, (tad) āścaryam / sādhu, bhagavan / adyāgreṇa, bhagavan, imānatyayān (vi-)varjayeyam / (yā) tathāgatenāsaṃkhyeyakoṭinayutaśatasahasrebhyaḥ kalpebhyo 'nuttarasamyaksaṃbodhiḥ samudānītā, imāmārakṣiṣyāmi dhārayiṣyāmi /
"(ye) 'nāgate ('dhvani) kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā bhājanabhūtāḥ, tebhya īdṛśaṃ sūtrāntaṃ hastagataṃ kariṣyāmi / (teṣāṃ) smṛtimupasaṃhariṣyāmi yayemamevaṃrūpaṃ sutrāntam / adhimucyodgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti parpavāpsyanti viveśayanti likhiṣyanti parebhyaśca vistareṇa samprakāśayiṣyanti / tānahaṃ, bhagavan, prasthāpayiṣyāmi / (ye) bhagavan, tena samayenāsminevaṃrūpe sūtrānte 'dhimucyante 'bhiniviśanti ca, te hi, bhagavan, maitreyasya bodhisattvasyādhiṣṭhānenādhiṣṭhitā veditavyāḥ" /
body.translated_text:
"By these two causes, <s>bodhisattvas</s> of profound aspiration also injure themselves and do not attain <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (patience with the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>). What are the two? They look down upon and disrespect beginner <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have not long practiced; they do not encourage, instruct, or teach them. They have little faith in the profound <s>Dharma</s>, do not honor the training, and help beings through material giving rather than through <s>Dharma</s>-giving.
"<s>Maitreya</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s> of profound aspiration injure themselves by these causes and do not quickly attain <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>." Thus he addressed him.
The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Well spoken by the Blessed One! It is wonderful, Blessed One. Blessed One, from this day onward I shall avoid these faults. I shall guard and uphold this <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> that the <s>Tathāgata</s> has accumulated over incalculable <s>koṭi-niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s>.
"Those sons and daughters of good family in the future who are vessels [for the <s>Dharma</s>]—I shall place such a <s>sūtra</s> in their hands. I shall bring forth in them the mindfulness by which they will accept, uphold, recite, penetrate, and comprehend this very <s>sūtra</s> of such a nature, and will copy and explain it in detail to others. Blessed One, I shall set them forth. Those, Blessed One, who at that time accept and devote themselves to such a <s>sūtra</s> of this nature—they, Blessed One, should be known as empowered by the empowerment of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>."

body.text: atha bhagavān maitreyāya bodhisattvāya sādhukāramadāt- "sādhu, maitreya, sādhu / subhāṣitaṃ tatte vākyam / tathāgato 'pi tatte subhāṣitamanumodayati" /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One praised the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: "Excellent, <s>Maitreya</s>, excellent! Well spoken is this word of yours. The <s>Tathāgata</s> also rejoices in your well-spoken word."

body.text: tatas (sarve) te bodhisattvā ekanirghoṣiṇaitadvākyamavocan- "vayamapi, bhagavan, tathāgate parinirvṛte, nānābuddhakṣetrebhya āgatāstathāgatasya buddhasyemāṃ bodhimupabṛṃhayiṣyāmaḥ / te 'pi kulaputrā adhimokṣayiṣyanti" /
body.translated_text: Then all those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, with a single voice, said: "We also, Blessed One, having come from various <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), after the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Buddha</s> has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, will promote this awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Buddha</s>. We too will cause those sons of good family to accept it."

body.text: atha bhagavantaṃ caturmahārājikā (devā) apyetadavocan- "yeṣu yeṣu, bhagavan, grāmanagaramigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣvevaṃrupo dharmaparyāyaścarito deśitaḥ samprakāśitaḥ, teṣu teṣu, bhagavan, vayamapi caturmahārājikā (devāḥ) sabalavāhanaparivārā dharmaśravaṇārtham eṣyāmaḥ / teṣāṃ dharmabhāṇakānām ā yojanāparisāmantakādrakṣāṃ kariṣyāmo yathā na kaścitteṣāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāmavatāraprekṣyavatāragaveṣyavatāraṃ lapsyate" /
body.translated_text: Then the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> heaven also said to the Blessed One: 'Blessed One, in whatever villages, cities, towns, kingdoms, and royal capitals this <s>Dharma</s> discourse is practiced, taught, and illuminated — to those places we too, the gods of the Four Great Kings, together with our armies, vehicles, and retinues, shall come for the sake of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. We shall provide protection to those <s>Dharma</s> preachers within a radius of one <s>yojana</s>, so that no one shall find an opportunity, seek an opportunity, or gain an opportunity to harm those <s>Dharma</s> preachers.'

body.text:
atha bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandametadavocat- "udgṛhṇīṣva tvam, ānanda, imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ, dhāraya pareṣāṃ ca vistareṇa samprakāśaya" / āha- "asmin dharmaparyāya udgṛhīte, ko nāmayaṃ bhagavan dharmaparyāyaḥ, kathaṃ cainaṃ dhārayāmi?"
bhagavānāmantrayate sma- "tasmādānanda, imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ 'vimalakīrtinirdeśaṃ' vā 'yamakavyatyastābhinirhāraṃ' vāpy 'acintyavimokṣaparivartannāma' dharmaparyāyaṃ dhāraya" /
idamavocad bhagavān / āttamanā licchavirvimalakīrtirmajuśrīśca kumārabhūtaḥ sa cāyuṣmānānandaste ca bodhisattvāte ca mahāśrāvakāḥ sā ca sarvāvatī parṣatsadevamānuṣāsura gandharvaśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti /
body.translated_text:
Then the Blessed One said to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Take up, <s>Ānanda</s>, this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, retain it, and expound it in detail to others.' He said: 'Having taken up this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, what is its name, Blessed One, and how shall I retain it?'
The Blessed One addressed him: 'Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, retain this <s>Dharma</s> discourse under the name "The Teaching of <s>Vimalakīrti</s>" (<s>Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s>), or "The Reconciliation of Opposites" (<s>Yamakavyatyastābhinirhāra</s>), or the <s>Dharma</s> discourse named "The Chapter on Inconceivable Liberation" (<s>Acintyavimokṣaparivarta</s>).'
Thus spoke the Blessed One. Delighted, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Crown Prince, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, those great <s>Śrāvakas</s>, that entire assembly, and the whole world with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: pūrvayogasya saddharmaparīnandanāyāśca parivarto nāma dvādaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: This is the twelfth chapter, entitled 'The Antecedent Practice and the Rejoicing in the True <s>Dharma</s>' (<s>Pūrvayoga</s> and <s>Saddharmaparīnandana</s>).

body.text: vimalakīrtinirdeśo nāma mahāyānasūtraṃ samāptam /
body.translated_text: The <s>Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s>, a <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtra</s>, is concluded.
